title: Barley Net Blotch Initiative (BNBI) Program 2 – Host and pathogen genetics
description:
Net blotches pose an escalating and urgent threat to Australian barley, costing the industry an estimated $122 million each year through disease-related yield losses, downgraded grain quality, and higher fungicide management costs. Widespread planting of susceptible varieties, the practice of growing barley on barley, and an over-reliance on fungicides with a singular mode of action are driving net blotch pathogens to evolve and spread faster than current surveillance, varietal resistance breeding, management and extension efforts can respond.
This investment seeks to help Australian barley growers keep ahead of a threat that is moving faster than current tools can handle. It will be delivered through a five-year, nationally focused Barley Net Blotch Initiative (BNBI) comprising three interlinked programs supported by a dedicated coordinator:
? Program 1 - Pathogen surveillance, monitoring, and screening
? Program 2- Host and pathogen genetics
? Program 3 - Integrated disease management and extension
? Program C - Coordination and capacity development
GRDC is seeking a capable partner to deliver BNBI Program 2 that will fast-track delivery of high levels of durable host resistance in well-adapted backgrounds supported by breeder-deployable validated markers, characterised resistance sources, insights and capability from foundational and expanded pathogenic genomics research, a new durability risk-assessment framework, and a feasibility assessment of genome-editing capability.

title: Open innovation call to realise step changes in soil and water productivity and unlock plant potential
description:
PLEASE SEE THE APPROACH TO MARKET ON THE GRDC WEBSITE FOR ALL AVAILABLE INFORMATION FOR THIS REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL: https://grdc.com.au/research/partnering-in-rde-investment/opportunities/current-opportunities/open-innovation-call-to-realise-step-changes-in-soil-and-water-productivity-and-unlock-plant-potential
Background to the open innovation call
A concerted RD&E focus on improving water use efficiency (WUE) has enabled Australian growers to become world leaders in dryland grain production. Improved varieties, agronomic practices, cropping sequences, soil amelioration and other innovations have underpinned these gains. However, growers still have a need to take these gains in water use efficiency and push them even further given climate projections of hotter, drier conditions across most of southern Australia, a decline in cool-season rainfall, and more frequent and extreme weather events. Growers’ ability to outpace these challenges through new frontiers in soil and water productivity and unlocking plant potential will be a key determinant of future profitability and resilience.
Overview of the open innovation call
There is significant value to be captured for growers through the removal of soil constraints, increasing water and nutrient uptake, and increasing the efficiency with which water and nutrient reserves are used by crops. GRDC has made substantial investments in soil amelioration and soil re-engineering to help growers and will continue to do so. These investments have generated valuable knowledge and demonstrated substantial productivity gains. However, key questions remain about the soil–plant–microbial processes behind these gains, particularly why some interventions do not deliver the expected benefits. This open innovation call will complement existing investments by addressing these and other knowledge gaps and unlock further production potential.
The opportunity to drive innovation in these areas is often constrained by a lack of foundational knowledge below-ground on soil-plant-microbial interactions. Foundational knowledge on root form, function, and diversity, soil microbial function and community dynamics, rhizosphere interactions, below-ground phenotyping and related areas underpin the opportunity to create new frontiers in soil and water productivity and the unlocking of plant potential.
Therefore, GRDC is progressing an open innovation call to address these foundational knowledge gaps and create the capacity and momentum that could enable crops to gain access to more water and nutrients and use them more effectively. GRDC is seeking project proposals that deliver against one or more of six-high level scope areas that represent key gaps in the GRDC portfolio (Table 1). GRDC expects that projects established through this open innovation call may be connected into a future ‘below-ground mission’ through research forums, study tours, and other mechanisms that foster mutually beneficial collaborations.
Applications are encouraged from:
• Australian and/or international organisations,
• Public and/or private entities, and
• Existing GRDC projects that could be strategically varied/expanded to address the scope areas.

title: Grain Automate Open Innovation Call
description:
Grain Automate is a national research, development and extension initiative of the Grains Research and Development Corporation. It seeks to accelerate the development, validation and adoption of machine automation, autonomy and intelligent systems, across a range of form factors, including machinery, implements, UAVs and digital systems, that deliver measurable value to Australian grain growers. The initiative is largely focused within the farm gate, while recognising relevant connections with logistics, suppliers and post-farm-gate systems.
The initiative complements existing investment in precision agriculture, digital agronomy and advanced analytics. It recognises that grower value will be created through a combination of industry readiness, targeted technology development, integration across physical and digital systems, and step-change improvements in precision. This call builds on the approach of the Grain Automate Program.

TRA currently provides access to these datasets through a data analytics platform used by internal staff, State and Territory Tourism Organisations (STOs), and a range of external subscribers including government agencies, educational institutions, research organisations and tourism businesses. The solution must maintain existing business-critical functionality, support evolving user requirements and ensure the ongoing delivery of tourism data services to stakeholders. title: Early Intervention Treatment and Triage Program
description:
The Department of Industry, Science and Resources is seeking a suitably qualified supplier to deliver an integrated, nationally accessible Early Intervention Triage and Treatment Program for eligible employees experiencing new or emerging physical or psychological injury, illness or symptoms that are affecting, or may affect, their ability to work.
The service will provide a single point of access to timely nurse-led clinical triage, assessment and advice. Where clinically appropriate and eligibility requirements are met, employees will be supported to access short-term treatment through suitably qualified and experienced health practitioners, including general practitioners, physiotherapists and psychological support services.
The service must provide coordinated pathways from initial contact and triage through to treatment, follow-up and completion of services. This includes appropriate referral and appointment coordination, communication with employees and practitioners, follow-up of treatment and required documentation, and, where relevant, information to support an employee's capacity to remain at work or safely return to work.
The successful supplier will be responsible for the effective end-to-end delivery of the service and active management of its practitioner network. This includes practitioner selection and onboarding, maintaining current program and referral information across the network, quality assurance, monitoring service delivery and documentation, and proactively identifying and addressing recurring or systemic issues.
The service must be accessible to employees across Australia, including regional and remote locations, with virtual or telehealth options where clinically appropriate. Service delivery must also be accessible, inclusive and responsive to disability and other accessibility requirements and individual cultural, communication and other needs.
The department is seeking a supplier that will actively manage the service throughout the contract period and work collaboratively with the department to maintain and improve service quality and employee experience. This includes proactive contract and relationship management, meaningful reporting and service insights, billing and financial administration, communication and promotion of the service, performance monitoring and continuous improvement.
The supplier will also be required to support transition and implementation of the service, including practitioner network readiness, service pathways, systems and administrative arrangements, reporting and billing arrangements, and operational documentation, communications, forms and templates required for service commencement.
Service performance will be monitored against agreed service levels and performance measures, including timeliness, accessibility, practitioner network performance, documentation, responsiveness, billing accuracy, reporting, issue resolution and implementation of corrective actions.

title: Request for Tender in relation to a Social Cohesion Framework for Schools
description:
This procurement is being undertaken to identify a supplier with the appropriate expertise, capability and capacity to develop a Social Cohesion Framework for Schools (the Framework). The Government is delivering the Framework in response to Recommendation 29 of the Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia's report, A National Response to Islamophobia: A Strategic Framework for Inclusion, Safety and Prosperity, which calls for a framework to address all forms of racism and discrimination in schools.
The Framework will be voluntary and non-regulatory in nature, and will provide practical, evidence-based guidance to support inclusive, safe and respectful learning environments and strengthen schools' ability to prevent and respond to racism, faith-based discrimination, and other forms of discrimination. It will be available for all schools and education sectors and will be designed to be nationally relevant while complementing existing jurisdictional and sector policies and processes. It is intended for use by school leaders, teachers, support staff, students, parents and carers, and school system and policy teams.
The project will include:
Extensive stakeholder consultation to ensure the Framework is practical, accessible and implementable for school sectors.
Review of contemporary research evidence and best-practice approaches for addressing social cohesion and discrimination the Australian context.
Development of the FRamework and accompanying practical implementation guidance products that will support schools to implement the Framework's guidance and key principles.
User testing of the Framework and its accompanying products.
Reporting requirements including a Project Plan and Project Report.
Please refer to the Statement of Requirements for the full description of services.

title: Private Hospital Services
description:
DVA is seeking the provision of Private Hospital services for Entitled Persons by publishing this Invitation to Provide Private Hospital Services to the Veteran Community.
DVA serves Australia’s veteran community, through the provision of programmes of care, compensation and commemoration.
DVA’s aim is to secure high quality private hospital care for Entitled Persons delivered for a fair price, at the most convenient locations for Entitled Persons. As the veteran community ages, their capacity to access a wider range of care appropriate to their needs is increasingly important. Managing emerging and different needs of contemporary veterans is also a priority. DVA also aims to continually improve the quality and safety of services, and the health outcomes for DVA clients, through the purchase of evidence-based treatment services.
DVA’s New Approach to Contracting for Private Hospital Services
In the past DVA contracted with Private Hospitals for services to Entitled Persons through a Request for Tenders (RFT).
The current process that DVA is engaging in with Private Hospital providers is not an RFT.
DVA has introduced new arrangements for providers to contract with DVA. This is a simplified contracting model that DVA is using to facilitate engagement with suitably qualified providers.
A summary of the key features of the new arrangements are:
maximising the numbers of participating providers to achieve wide access to private hospitals services for the veteran community;

title: Virtulisation Platform
description:
The Digital Transformation Agency (DTA), on behalf of the Australian Government, invites information on virtualisation platform options that could help agencies sustain or optimise existing environments, operate different platforms together, or transition to replacement or modernised environments.
Options may apply across on-premises, public cloud and hybrid environments, including approaches that preserve choice, portability and future flexibility.
Responses will help the DTA understand:
• what the market can deliver
• how available options could be implemented
• the full cost of available options over time
• security and sovereignty considerations
• workforce impacts
• purchasing options
• realistic transition timeframes.
The DTA seeks information on available virtualisation platform options, where they fit, how they integrate with existing environments, the dependencies they create or reduce, and their technical, commercial and operational implications over time.
This RFI is an information-gathering exercise. The DTA may decide not to proceed further. The DTA may also invite respondents to clarify their responses, present their capabilities or provide further information.
The DTA may use the information received to refine the requirement and decide whether and how to approach the market, including through a request for tender or request for proposal. Any later activity would be separate and at the DTA’s discretion.
The DTA may also provide information received through this RFI to other agencies to support market analysis, planning and future activities.
Please see full description in attached dta-rfi-93304 Virtulisation Platforms.dox

title: Notice of RFT - Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel of Outreach Program Counsellors for the
description:
This is a pre-release notice to provide advance notification of a proposed RFT for the Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel.
Please note, eligibility, application requirements, assessment processes, and contractual arrangements will be set out in the forthcoming RFT. No evaluation criteria, scoring methodology, or commercial terms are being released at this stage. The Department reserves the right to modify or cancel the proposed RFT at its discretion.
Background on Open Arms
Open Arms is Australia’s national accredited provider of mental health and wellbeing services for veterans and the families of veterans.
Open Arms provides mental health counselling, relationship counselling, peer support services, and group programs for people with Australian Defence Force (ADF) service (current and former serving members) and their immediate families.
Open Arms provides free and confidential counselling through a national network of multidisciplinary mental health professionals, delivered in dedicated Open Arms centres by the DVA’s staff, or through the Panel; being a network of accredited mental health clinicians, engaged to support the delivery of services on behalf of Open Arms across Australia through the Outreach Program.
Open Arms can provide counselling, care coordination and peer support services to veterans and the families of veterans within an episode of care model, where clients engage with our services for goal directed interventions for a defined period.
Open Arms aims to provide timely access to appropriate services and care, based on a comprehensive holistic assessment and integrated care pathways to meet client needs and support recovery. This includes working in partnership with health systems, including primary health, as well as other community agencies to ensure comprehensive support for our clients.
Background on the Panel and Outreach Program
Open Arms’ Model of Care provides the organisational framework that underpins the delivery of all Outreach Program services. It guides how we support veterans and the families of veterans through trauma-informed, military-aware, recovery-oriented care, while ensuring consistent clinical governance, quality service delivery and positive client outcomes. In 2024 the Panel was established through which Outreach Providers provide Open Arms services to clients. The Panel is the mechanism for Open Arms to engage with Outreach Providers to ensure the highest level of support can be delivered to clients. Only organisations or individuals appointed to the Panel can provide Open Arms Outreach Program Counselling Services.
The categories of services that are delivered through the Panel include:
Outreach Program Counsellors (OPCs), who provide individual, couples, or family counselling
Group Program Facilitators (GPFs), who facilitate evidence-informed, military-aware group programs that strengthen resilience, build practical skills, and promote wellbeing
Clinical Supervisors, who provide professional supervision to Open Arms’ staff.
Outreach Providers on the Panel can provide one, two or all three service streams, depending on their qualifications, experience and the services they are approved to deliver.
Go to the Open Arms website for further information:
https://www.openarms.gov.au/about/open-arms-outreach-program
Expansion of definition of OPC
In 2025 the Veterans’ Entitlements (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025 and the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025), were enacted which amended the MRCA Treatment Principles (No. MRCC 53/2013) and the Treatment Principles (Instrument 2013 No. R52) – (collectively the Treatment Principles) – to expand the types of professions who can provide Outreach Program Counselling as an Outreach Program Counsellor (OPC). Now that occupational therapists, registered nurses, social workers (general) and counsellors are recognised as additional profession types eligible to apply to become a provider, the Department wishes to update the Panel accordingly through the proposed RFT.
The Department is therefore looking to procure Outreach Providers from the following eligible professions:
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a psychologist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as an occupational therapist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a registered nurse;
a person who is eligible for membership with the Australian Association of Social Workers;
or
a person who is registered:
as a registered clinical counsellor with the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia;
as a counsellor at registration category Level 3 or Level 4 with the Australian Counselling Association Limited.
The Department is currently planning to release the RFT to market through publication on AusTender in September 2026, however this timeframe may be subject to change.
Please note that this is not an RFT and does not commit the Department to proceed. The Close Date and Time stated in this notice relates to this pre-release notice only and does not reflect the proposed RFT commencement and closing dates for potential tenderers to lodge their submissions. The RFT, where undertaken, will be published on AusTender and will include the Closing Date and Time for lodgement of submissions.

publicQuestions.question: Is 11,000 kg GVM a strict maximum requirement, or would a higher GVM be acceptable? Current chassis options within the 11,000 kg GVM range are limited, and a higher-rated chassis may provide greater flexibility for payload, equipment stowage, and operational capability.
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Valued Suppliers,

The mandatory requirement of an 11 tonne GVM chassis can be found at Attachment A2 Specification Response Schedule C1.a. Suppliers should also pay particular attention to B4.a and B1.g in relation to proportionately balanced axel weights. This size is necessary for the RFSQ so that the appliance can be accommodated within existing stations and brigade sheds, can be effectively driven by volunteers and can traverse narrow tracks located in rural and remote parts of Queensland. Generally, it is recommended that suppliers consider heights to 3.1 metres and length to 7.8 metres (dual-cab).

Kind Regards,

Mabel

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Queensland Fire Department Procurement Team,

Regarding ITO VP512877 – Supply of Minimum 70 x Medium Attack Appliances, we have reviewed Parts A, B and C and the associated technical specifications.

Before commencing detailed engineering, chassis selection and commercial pricing, we kindly request clarification of the following:

1. Overseas Manufacturer Eligibility

Can an overseas fire appliance manufacturer participate directly as the prime tenderer without an Australian ABN/ACN, provided it appoints suitably qualified Australian subcontractors for vehicle certification, delivery, servicing and warranty support?

Is Australian company registration or a minimum Australian local-content percentage mandatory?

2. Vehicle Certification and Approvals

Can Australian Design Rules (ADR), NHVR vehicle modification certification and applicable vehicle registration approvals be completed through authorised Australian engineering partners after contract award but before vehicle delivery?

Which certificates and approvals must already be submitted with the tender?

3. Chassis Manufacturer Authorisation

Can the required cab-chassis OEM authorisation and evidence of training for vehicle modification and maintenance be provided after contract award, or must they accompany the initial tender submission?

4. Partial Offers and Contract Allocation

Would QFD accept separate offers for the 30 × 8,000 kg GVM vehicles and the 40 × 11,000 kg GVM vehicles, or for individual vehicle configurations?

Must every bidder offer all 70 appliances?

5. Technical Compliance and Alternatives

Where an overseas manufacturer proposes an equivalent technical solution meeting the required operational performance and safety standards, may it be submitted as an alternative offer?

Which specification requirements are strictly non-negotiable?

6. Financial Security and Insurance

Please confirm whether any bid security, bid bond, cash deposit or performance bank guarantee is required.

Can the required AUD 20 million public/products liability and AUD 5 million professional indemnity insurance policies be arranged after selection and before contract execution?

We would appreciate clear written confirmation, particularly regarding eligibility and the timing of technical approvals, so that manufacturers can commence compliant design and production planning without delay.

Thank you for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 15/Nov/2026 03:45 PM)

Dear Valued Suppliers:

Please refer to QFD's responses below:

Answer to Q1: Whilst Australian companies are preferred they are not mandated.  As mentioned at the Industry briefing, reliability, serviceability and access to appropriately qualified local mechanics will be a key matter for consideration by the panel.  Any overseas company with no local presence cannot meet the local benefits element of the evaluation.

Answer to Q2: All vendors regardless of location must be capable of proving their ability to meet NHVR, ADR and TMR requirements.

Specifications Clause A2 requests evidence of compliance to meet standards, guidelines and transport requirements as a mandatory requirement. Tender response must comply with all mandatory requirements.

Answer to Q3: Must be at tender submission stage.

Answer to Q4: Separate offers are acceptable.

Answer to Q5: Mandatory criteria are non-negotiable.  Alternative options pursuant to DESIRABLE criteria will be considered.

Answer to Q6: Financial security at this stage is not necessary.  This will be dependent on the risk profile of the supplier and the department’s due diligence findings in regards to their financial viability.  Insurances must be obtained prior to the award of a contract.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Records management and Content Manager (Sections 2.2.3 and 2.3, Annexure A RMS-005, RMS-007, CRM-036, CRM-037) Annexure A requires a single authoritative repository for records (RMS-007) and bulk import of existing documents (RMS-005), and the CRM requirements (CRM-036 and CRM-037) address how documents and metadata are handled between the ERP and the records repository. The scope, however, refers to integration with Content Manager, and the Shire expects its own IT staff to build integrations to retained systems. A single platform that holds records and ERP transactions together would remove an interface, reduce ongoing integration effort for the Shire, and place accountability for records compliance and migration with one provider. Please confirm that respondents may propose replacement of Content Manager as part of the core solution, and that a replacement proposal will be evaluated on the same basis as an integration approach under the Fit for Purpose criterion. If so, please advise: (a) whether migration of existing records, metadata and retention and disposal information is in scope; (b) the approximate volume (record count and storage size); (c) whether replacement may be priced as an option alongside integration; and (d) whether a replacement solution may be hosted within the Shire's existing Microsoft 365 tenant.

2. Submission format and order (Sections 1.10 and 1.11) Please confirm that completed native Excel versions of Annexures A, B and C may be lodged in addition to the single PDF, that scanned copies of wet-ink signed pages are acceptable for the Offer Form and Pricing Schedule, and that the prescribed submission order applies to the required sections only, with supplementary documentation placed last.

3. Staff and user numbers (Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, Annexure C) Section 2.2.1 states 225 employees including 58 casual staff, Section 2.2.2 states approximately 165 permanent and 60 casual staff, and Annexure C refers to approximately 200 staff and 51 casual staff. Please confirm the correct payroll headcount and the numbers of users requiring full ERP access (stated as 10), approval or enquiry access (100) and employee self-service only (225), so that pricing is prepared on a comparable basis.

4. Price basis (Sections 1.32 and 5.8, Annexure C) Sections 1.32 and 5.8 require fixed lump sum prices for the duration of the Contract, while Annexure C provides for annual price adjustment and a five-year cost summary for recurring costs. Please confirm that recurring subscription charges may be adjusted annually as set out in Annexure C.

5. Contract term and liquidated damages (Sections 3.1 and 3.28) Section 3.1 states the Contract expires on completion of the Requirements, whereas the scope includes ongoing licensing and support. Please confirm the intended contract term for ongoing licensing and support. Section 3.28 refers to liquidated damages in an amount stated in the General Conditions, but no amount is stated. Please confirm the amount or basis.

6. Alternative Response (Sections 1.15 and 5.7) Please confirm that items listed in the List of Contract Departures Requested (Section 5.7) do not require the response to be marked as an Alternative Response.

7. Asset management scope (Section 2.3, Annexure B) Asset management and works maintenance management, including heavy plant maintenance schedules, is listed in both the Core Solution and the Optional Modules. Please confirm which functions are required in the Core Solution and which apply only to the Optional Module.

8. Leisure centre and HR integration (Sections 2.2.2, 2.2.3 and 2.3) Please confirm whether Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre staff are within the payroll, timesheet and rostering scope, and the expected scope and direction of integration with Pulse (HR) and the leisure centre system.

9. Data migration (Section 2.3.2) All dataset volumes in the indicative volume table are shown as TBD. Please advise when volumes will be provided, and who is responsible for extracting data from Community Hub (OpenOffice), given the OpenOffice data model is undocumented.

10. Award timing (Section 1.38) Section 1.38 indicates Council award in April or May 2027, while the Request Summary states a decision date of 9 June 2027. Please confirm the expected award date.

11. Requirement priorities (Annexure A) INF-037, CRM-019 and CRM-031 use "should" wording but are marked MUST, and INF-021 (DoT integration) is marked COULD while INF-051 (DoT data format) is marked MUST. Please confirm the intended priorities.
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1 Records Management & Content Manager

•	Respondents may propose native records management in place of Content Manager. Both approaches will be evaluated on the same basis under Fit for Purpose. Any replacement must meet the State Records Act 2000 and the Shire’s Recordkeeping Plan.

(a)	Yes. Migration of existing records, metadata and retention and disposal information is in scope where replacement is proposed.

(b)	Volumes are [TBC]. Respondents should state their assumed volumes in Annexure C.

(c)	Yes. Price replacement in the Records Management lines of Annexure C and show the integration-only cost separately in the Assumptions / Notes column.

(d)	Yes. Respondents should state any Microsoft 365 licensing or configuration dependencies.

Q2 Submission Format & Order

•	Annexures A, B and C are to be submitted in Excel, together with the PDF version of the RFT document. Scanned pages signed in wet ink are acceptable; pasted, typed or initialled signatures are not. Supplementary documentation is to be placed last.

Q3 Staff Numbers & Users

•	Total employees – 225 (60 of which are casual)

•	Full ERP access – 10

•	Limited ERP access – 100

•	Kiosk access – 225

Q4 Price Basis

•	Respondents may apply an annual adjustment to recurring subscription, licensing and support fees. Implementation costs remain fixed lump sum. Respondents must state the following in the Annual Price Adjustment section of Annexure C.

*whether an adjustment applies

*the basis of the adjustment (fixed percentage, CPI or other)

*any rate or cap

*the first adjustment date

Q5 Contract Term

•	Pricing is required for the initial five (5) year term, as set out in the Annexure C Costs Summary.

Q6 Alternative Response

•	Departures to the standard SaaS agreement listed in Section 5.7 (List of Contract Departures Requested) will be treated as part of a conforming response, and the response does not need to be marked as an Alternative Response.

Q7 Asset Management

•	Asset management is seen as an optional module and forms part of Annexure B

Q8 Leisure Centre & HR Integration

•	MALC staff are included in the 225 staff count for payroll, rostering & timesheets

•	Integration with Pulse (HR) software not a mandatory function but worth noting if readily available

Q9 Data Migration

•	The extent of data migration is yet to be determined and agreed with the successful vendor. Please provide an hourly rate at Section 5.5 if your solution offers assistance with data migration.

Q10 Award Timing

•	We anticipate a decision being made by Council by no later than May 2027.

Q11 Requirement Priorities

•	INF-037	Should be a “SHOULD”

•	CRM-019	Should be a “MUST” but the requirement should read “The system should identify a duplicate record and allow the user to accept or merge the record”.

•	CRM-031	Should be a “MUST”

•	INF-021	Should be a “SHOULD”

•	INF-051	Ignore INF-051

description:
MidCoast Council (the Principal) is seeking submissions from appropriately qualified and experienced Tenderers for the Design and Construction of the Wingham Sports Complex Lighting Upgrade. The works generally comprise the detailed design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of new LED sports lighting infrastructure, including two new sports lighting poles to Field 5, associated foundations, structural and electrical works, underground services and modifications to existing sports lighting infrastructure.

Tenderers are required to provide separate submissions and pricing for two delivery options:

•	Option 1 – Field 5 Lighting Expansion: Installation of two new sports lighting poles to the northern side of Field 5, together with new LED luminaires installed to the existing three poles located along the northern side of Fields 3 and 4, to provide a minimum maintained average horizontal illuminance of 100 lux to Field 5.

•	Option 2 – Field 5 Expansion and Full LED Upgrade: Installation of two new sports lighting poles to the northern side of Field 5, together with replacement and upgrade of the existing sports lighting across the six existing poles servicing Fields 3 and 4, to provide a minimum maintained average horizontal illuminance of 100 lux across Fields 3, 4 and 5.

The completed works are to comply with the Contract Documents, relevant Australian Standards, statutory requirements and MidCoast Council requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Wingham Sports Complex is an established community sporting facility servicing rugby league, touch football and soccer, including junior and senior training and competition activities.

Fields 3 and 4 are the primary illuminated playing fields within the complex and are currently serviced by six existing 20 m sports lighting poles fitted with metal-halide floodlights. The existing lighting infrastructure is approximately 20 years old and Council is seeking to upgrade the system to modern LED sports lighting to improve lighting performance, reliability, energy efficiency and ongoing maintenance outcomes.

Field 5 is located immediately north of Fields 3 and 4 and is currently used predominantly as an overflow field for junior sport and training. The field does not currently have sufficient sports lighting to support regular night-time use. With increasing participation across the resident sporting codes, Council has identified the need to increase the usable capacity of the complex by providing compliant sports lighting to Field 5.

The proposed works will extend lighting coverage to Field 5 through the installation of two new sports lighting poles along the northern side of the field and the utilisation of existing lighting poles on the southern side. Council is also considering the broader replacement of the existing metal-halide lighting servicing Fields 3 and 4 as part of the project.

The completed lighting system is intended to achieve a minimum maintained average horizontal illuminance of 100 lux across the nominated playing areas, providing suitable lighting for evening training and community-level sporting use while improving the overall capacity and flexibility of Wingham Sports Complex.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Woollahra Municipal Council,

We respectfully request clarification on the following points to help tenderers prepare an accurate Schedule of Rates:

1. Cleaning area

Could Council please advise the approximate area, in m², to be cleaned at each of the 15 business centres, or the total area across all centres under the annual cleaning program?

2. Indicative budget or historical spend

Could Council please provide an indicative annual budget, or the historical annual spend, for high-pressure cleaning of the business centres?

3. Additional and emergency works

Could Council please advise the expected frequency or volume of additional, urgent and emergency cleaning works beyond the annual cleaning program, for example the number of call-outs per year based on past demand?

4. Number of contractors

Does Council intend to appoint a single contractor or a panel of providers under this RFT? If a panel, how many providers does Council expect to appoint?

5. Site inspection

Will Council hold a site inspection or briefing for tenderers? If not, may tenderers inspect the business centres independently during the tender period?

6. Water and wastewater

Will Council provide access to water at the business centres, or must the contractor supply its own water? Are there approved locations for disposal of collected wastewater?

Thank you for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please see the below answers:

1. The total approximate area subject to the annual high-pressure cleaning program across the 15 business centres is 33,000 m².

2. Council will not be disclosing an indicative budget or historical expenditure for these services. Consistent with Council's procurement practices, Council resolved a number of years ago not to disclose indicative budgets for procurement activities, as doing so may influence pricing outcomes. This approach supports the achievement of competitive pricing and value for money through the tender process.

3. The frequency and extent of urgent or emergency works cannot be accurately predicted and will vary depending on operational requirements and unforeseen circumstances. Based on historical experience, Council has typically required approximately one to two emergency call-outs per year; however, this should be regarded as indicative only and does not represent a guarantee of future work volumes.

4. Council's preference is to appoint a single contractor to deliver the services under the contract. However, Council reserves the right to appoint more than one contractor should it determine that doing so represents the best value outcome and is in Council's interests.

5. Council does not intend to hold a formal site briefing or inspection. Tenderers may undertake their own inspections of the business centres during the tender period. Any inspections must be conducted from publicly accessible areas and in a manner that does not disrupt businesses, pedestrians or Council operations.

6. Contractors are required to supply their own water for the performance of the services.

Thank you.

Subject: Tender SC10186 – Request for Site Inspection and Clarifications

Dear Tender Team,

We are currently preparing our submission for Tender SC10186 – High-Pressure Cleaning Services and would appreciate clarification on the following matters:

Site inspection and scope

1. Would Council be able to arrange a site inspection or site briefing for prospective tenderers prior to the closing date?

2. Could Council provide an estimated breakdown of square metres requiring high-pressure cleaning at each of the 15 business centres?

3. Could Council clarify the exact boundaries of the cleaning areas, including whether kerbs, gutters, street furniture and adjoining public spaces are included in the annual cleaning program?

Existing contract and expenditure

4. Are these services currently delivered internally or through an external contractor? If outsourced, could Council identify the incumbent contractor?

5. Could Council provide the historical annual expenditure on these services for the past two financial years?

6. Approximately how many additional, urgent and emergency cleaning requests have been undertaken annually?

Operational requirements

7. Will Council provide access to water supply points at each location, or must contractors supply their own water?

8. Could Council clarify its specific requirements for wastewater collection, treatment and disposal?

9. Are any additional traffic management arrangements, permits or approvals anticipated for the nominated cleaning areas?

Contract structure

10. Would Council accept a tender from a principal contractor that manages the contract while subcontracting 100% of the physical cleaning services to suitably qualified and insured subcontractors?

11. Does Council intend to appoint a single contractor or establish a panel of service providers?

12. If a panel is established, how would work allocations be determined, and is there an anticipated minimum volume of work per provider?

Thank you for your assistance. We look forward to your response.

Kind regards
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please see the below responses:

Site inspection and scope

1. Council does not intend to hold a formal site briefing or inspection. Tenderers may undertake their own inspections of the business centres during the tender period. Any inspections must be conducted from publicly accessible areas and in a manner that does not disrupt businesses, pedestrians or Council operations.

2. The total approximate area subject to the annual high-pressure cleaning program across the 15 business centres is 33,000 m².

3. All footpaths and paved areas are inside the Business Centres. Kerbs included to maintain visual appearance of footpath area.

Existing contract and expenditure

4. Currently carried out by several contractors on an ad-hoc basis.

5. Council will not be disclosing an indicative budget or historical expenditure for these services. Consistent with Council's procurement practices, Council resolved a number of years ago not to disclose indicative budgets for procurement activities, as doing so may influence pricing outcomes. This approach supports the achievement of competitive pricing and value for money through the tender process.

6. Less than five (5) annually.

Operational requirements

7. Contractors are required to supply their own water for the performance of the services.

8. Must be managed in accordance with relevant legislation and environmental requirements.

9. Potential for traffic control requirements when cleaning footpaths on arterial roads.

Contract structure

10. Yes, this will be considered if a conforming tender is submitted.

11. Council's preference is to appoint a single contractor to deliver the services under the contract. However, Council reserves the right to appoint more than one contractor should it determine that doing so represents the best value outcome and is in Council's interests.

12. This will depend on contractor availability. No minimum volume of work will be provided.

Thank you

publicQuestions.answer: Council removes all weeds, rubbish and leaves as part of regular street sweeping schedule.

publicQuestions.question:
Subject: Clarification – Kerb and Gutter Cleaning Requirements

Dear Council Team,

Sam's Pressure Washing can remove weeds growing between pavement joints using appropriate high-pressure cleaning methods, where suitable for the surface.

We understand that the contractor is responsible for managing and disposing of debris and waste generated through pressure-cleaning activities.

However, we would appreciate clarification regarding the collection and removal of existing rubbish, leaves and accumulated debris along kerbs and gutters.

Could Council please clarify:

Is the contractor expected to collect and remove existing leaves, general rubbish and loose debris from kerbs and gutters, in addition to the debris generated through pressure cleaning?

If this additional collection is required, does Council provide a designated waste collection or disposal facility?

Would this work be covered by the existing schedule of rates, or could it be treated as additional work and priced separately with Council's prior agreement?

We would appreciate clarification to ensure our proposed pricing accurately reflects the required scope of services.

Thank you for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Sam's Pressure Washing
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council confirms that the Contractor is only required to collect, manage and lawfully dispose of debris, waste and other material generated as a result of performing the pressure cleaning services.

The Contractor is not required to collect and remove existing leaves, litter, sediment or other accumulated debris from kerbs and gutters that was present prior to the commencement of the cleaning works. Council undertakes the cleaning of leaves and debris within kerbs and gutters as part of its regular street cleaning program.

Where Council requires services beyond the specified pressure cleaning scope, such requirements will be separately identified and agreed with the Contractor prior to the works being undertaken.

The Contractor remains responsible for disposing of all waste generated from the pressure cleaning activities at an appropriately licensed waste facility. Council does not provide a waste collection or disposal facility for this purpose.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Services: The Price schedule lists individual services inside each group (e.g. "Windows Supply & Installation (Glazier)" under Building Services, or "Cleaning – High Level Windows" under Cleaning Services). Can we tender for individual services only, or must we tender for the entire group (e.g. all of Building Services, all of Cleaning Services)?

2. Rounds: We are looking at services across more than one round (e.g. Round 1 multi-trade and Round 3 glazing/specialist services). Should we lodge one submission or a separate one for each round?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's preference is to appoint a single contractor to deliver the services under this Contract. However, Council reserves the right to appoint multiple contractors where it determines that doing so represents the best value outcome and is in Council's interests.

Tenderers are requested to submit a single tender response and clearly identify whether they are tendering to provide the full scope of services or only a specific portion of the services.

title: Request for Information - Targeted Engagement Programs (TEP)
description:
The Department of Education (DoE) invites responses to this Request for Information (RFI) for the quality assurance assessment of suppliers seeking to provide Targeted Engagement Programs in Queensland state schools.

The purpose of this RFI is to establish and maintain a register of pre-qualified suppliers for the delivery of Targeted Engagement Programs in Queensland state schools.

This RFI sets out the mandatory requirements and pre-qualification criteria against which respondents will be assessed, including their capability, capacity, experience and suitability to deliver Targeted Engagement Programs.

The RFI will remain open on an ongoing basis to allow suppliers to submit responses over time. Responses received will be assessed periodically, with assessments expected to occur quarterly. The initial assessment is scheduled to commence late Quarter 4, 2026 with the preferred supplier list to be published for schools to access in Semester 1, 2027.

These assessments will support the ongoing development and maintenance of the pre-qualified supplier register, including consideration of new submissions received since the previous assessment.

VIDEO - Preferred Provider Register - Information Session:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YCYHaYozYtM

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Department of Education is supporting students who need it most by providing funding directly to Queensland state schools with identified challenges to implement a Targeted Engagement Program.

Targeted Engagement Programs aim to improve attendance, decrease school disciplinary absences, increase Years 10-12 retention and assist students to transition from school to employment, training or further education by providing wraparound support and safe spaces to students.

Targeted Engagement Programs will be at the discretion of each school to support re-engagement needs, regardless of cultural background allowing more students access to programs.

Interested suppliers are highly encouraged to watch the information presentation to ensure their services align with Targeted Engagement Programs aims.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Section 1 of the RFI describes the process as establishing a register of pre-qualified suppliers, with the SLA confirming pre-qualification. However, the draft SLA expressly states that inclusion does not constitute pre-qualification, approval or endorsement.

•	Could you clarify the intended status and purpose of the register?

•	What benefit will inclusion on the register provide to suppliers and schools, particularly given that schools can continue to engage providers who are not registered?

•	Will schools be encouraged or required to consider registered suppliers when procuring Targeted Engagement Programs?

2. How will this framework interact with existing arrangements between schools and external service providers, including Approved External Agency (AEA) arrangements for Youth Support Coordinators/Student Wellbeing Officers?

•	Will providers delivering existing programs need to participate in this process to continue offering those services?

•	Will existing contracts or arrangements be affected?

3. With regard to the scope of Targeted Engagement Programs –

•	Is the intention to assess suppliers' overall capability to deliver Targeted Engagement Programs, or are we required to submit fully developed programs for assessment? Can programs instead be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs?

•	Is there a defined scope or minimum set of requirements for what constitutes a Targeted Engagement Program?

•	Can programs include community-based activities, outreach and off-site learning experiences for disengaged students, or are they intended to be delivered exclusively on school premises?

•	Can suppliers nominate multiple programs or service models, and subsequently add or amend these without undergoing the full assessment process again?

4. With regard to contractual arrangements and responsibilities –

•	Will the Department provide a standard agreement for schools to use when engaging suppliers, or will contracts be negotiated directly between schools and providers?

•	How will responsibilities for student supervision, duty of care, risk assessment, attendance and incident management be shared between schools and providers?

•	Will schools be responsible for obtaining parental consent, assessing student suitability and providing relevant information about student needs and risks before participation?

•	Will providers retain the ability to decline or discontinue a student's participation where there are concerns about their suitability or safety?

5. With regard to insurance and liability –

•	Is product liability insurance mandatory for providers delivering educational and engagement programs that do not involve supplying products?

6. Assessment and ongoing requirements –

•	Will the register identify the specific programs or types of services each supplier has been assessed as capable of delivering?

•	Beyond the reassessment process outlined in the SLA, will suppliers be required to provide regular performance or program outcome reporting to the Department?

RFI Section 1:

1. Section 1 of the RFI describes the process as establishing a register of pre-qualified suppliers, with the SLA confirming pre-qualification.

The draft SLA expressly states that inclusion does not constitute pre-qualification, approval or endorsement.

Q1. Could you clarify the intended status and purpose of the register?

Clarification Q1: A revised RFI has been launched on VendorPanel which clarifies the purpose of the register.

Q2.a). How will this framework interact with existing arrangements between schools and external service providers, including Approved External Agency (AEA) arrangements for Youth Support Coordinators/Student Wellbeing Officers?

Clarification Q2a): TEP is a new program offering a range of services to a broader cohort of eligible students.

Q2b). Will providers delivering existing programs need to participate in this process to continue offering those services? Clarification Q2b): No

Q2c). Will existing contracts or arrangements be affected? Clarification Q2c): No.

Q3a). With regard to the scope of Targeted Engagement Programs – Is the intention to assess suppliers' overall capability to deliver Targeted Engagement Programs? Clarification Q3a): No.

Q3b). Will providers delivering existing programs need to participate in this process to continue offering those services? Clarification Q3b): No

Q3c). Can programs instead be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs?

Clarification Q3c): Programs can be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs.

Q3d). Is there a defined scope or minimum set of requirements for what constitutes a Targeted Engagement Program?

Clarification Q3d): Clarification: Refer to the RFI documentation which sets out the minimum criteria.

Q3e). Can programs include community-based activities, outreach and off-site learning experiences for disengaged students, or are they intended to be delivered exclusively on school premises?

Clarification Q3e): The schools will determine the specific requirements which will outline delivery requirements and locations.

Q3f). Can suppliers nominate multiple programs or service models, and subsequently add or amend these without undergoing the full assessment process again?

Clarification Q3f): Suppliers are recommended to identify all programs/service models suitable for TEP delivery to avoid potential re-assessment.

Q4. With regard to contractual arrangements and responsibilities –

Q4a). Will the Department provide a standard agreement for schools to use when engaging suppliers, or will contracts be negotiated directly between schools and providers?

Clarification Q4a). This is outlined in the RFI revision 1 - Schools will be provided with a Short-form Contract where the school's specific requirements will be negotiated with the selected Supplier

Q4b). How will responsibilities for student supervision, duty of care, risk assessment, attendance and incident management be shared between schools and providers?

Clarification 4b): This is outlined in the Short-form Contract which will also include their School Details Form.

Q4c). Will schools be responsible for obtaining parental consent, assessing student suitability and providing relevant information about student needs and risks before participation?

Clarification Q4c): The Supplier must obtain additional consent forms from the students and parents/guardians enrolled in the Program before starting the Program.

Q4d). Will providers retain the ability to decline or discontinue a student's participation where there are concerns about their suitability or safety?

Clarification Q4d): Parents/caregivers and/or school staff (i.e. teachers) may nominate eligible students for enrolment in the Program.

The School Principal must approve the enrolment and withdrawal of students from the Program. If Our School Principal determines a student is to be withdrawn from the Program, the date of and reasons for their withdrawal must be provided.

Q5. With regard to insurance and liability –

Is product liability insurance mandatory for providers delivering educational and engagement programs that do not involve supplying products?

Clarification Q5: Product Liability Insurance may be required if the Supplier provides products or equipment as part of the TEP deliverables specified by the school. This will be determined on a case-by-case basis.

Q6. Assessment and ongoing requirements.

 Q1a). Will the register identify the specific programs or types of services each supplier has been assessed as capable of delivering?

Clarification Q1a): No, the register will only state what regions of QLD the supplier services.

Q1b). Beyond the reassessment process outlined in the SLA, will the suppliers be required to provide regular performance or program outcome reporting to the Department.

Clarification Q1b): Yes, this will be outlined in the Short-form Contract between the School and the Supplier.

Q7. When it comes to attaching documents, is there a maximum amount that can be uploaded?

Q7 Clarification: The RFI section two (2) - Supplier's Response advises criteria and information required. Responses of max 500 words to each Criteria is advised. title: Low Loader Float Replacement
description:
Supply and delivery of one Tri-axle (3x4) Low loader with a payload capacity of 27-30T

Council’s existing Low Loader float is due for replacement. The float is an essential component of Council’s fleet and plays a critical role in providing service across all departments.

The Low Loader will be used to move Council owned Plant and Equipment throughout the Shire and will be towed by Council’s Mercedes Benz Actros 2651 Prime Mover.

Council’s new Tri-Axle Low Loader will incorporate the latest technology, meet today’s safety requirements, and provide enhanced efficiency, reliability and durability.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Byron Shire is a local government area located in the Northern Rivers region of New South Wales, Australia. The shire is located adjacent to the Tasman Sea about 50 kilometres (31 mi) south of the Queensland border. The shire, administered from the town of Mullumbimby, covers an area of 566.7 square kilometres (218.8 sq mi), and has existed as a local government entity since 1906. The shire was named for Cape Byron, itself named by Captain Cook in May 1770 in honour of Vice-Admiral John Byron.

title: MBCC-581 - Management and Operation of Aquatic Facilities
description:
City of Moreton Bay invites submissions from suitably qualified and experienced organisations to manage and operate one or more of Council's aquatic venues.

City of Moreton Bay operates one of Queensland's largest local government aquatic networks, comprising a diverse mix of regional and local venues that deliver swimming, aquatic recreation, learn to swim programs, health and fitness services, and opportunities for community connection.

Collectively, the venues attract more than 1.5 million visits annually and play an important role in promoting active lifestyles, water safety, community wellbeing and participation across the region. The network includes both year-round and seasonal venues, ranging from major regional aquatic and leisure centres to local community pools servicing smaller townships.

Council is seeking innovative, community focused and commercially capable partners that can deliver safe, efficient and high-quality aquatic services while supporting Council's vision of healthy, active and connected communities.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Mareeba Shire is a growing, confident and sustainable Shire on the Atherton Tablelands in Far North Queensland. A Shire of diversity with a vibrant, multicultural population and landscapes that vary from World Heritage Rainforest and breathtaking waterfalls to productive agricultural farms and cattle properties. Tenders are invited for the painting of roof trusses and associated works within Harvest Hall at Prahran Market, 163 Commercial Road, South Yarra VIC 3141.

1. We're a global SaaS provider. Every customer is on the same platform, content library, and service terms, so we can't vary our standard Cloud Service Agreement and General Terms and Conditions (published on our website) for individual customers.

Would Council consider contracting on our standard terms, subject to mutual review? These could be brought in through Special Conditions that take precedence over the GCOC. If not, can we submit a conforming tender with a schedule of proposed departures, or do departures need to go in a separate alternative tender under Tender Conditions clause 7?

Some GCOC clauses don't fit a SaaS subscription:

- 10.4–10.6 (storage on a "foreign computer" and mixing of material)

- 21.5–21.6 (IP vesting and licensing)

- 21.3 and 22 (uncapped indemnities)

- 12–13 (monthly invoicing on completion)

Answer 1.

Please refer to clause 7 Conforming and Non-conforming tenders of the Tender Conditions.

7 - Conforming and Non-Conforming Tenders

7.1

 A Tenderer may lodge non-conforming Tenders only if it has lodged a conforming Tender.

7.2

 Each non-conforming Tender must be accompanied by a clear summary of all points of difference between the non-conforming Tender and the conforming Tender.

7.3

Each non-conforming Tender must be submitted on a separate Tender Response.

7.5

A Tender may be considered as non-conforming if the Tenderer has failed to supply any of the information required by the Conditions of Tender, does not comply with any of the requirements of the Conditions of Tender or has been lodged subject to any condition or qualification.

7.6

If more than one conforming Tender is lodged, each Tender must be accompanied by a clear summary of all points of difference between each conforming Tender.

The Principal will not be obliged to consider any Tender that does not comply with the requirements of the Conditions of Tender.

2. Section 2.5 asks for a profit and loss statement and the latest financial return.

We don't publicly disclose our financial statements. We have a local physical office in Australia and support customers across Australia and New Zealand, including federal and state government agencies and local councils. Would Council accept alternative evidence of financial standing?

Answer 2.

You may submit a letter from your accountant

3. For section 2.8, do cloud hosting providers and third-party content publishers in the supplier content library count as subcontractors that need to be disclosed?

Answer 3

For the purposes of this tender, subcontractors should be disclosed where they provide a material component of the proposed service delivery and where Council may be exposed to operational, security, privacy, service continuity, or contractual risk through their involvement.

This would generally include cloud hosting providers and any third-party organisations responsible for supplying, maintaining, or updating content that forms part of the content library offered under the proposed solution.

4. The Tender Conditions and GCOC refer to Special Conditions of Contract (Part 5), but none were issued. Do any apply? If so, can Council provide them?

Answer 4

There are no Special Conditions of Contract for this project

5. The Response Form says tenders are irrevocable for 90 days, but Tender Conditions clause 8.7 says 120 days. Which applies?

Answer 5

90 days

6. The documents give two different extensions: mutual agreement in the Specification, Council's sole discretion in GCOC clause 3.2. Which is correct in each case?

Answer 6

Council's sole discretion to offer the extension of the contract however the tenderer can agree or disagree to accept extension.

7. The Schedule of Rates has no lines for implementation or content subscriptions. Should we price these in the Value-Add table, or add in the main table?

Answer 7

Pricing should be submitted in the Schedule of Rates where a relevant category exists.

Where implementation services, content subscriptions or other applicable costs are not specifically identified within the Schedule of Rates, tenderers should include these costs in the Value-Add table or clearly identify them as separate pricing components within their submission.

Tenderers should ensure all costs associated with the proposed solution are clearly detailed, including any implementation, subscription, licensing, content library, integration, training, support or other ongoing charges, to enable a transparent evaluation of total cost of ownership

8. Are there page limits or preferred file formats for the 3.1 A–D attachments? For the sample content catalogue in 3.1 B, is an Excel file or a link to an online catalogue acceptable?

Answer 8

Excel file would be accepted.

9. How many referees does Council require?

Answer 9

Tenderer can provide as many or as little as they wish

Requirements Clarification

1. Which HRIS and payroll system does Council use?

2. What does Council need the HRIS integration to do? For example,

Create and deactivate users, pass org structure and position data for automated assignment?

Write completions back to the HRIS?

Is there a preferred method, such as API, SFTP or middleware?

3. Apart from Entra ID SSO, which Microsoft 365 components are in scope?

4. Which BI tool does Council use? Would scheduled data exports be enough, or is a direct connector needed?

7. Please confirm count of system administrators, managers and in-house content creators will need access?

8. How will external training providers use the system? Will they manage their own sessions and record completions, or will Council staff do that?

9. For staff at remote and low-connectivity sites, would a mobile app (iOS and Android) with offline access to SCORM courses, videos and multimedia meet Council's needs?

10. Should competency tracking include externally issued licences and tickets, such as high-risk work and plant operator tickets, with evidence upload and expiry reminders?

11. Does Council need content specific to Queensland legislation, such as the WHS Act 2011 (Qld) and the Local Government Act 2009, or is national Australian content acceptable?

12. Which system holds Council's training records now, and when does that arrangement end? Roughly how many users and completion records are there, and how many years of history?

What export formats are available, and who will be responsible for cleaning the data before migration?

13. Our implementation and support team is physically based in Australia. Is a virtual implementation over Teams, with limited on-site travel, acceptable? If Council expects on-site attendance, which activities and how many visits?

14. For the shortlisted Teams demonstration, when is it likely to be held, given evaluation is set for 7–8 January? How long is the session, and will Council provide a script or scenarios?

15. Section 4.7 asks for measurable outcomes on adoption, compliance and reporting efficiency. Does Council have target KPIs or baseline measures in mind?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Which HRIS and payroll system does Council use?

IRC RESPONSE:

Technology One

2. What does Council need the HRIS integration to do? For example,

Create and deactivate users, pass org structure and position data for automated assignment?

Write completions back to the HRIS?

Is there a preferred method, such as API, SFTP or middleware?

IRC RESPONSE:

Council's preference is for an integration approach that is secure, scalable, supportable, and based on industry-standard methods. Tenderers should outline their recommended integration approach and any associated prerequisites.

For example, Council expects the integration to support:

Automated creation, update, and deactivation of user accounts based on HRIS employee records.

Synchronisation of employee and organisational data, including reporting relationships, business unit, department, location, position and employment status where available.

Automated assignment of learning, compliance training, and role-based learning pathways using HRIS data.

Regular updates to user records to maintain data accuracy and minimise manual administration.

3. Apart from Entra ID SSO, which Microsoft 365 components are in scope?

IRC RESPONSE:

Beyond Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on, Council does not mandate integration with any specific Microsoft 365 components at this stage.

4. Which BI tool does Council use? Would scheduled data exports be enough, or is a direct connector needed?

IRC RESPONSE:

Council has not mandated a specific business intelligence platform for this procurement. Where Power BI is utilised we currently run off Microsoft.

5. Are any other Council systems in scope for integration, such as contractor management, WHS/safety or rostering?

IRC RESPONSE:

Not at this stage

6. Does the 500-user figure include contractors and authorised external users? If not, roughly how many of each are there?

IRC RESPONSE:

Yes, it includes contractors and external users. We have approximately 450 direct council employees. 

7. Please confirm count of system administrators, managers and in-house content creators will need access?

IRC RESPONSE:

This is yet to be decided, current allocation will be approx. 5 administrators, 40 managers and 10 in-house creators, noting this may change

8. How will external training providers use the system? Will they manage their own sessions and record completions, or will Council staff do that?

IRC RESPONSE:

We will not have any external training providers using the system at this stage. 

9. For staff at remote and low-connectivity sites, would a mobile app (iOS and Android) with offline access to SCORM courses, videos and multimedia meet Council's needs?

IRC RESPONSE:

A mobile application supporting iOS and Android devices, with offline access to learning content and the ability to synchronise learner activity when connectivity is restored, would align with Council's operational requirements for remote and field-based employees.

10. Should competency tracking include externally issued licences and tickets, such as high-risk work and plant operator tickets, with evidence upload and expiry reminders?

IRC RESPONSE:

Not necessarily required.

11. Does Council need content specific to Queensland legislation, such as the WHS Act 2011 (Qld) and the Local Government Act 2009, or is national Australian content acceptable?

IRC RESPONSE:

Council does not mandate content aligned to specific Queensland legislation. Nationally relevant Australian content is acceptable.

However, tenderers are encouraged to identify and highlight any content that is aligned to Queensland legislative, regulatory and local government requirements, including but not limited to work health and safety, local government, governance, compliance and related topics.

Tenderers should clearly describe the scope, jurisdictional relevance and currency of any such content within their content library.

12. Which system holds Council's training records now, and when does that arrangement end? Roughly how many users and completion records are there, and how many years of history?

What export formats are available, and who will be responsible for cleaning the data before migration?

IRC RESPONSE:

Information regarding Council's current learning management system, the volume of learner records, completion records, historical data, and contract arrangements will be provided to the successful supplier during the implementation phase.

As part of their submission, tenderers may describe:

- Their approach to migrating learner, completion, competency, certification and historical training records.

- The types of source systems and data formats they can accommodate.

- Preferred and supported import/export formats (e.g. CSV, Excel, API-based transfer or other methods).

- Any assumptions regarding data quality, cleansing and validation.

- The respective responsibilities of the supplier and Council during data migration.

- Recommended approaches for verifying data integrity and migration success.

Council anticipates working collaboratively with the successful supplier to validate, cleanse and migrate relevant data as part of implementation planning.

13. Our implementation and support team is physically based in Australia. Is a virtual implementation over Teams, with limited on-site travel, acceptable? If Council expects on-site attendance, which activities and how many visits?

IRC RESPONSE:

Council is comfortable with a predominantly virtual implementation approach, including workshops, configuration, training, testing and project meetings conducted via Microsoft Teams.

14. For the shortlisted Teams demonstration, when is it likely to be held, given evaluation is set for 7–8 January? How long is the session, and will Council provide a script or scenarios?

IRC RESPONSE:

Demonstrations are anticipated to be conducted virtually via Microsoft Teams.

Council will provide any required tenderers with further details regarding:

Proposed demonstration dates and timeframes.

Session duration.

Demonstration requirements and evaluation criteria.

Any scenarios, use cases or scripted activities to be addressed.

Tenderers should ensure relevant personnel are available to participate in demonstrations during the period following the initial evaluation

15. Section 4.7 asks for measurable outcomes on adoption, compliance and reporting efficiency. Does Council have target KPIs or baseline measures in mind?

IRC RESPONSE:

Council has not established specific target KPIs or baseline measures for adoption, compliance or reporting efficiency as part of this procurement.

Tenderers should outline the measurable outcomes that their solution has achieved for comparable organisations and describe the approach they would recommend for establishing, monitoring and reporting on success measures

title: CN2027-025 – Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment
description:
The Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment Program is one of the projects being delivered through the Major Capital & Recovery Works Program of Douglas Shire Council (DSC) under contract CN2025-066. The project is supported by the Queensland Reconstruction Authority (QRA) Water Betterment funding.

Tropical Cyclone (TC) Jasper crossed the Queensland coast in the vicinity of Wujal Wujal in north Queensland on the evening of the 13th of December 2023. TC Jasper was associated with an extraordinary flooding event causing significant impacts to the region in north Queensland.

In the months following TC Jasper (16th of December 2023 to May 2025), pipeline failures increased noticeably against pre-event rates. It is considered that the cause of failure is in part, a result of the events that occurred during TC Jasper, including significant ground movement, prolonged saturation of the soil surrounding buried assets, and significant pressure fluctuation caused by repeated starting and stopping of the water supply, stressing pipe walls and joints. The traditional age-based renewal trigger previously used by DSC is likely to be inaccurate because it assumes typical operating conditions.

Therefore, the intent of the Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment Program is to undertake a complete condition assessment of DSC’s water supply and sewerage asset base so that renewal prioritisation moves from age-based triggers to measured condition, and so that post-TC Jasper renewal liability is quantified with field evidence rather than desktop estimation.

THIS TENDER REQUIRES A MANDATORY SITE VISIT.
