Section 5 of Document 03 requires professional engineering services to be provided by an appropriately registered RPEQ or under their direct supervision, where applicable.

Can Council clarify why RPEQ involvement is required for routine visual condition assessments and condition ratings across civil, electrical and mechanical assets? (while not explicitly required to be RPEQ certified as an engineer)

Would Council accept routine condition assessments undertaken by qualified and experienced water industry professionals, supported by appropriate quality assurance, without requiring RPEQ verification of every individual asset assessment?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to addendum NTT 01.

publicQuestions.question:
Q6– Switchboard inspections and access

Section 6.1.1 of the AECOM scoping document requires internal visual inspection of switchboards and electrical enclosures.

Can Council confirm whether these inspections are expected to involve opening energised electrical switchboards as this will require appropriate electrical licences to be in place?

Would Council consider an alternative approach based on external visual inspections and review of existing electrical maintenance records, inspection reports, thermography results and known defects, with internal inspections undertaken only where the available evidence is insufficient and safe access arrangements can be established?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to addendum NTT 01.

publicQuestions.question:
Q7 - Grouped Assets:

Within the asset register supplied, there are a number of aggregated assets. I.e. “Water Mag Flow Meter Works-Feb23”. Do these assets represent many assets and if so, are they considered part of the scope (classed as N/A) and how are they proposed to be assessed for condition?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to addendum NTT 01.

publicQuestions.question:
Q8 – Lighting assessment requirements

Section 6.1.4 identifies inspection of lighting assets, including consideration of lighting performance and visual discomfort.

Can Council confirm whether quantitative lighting assessments, including lux measurements, are required under the base scope?

Given the relatively low replacement value of many lighting assets, would Council consider limiting the assessment to visual condition, observable defects and existing maintenance records, with quantitative testing reserved for identified safety or compliance concerns?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.question:
Q9 – Buried transfer assets

Table 3 of the AECOM scoping document references a separate Buried Transfer Assets Condition Assessment Scoping Document.

Can Council provide this document for reference and confirm that buried water and wastewater network assets are excluded from Contract CN2027-025? Does this document identify the scope of assets to inspect to facilitate pricing?

As we understand, in the wake of TC Jasper, Detection Services did large amount of leak detection and condition assessment work for Council. Would council support use of this to determine broader network condition and performance, allowing a risk based approach to be followed?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.question:
Q10 – Limitation of liability

Item 9 of the Contract Reference Schedule (Document 02) limits Council's liability but places no limit on the contractor's liability.

Given that the project involves high-level visual condition assessments, would Council consider introducing a reasonable limit on the contractor's liability, proportionate to the contract value and nature of the services?

This would provide a more balanced allocation of risk between Council and the contractor.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.question:
Q11 – Indemnities and consequential loss

Would Council consider amending the indemnity provisions in Document 02 so that the contractor is only responsible for losses or damages to the extent caused by its own actions, omissions or breach of contract?

Would Council also consider excluding indirect or consequential losses for both parties, subject to appropriate exceptions?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.question:
Q12 – Limitations of visual condition assessments

The AECOM scoping document specifies a Tier 2 high-level visual condition assessment, which may not identify concealed defects or internal deterioration.

Can Council confirm that the contractor will only be responsible for defects that could reasonably be identified through the agreed assessment methodology, provided the assessment is undertaken with reasonable professional skill and care?

Would Council consider recognising these limitations within the contract?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.question:
Q15 – Availability and use of existing asset information

Can Council confirm what existing condition assessments, preventive maintenance records, defect registers, operational performance information, inspection reports and equipment testing records will be made available to the successful tenderer?

Would Council accept the use of this information to supplement visual condition assessments and avoid repeating inspections or tests where sufficiently recent and reliable evidence already exists?

This would support a more efficient assessment methodology while maintaining the traceability and reliability of the condition information required for renewal planning.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum NTT 001.

publicQuestions.answer:
Please find our response to the queries below:

1. SECTION B & C:

The section references on Drawing CD4 have been inadvertently interchanged.

The correct section references are as follows:

•	Section B on Drawing CD4 should correspond to Section C on Drawing CD2.

•	Section C on Drawing CD4 should correspond to Section B on Drawing CD2.

The project designers are currently amending the drawings to correct these discrepancies. The revised drawings will be issued as soon as possible.

The Contractor shall refer to the amended drawings once issued.

2. NEW ROOFLINE:

The design intent is to provide a continuous curved roof form over the proposed extension between Grids 6 and 8, generally consistent with the architectural concept.

The lower-level awning roof illustrated on Sections B and E of Drawing CD4 is not required and is to be omitted.

The space above the proposed toilet area is to be utilised for the new plantroom. The Contractor shall allow for the necessary structural provisions, access, ventilation and coordination with the mechanical and other building services.

The proposed new high-level window identified on the North Elevation is also not required.

The project designers are reviewing and amending the drawings to reflect the above requirements. Revised drawings will be issued as soon as possible.

The Contractor shall allow for the above requirements in its tender submission.

3. NEW WINDOW IN NORTH ELEV

The proposed new high-level window identified on Drawings CD1, CD3 and CD4 is not required and is to be omitted from the design.

The extension between Grids 6 and 8 shall incorporate the continuous curved roof form, with the space above the proposed toilet area utilised for the new plantroom, as outlined in the response to Clarification Item 2.

The project designers are currently amending the drawings to reflect these requirements. Revised drawings will be issued as soon as possible.

The Contractor shall exclude the proposed new high-level window from its tender allowance.

4. NEW PLANTROOM

A new plantroom is proposed within the roof space of the terminal extension, utilising the space above the proposed toilet area.

The extension between Grids 6 and 8 shall incorporate a continuous curved roof form. The lower-level awning roof illustrated on Drawing CD4 is not required and is to be omitted.

The Contractor shall allow for the design and construction of the plantroom, including:

•	Structural provisions to support the mechanical plant and associated equipment.

•	Suitable access for installation, inspection and ongoing maintenance.

•	Adequate ventilation and acoustic treatment.

•	Required fire separation and building services provisions.

•	Coordination with architectural, structural, mechanical and electrical services.

The proposed high-level window and lower-level awning roof are not required.

The project designers are currently amending the drawings to reflect the above requirements. Revised drawings will be issued as soon as possible.

The Contractor shall allow for the above requirements in its tender submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Please confirm if existing bathrooms are to be ‘renovated’ as annotated on drawing no. CD2

Please advise if continuation of architectural finishes such as the slat style ceiling finish to the departure’s terminal is required, or if we are to allow new throughout.

Please provide more information regarding the ‘new sky windows’ mentioned on drawing no. CD2
publicQuestions.answer:
Please find our response to the queries below:

1. Please confirm if existing bathrooms are to be ‘renovated’ as annotated on drawing no. CD2:

The existing bathroom facilities are to receive a general cosmetic refresh as part of the project. The Contractor shall allow for:

•	Repainting of existing walls and ceilings, where applicable.

•	General cleaning and tidying of existing bathroom areas.

•	Minor cosmetic touch-ups to existing finishes.

•	Making good of surfaces affected by the refurbishment works.

The existing bathroom layout, fixtures, fittings and services are generally to be retained. The scope is limited to a cosmetic refresh and does not require a complete bathroom renovation.

2. Please advise if continuation of architectural finishes such as the slat style ceiling finish to the departure’s terminal is required, or if we are to allow new throughout:

The existing slat-style ceiling finish within the departure terminal is not required to be continued throughout the upgraded terminal.

The design intent is to achieve a clean, simple and modern appearance without requiring a new ceiling finish throughout the proposed extension and refurbishment areas.

However, the Contractor shall include a provisional sum for the supply and installation of a slat-style ceiling finish throughout the proposed areas as an alternative for Council's consideration.

The Contractor shall provide details of the proposed slat-style ceiling finish, including materials, profiles and colours, for Council's review and approval during the design development stage.

3. Please provide more information regarding the ‘new sky windows’ mentioned on drawing no. CD2:

The proposed new skylights identified on Drawing CD2 are not required.

The Contractor shall exclude the provision of new skylights from the proposed works and allow for the continuous roof construction in accordance with the revised architectural design requirements.

The project designers are reviewing and amending the drawings to reflect the revised design intent. Updated drawings will be issued as soon as possible.

publicQuestions.question:
Airport terminal tender RFI questions

Wagga Wagga Airport Terminal Upgrade

Contract CT2027017 30 October 2026

Please clarify the following items so tenderers can establish consistent allowances for scope, design and operational requirements.

References below use the issued PPR, Design Requirements, concept drawings and furniture schedule. NCC clause references are to NCC 2022 Volume One, subject to confirmation under RFI 001.

RFI 001 Applicable NCC edition and certification pathway

The PPR refers to the NCC latest edition. Please confirm the NCC edition and referenced standards tenderers are to adopt, including whether Council requires NCC 2025 before its statutory adoption in NSW. Please confirm the building certification pathway under the proposed Part 5 approval process and how the applicable edition will be fixed for the project.

Reference: PPR Standards and Quality, page 10, and Certification, page 24.

RFI 002 Existing building compliance and fire safety records

Please provide available BCA assessments, approved building classifications, fire engineering reports, fire safety schedules and existing evacuation plans. Please identify known deficiencies and clarify the intended extent of upgrades to retained areas outside the alterations shown on the concept drawings.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 12, page 17. PPR Fire Services, page 26. NCC Sections C, D and E.

RFI 003 Passenger numbers and operational design criteria

Please provide the required peak simultaneous arriving and departing passenger numbers, accompanying visitors, staff numbers and anticipated flight overlap. Please distinguish the minimum seating capacity from total design occupancy and identify any future passenger growth allowance required for terminal planning and building services.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10, 13 and 18. NCC D2D18 and Part F4.

RFI 004 Existing amenities refurbishment and layout changes

CD2 identifies refurbishment of the existing amenities. Please confirm the extent of replacement of finishes, partitions, fixtures and services. Where compliant access or cubicle clearances require changes to the footprint or adjoining spaces, will Council accept those changes, subject to structural assessment of walls supporting the existing plant slab?

Reference: CD2. Design Requirements Section 22, page 34. NCC F4D5, F4D8 and Part I2.

RFI 005 Accessible adult change facility

Please identify any existing accessible adult change facility available to serve the terminal and confirm the preferred location for a new facility where required, including acceptance of associated layout changes. The supplied concept and furniture schedule identify a parents room and baby change station but do not identify an adult change facility.

Reference: CD2. Furniture Schedule FIX-05. NCC F4D12(1)(e) and Specification 27.

 RFI 006 Airside emergency egress

Please provide the existing approved airside evacuation arrangements and identify the routes, perimeter gates and assembly areas available to serve the upgraded terminal. Please confirm airport security restrictions affecting emergency gate operation, including any required fire alarm or access control interfaces.

Reference: PPR Emergency and Evacuation Plan, page 22. NCC D2D15 and D3D26.

RFI 007 Water supply pressure and flow testing

Please provide a current water authority statement of available pressure and flow, together with site pressure and flow test results representative of the proposed fire service connection. Results should identify the test location and date, static pressure, residual pressures and corresponding flow rates, and any supply limitations. If current results are unavailable, please arrange testing before tender close. We have experienced low water pressure on other works in the area and need this information to assess potential fire water storage, pumps or supply upgrades. Please also provide records of existing fire water infrastructure available to serve the terminal.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 9 and 12. NCC E1D2 and AS 2419.1. FRNSW Hydraulic fire safety system design position statement.

RFI 008 Retained glazing and Section J upgrade scope

Please provide any existing energy assessment and clarify the required treatment of retained glazing and building fabric where existing and new spaces are combined. Please confirm the scope boundary for upgrades identified by the contractor's Section J assessment, including retained departure lounge glazing and areas outside the highlighted refurbishment footprint.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10 and 23. PPR Sustainability, page 29. NCC Section J.

RFI 009 Mechanical coverage and performance requirements

Section 10 requires new reverse cycle heating and cooling throughout the entire terminal. Please provide Council's required indoor design conditions, operating hours and zoning criteria, including the front waiting area, cafe, baggage collection and exit areas. Please identify any spaces intended to remain unconditioned and requirements associated with frequently opening external doors.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10, pages 13 and 14. PPR Mechanical, pages 26 and 27.

RFI 010 Alternative heating solutions

Would Council consider hydronic or radiant heating as a supplement to, or a separately priced alternative to, the specified reverse cycle arrangement? Please confirm the acceptance criteria and tender presentation requirements for any alternative proposed to address the high internal spaces and intermittent terminal occupancy.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10. PPR Value for Money, page 20.

 RFI 011 Plant room location discrepancy

Please reconcile the plant room shown on CD2 and the north elevation on CD3 around grids 6 and 7 with Section EE on CD4, which shows plant above the parents room and cafeteria around grids 5 and 6. Please confirm any mandatory location or slab requirement and whether alternative engineered support arrangements may be proposed.

Reference: CD2, CD3 and CD4 Section EE. Design Requirements Section 22, page 34.

RFI 012 Plant access and external openings

Please arrange tender inspection access to the plant rooms and equipment that could not be accessed during the site visit. Please identify restrictions on introducing external louvres, maintenance openings or temporary openings for plant removal and replacement, and any plant access routes that must remain available throughout construction.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10, 22 and 24. PPR Roof and Other High Level Access, page 21.

RFI 013 Existing structural drawings and investigation records

Please provide the 1984 and 2007 existing airport drawings referenced in the PPR attachments, together with any available original structural calculations and historical geotechnical records, including records held by the original structural engineer. We note that no geotechnical report has been issued and that existing information requires verification by the contractor.

Reference: PPR Site Information, pages 13 and 14, and Section 7 Attachments. Design Requirements Sections 2, 3 and 7.

RFI 014 Electrical supply capacity and upgrade boundaries

Please provide available electrical single line diagrams, switchboard schedules, supply capacity information and relevant authority correspondence. Please confirm the geographical extent of incoming supply upgrades to be included, including any upstream network works, and identify known supply authority restrictions or required upgrades relevant to the proposed terminal loads.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 11, page 15. PPR Electrical, page 25.

RFI 015 Stormwater infrastructure and drainage constraints

Please provide existing drainage surveys and records showing pipe sizes, levels, pits and outfalls around the road and proposed extension. Please identify infrastructure that must remain in position, approved discharge points, and restrictions on diversions or road excavation. Please confirm any mandatory constraints affecting roof drainage connections and overflow discharge locations.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 8, page 11. PPR Civil and Roof Drainage, pages 24 and 25.

 RFI 016 Cafe scope and retained fitout

Section 19 states that the cafe is to remain generally unchanged. Please confirm whether Council requires any cafe fitout or equipment work beyond the specified replacement furniture, protection and necessary service interfaces. Please identify additional requirements arising from the existing lease or cafe operator, including any nominated future tenancy works.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 19 and 20. Furniture Schedule DEP-04.

RFI 017 Furniture quantities and charging positions

Please confirm whether the minimum 160 departure seats, 20 table or stool or chair positions, 20 working bench positions, four modular or booth sets and four cafe sets are separate cumulative requirements. Please nominate seats per booth set and chairs per cafe set, and confirm the required overall seating capacity. Please confirm the charging requirements for each relevant furniture group.

Reference: Furniture Schedule DEP-02 to DEP-06. Design Requirements Sections 20.2, 20.3 and 20.5.

RFI 018 Screening equipment and passenger recomposure facilities

Please provide the Council supplied screening equipment schedule, layouts, service requirements, installation clearances and delivery dates. Please confirm responsibility for equipment installation and commissioning. Please also confirm the required quantity and arrangement of seating and benches immediately after screening for passengers to replace footwear and repack belongings.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 14, pages 20 and 21, and Section 18, page 26.

RFI 019 Aboriginal artwork and relocation requirements

Section 20.4 requires retention or relocation of existing artwork glazing, while CD2 identifies cladding with Indigenous artwork. Please confirm whether the cladding incorporates relocated artwork, reproduction of existing images or newly commissioned artwork. Please provide the required extent, relocation destination and approval arrangements, including any restrictions on removal or temporary storage.

Reference: CD2. Design Requirements Section 20.4, page 29.

RFI 020 Curved roof barge and external door requirements

Please confirm any mandatory architectural requirements for the curved roof barge, including whether a continuous rolled finish is required or segmented construction is acceptable. Please also identify any nominated external door construction, or confirm that durable metal faced or metal clad doors may be proposed through design development.

Reference: CD3 and CD4. Design Requirements Sections 5, 20 and 23.

RFI 021 Operational staging and service changeovers

Please provide operational restrictions relevant to staging, including minimum passenger facilities, permitted service shutdown windows, cafe continuity requirements and notice periods. Please identify constraints affecting mechanical plant removal, temporary heating and cooling, and retention of existing walls until later construction stages. Please confirm the process and review periods for approving these arrangements.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 6, 24 and 25. PPR Contractor's Program and Emergency and Evacuation Plan.

publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Required Timeframe for Completion

Council has not specified a separate timeframe for completion. The Contractor shall develop and submit a detailed program identifying the proposed design, approvals, construction, testing, commissioning and handover activities, with completion in accordance with the submitted and approved program and the Contract requirements.

2.	Physical Security Requirements

The Contractor shall provide physical security measures appropriate for the Airport Terminal, in accordance with the RFT requirements, applicable aviation security legislation, the Airport Operator's security requirements and the National Construction Code (NCC).

The RFT does not prescribe specific wall construction specifications, minimum wall heights or security glazing specifications. These shall be determined by the Contractor as part of the detailed design, taking into consideration the security requirements of the building and the separation between public, staff and security-controlled areas.

Glazing shall comply with the applicable NCC requirements and relevant Australian Standards, including AS 1288 (Glass in buildings – Selection and installation) and AS 2047 (Windows and external glazed doors in buildings), as applicable.

The Contractor shall submit the proposed wall, door and glazing specifications and associated security arrangements to Council and the Airport Operator for review and approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Please see below RFIs:

Can you please confirm the scope of works to occur within the 'Cafe/Caffeteria' space?

Are there any height restrictions/requirements for crane operations during construction?

Can you please confirm the number of seats that need to be supplied for the 'Departure Lounges'. There is a quantity of 378 shown in the concept drawings which conflicts with the 160 listed on the Furniture & Finishes Schedule.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The existing café area within the Airport Terminal is to remain generally unchanged as part of the project.

The Contractor shall allow for protection of the existing cafe fitout and equipment, together with coordination of any necessary building services interfaces associated with the Works.

No additional cafe fitout or equipment replacement is required beyond the documented scope. Any works arising from the existing cafe lease or operator requirements that are not identified in the RFT documentation shall be referred to Council for direction.

2. No specific maximum crane height.

The Contractor shall coordinate all crane and lifting operations with Council and the Airport Operator before commencement. The Contractor shall submit a crane and lifting plan identifying the proposed crane location and configuration, date and duration, maximum crane height, operating radius and potential impacts on aircraft operations, passenger movements, airport access, security and emergency access.

All required approvals must be obtained before crane operations commence. Operations shall only occur during approved hours. Any operation outside approved hours requires prior approval from Council and the Airport Operator.

3. The concept drawings are provided for reference purposes only. The Contractor shall allow for the supply and installation of all seating and furniture in accordance with the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

The quantities identified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule are separate requirements and shall be allowed for cumulatively, as follows:

DEP-02: 160 individual Departure Lounge seats.

DEP-03: 20 table/stool/chair positions.

DEP-04: Four café furniture sets.

DEP-05: 20 working bench positions.

DEP-06: Four modular/booth seating sets.

The quantity of 378 seats shown on the concept drawings is indicative only and does not override the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

The Contractor shall develop the final furniture layout and propose the number of seats within each booth and cafe furniture set, ensuring adequate passenger circulation and accessible paths of travel, for Council's review and approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Can you please review and respond to below:

Pricing and contract

1.	Where provisional sums and alternatives go. “The pricing schedule (Part B2) has no line items for the provisional sums and separately priced alternatives Council has asked for. These are the slat ceiling, bathroom compliance changes, and the hydronic/radiant heating alternative. Please confirm how and where these are to be shown.”

2.	Unknown risks. “Will Council accept provisional sums for items that can’t be quantified before tender? These are asbestos or hazardous materials outside the 2015 register, a substation or supply authority upgrade, and fire water storage or pumps. PPR 6.8.5 refers to areas ‘the Principal will remedy separately’. Please confirm whether hazardous materials not identified in the register will be treated as a variation.”

3.	Completion date and novation. “The Date for Practical Completion is ‘TBC’ (Annexure Item 9) and liquidated damages are $2,000 per day. Please confirm the date will be set from the tendered program, and whether any separable portions apply. Please also clarify what Council expects tenderers to nominate under Item 24 (subcontractors that may be novated).”

Services

4.	Substation upgrade. “If maximum demand exceeds the existing 300 kVA substation, are the substation and upstream network works in the Contractor’s scope? Has Council had any correspondence with the network operator?”

5.	Fire detection. “The Fire Safety Schedule (7 Jul 2025) lists no fire detection or alarm system. Please confirm whether the terminal has any detection or occupant warning system. If the Works trigger one, is it required for the whole terminal or only for new and altered areas? Please also provide the fire safety certification mentioned in RFI 002 once it is issued.”

Airport security and operations

6.	Security approvals. “Will the upgrade need a change to the airport’s Transport Security Program or approvals. If so, who prepares and lodges it, and how long should the program allow?”

7.	Screening during construction. “Will the existing screening equipment stay in use until the ProVision 2 is commissioned? Is removing the existing equipment in the Contractor’s scope? When will Council deliver the ProVision 2, and who receives and stores it?”

8.	Working hours. “The PPR allows work from 7 am to 5 pm on weekdays. Will Council permit night or weekend work for shutdowns, noisy work, and work in passenger areas outside flight times?”

Scope gaps

10.	Passenger information. “What does pricing item E3 (passenger information systems) require? Please give the number and locations of flight information screens, the existing system or data feed, and who supplies the software and licences.”

11.	Hire car desk and pay station. “Who supplies the car park pay station machine, and what parking management system and supplier must it connect to? Is the hire car desk one shared counter or one per operator?”

12.	Public Wi-Fi. “Is public passenger Wi-Fi required, and does Council have an existing provider?”

Approvals and design

14.	REF timing. “What timeframe should tenderers allow for Council’s REF determination? Can investigations or enabling works proceed before determination?”

15.	Artwork. “For the Indigenous artwork cladding, is there a budget or provisional sum? Who is responsible for engaging an artist and for Aboriginal community consultation?”
publicQuestions.answer:
Pricing and contract

1. Where Part B2 does not provide specific line items, Tenderers may provide the relevant provisional sums and separately priced alternatives on a separate sheet within the Returnable Schedules, clearly identifying and cross-referencing each item.

The base tender price shall remain clearly identifiable. Separately priced alternatives shall not be included in the base tender sum unless expressly stated.

2. The Contractor shall undertake site investigations and verify existing conditions. The 2015 Asbestos Register and Management Plan has been provided as available site information.

Under PPR Section 6.8.5, the Contractor must immediately notify the Superintendent if asbestos or other contamination is discovered. The affected material must not be disturbed. The discovery of hazardous materials outside the areas identified in the 2015 register will be assessed in accordance with the Contract and will not automatically constitute a variation.

Council accepts substation or upstream network upgrades, and additional fire water storage or pumping infrastructure, as provisional items.

Tenderers shall separately identify and price these items as provisional sums in the Returnable Schedules. The final scope will be confirmed following the Contractor's investigations and consultation with the relevant service authorities. Any expenditure will be subject to Council's direction and acceptance in accordance with the Contract.

3. Tenderers shall provide a detailed construction program identifying the proposed duration, key milestones, critical path, design and approval periods, construction stages, testing, commissioning and handover.

The Date for Practical Completion will be established in accordance with the agreed Contract Period and the executed Contract. The applicable liquidated damages remain as stated in the Contract Annexure.

No separate separable portions have been identified in the RFT documentation. Any proposed separable portions shall be clearly identified by Tenderers, including their proposed scope and completion milestones, for Council's consideration.

Under Item 24, Tenderers shall identify any proposed subcontractors or specialist suppliers that they consider may be suitable for novation to Council or the successful Contractor, where applicable. Tenderers should provide the relevant company details, proposed scope of services and current contractual arrangements. Any novation will be subject to Council's review and agreement and the terms of the Contract.

Services

4.The Contractor shall undertake electrical investigations and maximum demand calculations to establish the capacity and suitability of the existing electrical supply for the proposed terminal upgrade. Where the existing supply or distribution infrastructure is inadequate, the Contractor shall identify the required upgrades and allow for the necessary electrical works.

The RFT does not confirm the available capacity of the existing 300 kVA substation or establish whether upstream network augmentation will be required. Tenderers shall identify this as a design and authority coordination risk and allow for investigations and consultation with the relevant electricity network operator.

Council will need to confirm whether any existing correspondence with the network operator is available for issue. The extent and responsibility for any upstream network augmentation will be clarified following confirmation of the maximum demand assessment and network operator requirements.

5. The Contractor shall investigate and verify the existing fire protection and life safety systems, including any existing detection and alarm arrangements, as part of the detailed design.

In accordance with Design Requirements Section 12 and the PPR Fire Services requirements, the Contractor shall develop the fire protection and life safety design for the completed terminal. This shall include fire detection, alarm and emergency warning systems as required by the applicable NCC, Australian Standards and approved design.

The extent of any new or modified system, including whether additional coverage is required in retained areas, shall be determined through the Contractor's fire engineering and compliance assessment and submitted to Council for review.

Council will provide the available fire safety certification documentation once it has been finalised and is available for issue.

Airport security and operations

6.The Airport's Transport Security Program (TSP) will require amendment to accommodate the proposed upgrade. The amendment will be prepared and lodged by Airport Management.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Airport Management and allow for the required consultation and approval process within the construction program.

7.The existing screening equipment will remain operational throughout the works.

Council will receive and store the ProVision 2 equipment and arrange delivery to site when required. The existing screening equipment provider will be responsible for relocating and removing the existing equipment as required.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Council, Airport Management and the equipment providers to facilitate the installation and integration of the ProVision 2 into the terminal.

8. The permitted working hours are 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday. Saturday works require prior approval from the Superintendent. Work on Sundays and public holidays is not permitted without prior written approval.

Any proposed night works, weekend works, noisy activities or works requiring service shutdowns or access to passenger areas outside the permitted hours must be submitted to the Superintendent for approval. Tenderers shall identify these activities in their construction methodology and program. All works must be coordinated with Airport Management to minimise disruption to airport operations.

Approval for works outside the permitted hours will be subject to Council's consideration and is not guaranteed.

Scope gaps

10. Council confirms that the existing Flight Information Display System (FIDS) is a standalone system operated by the airport check-in staff.

The existing arrangement includes two display screens at the check-in area, with a small cabinet housing the computer.

Two additional display screens will be provided in the passenger seating area.

The Contractor shall allow for the installation of the additional screens, including the required power and communications connections, and coordinate with Council regarding integration with the existing FIDS.

11.

Car Park Pay Station

APS is the existing car park service provider. Council will arrange with APS to relocate the existing pay station to the new location.

The Contractor shall provide the required power point at the new location. Council will arrange for the relocation of the existing communications cabling.

Hire Car Desk

The hire car desk shall comprise one continuous bench counter with six (6) individual workstations, one for each hire car operator.

The Contractor shall allow for the supply and installation of the counter, including the required power points and relocation of existing communications connections to the new location.

12. The public passenger Wi-Fi service is owned and operated by Council.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Council's IT team to confirm the required network connections, data cabling, equipment locations, power supply, network access and integration with the existing Council network. The Contractor shall submit the proposed arrangements to Council's IT team for review and approval prior to installation.

The Contractor shall also coordinate testing and commissioning with Council's IT team to ensure the Wi-Fi service is operational before handover.

Approvals and design

14. A period of two (2) weeks for review and determination of the REF following submission of the complete REF and supporting documentation.

The Contractor shall prepare and submit the REF and supporting documentation to Council and allow for the two-week review period in the construction program.

Site investigations may proceed before REF determination, provided they are legally permissible and all necessary approvals are obtained. Construction or enabling works requiring REF determination or other statutory approvals shall not commence until the relevant approvals are in place.

15. Council will be responsible for engaging the artist and undertaking the Aboriginal community consultation.

The Contractor shall allow for the design and detailing required to carefully remove and relocate the existing Indigenous artwork cladding to an alternative location within the Airport, as agreed with Council.

The Contractor shall also allow for the careful removal, protection, relocation and reinstallation of the existing artwork, including all associated installation works.

Please confirm whether check-in bag drop belts, outbound conveyors or changes to the baggage make-up area are in scope, or only the arrivals claim carousel.
publicQuestions.answer:
The scope includes the provision of one new arrivals baggage claim carousel, together with all associated equipment, supports, guarding, controls, power, communications and other components required for a complete and operational system.

The existing check-in baggage drop-off area is already available and does not require any additional works or upgrades with the exception of carpet replacement. No check-in bag drop belts, outbound baggage conveyors or modifications to the existing baggage drop-off area are required.

ProVision 2 screening equipment will be supplied by Council.

The Principal’s Project Requirements (pp. 9 and 14) require the Contractor to prepare the Review of Environmental Factors (REF) and supporting assessments for Council’s Part 5 determination. publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

Please clarify the following for RFT CT2027017 Wagga Wagga Airport Terminal Upgrade.

1. Second plantroom. The marked-up sections issued on 17 November (Markup 5.11.2026, Sections CC and EE) show a "Possible plant room" over Grids 5-6, above the existing parents room and cafe. The response to RFI 011 (4 November) states that the plantroom is not intended to be located above the parents room or cafe. Please confirm whether tenderers should allow for one plantroom only, over the new toilets, or also for the possible plantroom over Grids 5-6.

Please confirm whether the provisional sums (existing bathroom compliance works, substation or upstream network upgrade, and fire water storage and pumps) are to be included in the lump sum in Returnable Schedule 2, or shown only on the separate sheet and excluded from the lump sum.

4. Council sewer. Before You Dig records show a Council gravity sewer about 15-20 m west of the existing west wall, on or beside the extension footprint and the Grid 9 footings. Will Council, as sewer authority, allow building over or beside the sewer (for example on piers founded below the zone of influence), or will it require encasement or a diversion? As this cannot be verified before tender, will Council accept sewer protection or diversion, and any new stormwater outfall needed if the existing car park drainage is found unsuitable, as provisional sums in the same way as the substation and fire water items?

7. Tile mural. The external tile mural on the curved brick wall at the west end of the terminal is in the works area. Is it to be salvaged and reinstated, handed to Council, or demolished? If it is Aboriginal artwork, please confirm it is to be treated under Design Requirements Section 20.4.

publicQuestions.question:
Subject: Insurances – Professional Indemnity and Contract Works

1. Professional Indemnity

Returnable Schedule 3, Section 6 and Annexure A Items 31–34 require Professional Indemnity insurance of $5,000,000 for the Contractor and for each design consultant. Part A, Section 3(b) allows a tenderer to have the Required Insurances in place, or to be willing and able to put them in place as required by the Works Contract.

Can Council please confirm whether the following would be accepted at tender submission:

a. Contractor’s PI: a quotation or invoice from the Contractor’s insurer for a $5,000,000 Professional Indemnity policy covering the Works. The policy will be bound and the certificate of currency provided on award, before the Works start.

b. Consultants’ PI: written confirmation that all design consultants will hold $5,000,000 Professional Indemnity insurance for the periods in Annexure A Item 34. Their certificates of currency will be provided on award, before any design work starts.

If this is not acceptable, can Council please advise which certificates of currency are mandatory at submission.

2. Contract Works

Annexure A Item 28 (Alternative 2) and Returnable Schedule 3, Section 2 state that Contract Works Insurance will be obtained by the Principal. Can Council please confirm:

a. that the policy will be in the joint names of the Principal and the Contractor, and will cover the Contractor’s subcontractors and consultants;

b. the excess (deductible) under the policy, and which party is responsible for it;

c. that the Contractor is not required to take out a separate contract works policy for the Works.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Professional Indemnity

As outlined in Part A Section 3 (b) Tender must have the required insurance in place, or be willing and able to have the required in place before as requested by the Works Contract. A written confirmation will be acceptable and the certificate must be provided on award and before any work has started.

2. Contract Works

Council's project insurance is separate from the Contractor's insurance obligations. The Contractor is responsible for arranging and maintaining its own Contract Works Insurance and other required insurances in accordance with the Works Contract. Council's project insurance does not replace or remove the Contractor's insurance obligations.

• Council: Arranges its own project insurance, including Material Loss and Damage and/or Public and Products Liability, depending on the project risk assessment.

• Contractor: Must independently maintain all insurance required under the Works Contract, including Contract Works Insurance if required by the contract, Professional Indemnity and Public Liability.

1.	Carpet extent – check-in and screening areas - refer to uploaded file: Carpet area_25.11.26

Carpet tiles are required in the areas outlined in red and hatched on the attached drawing, including:

a.	Check-in area, including behind the check-in counters

b.	Security screening area and screening line-up

c.	Main entry area.

d.	Security room can either be carpet or vinyl flooring.

2. Extent of the Arrival Lounge (terrazzo)

Yes. Terrazzo flooring is required throughout the Arrival Lounge, including:

a. The entire Arrivals Baggage Collection area between Grids 7 and 8, up to the new glazed wall at Grid 7.

b. The customer side of the Hire Car Desk. (Alternative can be proposed)

c. The exit area leading to the north auto door. (Alternative can be proposed)

3. Floor finishes not nominated

For the areas where floor finishes have not been nominated in the Finishes Schedule, the Contractor shall propose suitable finishes in accordance with Section 20 of the Design Requirements and submit them to Council for review and approval.

For the external Baggage Drop Off area, the Contractor shall determine the appropriate slab and pavement design loads, including baggage tug and trolley traffic, as part of the detailed design and submit the design for Council's review.

4. Entrance matting

The Contractor shall propose suitable entrance matting at the external entry and exit doors, including the main entry, arrivals exit, airside arrivals door and departure gates. Product selection and extent shall be submitted to Council for review and approval. No specific product has been nominated by Council.

5. Fire safety certification

The existing Fire Safety Schedule dated 7 July 2025 is the latest available and shall be taken as current for tender purposes.

6. Terrazzo alternative (optional)

Yes. Council will consider a separately priced large-format porcelain tile alternative. Poured terrazzo shall remain the conforming base tender offer.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.answer:

3.	The consultant is expected manage and coordinate the delivery of this content. publicQuestions.question:
Hello.

1. Noting your request is for Marketing Consultancy (hours and delivery), has a budget been identified for this element of the project?

2. In addition has a budget been developed for the project overall including marketing, events and activations etc.

Many thanks.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	 Yes, but budgets cannot be shared during open tender processes.

publicQuestions.question:
The brief describes the role as coordination. Can you clarify whether this project covers only coordination, or also delivery of the items in Attachment A?

Specifically:

- content production (video & photo)

- collateral design and printing (trail map, signage, brochures, flyers, famil packs, posters)

- merchandise

- microsite design and build

- webcam hardware

- installation and hosting

- paid media spend
publicQuestions.answer:
The consultant is not expected to directly deliver all items listed in Attachment A. Elements such as content production (video and photography), collateral design and printing; merchandise, microsite design and build, webcam hardware, installation and hosting, and paid media placement may be delivered by specialist suppliers.

The consultant will be responsible for developing the delivery program, coordinating suppliers, managing budgets and schedules, ensuring brand consistency, and overseeing the implementation of marketing activities. Where external services are required, the consultant should identify these requirements and manage their procurement and delivery in consultation with Council.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Is the expectation that the appointed consultant will be based in the Jindabyne office throughout the three-month engagement, or would Council consider a remote-first approach with scheduled site visits and attendance at key events?

2. Is the consultant’s fee intended to cover coordination services only, with creative production, advertising and external supplier costs allocated separately?

3. Will there be opportunities for specialist creative suppliers to quote on individual components of the marketing program, such as film production, campaign creative, collateral and website design?

Thanks so much!
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The expectation is to be based in Jindabyne. Council will consider a tender submission that is as part of its evaluation process.

2. Yes. The consultant's fee is intended to cover the coordination, planning and management service.

3. No. The entire scope must be priced to be considered a complying tender.

publicQuestions.question:
The RFQ describes the engagement as the provision of marketing coordination services, including coordinating photography, videography, advertising, media and influencer engagement, promotional materials and launch activities.

Can Council please confirm that the lump-sum quotation is to cover only the nominated consultant's professional fees, travel, accommodation and other costs directly associated with providing that consultant?

Our proposed delivery model is that the consultant will coordinate the procurement and delivery of specialist marketing services, with all third-party production, advertising, printing, merchandise, influencer, event and other marketing expenditure approved, contracted and paid for directly by Council, separately from the consultant's fee.

On this basis, our quotation would exclude the costs of those third-party services and would not include estimates or allowances for them.

Please confirm whether this approach is acceptable and compliant with the RFQ pricing requirements.

If Council instead expects respondents to include third-party marketing expenditure within their lump-sum quotation, could Council please identify the required activities, quantities, budgets and specifications that must be priced?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes. The consultant's fee is intended to cover the coordination, planning and management service. Where third-party services are required, the consultant should identify these requirements and manage their procurement and delivery in consultation with Council.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello,

Could Council please clarify the following:

- Hours and location: Is the role expected to be full-time (Monday to Friday, standard business hours) for the three-month period? Does the consultant need to work from Council's Jindabyne office, or would Council accept a consultant working mainly from their own local premises, attending the office for meetings, site visits and regular in-person visits as required?

- Eligibility for related services: Would the successful respondent be eligible to quote for the third-party services Council procures to deliver the program (e.g. content production & design collateral)? Or, would they be excluded because of their coordination role?

Thanks in advance
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The expectation is to be based in Jindabyne. Council will consider a tender submission that is as part of its evaluation process.

2. They would be excluded because of their coordination role.

publicQuestions.question:
We note Council's clarification that submissions from recruitment and consultancy businesses will not be accepted.

Could Council please clarify whether such an exclusion also extends to professional services providers?

Under such a professional services model, the tenderer would provide a nominated specialist marketing consultant as key personnel and remain responsible for delivering the complete scope of services.

Council would have no employment or direct contractual relationship with the nominated consultant, and no recruitment or placement fee would apply.

The proposal would be based on a lump-sum fee, with payments linked to agreed project milestones, consistent with the RFQ requirements.

Would Council accept and evaluate a submission under this professional services delivery model?
publicQuestions.answer: The exclusion extends to the model described. A submission on that basis would not be accepted or evaluated. The exclusion is not only about recruitment or placement, it also reflects how Council requires the work to be priced. Council's requirement is a professional service fee for the consultant's advice and delivery, with production and pass on costs procured by Council directly at cost. A lump-sum fee covering the complete scope includes those costs, so a submission on that basis would not be accepted.

publicQuestions.question:
Paid media: budget and channel management

The Scope of Work lists paid channels (Meta, Instagram Reels / TikTok, Google Search and Display, Trailforks, regional press and radio, and tourism partner channels), but the RFQ doesn’t give a media budget. Your answer 3.3 says Council pays third-party suppliers directly. Could Council confirm how paid media will work:

1. Budget: Is there an approved paid media budget for the campaign? If so, could you share the amount? If not, should the consultant recommend the budget and channel split for Council to approve?

2. Running the campaigns: Will the consultant set up and manage the campaigns in Council’s own Meta and Google ad accounts, with Council paying the platforms directly? Or will Council’s team run the channels from the consultant’s plan and creative?

3. After March: Answer 8.1 says spend after the March 2027 funding deadline will be managed by Council. Should the consultant’s plan run only to March, or also cover a recommended peak-season plan for Council to continue?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Budget: Is there an approved paid media budget for the campaign? If so, could you share the amount? If not, should the consultant recommend the budget and channel split for Council to approve?

Yes, third-party costs will be paid separately. The budget will be discussed with the successful tenderer. Consultant can recommend budget and channel split for Council to approve.

2. Running the campaigns: Will the consultant set up and manage the campaigns in Council’s own Meta and Google ad accounts, with Council paying the platforms directly? Or will Council’s team run the channels from the consultant’s plan and creative?

Council’s team will run the channels from the consultant’s plan and creative.

3. After March: Answer 8.1 says spend after the March 2027 funding deadline will be managed by Council. Should the consultant’s plan run only to March, or also cover a recommended peak-season plan for Council to continue?

Yes, recommended plan for council to continue.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Commencement and timing

1.1 What is Council’s expected commencement date: late December 2026 or early January 2027? And when does Council expect to award the contract? Could Council also confirm its Christmas and New Year shutdown period, and the date from which the key Council staff involved in the project (including the project manager and anyone approving materials) will be back and available onsite?

1.2 The Scope of Work says the community open day is planned for late spring 2026. With a December or January start, has the open day been moved? If so, is there a target date or window?

1.3 Is the official opening (March 2027, subject to the Minister’s availability) within the consultant’s engagement? If the date moves past the end of the three-month contract, how would Council like that handled?

2. The consultant’s role across the marketing plan phases

2.1 The RFQ has three deliverable phases (Planning, Implementation, Finalisation) over three months. The Scope of Work has four marketing phases (Build, Launch, Peak, Continue) running into autumn 2027. Could Council confirm which marketing phases fall within this engagement? In particular, does the consultant have any responsibility for Phase 3 (Peak) and Phase 4 (Continue) after the contract ends?

2.2 Is the consultant’s role purely to coordinate the marketing plan as written? Or is Council open to recommendations that refine or add to it, presented alongside a compliant response?

3. Third-party costs and budget

3.1 Is the lump sum fee for the consultant’s professional services only? Or must it also cover third-party delivery costs? These include videography and photography, design, printing, merchandise, paid media, the microsite build, webcams, influencer fees and expenses, catering, bike demos, minibus hire and cultural service fees.

3.2 If third-party costs are paid separately, is there an indicative budget for them, either in total or by activity?

3.3 Will Council pay third-party suppliers directly, or should the consultant engage and invoice them as part of milestone billing?

4. Suppliers, procurement and existing resources

4.1 The volume of activity in this program is large and the timeframe is tight. Is the consultant allowed to engage their own specialist suppliers and subcontractors, under the consultant’s management and responsibility?

4.2 If so, do Council’s procurement policies (for example, a minimum number of quotes above set thresholds) apply to suppliers the consultant engages? If they do, what are the thresholds and quote requirements? This will significantly affect delivery timeframes and pricing.

4.3 Are there internal Council resources (for example, design, communications, web or GIS teams) or suppliers Council has already engaged that the consultant must use for any part of this program, such as PR or Graphic designers

5. Approvals and governance

5.1 Could Council describe the approval pathway for campaign materials, content and spend? This includes the review stages, who signs off (for example, the project manager, the communications team, senior management, Councillors) and expected turnaround times.

5.2 Will the Coordinator of Engagement and Corporate Projects / Senior Project Manager be the single point of contact for day-to-day decisions and approvals?

5.3 How does Council intend to brand the trail network? As we understand the trails have their own stand-alone brand and visual identity (for example, a trail name, logo and wayfinding style), or will they sit under the Council brand and visual identity?

5.4 If a stand-alone brand is intended, does it already exist, or is developing it part of this scope? Separately, are there Council brand guidelines, style requirements that all materials must follow?

6. IT environment and representation

6.1 Will the consultant be expected to work within Council’s IT environment, using a Council email address and systems? Or may the consultant use their own systems while communicating on Council’s behalf?

6.2 What will the consultant be authorised to do when representing Council with media, influencers, operators and suppliers? Will the consultant use Council branding in correspondence?

6.3 For the Finalisation Phase, what format and process does Council require for handing over records, files and images into its records management system?

7. Website and webcams

7.1 What CMS and technical environment does Council’s website use? Can it support the proposed microsite features, such as embedded live webcam streams, interactive trail maps and video?

7.2 Who will build the microsite: Council’s web team, the consultant, Who will manage it on an ongoing basis after the engagement ends?

7.3 Are the webcams within the consultant’s scope (for example, specifying the hardware, procuring it and coordinating installation)? Or will Council’s assets or IT team handle them?

8. Grant funding and acquittal

8.1 Must all program expenditure be committed or acquitted by a set date (for example, March 2027) under the NSW Government funding? If so, how should the consultant handle activity planned beyond that date, such as paid advertising sustained through the peak season?

9. Stakeholders and assets

9.1 Does Council have an existing relationship and agreed protocols with Ngarigo representatives for cultural elements of the open day and official opening? Should the consultant lead that engagement or support Council in it?

9.2 What existing assets can the consultant use? For example: reserve branding or a logo, GIS or trail data for the map, existing photography, trail counter data, and the Trailforks listing.

9.3 Who will own the intellectual property and content usage rights in material produced? Are there any Council requirements for paying influencers or for influencer contracts?
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 27/Nov/2026 11:33 AM)

1.	Commencement and timing

1.1.	What is Council’s expected commencement date: late December 2026 or early January 2027? And when does Council expect to award the contract? Could Council also confirm its Christmas and New Year shutdown period, and the date from which the key Council staff involved in the project (including the project manager and anyone approving materials) will be back and available onsite?

Council aim to award the contract on the 18/12/2026. Christmas shut down is from 24/12 to 04/01. Relevant project manager will be available any time out of the shutdown period.

1.2.	The Scope of Work says the community open day is planned for late spring 2026. With a December or January start, has the open day been moved? If so, is there a target date or window?

A date hasn’t been firmly selected. Council would like to aim for late January 2027.

1.3.	Is the official opening (March 2027, subject to the Minister’s availability) within the consultant’s engagement? If the date moves past the end of the three-month contract, how would Council like that handled?

Any changes as result to the Minister availability may be treated as a variation.

2.	The consultant’s role across the marketing plan phases

2.1.	The RFQ has three deliverable phases (Planning, Implementation, Finalisation) over three months. The Scope of Work has four marketing phases (Build, Launch, Peak, Continue) running into autumn 2027. Could Council confirm which marketing phases fall within this engagement? In particular, does the consultant have any responsibility for Phase 3 (Peak) and Phase 4 (Continue) after the contract ends?

The four marketing phases have been consolidated into the three RFQ deliverable phases. The consultant is responsible for delivering all activities required during the contract period, including transitioning campaign activity to evergreen content, measuring and reporting outcomes, capturing key learnings, planning Year 2 activities, and completing a handover to Council staff to ensure continuity after the contract ends. While Phases 3 (Peak) and 4 (Continue) extend beyond the contract period, the consultant's role is to prepare Council for these phases rather than deliver ongoing marketing activities after contract completion.

2.2.	Is the consultant’s role purely to coordinate the marketing plan as written? Or is Council open to recommendations that refine or add to it, presented alongside a compliant response?

Tenderers are encouraged to submit a compliant tender, opportunities for improvements may be submitted by the tenderer but may not impact the scoring of any compliant submission.

3.	Third-party costs and budget

3.1.	Is the lump sum fee for the consultant’s professional services only? Or must it also cover third-party delivery costs? These include videography and photography, design, printing, merchandise, paid media, the microsite build, webcams, influencer fees and expenses, catering, bike demos, minibus hire and cultural service fees.

The lump sum fee is for the consultant’s professional services only.

3.2.	If third-party costs are paid separately, is there an indicative budget for them, either in total or by activity?

Yes, third-party costs will be paid separately. The budget will be discussed with the successful tenderer.

3.3.	Will Council pay third-party suppliers directly, or should the consultant engage and invoice them as part of milestone billing?

Council will pay third-party suppliers directly.

4.	Suppliers, procurement and existing resources

4.1.	The volume of activity in this program is large and the timeframe is tight. Is the consultant allowed to engage their own specialist suppliers and subcontractors, under the consultant’s management and responsibility?

Yes, but specialist suppliers and subcontractors need to be included in the consultant’s fee.

4.2.	If so, do Council’s procurement policies (for example, a minimum number of quotes above set thresholds) apply to suppliers the consultant engages? If they do, what are the thresholds and quote requirements? This will significantly affect delivery timeframes and pricing.

If the subcontractors are included in the tenderer’s fee, it is not necessary to follow Council’s procurement policies.

4.3.	Are there internal Council resources (for example, design, communications, web or GIS teams) or suppliers Council has already engaged that the consultant must use for any part of this program, such as PR or Graphic designers.

Council have internal resources that can support GIS, website content, and some simple design work. Suppliers have not been engaged yet.

5.	Approvals and governance

5.1.	Could Council describe the approval pathway for campaign materials, content and spend? This includes the review stages, who signs off (for example, the project manager, the communications team, senior management, Councillors) and expected turnaround times.

Approval pathway with vary. The consultant will work directly with Engagement team and spend will be approved by Senior Project Manager.

5.2.	Will the Coordinator of Engagement and Corporate Projects / Senior Project Manager be the single point of contact for day-to-day decisions and approvals?

Yes.

5.3.	How does Council intend to brand the trail network? As we understand the trails have their own stand-alone brand and visual identity (for example, a trail name, logo and wayfinding style), or will they sit under the Council brand and visual identity?

The Trails have their own stand-alone brand and visual identity, which is influenced by Council’s brand.

5.4.	If a stand-alone brand is intended, does it already exist, or is developing it part of this scope? Separately, are there Council brand guidelines, style requirements that all materials must follow?

Yes, the trails stand-alone brand already exist. Yes, there are Council brand guidelines. Improvements or modifications to the brand may be suggested.

6.	IT environment and representation

6.1.	Will the consultant be expected to work within Council’s IT environment, using a Council email address and systems? Or may the consultant use their own systems while communicating on Council’s behalf?

The consultant will use their own systems.

6.2.	What will the consultant be authorised to do when representing Council with media, influencers, operators and suppliers? Will the consultant use Council branding in correspondence?

Yes. The consultant will use Council branding in correspondence.

6.3.	For the Finalisation Phase, what format and process does Council require for handing over records, files and images into its records management system?

Supply of images etc through a one drive link, managed as assets become available.

7.	Website and webcams

7.1.	What CMS and technical environment does Council’s website use? Can it support the proposed microsite features, such as embedded live webcam streams, interactive trail maps and video?

The name of Council's CMS is Granicus Websites & CMS OE. Yes.

7.2.	Who will build the microsite: Council’s web team, the consultant, Who will manage it on an ongoing basis after the engagement ends?

Council will build and Council will manage with supplied assets and written content from the contractor.

7.3.	Are the webcams within the consultant’s scope (for example, specifying the hardware, procuring it and coordinating installation)? Or will Council’s assets or IT team handle them?

Webcams are within the consultant’s scope.

8.	Grant funding and acquittal

8.1.	Must all program expenditure be committed or acquitted by a set date (for example, March 2027) under the NSW Government funding? If so, how should the consultant handle activity planned beyond that date, such as paid advertising sustained through the peak season?

Yes. Anything beyond the date will be managed by Council.

9.	Stakeholders and assets

9.1.	Does Council have an existing relationship and agreed protocols with Ngarigo representatives for cultural elements of the open day and official opening? Should the consultant lead that engagement or support Council in it?

Council has a well-established relationship with Ngarigo representatives. The Consultant will need to lead this.

9.2.	What existing assets can the consultant use? For example: reserve branding or a logo, GIS or trail data for the map, existing photography, trail counter data, and the Trailforks listing.

This will all be made available for the consultant to use.

9.3.	Who will own the intellectual property and content usage rights in material produced? Are there any Council requirements for paying influencers or for influencer contracts?

Council will own the intellectual property and content usage rights.

publicQuestions.question:
Could you share how QGAir has previously arranged drug and alcohol testing at Horn Island, particularly after an incident? Were testers generally flown in from Cairns or another mainland base, or did QGAir use a qualified tester on Horn Island or Thursday Island?

If figures are available, roughly how many planned visits and urgent callouts were there in the past 12 months, and how many urgent callouts occurred overnight or on weekends?

In particular, when the next scheduled flight was too late to complete breath testing within eight hours of an incident, what arrangement worked in practice? If this hasn’t occurred, what fallback would QGAir consider acceptable?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your question.

QGAir has no confirmed historical delivery arrangements or a reliable breakdown of planned visits, urgent callouts and overnight or weekend attendance at Horn Island. We cannot provide verified figures or examples of previous incident responses at this stage. This should not be interpreted as nil activity. Any further information made available will be shared with all participating suppliers through VendorPanel.

The RFP invites suppliers to propose a practical service model for Horn Island. This may involve local providers on Horn Island or Thursday Island, mainland-based personnel, or a combination of arrangements. Suppliers should distinguish existing capability from arrangements that would need to be established before commencement. QGAir is seeking timely access to testing, clear arrangements for urgent requests and reliable alternatives when travel or local services are unavailable. Proposals should explain:

-how planned and urgent testing would be delivered, including overnight and weekend coverage

-how alcohol testing within eight hours and drug testing within 32 hours of an accident or serious incident would be supported

-the proposed fallback where scheduled flights would not allow testing within those timeframes

-any limitations, dependencies, establishment costs or additional callout and travel charges.

Suppliers may propose separate arrangements for local breath testing and urine collection, provided they explain how each would meet the specified testing, competency, equipment, reporting and quality requirements. Any reliance on QGAir personnel, equipment or transport must be expressly identified and must not be assumed.

QGAir has not nominated a pre-approved fallback for circumstances where timely testing cannot be achieved. Proposed alternatives will be assessed against the RFP requirements and QGAir’s DAMP.

Suppliers must clearly identify any circumstances in which they cannot meet the required timeframes, together with their proposed escalation and response arrangements.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We would like to clarify please whether 'clinics' a mandatory requirement or simply a wording choice? Can all testing be conducted on site at QGAir locations or are there specific instances where off site testing must be conducted please?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your question.

References to clinics describe an intended service delivery option. The Supplier is not required to own or operate a clinic and may provide this capability through suitable collection centres, subcontractors, or partner providers.

QGAir requires both onsite testing and access to offsite testing. Offsite testing is specifically included for pre-employment or commencement testing, including candidates located outside QGAir’s primary locations. The indicative pricing assumptions also use clinic-based testing for Mt Isa routine testing and additional individual testing, such as missed or return-to-work tests.

Planned group testing is generally intended to occur onsite at QGAir locations. The location for other testing events will depend on the circumstances, available facilities, and the authorised testing request. Suppliers should not assume that every person requiring testing can attend a QGAir base.

Suppliers may propose an alternative delivery model, including greater use of mobile or onsite testing.

The proposal must explain how it would meet the complete requirement, including access for pre-employment candidates outside QGAir locations, individual appointments, and urgent testing. Identify any reliance on QGAir facilities or personnel, service limitations, and all associated charges.

Any alternative must be clearly identified, with departures recorded in Section 2.3. QGAir will assess the proposed arrangements against the RFP requirements, service accessibility, and value for money.

publicQuestions.question: Does QGAir expect all 40 pre-employment tests each year to take place in Mount Isa? If testing is expected elsewhere, which other towns or regions should we allow for when pricing room hire and travel?

description:
Balranald Shire Council invites quotations from suitably qualified contractors for the assessment, surface correction, resealing and remarking of the sealed runway and taxiway at Balranald Aerodrome.

The objective of this project is to improve pavement condition, rectify ride quality concerns, address localised ponding issues where practical, extend pavement life and reinstate all required aerodrome markings in accordance with applicable aviation standards. The aerodrome's runway and taxiway have undergone periodic crack sealing over recent years, and Council has identified surface irregularities, rough ride characteristics and localised water ponding requiring investigation and treatment.

All aerodrome markings shall be reinstated in accordance with the applicable requirements of Part 139 (Aerodromes) Manual of Standards 2020 and relevant guidance material issued by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA).

title: Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment
description:
The Opportunity:

Ports North is pleased to advise that Request for Proposal (RFP) Phase 1 for the Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment Opportunity has now commenced.

Ports North is proposing the development of the Cairns Marine Precinct – Common User Facility, a major maritime infrastructure project, to expand the marine vessel maintenance capability and capacity in Far North Queensland to support the continued growth of the region’s maritime industry. The proposed facility responds to increasing demand for maritime maintenance, repair, and overhaul services as global vessel fleets expand and age, alongside sustained investment in Australia’s maritime defence capability driving long-term sustainment demand.

Ports North has identified a Finance (co-funded), Design, Build, Operate and Maintain (FDBOM) commercial delivery model as the most efficient means of Project delivery to successfully facilitate achievement of the Project Objectives. As the Project will benefit from a significant contribution of funds from the Queensland and Commonwealth Governments, the physical facilities coming into existence as a result of the Project will be a common user facility available for use by the operator and customers including vessel owners and ship maintenance and repair service providers.

Ports North is seeking a private sector proponent to co-fund, develop, operate and maintain the facility under a long-term arrangement on Ports North-owned land at the Port of Cairns.

This RFP follows the successful completion of an Expression of Interest (EOI) process. Participation in the EOI process was not a prerequisite for participation in RFP Phase 1. Ports North welcomes registrations and proposals from organisations that did not participate in the EOI and may be engaging with the opportunity for the first time.

Purpose of this Request for Proposal:

The purpose of this RFP is to elicit proposals from the market that address the Project Objectives and develop the CMP-CUF, including the following:

•	the co-funding of the Project;

•	the design, construction and commissioning of the CMP-CUF; and

•	the operation and maintenance of the CMP-CUF on a common user basis.

How to Participate in RFP Phase 1:

Proposals are being accepted only via the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room. Submissions via this Queensland Procurement Solution may not be eligible.

title: Supply, Delivery and Installation of Modular One and Two Bedroom Dwellings to Northern Peninsula
description:
Northern Peninsula Area Regional Council (NPARC) is seeking tenders for the supply, road delivery and installation of modular one and two bedroom dwellings.

Goods and services required:

Design, construction and supply of factory-built modular dwellings that meet a mandatory cyclonic, tropical and remote-area performance specification.

Road delivery to the Northern Peninsula Area (NPA). Barge delivery may be offered as a separately priced alternative.

Installation on footings at residential lots, with connection and final certification completed by local contractors.

Quantities:

Separable Portion A: 4 one-bedroom dwellings with carports.

Separable Portion B (option): additional one-bedroom dwellings, up to 40 in total, priced in batches of 10.

Separable Portion C (option): two-bedroom dwellings, up to 40, priced in batches of 10.

Only Separable Portion A could lead to a firm order. Council may take up Separable Portions B and C in whole or in part, and is not committed to buying any quantity. Tenderers are encouraged to price all three portions so that Council can compare tenders.

Expected timing:

Released: 26 November 2026.

Questions close: 4:00 pm AEST, Thursday 10 December 2026.

Tender closes: 11:59 pm AEST, Wednesday 16 December 2026.

The first 4 dwellings must be installed by Monday 31 May 2027.

Location of delivery: the NPA communities of Bamaga, Seisia, New Mapoon, Umagico and Injinoo, Cape York, Queensland. The work cannot be provided remotely. The dwellings are built off site, delivered by road and installed in the NPA.
