title: Cold Chain Monitoring - Bayside
description: The procurement is for the implementation of a cloud-based cold chain monitoring system across Bayside Health Service (BHS) to monitor the temperature of medication, vaccine, and pathology storage refrigerators. The solution will replace three separate legacy monitoring systems currently in use: ACR Trendreader (AXIOM), Quirks LogTags, and BMS. The new system will provide continuous 24/7 temperature monitoring, real-time alerts, centralised data access, audit trails, reporting, and regulatory compliance capabilities. The need arises from ageing and unsupported infrastructure, fragmented monitoring processes, incompatibility with newer refrigeration equipment, and increasing clinical and operational risks associated with temperature-sensitive products.
buyer: Metro South Hospital and Health Service

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The procurement requires:

•	A cloud-based cold chain monitoring platform.

•	Temperature monitoring hardware and sensors capable of monitoring existing and new refrigerators.

•	Real-time SMS and email alerting functionality with escalation workflows.

•	Data storage and reporting capability with retention of historical data for at least two years.

•	Integration with existing Metro South Health infrastructure, including BMS and alert escalation pathways.

•	Remote monitoring capability through QH-certified devices and VPN access.

•	Installation, calibration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and ongoing support services.

•	Documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and training materials.

•	A scalable solution capable of deployment across wards, departments, and satellite services.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Compatibility and integration requirements include:

•	Retrofitting to existing refrigerators and compatibility with new refrigerator installations.

•	Connectivity via Ethernet to Queensland Health-certified infrastructure.

•	Integration with Metro South Health-hosted servers currently located at Logan and PAH.

•	Integration with existing BMS systems and alert escalation pathways.

•	Access through Queensland Health-certified devices.

•	VPN-enabled remote monitoring and administration capabilities.

publicQuestions.question:
Bar-Tech Automation — clarification questions

RFQ: Cold Chain Monitoring – Bayside (VendorPanel VP534385, MSH ref SP25-474)

Rev A — 25/11/2026 (Brisbane)

We understand the works are mainly a retrofit of temperature monitoring to MSH's existing fridges, freezers and cool rooms across the Bayside sites, and must also suit new appliances (BR-18). The RFQ does not state how many appliances or touch screens are to be monitored, or where. So that we can price accurately, please provide the following:

QUANTITIES AND LOCATIONS

1. Please provide the FF&E schedule / register (dRofus extract or room data sheets) for each Bayside site in scope, listing every fridge, freezer and cool room to be monitored with its room number and name. If it uses Queensland Health FF&E codes, the rows we need are MMGE-968 (device: fridge monitoring), ITNE-918 (display screen: fridge monitoring), MMGE-034 / MMGE-036 (drug fridges) and any freezers, blood fridges and cool rooms.

2. Please provide floor plans or FF&E layouts marked up with the location of each monitored appliance and each touch screen (or the rooms where they are wanted).

3. Which sites and departments are in scope (Redland Hospital, Redland Residential Care, Redlands Satellite Hospital, Wynnum-Manly CHC, Marie Rose Centre Dunwich, Bayside Addiction & MH Centre, others), with street addresses? Any to be staged or excluded?

4. How many appliances of each type at each site: medication / vaccine fridges, blood fridges, freezers (about -20 °C), ultra-low freezers (below -30 °C, e.g. -80 °C), combined fridge/freezers and cool rooms — and which are existing and which are new (or on order)?

5. How many touch screens, and where? Touch screens are typically located in the Staff Stations and Medication Rooms. Please confirm per area: a dedicated 4" screen per fridge, a group screen (10" up to 8 appliances, 14" up to 12, 22" up to 24), or no local screen (web dashboard and alerts only).

6. How many AXIOM / LogTag loggers are in use at Bayside today, and in which rooms?

RETROFIT — EXISTING APPLIANCES AND COOL ROOMS

7. (a) For the existing fridges, freezers and cool rooms: make, model and age; do they have door-status and fault volt-free contacts on an external terminal strip, and a probe entry for the temperature sensor? Bar-Tech supplies the temperature sensors (one per DGM): will MSH / BEMS fit them, and any door / fault contacts needed, to the existing appliances? Are the existing AXIOM / LogTag / BMS probes and loggers to be removed, and by whom?

 (b) New appliances (now or future purchases): will new appliances be ordered with the sensor, door and fault contacts factory-fitted? Bar-Tech free-issues the sensor to the appliance manufacturer with its Appliance Supplier Information Sheet.

8. For each cool room: number of entry doors, and is a common-fault volt-free contact available from the master refrigeration controller?

SOFTWARE, INTEGRATION AND DATA

9. Alarm messaging and phone-call escalation will use Bar-Tech's existing Mobicall integration. Please confirm the escalation tiers required, and how many staff users and alarm recipients (users log in through Active Directory).

10. AXIOM, LogTags and the BMS all allow a CSV export, and Bar-Tech will import that data into openCCMS with its CSV importer. How much history should be imported (period and approximate volume per system), and who at MSH will run the exports?

11. Which BMS systems at Bayside should alarms integrate with?

SERVICE, COMMERCIAL AND PROGRAMME

12. Required service levels (support hours, response times, availability) and support term in years for the whole-of-life comparison?

13. Calibration standard and frequency required (e.g. NATA-traceable, annual)?

14. Price format: will a schedule of rates plus an indicative total on stated quantities be accepted, if quantities cannot be confirmed before close? Staged rollout by site?

15. Which conditions apply — Basic or General Conditions of Contract — and which insurances (medical indemnity, cyber)?

16. Target implementation dates, working hours (after-hours or weekend access in clinical areas), site induction requirements, and can a site walk-through be arranged before close?

If quantities cannot be confirmed before close, we will price a schedule of rates plus an indicative total on stated assumed quantities.

Regards,

Jamie van Aalst

Estimator — Bar-Tech Automation

title: Supply & Install - New HVAC Heating - Springwood Aquatic Centre
description:
Council, through this Request for Tender (RFT) No 2026/27-504006A is seeking the services of a suitable qualified Contractor to undertake the removal and disposal of the relevant existing HVAC heating system at Springwood Aquatic and Fitness Centre and the Supply and installation of new HVAC Heating system at Springwood Aquatic and Fitness Centre.

Council will conduct a compulsory site inspection for tenderers to be held 10am on 19 November 2026 at Springwood Aquatic Centre.

Council will not consider a Tender submission lodged by a Tenderer who fails to attend this briefing or fails to ensure that a representative attends on its behalf.

Please confirm with the nominated contact your attendance at this meeting no later than 12pm on 16 November 2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please confirm the following commercial provisions for the Springwood HVAC tender? We seek clarification so all tenderers can price these obligations on a consistent basis.

1. Liquidated damages

Annexure Part A, Item 27 lists $4,000 per day for delivery and $4,000 per day for practical completion. These rates appear substantial for works of this nature.

Please confirm:

a) Whether both $4,000 daily rates are intentional?

b) Whether the rates can apply concurrently, resulting in $8,000 per day during an overlapping delay?

c) The delivery milestone/date that would trigger delivery damages?

d) Whether an aggregate cap applies and, if so, its amount or percentage?

If these entries do not reflect Council’s intended application, could Council please issue revised provisions?

2. Defects liability and maintenance

Item 30 specifies a 24-month defects liability period, with the specifications also requiring maintenance and breakdown attendance during that period. This extended period materially affects maintenance, warranty and security costs.

Please confirm whether the full 24-month period is intentional, or whether Council would consider a revised 12-months DLP for this project?

3. Bank guarantee release

Item 14 requires two bank guarantees, each equivalent to 2.5% of the contract sum.

Will Council please confirm when each guarantee will be released, including whether one is released at practical completion and the other following the defects liability period?

4. Equipment payments

Item 32 does not identify if equipment purchased for this tender is eligible for payment before installation.

Will Council please confirm whether Council offers progress payments that can cover manufacturer deposits, manufacturing milestones or completed equipment held off site, and any associated security or documentation requirements?

We would appreciate Council’s confirmation or any revised provisions asap.

Thank You
publicQuestions.answer:
Q. Liquidated damages: Annexure Part A, Item 27 lists $4,000 per day for delivery and $4,000 per day for practical completion. These rates appear substantial for works of this nature.

a) Whether both $4,000 daily rates are intentional?

Answer - No - Delivery only applies with this linked only to a delay that forces the site to be closed to the public longer than tendered.

b) Whether the rates can apply concurrently, resulting in $8,000 per day during an overlapping delay?

 Awnser - No they would not be concurrently applied.

Delivery only with this linked only to a delay that forces the site to be closed to the public longer than tendered.

c) The delivery milestone/date that would trigger delivery damages?

Answer: Council would only apply Liquidated damages if the site remained closed to the public beyond the nominated closure dates. We will update the annexure accordingly.

d) If these entries do not reflect Council’s intended application, could Council please issue revised provisions?

Answer: Tenders may also propose departures to the contract. If you are doing this please include to price for meeting the current contract conditions.

2. Defects liability and maintenance

Item 30 specifies a 24-month defects liability period, with the specifications also requiring maintenance and breakdown attendance during that period. This extended period materially affects maintenance, warranty and security costs.

Answer: Council will accept a 12 month DLP. If you choose this please list this clearly as a contract departure in your response.

title: Request for Information - HSE Assurance Technology
description:
Energy Queensland (EQL) is seeking information from the market about software and services for HSE assurance and contractor assurance. EQL wants to replace several separate assurance systems with a single, shared Software as a Service platform covering forms and content governance, assurance planning, mobile field completion (including with no network coverage), findings and actions, contractor participation, workflow and reporting.

This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. It is market research to help EQL refine its requirements, budget, timeframe and sourcing approach. Responses will not be evaluated, no shortlist will be made and no contract will be awarded from this RFI. Partial responses are welcome.

Timing: RFI issued Friday 20 November 2026. Questions close 12.00pm (Queensland time) Friday 4 December 2026. Responses close 2.30pm (Queensland time) Monday 14 December 2026.

Location: the solution is to be delivered as Software as a Service, with all EQL data, including backups, held in Australia. Users are across Queensland, including field staff and contractors in areas with poor or no mobile coverage. Implementation services may be delivered remotely or in Brisbane.

Respond using the Response Schedule (Attachment 1), lodged in PDF format through VendorPanel. The Contact Officer is Phillip O'Brien, Phillip.OBrien@energyq.com.au.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
EQL is a Queensland Government Owned Corporation that includes Energex, Ergon Energy Network, Ergon Energy Retail and Yurika. Its distribution businesses cover the whole of Queensland, with a large, dispersed field workforce and a significant contractor workforce.

EQL's HSE assurance capability currently sits across several separate systems, including a mobile audit platform, a field forms platform and an HSE management system, each with its own data structure. This limits whole-of-business reporting, form governance, action tracking and contractor participation.

A new solution needs to integrate with EQL's existing systems:

- SAP S/4HANA (ERP, HR and organisational data, HSE incident management and HSE operational risks)

- SAP Ariba (supplier management)

- an enterprise identity provider (single sign-on and user provisioning)

- Microsoft Power BI (reporting)

- EQL learning management systems (SAP SuccessFactors and aXcelerate)

- a Databricks-based enterprise data and analytics platform.

SAP S/4HANA remains the system of record for incidents, and the learning management systems are not being replaced.

Indicative users: about 10,000 EQL staff, 500 contractor companies and 2,000 contractor workers.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
EQL is looking for offerings that:

- replace the current HSE assurance systems as soon as possible, at a minimum for the capabilities they provide today, with a single shared platform for HSE assurance and contractor assurance

- bring contractors into the assurance process, with access limited to their own information

- provide end-to-end traceability and reliable reporting, from risk and control through to verified action closure

- can be extended to other HSE, quality, risk and compliance processes through configuration rather than re-platforming

- let business users configure forms, workflows and reports without code.

Of interest but not core: contractor management and performance rating; risk and control management; incident and hazard management; competency, licence and training management; permit to work; plant and equipment management; site access and sign-in.

Indicative service targets: 99.5% availability, Recovery Time Objective of 4 hours and Recovery Point Objective of 24 hours. EQL owns its data. EQL data must not be used to train AI models without EQL's written consent.

The RFI asks for an indicative, non-binding cost range in Australian dollars, exclusive of GST, and for market feedback on how EQL should approach any future procurement.

title: Gold Standard Early Intervention – Proven Initiatives Round 3
description:
The Department of Youth Justice and Victim Support (the Department) is seeking proposals to deliver the Gold Standard Early Intervention – Proven Initiatives program. This program is designed to prevent and reduce youth offending and improve life outcomes for youth at-risk of offending.

The target cohort for this program is youth aged 8 to 17 years who are:

• displaying early signs of criminal and/or anti-social behaviours (e.g. drug and alcohol misuse, anger management issues); and

• disengaged from school or at high risk of exclusion; or

• at risk of coming into contact with police and/or court systems; or

• siblings of youth on youth justice orders.

This group is at risk of escalating into the statutory youth justice system without timely and effective intervention.

The program aims to:

• Provide timely and effective interventions for youth at risk of entering the statutory youth justice system.

• Strengthen family and community supports to build protective factors.

• Improve engagement with education, training, or employment.

• Enhance wellbeing and resilience.

Suppliers are expected to deliver structured, evidence-based services that align with these goals and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

publicQuestions.question:
We are preparing a submission for ITT263 – Memorialisation Products, Materials and Services, limited to Separable Portions A and D, and would appreciate clarification on the following additional matters. These questions do not repeat earlier enquiries lodged on 15 and 16 November 2026.

1. Clarification cut-off

The VendorPanel request states that the cut-off for supplier queries is Thursday, 3 December 2026 at 12:00 PM Australian Eastern Standard Time. Invitation to Tender, Schedule 1 Item 8, states that requests for clarification or further information “will not be accepted on or after the date that is 3 business days prior to the Closing Date.” Three business days prior to the Closing Date of Tuesday, 8 December 2026 is Thursday, 3 December 2026, which can be read as meaning that questions are not accepted on that date.

Could Council please confirm the last date and time at which clarification questions will be accepted?

- Document and clause: VendorPanel Request Summary, “Cut-off date for supplier queries”; Invitation to Tender, Schedule 1 Item 8 (and Process Terms cl 3.10, as cited in that Item).

- Reason: The two documents can be read as setting different last times, and the remaining questions below need a clear deadline.

2. Information session

Page 1 of the Invitation to Tender, and the VendorPanel Request Summary, state that an online Information Session will be held covering all Separable Portions. Invitation to Tender, Schedule 2, states “Not applicable” and no date or joining details are given.

Could Council please confirm whether an information session will be held and, if so, the date, time and how respondents may attend?

- Document and clause: Invitation to Tender, page 1 (Contract Overview) and Schedule 2; VendorPanel Request Summary, “What’s required.”

- Reason: The pack contradicts itself, and respondents should not miss a session if one is in fact being held.

3. Online design platform and proofing (clause 5)

Service Specification clauses 5.1 to 5.4 require the Contractor to provide methods and technologies that reduce proofing time, and a secure, user-friendly online self-service design platform that enables Council customers to design memorial plaques, review proofs and request amendments, with a version history and with Council’s final approval required before manufacture.

Could Council please confirm:

- whether clauses 5.2 to 5.4 apply to a respondent tendering only for Separable Portions A and D on a supply-only basis;

- whether a platform provided by an authorised manufacturer or wholesaler, used under the principal contractor’s contract and giving Council final approval before manufacture, would satisfy clauses 5.2 to 5.4; and

- whether a respondent supplying only laser-engraver materials under Portion D (with Council undertaking engraving in-house) is still required to provide a customer-facing plaque design platform?

- Document and clause: Service Specification (Schedule 5, Attachment 1), clauses 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 (including 5.3(a)–(d)) and 5.4, page 3 of 14; Tender Response Form, Part 3.2, value-added services and systems.

- Reason: The platform is written as mandatory for “the Contractor,” but it sits in the general specification rather than in the Portion A or D scope, and it is a substantial system obligation for a supply-only model.

4. Proof and amendment turnaround after the first proof

Clause 3.3 requires custom proofs and/or quotations within five (5) business days of a request. Clauses 5.2 and 5.3 contemplate multiple rounds of review and amendment, but no timeframe is stated for subsequent proofs after the first.

Could Council please confirm the required turnaround, in business days, for revised proofs and for responding to customer or Council amendment requests after the first proof has been issued?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.3, 5.2 and 5.3, pages 2–3 of 14.

- Reason: The first-proof time is clear; later rounds, which the platform must support, have no stated service level.

5. Samples and technical data for Portions A and D

The Service Specification requires physical colour swatches and certificates of origin at commencement for Portion B (clause 8.6), and samples and product information at commencement for Portion E (clauses 11.6 and 11.7). No equivalent sample, swatch or technical-data requirement is stated for Portions A or D, and no pre-award samples are requested in the Tender Response Form.

Could Council please confirm whether respondents for Portions A and D must provide, either with the tender or at commencement of the contract, product samples, colour swatches, coating specifications, or manufacturer’s technical data and warranty documentation and, if so, for which items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 7.3, 8.6, 10.1–10.2, 11.6–11.7; Tender Response Form, Parts 1–4 (no sample schedule).

- Reason: Sample obligations are spelled out for B and E only, leaving A and D unclear, including where an alternative coating is proposed under clause 7.3.

6. Portion D delivery location

Portion A has nominated delivery addresses for plaques and for above-ground ashes products (clauses 7.14 and 7.15). Portion D has a four-week delivery time (clause 10.3) but no portion-specific delivery address. General clauses 3.6 to 3.9 require pre-arranged delivery, possibly to alternate locations within the Sunshine Coast local government area, at the contractor’s cost.

Could Council please confirm the default delivery address, or addresses, for Portion D laser-engraver materials, and whether the addresses in clauses 7.14 and 7.15 also apply to Portion D unless otherwise directed?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.6–3.9, 7.14, 7.15 and 10.3, pages 2, 5 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-D ~ Laser Engraver Materials.”

- Reason: Freight must be included in the unit rates, but the destination for Portion D is not stated.

7. Portion D material specification (thickness, alloy, default colour, edges and fixings)

Clauses 10.1 and 10.2 require architectural-grade aluminium with an exterior-grade powder coating or an external-quality anodised finish, suitable for long-term outdoor use in South-East Queensland. The Schedule of Rates does not state sheet thickness, alloy grade or temper, edge finish, or hole size and position. Only two line items specify a colour (50 × 30 Reserve tag (red) and 50 × 30 Vacant (green)). Other sizes have no default colour. Fixings are a separately priced extra.

Could Council please specify, for each SP-D line item where it is known:

- the required or typical sheet thickness;

- the required alloy grade and temper, if any, beyond “architectural-grade aluminium”;

- the default colour and finish for items that do not have a colour in the line description;

- any required edge finish; and

- standard hole sizes, positions and clip types, where fixings are ordered?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 2.4, 10.1 and 10.2, pages 2 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-D ~ Laser Engraver Materials,” heading and rows for 380 × 280, 254 × 152, 160 × 140, 200 × 150, 15 × 50, 160 × 70, 100 × 50, 50 × 30 Reserve tag (red), 50 × 30 Vacant (green), additional cost for a non-standard colour, and additional cost for fixings.

- Reason: These physical details are needed to obtain comparable wholesale prices. This question does not ask whether red or green, or anodised or powder-coated finishes, are mandatory, which was raised on 16 November 2026.

8. Warranty period for Portion D materials

Clause 6.6 warrants all memorial products against manufacturing defects, from delivery, for 20 years for plaques, 50 years for granite memorial installations, and otherwise the manufacturer’s standard warranty but not less than twelve (12) months. Clause 10.1 refers to Portion D items as “laser-engraved aluminium plaques.”

Could Council please confirm which warranty period in clause 6.6 applies to Portion D laser-engraver materials, including blanks, tags, row markers and name markers: the 20-year plaque warranty, or the manufacturer’s standard warranty of not less than 12 months?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 6.6 and 10.1, pages 4 and 9 of 14.

- Reason: The 20-year and 12-month periods differ substantially, and clause 10.1’s use of “plaques” makes it unclear which period applies to blanks and tags.

9. Lead time for above-ground ashes interment products, and for custom-sized plaques

Clause 7.12 requires alloy plaques to be delivered within six (6) weeks of the order. Clause 3.2, which deals with inability to meet prescribed lead times, cites clauses 7.12, 8.11, 8.12 and 10.3 only. There is no stated lead time for above-ground ashes interment products (sleepers and cylinders) under clauses 7.15 and 7.16 or the corresponding Schedule of Rates items. Clause 7.6 also requires custom-sized plaques, without a separate lead time.

Could Council please confirm:

- the required delivery period for sleeper and cylinder products under Portion A; and

- whether custom-sized plaques under clause 7.6 must also be delivered within the six-week period in clause 7.12, or whether a different period applies?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.2, 7.6, 7.12, 7.15 and 7.16, pages 2, 4 and 5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” rows “Sleeper/ Cylinder (Small)” to “(XLarge).”

- Reason: Cancellation rights in clause 3.2 turn on “prescribed lead times,” but two product groups in Portion A have no clear prescribed time.

10. Sleeper and cylinder sizes

The Schedule of Rates prices sleeper/cylinder products as Small, Medium, Large and XLarge. Clause 7.16 sets material standards (durable materials, consistent cast bronze, Grade 316 marine-grade stainless steel hardware, and resistance to corrosion and galvanic reaction) but does not give dimensions, capacities or configuration. Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (Standard Drawings) contains typical details for granite and concrete monuments only, and does not include sleepers or cylinders.

Could Council please provide the required dimensions, capacity, configuration and any drawings or reference products for the Small, Medium, Large and XLarge sleeper/cylinder items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clause 7.16, page 5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-A, “Above Ground Ashes interment options”; Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (no corresponding drawing).

- Reason: These four lines cannot be priced, or sourced from a manufacturer, without sizes or a drawing.

11. Bookstyle plaque pricing structure

The Schedule of Rates includes, as separate lines, “380 × 280 Bookstyle Bronze Plaque,” “380 × 280 Bookstyle Aluminium Plaque,” “380 × 280 Bookstyle Bronze Plaque – With first plaque,” and “Second plate for Bronze bookstyle plaque.” A refurbishment line is described as “Bookstyle plaque with first leaf (380 × 280).”

Could Council please confirm what is included in each of these rates — in particular, whether the “Bookstyle” rate is for the base or cover only, whether “With first plaque” includes the bookstyle unit plus the first inscription plate, and whether the “Second plate” is only the additional detachable plate?

- Document and clause: Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” burial plaque and refurbishment rows; Service Specification, clauses 7.8 and 7.9.

- Reason: The three new-supply bookstyle lines can be read in more than one way, and a misreading would produce inconsistent prices.

12. Undefined additional options on SP-A

Several priced options are not defined in the Service Specification or the Standard Drawings:

- “165 × 133 Bronze plaque with soldier hump” — no drawing or profile is provided;

- “120 × 160 Leaf shaped plaque” — no outline or thickness is provided;

- “Perpetual emblem for a bronze plaque”;

- “Plaque cleaner”;

- “Fast-tracked order cost (per order)” — no delivery period is stated that this extra rate must achieve;

- “Smart memorial added to an existing plaque/memorial order” and “Stand-alone smart memorial” (including what hardware, hosting, term, data and artwork are included in the rate); and

- “Tier 1 – simple,” “Tier 2 – intermediate” and “Tier 3 – complex” custom artwork re-draw — no criteria or examples distinguish the tiers.

Could Council please provide a short definition, specification or example for each of the items listed above and, for a fast-tracked order, the required delivery period from receipt of the order?

- Document and clause: Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” the rows named above (including the sheet spellings “Smart mewmorial” and “red-draw”); Service Specification, clauses 7 and 5.5; Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (no metal-plaque or smart-memorial drawings).

- Reason: These are priced lines on a sheet that, on its face, requires a unit rate for each item, but they cannot be quoted from the current specification.

13. Ceramic photo shapes and chrome plate specification

Clause 7.10 requires ceramic photos in oval, square and rectangular shapes, full bleed, surface-mounted and frameless. The Schedule of Rates prices photos only by size and by black-and-white or colour. Clause 7.9 states included inscription lines for ashes and burial plaques, but not for detachable plates. Chrome detachable plates have no alloy or finish standard, unlike bronze (C83600, AS 1565:2023) and aluminium (DA601, AS 1874:2000).

Could Council please confirm:

- whether the listed ceramic photo rates apply to all three shapes at the stated size, or whether shape is priced differently;

- how many inscription lines, if any, are included in the detachable plate rates; and

- the required material and finish standard for the 100 × 75 chrome plate?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 7.1, 7.2, 7.9 and 7.10, pages 4–5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-A, detachable plates and photo options.

- Reason: Shape, included lettering and the chrome standard all affect cost and are not aligned between the specification and the price sheet.

14. Brass in the Invitation to Tender versus bronze in the specification

The Invitation to Tender overview, and the VendorPanel Request Summary, describe Portion A as including “bronze, brass and aluminium.” Service Specification clause 2.1 refers to “bronze, chrome and aluminium.” Clauses 7.1 and 7.2, and the SP-A price sheet, specify bronze and aluminium (and chrome plates) only. There is no brass line item and no brass alloy standard.

Could Council please confirm whether brass plaques are required, or whether “brass” in the overview should be read as bronze, consistent with clauses 7.1 and 7.2 and the Schedule of Rates?

- Document and clause: Invitation to Tender, page 1, Separable Portion A; VendorPanel Request Summary, “What’s required”; Service Specification, clauses 2.1, 7.1 and 7.2; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques.”

- Reason: An unexplained brass requirement would change the product range and pricing; it looks like an inconsistency between the overview and the detailed specification.

15. Packaging of Portion D materials

Clause 3.7 requires packaging that facilitates safe and convenient unloading by Council’s forklift if required, and states that items should be palletised and/or placed on Council work benches on delivery. Many Portion D items are small tags and markers (including 15 × 50 mm and 50 × 30 mm).

Could Council please confirm the expected packaging, palletisation and marking for Portion D materials, including small tags, and whether clause 3.7 applies in full to those items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.7, 3.8 and 10, pages 2 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-D line items.

- Reason: The general packaging rule is written for larger memorial products and needs to be confirmed for small engraved-blank deliveries.

16. Supply-only application of experience, reporting and systems obligations

Several general contractor obligations are written as applying to “the Contractor” or to “all personnel undertaking the works,” without being limited to on-site portions:

- Service Specification clause 12.4, which requires personnel to have a minimum of five (5) years’ relevant industry experience;

- Service Specification clause 16, which requires a training matrix, completion schedule and defects and hazards reporting;

- Service Specification clause 17, which provides that contractors may be required to use Council’s Confirm asset management system; and

- General Terms and Conditions clause 7.1(d)(v) and clause 7.5, which require a statutory declaration in the form of Schedule 3, and a subcontractor payment register, with every payment claim.

Could Council please confirm which of these obligations apply to a respondent engaged only to supply and deliver products under Portions A and D, with no installation or cemetery-site work?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 12.4, 16.1–16.2 and 17.1, pages 11 and 14 of 14; General Terms and Conditions, clauses 7.1(d)(v) and 7.5, and Schedule 3.

- Reason: These are operational and compliance obligations that may or may not be intended for a supply-only contractor. This question does not ask again about insurance types or the Part 2.1 safety documentation, which were raised on 15 November 2026.

Thank you for your assistance.

title: Richmond Village Green and Playground Upgrade - Design & Documentation Consultancy
description:
Clarence City Council (CCC) invites Quotations from suitably qualified Respondents to undertake a consultancy for the preparation of an Issue for Tender Package, including concept design, detailed design, drawings, details, schedules, specifications and supporting documentation as required under the Contract for the upgrade of the Richmond Village Green and playground at 54-56 Bridge Street, Richmond, Tasmania 7025

The Richmond Village Green and Playground Upgrade is the first project proposed for delivery under the Richmond Village Master Plan 2026, a strategic framework adopted by the CCC in June 2026 to guide planning, investment and development within Richmond over the next 20 years.

The Master Plan, developed and informed by engagement with residents, business and key stakeholders, establishes a vision for enhancing Richmond’s public spaces while protecting the village’s nationally significant heritage values and character. Key priorities include improvements to accessibility, pedestrian safety, visitor management and the quality of public open spaces.

As the first priority project identified within the Master Plan, this project is intended to contribute to these objectives by enhancing a key community gathering space for residents and visitors. Funding has been secured for the design phase of the project, including technical investigations and community engagement to inform the development of a preferred design.

The Master Plan establishes the preferred concept for the project. The role of the Consultant is to validate, refine and further develop the Master Plan recommendations through concept design, community engagement, cost planning, detailed design and construction documentation, rather than prepare alternative precinct concepts.

The purpose of this consultancy is to prepare a complete and coordinated design and documentation package to support future implementation of the project. While funding has been secured for the design phase, construction funding may be subject to future funding availability. Respondents should therefore assume that the primary outcome of this consultancy is the preparation of a tender-ready package for future procurement.

PRE-QUOTATION SITE MEETING

For clarification of the Services, a pre-Quotation site meeting is scheduled for at 10am Tuesday 17 November 2026. This meeting will convene on Site at the Forth Street Carpark by the Richmond Village Green at 54 Bridge Street, Richmond, Tasmania.

Attendance at the site meeting is not mandatory; however, Respondents are strongly encouraged to attend to familiarise themselves with the Site and project requirements prior to submitting a Quotation.

Respondents intending to attend this meeting are requested to inform the contact person nominated on the front cover of this Quotation Invitation prior to the meeting.

CLOSE OF QUOTATIONS

3pm Tuesday 1 December 2026

LATE QUOTATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

This heritage listed place, Unara, is a heritage-listed detached Federation Bungalow, originally built for Sir Littleton Groom Circa 1906. The Northern and Southern wings were added in the 1950’s & 1960’s respectively. Along with various alterations & additions over the years. The building currently houses Drug & Alcohol residential rehabilitation.

The building is currently experiencing roof leaks, with some isolated interior damage caused. It has been determined that new roofing including flashings and stormwater reticulation remediation is required. Structural tie down and insulation will be improved while the sheeting is off and the chimneys will be repointed to retain their integrity.

The stormwater reticulation downstream of the downpipes is in a failed state. The above ground reticulation, suspended from the floor joists, appears to have backfalls and some charged lines. Reticulation enters the ground on the Western side of the Northern extension, via a retention pipe which is currently disconnected from the inground pipe, discharging all stormwater to surface in the undercroft. This is presumably because the inground system is blocked. The inground stormwater reticulation direction, route & discharge point is unknown.

title: Identity Governance Administration (IGA) & Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solutions and Services
description:
Suppliers are invited by the State of Queensland (acting through the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) – the Customer) to submit Offers for either one or both Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) Solution and / or Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solution and associated maintenance and support Services as further specified in this Invitation to Offer (ITO) TMRICT26098.

Suppliers may submit an Offer for:

	(a) an IGA Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(b) a PAM Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(c) both an IGA Solution and PAM Solution, with maintenance and support Services for both/each; or

	(d) a single Solution that meets the Requirements for both IGA and PAM, with maintenance and support Services.

All technology types will be considered (that is, Suppliers are not limited to submitting Offers for As a Service based solutions only), as well as alternative and innovative solutions which meet the Customer’s objectives and Requirements.

The Requirements are set out in the Invitation Documents and include the following in-scope Products and Services:

(a) IGA Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the identity governance and administration Requirements including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement; and/or

(b) PAM Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the privileged access management Requirements, including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software; and Hardware or on-premise installed components (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement.

The following is out of scope:

	(a) configuration and customisation of the offered Solutions;

	(b) provision of integration services (other than supply of out-of-the-box connectors);

	(c) implementation services (including transition-in and transition-out services); and

	(d) end user help desk support (Level 1 Support Services) for the Customer’s end users – this will be managed by the Customer.

Any contract formed subsequent to this Invitation must be governed by the QITC Framework, Comprehensive Contract Conditions - ICT Products and Services, and the Draft Contract issued with the Invitation Documents.

Please submit all enquiries or clarifications directly through Vendor Panel.

DATA SOVEREIGNTY (MR2)

1. Does MR2 apply equally to all categories of Customer Data held by an identity governance or privileged access platform (for example, usernames, group memberships, entitlement metadata and authentication logs), or will TMR consider a risk-based approach based on the data's security classification?

2. What information security classification does TMR expect the Customer Data in the IGA and PAM Solutions to carry (for example, OFFICIAL or OFFICIAL: Sensitive)?

3. Schedule TMR1 requires that only false or non-personally identifiable data is used in non-production environments. Would TMR consider an offer where the Design, Build and Implement phase uses non-production environments hosted outside Australia (containing no Customer Data), with production hosted in Australia before go-live?

4. Will TMR consider an offer where Australian hosting is committed to by a contractual date, for example before production go-live of the relevant Solution?

5. Would customer-managed encryption keys held within Australia (so that data cannot be decrypted by parties outside Australia) be considered in assessing compliance with the "accessed" component of MR2?

6. Schedule D allows Innovative Offers that may not meet one or more Mandatory Requirements. Will TMR evaluate an Innovative Offer that does not fully meet MR2 against the same criteria as Conforming Offers? Are there particular conditions under which TMR would consider one?

SCOPE AND OFFER STRUCTURE

7. Part A 6.3(d) allows TMR to accept "Offers in part". Would TMR consider a PAM offer that addresses a defined subset of the PAM capability domains (for example, endpoint privilege management, credential and secrets vaulting, and password management), to sit alongside another supplier's solution for the remaining domains?

8. Is TMR intending to retain OpenText NetIQ for any identity functions after the IDAM Project, or is it expected to be fully replaced?

9. Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance capabilities (under TMR's E5/E7 entitlements) does TMR already intend to use, and where specifically does TMR see the remaining gap that the IGA Solution must fill?

VIABILITY SCREENING AND EVALUATION

11. For a PAM-only offer, how will the SAP firefighter, IBM RACF and OT-related requirements be weighted in screening and evaluation relative to core PAM capabilities?

12. Would TMR accept a cloud-brokered session management approach (no customer-hosted jump box) as meeting the jump box and session isolation requirements (C1 3.6.12 to 3.6.14)?

SAP AND IBM RACF

13. How central is native SAP S/4HANA and IBM RACF connector governance to the IGA evaluation? Would TMR consider an approach where SAP and RACF governance continues through existing tooling, with the IGA Solution integrating via API or SCIM?

title: Culvert Replacement Works - Kellys Road, Omeo Valley
description:
Two existing failing pipe culverts that are located along Kellys Road over minor tributaries of the Mitta Mitta River are the subject of this report. At each of the sites, an existing reinforced concrete pipe culvert has deteriorated in condition to the extent that the East Gippsland Shire Council is investigating repair or replacement works.

An assessment of the existing sites has been carried out to determine and assess the range of options available for replacing each of the culverts. It is proposed for Site A that the existing DN1200 mm concrete pipe be replaced with single cell reinforced concrete culvert on a similar horizontal and vertical alignment as currently exists. The existing DN900 mm pipe at Site B can be repaired to a serviceable condition by re-laying the pipes at the culvert outlet.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Kellys Road extends from the south east end of the Omeo Valley Road, which follows the Livingstone Creek from the Omeo Highway to the Hinnomunjie bridge across the Mitta Mitta River. The section of Kellys Road that is under the control of the East Gippsland Shire Council continues for 9.7 km to the Nine Mile Creek crossing. The road section that is the subject of this report was reconstructed and substantially upgraded by the former Omeo Shire Council in the early 1970’s, in accordance with an overall strategy to establish an alternative route between Omeo and Mitta Mitta that was less susceptible to winter snowfalls.

The road initially passes through open farmland that is used for stock grazing, before entering the Alpine National Park. The road section has a formed and gravelled surface, which is well maintained by the Council. The road has been subjected to oversize vehicles for past logging and bushfire suppression operations in the area but is predominately used for access to the farm properties, as well as by 4WD based visitors to numerous camping spots along the nearby Mitta Mitta River and within the National Park.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.01 – Construction window

Reference: Part 1 Item 4 (Tender Timetable); Part 2 Annexure Part A cl 27.1 & 35.2; Part 3 cl 1.25 (Project Timelines)

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.02 – Date for Practical Completion – conflicting provisions

Part 2 fixes the Date for Practical Completion at 12 weeks from possession of Site, while Part 3 cl 1.25 requires tenderers to nominate the contract period, commencing from acceptance of Tender. Please confirm which provision governs.
publicQuestions.answer: Contractors are required to nominate when works will commence and be completed, within the 12 week window from possession of site.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.03 – Liquidated damages cap / inclement weather

Reference: Part 2 Annexure Part A – Liquidated Damages; Part 3 cl 1.25 (Project Timelines)

Liquidated damages are $250.00 per day with the limit stated as 'Unlimited'. Please advise whether Council will accept a cap (e.g. 10% of the Contract Sum), and confirm that extensions of time apply for inclement weather and total fire ban days.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will not accept a cap on liquidated damages of 10%. Extensions of time do apply for inclement weather and total fire ban days. Contractors will be required to notify Council on the day where either instance occurs.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.04 – Site inspection and access

Reference: Part 1 Item 3 (Tender Briefing / Site Inspections)

No briefing or site inspection is scheduled. Please confirm tenderers may inspect both sites unaccompanied, and advise any access restrictions and a contact for access.
publicQuestions.answer: Council requests that all tenderers familiarise themselves with the site prior to submitting tender. Both sites are still open to the public and do not require access approval.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.05 – Side track vs road closure (Site A)

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.3 (Site A) & cl 1.10 (Site Access); Att. 2 Site A item 1.6

Part 3 cl 1.10 requires the road to remain open with a side track. Please confirm: (a) whether a short full closure with detour would be accepted at Site A for critical activities; (b) any requirements for the side track location or design (item 1.6 notes it is subject to the Superintendent's Representative's approval); and (c) that the side track footprint is covered by the NECMA permit and cultural heritage due diligence.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will consider a short full closure. Tenderers should provide details and benefits as a part of their tender submission. The installation of the sidetrack will be covered by the terms of the contract and will to ensure excavation and vegetation removal are kept to an absolute minimum.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.06 – Site A pipe class and construction method

Please confirm whether the construction method described in the Part 3 Site A Scope Statement (rebuilding and compacting the embankment, then trenching through the compacted fill) is mandatory, or whether Council would consider alternative methods or pipe classes put forward by tenderers.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.10 – Site A – in-situ culvert backfill quantity

Reference: Att. 2 Site A item 2.4; Att. 6 (CPAA PipeClass – Site A); Dwg 256999A_9

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.11 – Site A – imported haunch/side/overlay zone material

Reference: Att. 2 Site A items 3.1 & 3.4; Att. 6 PipeClass; Part 3 cl 1.17

The basis of the imported haunch, side and overlay zone quantity in item 3.4 (50 m³) is unclear. Attachment 6 sets a 1.829 m trench width ('not to be exceeded') and a 100 mm bed zone, whereas Part 3 cl 1.17 requires the culvert base to extend 300 mm beyond the pipe (approx. 1.97 m wide) with 200 mm of bedding. publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.12 – Site A – pavement depth and extent

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:

Good Afternoon,

We have reviewed your RFT requirements. Our current Cyber Insurance is $5m. You have requested $10m.

We are compliance with other insurances requested. Will this preclude us from bidding on your RFT? Or categorise us as a non-compliant bid that could not be considered? Our insurances are with Chubb, under PremierTech2 (or Premier Tech II) for technology liability and cyber insurance. Thanks, Nick
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your query.

Generally the RFT terms require that where a tender is non-conforming it should also be accompanied by a conforming tender (RFT26-024 clause 2.8).

However under clause 2.11(m) the City has a broad discretion to accept or reject:

(1) a partial Tender or a non-complying Tender; or

(2) a Tender if the Tenderer or the Tender does not comply with this Request for Tender.

On this basis this will not preclude your bid from being considered.

Regards

City of Busselton

(a) the City's current Microsoft 365 and security licensing (e.g. E3/E5, Defender for Endpoint P2, Defender for Identity, Entra ID P1/P2);

E5 – 475, F3 - 160

(b) whether tenderers may use licences the City already holds;

Yes, may use existing licences.

(c) whether the SIEM can run in a City-owned Azure subscription with consumption billed to the City, or must be included in the Fixed Annual Service Fee.

Fixed Annual Service Fee is preferred.

5. Liability

Clause 7 of the General Conditions provides an uncapped indemnity. Will the City consider an aggregate liability cap (e.g. a multiple of annual fees) and an exclusion of consequential loss? Should these be raised as departures or through an Alternative Tender under section 2.8?

Yes the City will consider this approach, it would assist if such non-conforming aspects can be set out in a departures/clarifications table in Word format.

6. Termination for convenience and invoicing

Given clause 30 (termination for convenience on 14 Business Days' notice) and clause 17(2) (monthly invoicing), will the City accept:

(a) annual invoicing in advance for software and licence components; and

The City may consider this approach, it would assist if such non-conforming aspects can be set out in a departures/clarifications table in Word format.

(b) recovery of committed licence costs on termination for convenience?

Yes the City would consider recovery of such costs on a reasonable basis as per clause 30(2) of the General terms and conditions ‘in the event of the termination of the Contract under sub-clause (1), the City must pay the Contractor in respect of any portion of the Goods and Services which have been properly supplied and not paid for at the date of termination, as determined by the City (acting reasonably).’

7. Price evaluation and exit costs

Will the 40% price criterion be scored on the Core Three-Year Total (Attachment A, Part A) only, or also Parts B and C? REQ-10 requires capped exit transition costs, but the Schedule of Prices has no line for this. Where should these be priced?

Price evaluation will be based on the three year total for Part A.

Contract

8. Hours of work

Clause 16 limits work to 8:30am to 5:00pm weekdays, and the General Conditions take precedence over the Specification (clause 2(2)). Please confirm contract award constitutes approval for 24/7/365 service delivery, including after-hours response actions.

Yes, Contract award constitutes approval for 24/7/365 service delivery, including after-hours response actions.

9. Intellectual property

Please confirm clauses 10(4) and 10(6) apply only to deliverables produced for the City (reports, City-specific configurations and custom detections under REQ-04), not to the tenderer's pre-existing platforms, detection libraries, playbooks and methods – not to pre-existing platforms etc

Yes confirmed.

10. Insurance levels

Section 6.2(j) of Part 6 requires $10 million each for Professional Indemnity and Cyber Liability, while clause 8(1)(h) requires $2 million PI and no Cyber Liability. Which levels apply, and are they per claim or aggregate?

Section 6.2(j) of Part 6 takes precedence. The limit of cover is $10m for both PI and Cyber (in the aggregate).

Solution and delivery

11. Endpoint estate

Which EDR products are currently deployed on workstations and servers, and on approximately how many endpoints each?

Microsoft Defender is our current EDR.

AV is a blend of Microsoft Defender and Sophos Endpoint.

Refer to Scope – Endpoints table

For REQ-42, which MDM platform will manage iOS, iPadOS and Android devices at commencement, and is any MDM migration planned during onboarding?

Combination of Intune and Meraki MDM, no migration planned.

13. TechnologyOne

For REQ-49, is TechnologyOne hosted by TechnologyOne (SaaS/CiA) or on-premises, and what audit log export methods are available?

SaaS hosted instance. Log volume is unknown. TechOne ETL process will be used to extract logs to local storage where it can be ingested by MDR.

14. Onboarding timing

What is the City's target go-live date, and are there any blackout periods for onboarding?

Target go live is prior to 30 June 2027. There are no current blackout periods.

title: TRAILS Componentisation
description: Suppliers are invited by the State of Queensland (acting through the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) – the Customer) to submit an Offer for TRAILS Componentisation PoC as further specified in this ITO TMRICT26212 OR Part B – Draft QITC Contract (specifically Schedule TMR1 – Requirements and references therein).

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The Department of Transport and Main Roads provides reliable, resilient and responsive transport networks and digital services that are safe and accessible for everyone. This procurement is led by TMR's Information Technology branch (ITB).
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Friday 22 January 2027 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Registration and licensing services are fundamental to road safety, personal mobility, economic activity and government service delivery across Queensland. They support customers and businesses, frontline employees, enforcement and regulatory activities, revenue collection, other government agencies, national transport arrangements and a large network of external service and data consumers.

At the center of this environment is the Transport Registration and Integrated Licensing System (TRAILS), first implemented in 1993 and progressively extended over more than three decades to support changing legislation, registration and licensing products, offences and sanctions, payments, customer channels, credentials and external interfaces.

TMR are seeking to determine whether a bounded Registration and Vehicle business capability can be progressively separated from the broader Registration and Licensing Services ecosystem without unacceptable disruption to services that remain dependent on TRAILS. The engagement must demonstrate how modern and legacy services can coexist; how nominated business processes, rules and transactions can operate outside TRAILS; how routing, integration, data ownership, write-back, synchronisation, reconciliation, security, recovery and operational continuity will be managed; and how the approach can scale beyond the initial use case without fundamental redesign. The resulting components and delivery patterns must reduce delivery risk, cost, dependency and complexity, provide a repeatable pathway for future modernisation horizons, materially reduce legacy dependency and establish retirement readiness. TMR must also retain sufficient knowledge, rights and practical capability for TMR or another delivery partner to operate, maintain, change and extend the resulting components independently.

TMR invites Offers for a market-led TRAILS Componentisation Proof of Concept (PoC)/Proof of Delivery focused on a bounded Registration and Vehicle capability. TMR may select one or more Suppliers for funded Concept Design. Suppliers that successfully satisfy the applicable progression criteria may subsequently be invited to deliver the Simple, Medium and Complex Use Case stages. Progression is not automatic, and TMR may stop or progress one or more Suppliers at each gate.

While the scope of this ITO covers the Funded Concept Design and potential PoCs, the PoCs will inform TMR’s future delivery and sourcing approach. TMR may progress one or more successful PoC Suppliers to subsequent implementation or scale activities or undertake a broader market approach. Any future approach will consider PoC outcomes, market and technology developments, value for money and TMR requirements. Participation in the PoC does not guarantee future work and progression may stop before Gate 5.

title: Bulloo Shire Council: EOI - External Operation and Management of Council’s Fleet and Plant Workshop
description:
Bulloo Shire Council operates a well-equipped and well-maintained workshop facility located within the Council depot, providing the infrastructure necessary to support the servicing, maintenance and mechanical repair of Council's vehicle and plant fleet. The workshop is appropriately configured to accommodate both heavy plant and light vehicle maintenance activities and is supported by suitable tooling, equipment, storage areas and workspaces.

The facility provides a functional and efficient operating environment, with its layout supporting the effective movement of vehicles, plant, parts and personnel. The workshop's condition and level of equipment reflect a significant investment in fleet maintenance infrastructure and provide Council with the capability to undertake a broad range of servicing and repair activities in-house.

As a key operational asset within the depot, the workshop supports the ongoing availability, reliability and maintenance of Council's fleet and plant assets and provides a strong foundation for the delivery of mechanical services under either a Council-operated or outsourced service model.

Council invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified and experienced individuals or organisations to assume responsibility for the operation and management of Council's Fleet and Plant Workshop, including the maintenance, servicing and repair of Council's vehicles, plant and equipment assets.

This EOI process is being managed by Peak Services on behalf of Bulloo Shire Council.

What site hygiene, disinfection, accepted sampling reinstatement materials and waste disposal arrangements apply? Who will accept the reinstated sample areas and operational handback?

6 | Operational interface • Scope ••2.3 and 5

Please confirm the pipework datum, required plan format and whether Council can provide editable base drawings, operator attendance, valve identification and a consolidated review of the week 7 draft by the week 9 workshop.

7 | Access disruption • Contract clauses 13–14

How will Council-directed changes to the agreed isolation window, water clearance timing or access restrictions after mobilisation be assessed for time and cost under the contract?

publicQuestions.answer:
Answers to your questions:

1. The exact details are unclear. It has been a long time since the tank has been accessed. As per BC3111-01 It is understood there is a 300mm opening at the base of the wall of the internal tank, this will allow the tank to drain and can be used to pass materials through, but would not be suitable for personal access. It should be assumed that the systems will need to be installed to access over the wall of the internal tank.

2. The entire area around the tank can be used for setup. Operational access will not be required to be maintained during the works. There are no overhead obstructions. The northern corner of the tank site is fill with unknown bearing capacity and may not be suitable for setting up a crane. There is generally a 5m wide bitumen surface around the perimeter of the tank. It is recommended that tenderers visit the site to undertake any measurements or assessments required to plan access arrangements. There is no gate or fence around the tank so tenderers can visit any time. Note no climbing of the reservoir is permitted

3. It is expected that the water depth after draining will be a few centimetres or less. The scope will be updated to make sweeping of the remnant water to the scour part of the contract so no operator involvement will be required.

4. There is no further information available than what has already been provided within the project brief and appendices

5. The reservoir is offline and not intended to be returned to service. Any materials brought into the tank shall be Free of dirt, debris, oil & contaminants. Materials are not required to be disinfected. As long as no contaminants are introduced to the tank, any sample areas should be reinstated and generally cleaned (wipe down/sweep up). If internal sampling will introduce contaminants, the contractor shall provide details of the products and the management plan for approval prior to use. Final cleaning and return to service of the tank are outside the scope. The project manager will accept the reinstated sample areas.

6. For the purposes of this inspection a hand markup of General arrangement drawing BC3111-01 is suitable. Basic measurements with a tape measure +-20mm are sufficient. Contractor to use existing pipes/pits as datums. It is anticipated that detail survey will be undertaken during the refurbishment works. Editable drawings are not available.

7. Standdown rates are to be provided. The Reservoir is currently offline and there is no intent to bring it online until defects are rectified, so there is minimal likelihood of council directed changes.

8. Present proposed changes/contract departures in response schedule.

publicQuestions.question: Can you please clarify if the costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent testing of geosynthetic material is to be included in this tender? As we have in-house NATA labs that can perform these tasks, we would like to include this price to give best value to the Council.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that tenderers are to include costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent geosynthetic material testing as part of their tender submission.

Geomembrane destructive testing is already included under Item 16 of the Schedule of Rates and should be priced per test. As outlined in Clause 7.3.8.5 of S14, Council is responsible for the initial laboratory testing costs, with any additional testing resulting from failed destructive tests being the responsibility of the Geosynthetic Contractor.

Independent conformance testing of the GCL, HDPE geomembrane and protection and separation geotextiles is also required under the CQA Specification and S14. Tenderers should include separate rates for these tests under the ""Please insert any other applicable rates required to complete the works in accordance with the Specification"" section of the Schedule of Rates, including any associated sampling, transport and laboratory reporting costs.

Council has no objection to tenderers using their own in-house NATA-accredited laboratories, provided they are accredited for the relevant test methods, meet the independence requirements of the CQA Specification and are approved in accordance with the tender requirements.

All testing is to be carried out in accordance with the specified methods and frequencies. The Geosynthetic Contractor's existing CQC testing responsibilities remain unchanged.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.answer:

Tenderers are to allow for appropriate electrical leak-location testing methods suitable for the specified liner system, including the necessary electrical continuity and isolation arrangements in accordance with the applicable ASTM standards.

description:
The University of the Sunshine Coast (UniSC or the University) invites Expressions of Interest from suitably qualified and experienced Contractors for the delivery of the Moreton Bay Stage 3 (MBS3) project at the UniSC Moreton Bay Campus.

MBS3 comprises the construction of a new six-storey Building B1 and adaptive reuse of Building A1 Level 1, delivering additional teaching, learning, research, workplace and community-facing facilities required to support the continued growth of the Moreton Bay Campus.

Building B1 is anticipated to be approximately 11,500m² Gross Floor Area (GFA) and will incorporate a mix of contemporary learning and teaching spaces, learning commons, staff workspaces, research and industry collaboration facilities, simulation and visualisation environments, student-focused facilities, food and beverage offerings and community-facing clinical and engagement spaces.

Building A1 Level 1 will be refurbished and repurposed to provide specialist teaching, laboratory, simulation, research and support spaces integrated with the broader campus environment.

The project is being designed as a contemporary, high-quality higher education facility that reflects the University's strategic objectives for learning, research, industry engagement and sustainability. The design incorporates a hybrid mass timber and concrete structural solution, requiring respondents to demonstrate relevant capability and experience in the delivery of mass timber projects and associated procurement, construction and supply chain management activities.

Temora Shire Council is assisting Visit Riverina with publication of this RFQ, the contracting client is Visit Riverina, not Temora Shire Council. Enquiries may to be directed via: admin@theriverina.com.au

Visit Riverina is seeking quotations from suitably qualified marketing and public relations agencies to develop and deliver an integrated destination marketing and PR campaign for the Riverina region of NSW in autumn 2027.

The engagement will establish a distinctive regional destination campaign proposition and deliver targeted paid marketing and earned media activity to increase awareness of the Riverina in metropolitan, interstate and national visitor markets.

 The scope includes:

1. Destination positioning, campaign strategy and creative development.

2. Autumn paid destination marketing, including audience targeting, media planning, creative production, media buying and optimisation.

3. Public relations strategy, proactive media pitching and earned media opportunities.

4. Campaign management, performance monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

The campaign will explore the Riverina's scale and diversity, with the potential creative concept of "A Country Within a Country" identified as a starting point rather than a predetermined campaign direction.

Visit Riverina is seeking agencies with demonstrated experience in destination marketing, tourism campaigns, strategic creative development, paid media and public relations.

The total available budget is $40,000 including GST and all campaign delivery costs.

The successful agency will be engaged for an initial three-month period, with commencement anticipated in February 2027.

publicQuestions.question:
Is there an existing pond on site to dump the sludge from site?

Can you indicate an anticipated depth of sludge we expect to find in the tank if any?

Will there be an opportunity to work till 5pm?

Delineation between operational areas - are you expecting fencing within the site?

Are we treating the work as confined space? The documents leave this open to intererptaion

Are we coating the top of the walls? Photos show no coating on top

Are we keying in at the top of the walls (I assume this is a design detail). Similarly are we providing a termination detail at all isolation gates?

Are we temporarily moving the floor grates to access the tank or will that we carried out by MCC?

Are there any joint repairs? The drawings do not show any joints

Document refers to Instrumentation but there is no reference on the drawing.

Document refers decommissioning and removal of existing elements however there is no reference on the drawing.

Contractors WHS Representative - minimum of 2 times a week. Can you confirm that this must not be the site supervisor?

In the case of a random large wet weather event, are we expected to allow the STP to operate and remove all equipment from the tanks?

Will MCC manage any double isolation leaks?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. No. The sludge must be removed from the site and disposed of at a waste facility that is lawfully authorised to accept the waste.

Refer to Part 2A – Job Specification, Clause 10.2, which requires the Contractor to demolish, recycle and dispose of waste and pay all applicable off-site disposal fees.

2. Council is unable to confirm the depth of sludge at this stage. The tank could not be completely emptied before implementing a bypass system. Accordingly, tenderers are responsible for assessing and allowing for the likely sludge depth and disposal requirements.

Tenderers were provided with an opportunity to inspect the site and raise questions during the optional pre-tender meeting.

3. Yes. Work that does not require Council supervision may be undertaken until 5:00 pm, subject to the Contractor complying with all site, safety and operational requirements.

4. Part 2A – Job Specification, Clause 3 "The Contractor shall provide clear delineation between operational areas and areas where construction activities are being undertaken."

5. Council does not determine whether a particular area or work activity constitutes confined-space work. The Contractor is responsible for assessing the work areas and activities and determining whether they are classified as confined spaces, in consultation with MidCoast Council where required.

6. No. The coating is required only on the internal wall surfaces and the floor, as specified in the RFT documents.

7. Yes. The Contractor must provide suitable coating termination details at the top of the walls and at the isolation gates in accordance with the RFT requirements and the approved coating system.

8. The Contractor is responsible for removing and reinstating the floor grates as required to undertake the Works.

9. No joint repairs have been identified or are currently anticipated. If the Contractor identifies defective or deteriorated joints during the Works, the Contractor must notify Council before undertaking any additional repair work.

10. Refer to Part 2A – Job Specification, Clause 6.1 – Hold and Witness Points.

If the Contractor is required to disconnect or otherwise interfere with any instruments as part of the proposed work method or bypass arrangement, the relevant activity will be treated as a Witness Point.

If no instrumentation disconnection or interference is required, the relevant Witness Point will be considered not applicable.

11. The need to decommission or remove existing elements will depend on the bypass arrangement adopted by the Contractor.

12. The RFT documents do not require the Contractor’s WHS Representative to be a different person from the Site Supervisor.

The Site Supervisor may also perform the role of WHS Representative, provided that they meet the requirements of Part 2A – Job Specification, Clause 7.3, including having appropriate industry experience and demonstrated experience in construction WHS management.

13. If the bypass system is unable to safely manage the flows, the Contractor must cease the affected works, remove the bypass equipment and any other equipment that may obstruct the operation of the STP, and allow the STP to operate normally.

14. Council will manage the existing double isolation arrangement shown in the Flow Management Plan.

If the Contractor proposes an alternative bypass or isolation arrangement, the responsibilities for managing any leakage or isolation issues will be reviewed and agreed with Council before the alternative arrangement is implemented. Any alternative arrangement remains subject to Council’s approval.
