publicQuestions.question:
1.	Does QFD require the automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder to be OEM factory fitted, or is an approved post-OEM conversion acceptable?

2.	The milestone payments in 3.2 add up to 100% (20/20/50/10) without any payment for receipt of the chassis. Will QFD consider a progress payment when the cab chassis is received, given its cost?

3.	Clause 15.1 asks for a “fully integrated hydraulic retarder”. Would an OEM exhaust or engine brake be acceptable as an alternative? Hydraulic retarders are limited or unavailable on most 4x4 chassis in this class.

4.	Clause 27.4 requires GOM and axle group loads not to exceed 90% of the Queensland regulatory maximum permissible limits. Please confirm whether the 90% requirement applies to the regulatory GVM/axle limits only, or also to the chassis manufacturer's plated GVM and axle ratings. For an 11,000 kg GVM chassis, does QFD therefore require the fully operational GOM to be no greater than 9,900 kg?

5.	The inventory tabs use colour coding for Contracted Supplier Supplied and QFD Supplied items; however, a significant number of items appear uncoloured. Please provide or confirm the definitive supply responsibility for every inventory item, including whether the listed weights and dimensions are the values to be used for tender mass and stowage calculations.

6.	33.1 ROPS. Please provide the required engineering/certification basis for the rollover protection structure, including the required load cases, factors of safety and applicable standard or QFD test criteria. Is QFD's preference for an internal cabin ROPS, an external/body-mounted structure, or is either arrangement acceptable subject to certification?

7.	Clause 13.5 states that the suspension system should be capable of being lowered when required. Please confirm whether this requirement applies to the iZone Medium 4x4 appliance and, if so, please define the required lowering functionality and purpose.

8.	13.2 108km/h. Please confirm whether the requirement to sustain a minimum 108 km/h at operational mass is an acceptance requirement. Where the selected chassis has an OEM speed limitation, does QFD expect that limitation to be modified, and will QFD's authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process?

9.	Clause 44 – Deluge System – Flow, Pressure and Operating Requirements

Clause 44.9 references Attachment E, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification, which specifies a nominal operating pressure of 220 kPa and total water flow of 10 L/min.

As this specification was developed for a single-cab ultralight appliance, could QFD please confirm whether these flow and pressure requirements are applicable to the larger iZone medium crew-cab appliance, particularly given the additional front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection requirements?

10.	The IRR (3.75 m × 1.8 m) must be stowed below cab height (50.1). Is it acceptable for it to extend past the body footprint, given the length guideline of under 7,000 mm?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Chris,

See below responses.

Does QFD require the automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder to be OEM factory fitted, or is an approved post-OEM conversion acceptable?

Automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder are preferred to be OEM, but an approved post-OEM conversion is acceptable.

2. The milestone payments in 3.2 add up to 100% (20/20/50/10) without any payment for receipt of the chassis. Will QFD consider a progress payment when the cab chassis is received, given its cost?

The intent as stated in clause 3.2

1. Cab chassis - 100% receipt of base cab chassis (allows payment on the receipt of cab chassis)

2. Cab chassis - 100% receipt of cab chassis accessories and completion of Pre Delivery (allows payment on the receipt of accessories and completion of Pre Delivery at end of build)

3. Clause 15.1 asks for a “fully integrated hydraulic retarder”. Would an OEM exhaust or engine brake be acceptable as an alternative? Hydraulic retarders are limited or unavailable on most 4x4 chassis in this class.

A fully integrated hydraulic retarder is preferred but QFD is open to alternate offers.

4. Clause 27.4 requires GOM and axle group loads not to exceed 90% of the Queensland regulatory maximum permissible limits. Please confirm whether the 90% requirement applies to the regulatory GVM/axle limits only, or also to the chassis manufacturer's plated GVM and axle ratings. For an 11,000 kg GVM chassis, does QFD therefore require the fully operational GOM to be no greater than 9,900 kg?

This clause relates directly to the offered cab chassis taking into account front and rear axle limitations. At GOM - should not exceed 90% of front axle limits (TMR or OEM). At GOM - should not exceed 90% of rear axle limits (TMR or OEM).

5. The inventory tabs use colour coding for Contracted Supplier Supplied and QFD Supplied items; however, a significant number of items appear uncoloured. Please provide or confirm the definitive supply responsibility for every inventory item, including whether the listed weights and dimensions are the values to be used for tender mass and stowage calculations.

The uncoloured equipment is a reference to what is to be stored but not supplied by either Supplier or QFD. The supplied weights and dimensions are to be used for weight calculations and to identify storage solutions and locations.

6. 33.1 ROPS. Please provide the required engineering/certification basis for the rollover protection structure, including the required load cases, factors of safety and applicable standard or QFD test criteria. Is QFD's preference for an internal cabin ROPS, an external/body-mounted structure, or is arrangement acceptable subject to certification?

QFD would request a minimum of a FEA Analysis report of the proposed system as per Annex 5 ADR59/00 guideline. The calculation should consider loads according to ADR 59/00 Omnibus strength and conducted by a Registered RPEQ Engineer. QFD do not have a preference for an internal cabin ROPS or an external/body-mounted structure, either arrangement or combination is acceptable subject to certification.

7. Clause 13.5 states that the suspension system should be capable of being lowered when required. Please confirm whether this requirement applies to the iZone Medium 4x4 appliance and, if so, please define the required lowering functionality and purpose.

If an air bag suspension is offered this should have the ability to be lowered (to provide better ergonomics), however if this is not available on the offered cab chassis details of suspension should be provided.

8. 13.2 108km/h. Please confirm whether the requirement to sustain a minimum 108 km/h at operational mass is an acceptance requirement. Where the selected chassis has an OEM speed limitation, does QFD expect that limitation to be modified, and will QFD's authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process?

QFD will provide an authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process.

9. Clause 44 – Deluge System – Flow, Pressure and Operating Requirements

Clause 44.9 references Attachment E, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification, which specifies a nominal operating pressure of 220 kPa and total water flow of 10 L/min.

As this specification was developed for a single-cab ultralight appliance, could QFD please confirm whether these flow and pressure requirements are applicable to the larger iZone medium crew-cab appliance, particularly given the additional front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection requirements?

QFD intent is to base the function on the, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification (Halo) and understand that there will be variances. Additional systems front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection would be designed separately.

10. The IRR (3.75 m × 1.8 m) must be stowed below cab height (50.1). Is it acceptable for it to extend past the body footprint, given the length guideline of under 7,000 mm?

 

The IRR is acceptable to be partially inflated and as long as all regulatory requirements are met could extend past the rear body line.

Clause 34.1 – Pump-and-Roll Performance

Could QFD clarify the minimum and maximum vehicle speeds required when conducting pump-and-roll operations with both the Normal Pressure (NP) and High Pressure (HP) pumps operating?

Clause 45.6 – 8-Hour Continuous Duty Test

Could QFD clarify the requirements for the eight-hour continuous duty test, including:

Whether both NP and HP pumps are required to operate simultaneously during testing;

The required operating outputs and duty cycle; and

Whether testing must be conducted under specified ambient temperature conditions?

This information will assist tenderers in accurately demonstrating compliance with the performance requirement.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Richard,

Please see below responses:

Clause 2.1 – Off-Road Capability

The specification requires the appliance to operate in various off-road conditions, including dry creek crossings, loose sand, steep side slopes, fire trails, and rutted tracks. Could QFD please clarify whether there are any minimum performance requirements or acceptance criteria relating to:

Ground clearance;

Approach, departure and ramp-over angles;

Wading depth;

Maximum gradeability and side-slope capability; and

Any specific off-road demonstration or validation testing requirements?

If no specific criteria apply, will OEM-published performance data be accepted as evidence of compliance?

QFD's intent is to have a fit for purpose vehicle able to safely perform in the stated environments. OEM-published performance data is acceptable as evidence of compliance.

Clauses 4.1 and 12.2 – AdBlue System Requirements

Clause 12.2 requires the engine to continue operating without fault if the AdBlue tank is empty, while Clause 4.1 requires compliance with all applicable Australian Design Rules and Standards.

Could QFD clarify how compliance will be assessed where OEM engine management systems incorporate AdBlue-related warnings and engine derating strategies to meet ADR and emissions certification requirements? In such circumstances, how should any conflict between these requirements be addressed?

As QFD operates in emergency situations require the ability to continue to operate with OEM systems limiting operations. This would only likely occur rarely. QFD will access on the ability to continue operating without fault if the AdBlue tank is empty and QFD acknowledges that this outside of ADR and emissions certification requirements.

Clause 4.25 – Laden Mass Calculation

The laden mass calculation includes four crew members at 120 kg each.

Could QFD confirm whether the 120 kg allowance per occupant includes PPE and personal equipment, or whether these items should be accounted for separately in the laden mass calculation?

120kg is inclusive of personal PPE.

Clause 13.4 – Vehicle Performance

Could QFD clarify the minimum performance criteria expected for:

Uphill speed maintenance on a 6% grade;

Startability from a standstill on an incline;

Acceleration performance; and

General gradeability requirements?

Will OEM chassis manufacturer performance specifications be accepted as evidence of compliance?

QFD will accept OEM chassis manufacturer performance specifications as evidence of compliance providing all requirements are provided.

Clause 15.1 – Auxiliary Braking System

The specification requires a fully integrated hydraulic retarder.

Could QFD advise whether alternative OEM-approved auxiliary braking systems will be considered where a hydraulic retarder is not available for the proposed chassis?

A fully integrated hydraulic retarder is preferred but QFD is open to alternate offers.

Clause 17.1 – Pump Drive Arrangement

Given the requirement for pump-and-roll operations, could QFD clarify whether there is a preferred pump drive arrangement, or whether either PTO-driven or independent engine-driven pump systems will be considered, provided all operational requirements are met?

Either PTO-driven or independent engine-driven pump systems will be considered, provided all operational requirements are met.

Clause 34.1 – Pump-and-Roll Performance

Could QFD clarify the minimum and maximum vehicle speeds required when conducting pump-and-roll operations with both the Normal Pressure (NP) and High Pressure (HP) pumps operating?

QFD intent would have a range from 0-15 KPH.

Clause 45.6 – 8-Hour Continuous Duty Test

Could QFD clarify the requirements for the eight-hour continuous duty test, including:

Whether both NP and HP pumps are required to operate simultaneously during testing;

The required operating outputs and duty cycle; and

Whether testing must be conducted under specified ambient temperature conditions?

This information will assist tenderers in accurately demonstrating compliance with the performance requirement.

QFD would prefer pump test to be performed while operating simultaneously.

Testing can be performed at ambient temperature conditions of time of test (preference would be for higher temperatures).

title: Construction works for Longreach Hospital Chillers Replacement Project
description:
Central West Hospital and Health Service (CWHHS) is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced mechanical services contractor to undertake the replacement of three existing air-cooled chillers at Longreach Hospital.

The works include the removal of the existing chillers and the installation, integration, testing and commissioning of three Principal-supplied Carrier 30RBP-670R air-cooled scroll chillers.

The successful contractor will be responsible for delivering all associated construction works required to provide a complete, fully operational and compliant chilled-water system. This includes coordinating the works within an operational hospital environment and minimising disruption to patients, staff and clinical services.

Expected timing: Construction required to be completed by 30 June 2027

Location: Longreach Hospital, Longreach, QLD, 4730

Tenderers must refer to the project specifications and drawings for the Longreach Hospital Chiller Replacement Project for detailed information regarding the scope, technical requirements, site conditions and contractor responsibilities.

The tenderer is responsible for reviewing all RFQ documentation and identifying any discrepancies, exclusions, assumptions or additional information required to deliver the works.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Three existing air-cooled chillers located at the Longreach Hospital have reached their end of life. Two Chillers have failed and one Chiller is currently operational.

Central West Hospital and Health Service (CWHHS) engaged Stantec to undertake the detailed design and development of the engineering specifications for the Longreach Hospital Chiller Replacement Project.

Due to the anticipated manufacturing lead times associated with the new Chillers, CWHHS procured the three Chillers directly as a separate procurement package.

Carrier 30RBP-670R Chillers were selected as the preferred option that meets CWHHS’ requirements.

The Chillers are estimated to arrive in Longreach in January 2027.

It must operate under Longreach climatic conditions and be delivered with complete commissioning records, verified performance, operator training, warranties, asset information and as-constructed documentation.

The works must minimise disruption to patients, staff and clinical services and provide effective contingency arrangements throughout all shutdowns and changeovers.

The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

title: Civil, Landscaping and Lighting Works at Hazelbrook Town Centre
description:
Blue Mountains City Council invites tenders for RFT 2026/27-600013 – Civil, Landscaping and Lighting Works – Hazelbrook Town Centre.

Council seeks a suitably qualified contractor to undertake the civil, landscape and lighting works associated with the Hazelbrook Town Centre activation, in accordance with the Request for Tender, drawings, specifications and contract documentation.

The works will be undertaken within Hazelbrook Town Centre in the Blue Mountains local government area.

The contractor is required to provide all labour, plant, materials, supervision, and management to complete the works in accordance with the design drawings, specifications, and relevant authority requirements.

The contractors are expected to read through this Vendor Panel RF(x) where general information is presented, alongside with all uploaded documentation – attached to this Request for Tender.

Tenderer's briefing held on 1st December 2026 at BMCC offices, 2-6 Civic Place, Katoomba.

The briefing can be attended in person or via the teams link below, RSVP and any queries can be sent to the email nominated in the RFT.

https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/421863969315210?p=DEB6Mr99DDBBGzBPbV

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Council is committed to leading our City, protecting our environment, caring for our people, making our City vibrant, liveable, healthy and accessible, and economically and financially sustainable.
The Blue Mountains is one of only two cities in the world surrounded by a World Heritage Area and sits within the Sydney drinking water catchment servicing 1.7 million people.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Friday 11 December 2026 02:00 PM (AUS Eastern Daylight Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The project involves delivery of civil, landscaping and lighting improvements within Hazelbrook Town Centre. The works are intended to improve the quality, functionality and presentation of the public domain, including the interfaces between pedestrian areas, existing infrastructure and local businesses.

The Hazelbrook Town Centre works form part of Council’s town centre activation program. Tenderers should refer to the RFT and accompanying project documents for the defined scope, specified in the documentation provided in this tender and particularly in the returnable schedules – for evaluation purposes.

To deliver this project, the contractor must comply with relevant Blue Mountains City Council requirements, civil and landscape specifications, applicable Australian Standards, Work Health and Safety legislation, environmental management obligations and conditions of statutory approvals, including Part 5 approval conditions. The methodology must address safe work in an operating town centre and minimise disruption to local businesses, including consideration of night works.

Construction must integrate with existing footpaths, kerbs, services and other town centre infrastructure, while managing pedestrian access, business interfaces and environmental impacts. Materials, construction methods, lighting installation and finishing works must comply with the supplied drawings, specifications and applicable standards to provide a durable, coordinated public-domain outcome.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Nice to haves

• Delivery of safe, accessible, user-friendly and high-quality civil, landscape and lighting improvements within Hazelbrook Town Centre.

• Integration of landscaping and public-domain finishes to improve the town centre’s visual character and amenity.

• Clear, safe pedestrian movement and appropriate wayfinding and lighting interfaces consistent with the approved design.

• Compliance with all relevant Blue Mountains City Council standards, civil and landscape specifications, and Australian Standards.

Service Level Agreements

• Adherence to Work Health and Safety legislation and environmental management requirements.

• Maintain 3rd party certifications active and visible in company’s Vendor Panel Dashboard

• WHS Third-party current certification ISO 45001:2018

• EMS Third-party current certification ISO 14001:2015

• QMS Third-party current certification ISO 9001:2015

Regarding Sub-Contractors

• Authorised agents, significant subcontractors (including partners), resellers and dealers must be named under the contract by the approved contractor.

• This information is provided within Vendor Panel under each Supplier Details in the ‘Attachment(s)’ uploaded file named ‘LGP Contract number - Company name – subcontractor register’ – individual file.

• The approved contractor must advise of and name any subcontracting parties in their response to this RFT.

• Conformance with statutory approvals, utility service conditions, TfNSW, Sydney water, Endeavour Energy, and any other external asset owner requirements.

• Timely completion of the civil, landscape and lighting works within the agreed construction program (refer to the RFT and construction documentation for applicable milestones and completion requirements).

• Prompt response to defects or required remedial works during the defects liability period.

• Effective communication and coordination with Council representatives and relevant authorities.

Project Benefits

• Improved pedestrian safety, accessibility and amenity within Hazelbrook Town Centre through coordinated civil, landscape and lighting improvements.

• A more welcoming, functional and attractive town centre public domain that supports local businesses, visitors and community activity.

• Positive environmental outcomes through careful landscaping, restoration, and adherence to heritage and World Heritage Area protections.

• Long-term public-domain value through durable works integrated with existing footpaths, kerbs, utilities and other town centre infrastructure.

Clause 7 of Attachment C (Draft QITC Comprehensive Contract V1) incorporates both Module Order Form 2 (Software) and Module Order Form 3 (As a Service), and while Module Order Form 3 identifies the acquisition as Software as a Service and specifies that the As a Service shall be provided on private infrastructure within Australian jurisdiction, the same document leaves unchecked the field under Module 3 that asks whether the As a Service will be hosted by a third party, and Module Order Form 2A contemporaneously allocates backup responsibility to the Customer; accordingly, the Supplier respectfully seeks confirmation from the Buyer that: (a) the intended deployment model is Software as a Service whereby the Supplier is solely responsible for provisioning, maintaining, securing and operating the infrastructure and environment on which the solution runs; (b) Queensland Health will not be required to host, procure, maintain, or operate any infrastructure or server environment in connection with the solution; and (c) the allocation of backup responsibility to the Customer in Module Order Form 2A is a template default that is superseded by Module Order Form 3 and does not impose on Queensland Health any obligation to manage data backup or storage infrastructure.
publicQuestions.answer:
Queensland Health is open to considering both Software as a Service (SaaS) and Queensland Health-hosted deployment models.

Suppliers are requested to provide details of their proposed solution, including the deployment model and associated infrastructure, hosting, maintenance, backup and support requirements and responsibilities.

Suppliers should provide the relevant pricing information in accordance with the options outlined in the Invitation to Offer.

Module Order Form 2 (Software) applies to Queensland Health-hosted solutions, while Module Order Form 3 (As a Service) applies to Software as a Service. The applicable module will be determined by the proposed deployment model.

Suppliers should indicate in Attachment C (Draft QITC Comprehensive Contract V1) which Module will apply.

Currently we are pricing RFT-58 (Easton Park and Birchgrove Oval Floodlighting Upgrade). Could Council please clarify the items below. They affect excavation, spoil, reinstatement and program, so we'd appreciate a response before tenders close.

A. EXISTING CONDUITS AND FOOTINGS

1. Reuse of existing in-ground conduits

The demolition plans (L06) and Spec 2.1 require removal of the existing sub-circuit cabling and in-ground conduits. L01 shows new trenching from each main switchboard to the new poles, around 650 m across both sites. To reduce trenching and turf reinstatement on the playing fields, would Council accept the following where the existing conduits are serviceable?

- Locating the existing conduits during the services scan, then proving them (rodding / mandrel test)

- Reusing them for the new sub-circuit cabling

- Excavating only where needed to cut in and extend to the new pole and pit locations

- Abandoning in place any conduits not reused, instead of excavating them

- Whether conduits smaller than the 50 mm minimum (Spec 2.9) would be accepted

2. Removal of existing pole footings

L06 requires existing poles to be "decommissioned and removed, including footing" (Easton Park: 2 poles; Birchgrove: 5 poles). Please confirm whether:

- The footings must be fully removed, or

- They may be broken down to a set depth below finished surface level (e.g. 500 mm), with the void backfilled, topsoiled and turfed

If partial removal is acceptable, please confirm the minimum depth Council requires.

B. TRENCHING AND CONDUITS

3. Conduit configuration

L01 notes 2 x 50 mm conduits per pole. Please confirm whether:

- Each pole is to have its own pair of conduits back to the main switchboard (4 x 50 mm on shared runs), or

- 2 x 50 mm per trench run is acceptable, with cabling looped pole to pole

4. Trench backfill

The L03 trench detail is marked "conceptual only". Can site-won material be reused as backfill above the sand bed/surround, or is imported backfill required?

5. Path and hard-surface crossings

Where routes cross paths or other hard surfaces:

- Is open trenching acceptable, or is under-boring required?

- Please advise Council's reinstatement specification.

6. Irrigation

Are there irrigation systems in either field? If so, can Council provide layouts, and confirm responsibility for repairing any damage found during excavation?

C. FOOTINGS AND POLES

7. Geotechnical and contamination information

Does Council hold any existing geotechnical, contamination or fill reports for either park? This affects footing depth and spoil classification.

8. Footing pricing basis

The footing design follows award (Spec 2.2 / 2.7). Will Council accept tenders based on a stated provisional footing size, with a schedule of rates for extra depth or diameter once the engineer's design is complete?

9. Pole finish

Please confirm hot-dip galvanised poles are acceptable, with no powder coat finish required.

10. Luminaires

Spec 2.7 refers to WEEF luminaire installation guidelines, while the pole and crossarm designs are based on Philips Optivision BVP528. Please confirm the specified luminaire, noting clause 3.11 (no alternatives).

11. Bird spikes

Please confirm bird spikes are required on all head frames (Spec 2.7), and any required type or product.

D. SITE AND PROGRAM

12. Access, hours and program

Please advise:

- Site access routes for plant and deliveries

- Permitted working hours

- Compound / storage locations

- Whether the fields can be closed during the works

- Any sports seasons, bookings or events to work around

13. Ground protection

Does Council have minimum requirements for ground protection (e.g. matting) for cranes, drilling rigs and plant crossing the fields?

14. Trees

Are there tree protection zones near the proposed routes or pole locations (particularly Easton Park's northern run)? Is an arborist required for works within TPZs?

15. Turf reinstatement

Please advise:

- Council's reinstatement specification (e.g. kikuyu roll-on turf)

- The required establishment / maintenance period and responsibility for watering

- Whether turf is required around the new poles and pits, or only along the trench lines

16. Inspection hold points

Spec 3.13 requires inspections before trenches are covered and before footings are poured. What notice does Council require for each?

17. Cranes for aiming and night-time survey

Please confirm:

- The cranes for luminaire aiming and the night-time survey (Spec 2.7) form part of the electrical works

- Any requirements for after-hours work during the night-time survey

Thanks for your assistance.

1. Please allow for all new conduits n main costing. A secondary option may be provided. 'Abandoning in place any conduits not reused, instead of excavating them' - acceptable

2. Confirmed, top of footing to be removed to a depth of 400mm with the void backfilled, topsoiled and turfed.

3. We have shown separate conduits for each cable run to each pole, so no shared conduits with different circuits.

4.Confirmed, site-won material be reused as backfill above the sand bed/surround as long as it achieves the required compaction during backfilling.

5. Underboring preferred where possible subject to site condition.

6.There are no irrigation plans, Council can mark all irrigation heads prior to works. Contractor is responsible for repairing any damage during excavation.

8. Yes

11. Confirmed.

12. Contractor to conduct their own investigations on site access route. 7am-5pm Monday to Friday, 8am-1pm on Saturdays. Sports events - this will be discussed when council receives the contractors proposed delivery program.

Hi Council ,

Could you please mark up drawing S04.50 to identify the permanent piles, pile caps and supporting beams included in the flood-mitigation contractor’s scope, particularly those supporting Pit A01-3 and the connecting culverts.

Please provide the required pile quantities, diameters, founding levels/socket requirements and structural connections, and confirm whether the developer’s piled arrangement is to be adopted or redesigned for standalone Stage 1 delivery.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi, please refer to tender addendum 2:

-	Tenderers shall allow for the construction of piles, pits, and associated structures based on the available geotechnical investigation and issued design documentation. publicQuestions.question:
Preliminaries clause 3.3 nominates KBR as the preferred subcontractor for Engineering Design.

We have approached KBR regarding completion of the detailed design and IFC documentation. KBR has advised that it has decided not to pursue this project.

Could Council please confirm whether it has a preferred alternative engineering consultant, or whether we may nominate a suitably qualified replacement in accordance with GC21 clause 29.3?
publicQuestions.answer: Council has no other preferred alternative engineering consultant; contractor can nominate any suitably qualified replacement.

publicQuestions.question: Could Council please arrange an additional site inspection for the Baxter Road and Botany Lane Flood Mitigation Project? Please advise whether a further inspection is available and how to register.
publicQuestions.answer:
At this stage, Council is unable to arrange an additional site inspection for the Baxter Road and Botany Lane Flood Mitigation Project.

Should multiple prospective tenderers express a need for a further site walk, Council may consider arranging an additional inspection. If this occurs, all registered tenderers will be notified accordingly.

In the meantime, tenderers are requested to refer to Addendum 2, which contains the relevant information, clarifications, and records from the site inspection that was previously held.

Council encourages all tenderers to submit a conforming tender based on the information provided in the Request for Tender documentation and subsequent addenda.

publicQuestions.question: Hi Council, could you please provide the required design loads for the four P1 piles supporting Pit A01-3, including compression, uplift, lateral loads and moments where applicable, so our piling specialist can assess a suitable arrangement? They have advised that 22 m deep CFA piles would require plant unsuitable for the available access and working space. Would Council consider a greater number of shorter piles, approximately 12 m deep, allowing the use of a rig under 30 tonnes, subject to geotechnical verification and an approved structural design?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has provided all available information for tender purposes and has been unable to obtain any further information. We note that the design of Pit A01-3 was originally completed by the developer. However, Council remains open to considering alternative piling arrangements that better suit site conditions and constructability requirements, subject to the necessary geotechnical assessment and structural design approval.

For the purposes of tendering, proponents are requested to:

1.	Submit a conforming tender price based on the current design documentation.

2.	Provide an alternative price based on the proposed methodology, including any alternative piling arrangement considered more suitable for the site constraints. Any alternative proposal will be subject to geotechnical verification and structural design approval.

Tenderers are advised that the detailed design of the pits, including boring and piling requirements, will be undertaken by the successful contractor during the Design Phase. The level of detail provided in support of any alternative methodology will assist Council in assessing submissions under the non-price weighted criteria.

publicQuestions.question: Hi Council, could you please provide a marked-up plan identifying the existing surface types within the proposed work areas at Baxter Road and Botany Lane, together with the required reinstatement profiles? Please confirm asphalt thickness and mix, pavement base/subbase materials and thicknesses, and concrete thickness, reinforcement and finish where applicable.
publicQuestions.answer:
Tenderers are to allow within their tendered price for reinstatement works to match existing surface types, profiles and finishes.

Tenderers shall refer to the attached Addendum 3 containing Public Domain Technical Specifications and Bayside Council Standard Details, including (but not limited to) PD.CE.13 and PD.CE.01, when pricing pavement, asphalt, concrete and other surface reinstatement works.

Tenderers are responsible for making suitable allowances based on the available information, site inspection observations, and the referenced specifications. Verification of existing conditions will be required during the Design Phase.

publicQuestions.question: Please confirm whether ARTC will levy any possession booking, access, attendance or rail-operator disruption charges for the Baxter Stage 1 crossing, provide available estimates, and confirm whether these costs are payable by the Principal or Contractor.
publicQuestions.answer:
To Council's understanding, ARTC's base fee is $25,000 + GST, which covers the Engineering and Safety reviews, as well as the TPW Project Manager time to coordinate the approvals and access requirements, possession bookings, etc. This fee is subject to additional costs for extended or multiple engineering reviews, design reviews, Works Licences, and extended periods of engagement, if required. The Contractor is to allow for these costs.

This fee does not cover the cost of a Protection Officer when required (when works are within the ARTC boundary or active tunnelling is occurring under the rail line during a possession). Please note that a Protection Officer is not required for works occurring outside the corridor, e.g. general site establishment works. The Protection Officer is to be directly engaged by the Contractor for these activities. A list of companies on the ARTC Safe Working Panel was issued within the original tender pack.

Tenderers are responsible for identifying and allowing for all construction, approval, rail access, safe-working, monitoring, and associated costs required to complete the works. Should a Tenderer identify any additional ARTC-related costs, they are to make their own enquiries and allow for such costs within their tendered price.

If there are fees associated with the Infrastructure Licence this will be covered by Council.

publicQuestions.question:
Could council please clarify the scope of utility relocations for the optional Baxter Road Stages 2 and 3.

The Scope Split Markup (Rev A, 18/09/2026) states that Stage 2 "includes relocation of sewer and Telstra pit" and Stage 3 "includes all utility relocation to complete Stage 3".

However, the KBR drawings show these works as by others as part of the future development works on 50-52 Baxter Road:

- SEC471-01-DW-0000-CV-PLN-1004: Telstra pit, TEL02/TEL03, SEW01–SEW03, WAT01/WAT02 and EL01 relocated by others

- SEC471-01-DW-0000-CV-LSX-1001: comms relocated by others, sewer removed by others

Please confirm whether the relocation of these services is included in the Contractor's scope for Stages 2 and 3 or is to be undertaken by the developer.
publicQuestions.answer:
The relocation of the services identified on the KBR drawings, including the Telstra pits, communications services, sewer, water and electrical assets, together with all associated make good and reinstatement works, is included within the Contractor's scope for the optional Baxter Road Stages 2 and 3.

For the avoidance of doubt, notwithstanding any references within the KBR drawings indicating that these works are "by others" or associated with future development works at 50-52 Baxter Road, Tenderers are to allow for all utility relocation works required to deliver Stages 2 and 3 within their tendered price. Any necessary coordination with utility providers and stakeholders forms part of the Contractor's scope.

title: TEN/3199 Alexandra Park Zoo Emu/Wallaby Enclosure Fence Replacement
description:
Project Overview

Alexandra Park Zoo requires the replacement of the existing perimeter fence surrounding the Emu and Wallaby enclosure. The existing fence is nearing the end of its service life and is to be replaced with a new fence that maintains animal containment, improves durability and continues to meet relevant animal welfare and biosecurity requirements. The enclosure perimeter is approximately 140 linear metres.

All works as per scope below will need to be completed by the 31/05/2027

Site Inspection

A site visit is recommended but not mandatory for prospective contractors to familiarize themselves with existing site conditions, access constraints, and the extent of the Works.

Council will host a non compulsory site inspection on Monday 30/11/2026 at 9.30 am for 1hr meet at the 29 Quay St, corner Quay and Burrum Streets, Bundaberg West QLD 4670. Attendance at the site inspection is optional.

Contractors wishing to attend the site inspection or request an alternative site visit must confirm their attendance via Vendor Panel. All site visit enquiries and arrangements shall be managed through Vendor Panel only. Please RSVP by 12.00pm on the 27th of November 2026 if you wish to attend. If you don’t RSVP, it will be taken that you will not be attending.

Please refer to to the documents attached.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Replacement of existing laboratory autoclaves at Pathology Queensland's Coronial and Public Health Sciences (CPHS) facility.

Supply, delivery, installation, commissioning and whole-of-life maintenance of three laboratory autoclaves.

Equipment must be suitable for operation within a specialist laboratory environment supporting public health, diagnostic, scientific and forensic services.

Compliance with applicable Australian Standards, safety requirements and Queensland Health operational requirements.

Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) and commissioning activities required.

Integration with existing building services and laboratory infrastructure.

Suppliers must demonstrate capability to deliver, install and commission the proposed equipment with minimal disruption to laboratory operations.

Long-term maintenance support, spare parts availability and lifecycle support capability are required.

Mandatory site inspection and briefing
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Reliable, fit-for-purpose laboratory autoclaves meeting all technical and operational requirements.

Short manufacturing lead times and high delivery certainty strongly preferred.

Demonstrated experience delivering and supporting comparable laboratory autoclave installations.

Robust project management, delivery and commissioning methodology.

Comprehensive operator and maintenance training.

Minimum manufacturer's warranty and ongoing technical support arrangements.

Australian-based preventative maintenance and breakdown support capability.

Long-term spare parts availability and lifecycle support commitment.

Competitive whole-of-life cost of ownership, including maintenance and support costs.

Suppliers demonstrating local industry participation, supply chain resilience and sustainable procurement outcomes will be viewed favourably.

title: Request for Expression of Interest - Digital Mailroom Solution
description: Ipswich City Council is seeking Expressions of Interest from suitably qualified suppliers on contemporary Digital Mailroom Solutions that can support the Council's mail handling, governance, continuous improvement and digital transformation objectives.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
1 Nicholas St

Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ipswich is centrally located in the booming south east Queensland region of Australia. To the east is the capital city Brisbane, and to the west are the rural and agricultural areas of the Brisbane, Lockyer and Fassifern Valleys. The city is ideally positioned on the national road network - 40 minutes drive from Brisbane, an hours drive from the Gold Coast and 60 minutes drive from domestic and international air and sea ports.
Ipswich comprises an area of 1090 square kms and has a population of 180,000 people. Ipswich enjoys a subtropical climate and is a safe, friendly and multicultural city. Residents come from 115 different ethnic backgrounds, speaking 84 languages.
As Queensland's oldest provincial city, Ipswich has a rich history. It is renowned for its architectural, natural and cultural heritage. Ipswich proudly preserves and still operates from many of its historical buildings and homes, with more than 6000 heritage-listed sites. Ipswich also has a range of charming townships within the western rural areas of the city, each with its own legitimate claims of historical significance.

buyerQuestions: Does your solution have the capability for data to be hosted onshore in Australia?

publicQuestions.question:
1. What are Council's estimated annual, monthly, or daily volumes for incoming physical correspondence (letters, envelopes, parcels, packages)?

2. What proportion of inbound mail arrives as standard flats/letters versus large envelopes, bound booklets, cheques, plans, forms, ID cards, USB drives, or physical items/parcels?

3. What is the estimated annual volume or percentage of outbound mail returned as RTS, and what specific action is required upon scanning (e.g., automated address flagging, task allocation, or basic archiving)?

4. What are Council’s requirements for physical document retention post-digitisation (e.g., standard 90-day quarantine prior to certified destruction, or permanent retention of original paper source records)?

5. Does Council anticipate redirecting physical mail via an Australia Post PO Box / DX service directly to an off-site outsourced scanning facility, or a hybrid/on-premise model where hardware/software is deployed within Council premises for local staff?

6. What are the expected service level agreements (SLAs) from mail delivery at the digitisation facility to availability within Council systems (e.g., same-day ingestion by 12:00 PM for mail received by 8:00 AM)?

7.How should non-scannable, original legal/notarised documents, tenders, cash/cheques, or sensitive/confidential executive mail be segregated and physically routed to Council?

8. What level of data capture is expected during scanning: basic metadata indexing (date, sender, doc type, recipient) or advanced line-of-business extraction (Rates Assessment No, Property ID, Application/DA No, CRN, invoice data)?

9. Is full-text searchable PDF (specifically PDF/A-1a or PDF/A-1b for long-term archiving) required for all ingested inbound documents?

10. Does Council seek machine-learning/rules-based document classification to automatically route correspondence to specific teams or individual officers, or will Council's Information Management Team manually triage digitised queues?

11. How does Council envisage digitised mail entering Objective ECM (e.g., via Objective Connect/API, automated folder drop/ingestion agent, or email ingest), and is there an existing mandatory metadata taxonomy?

12. For specific inbound types (e.g., invoices, customer applications, rate queries), does Council require automated direct-to-record creation or workflow triggers inside Oracle Fusion or other line-of-business systems?

13. Does Council have specific technical digitization standards for Queensland State Archives (QSA) compliance (e.g., minimum 300 DPI, full color vs. greyscale, image enhancement rules, and digital chain of custody certificates)?

14. How does Council require redaction or restricted access controls to be handled for sensitive incoming correspondence (e.g., legal notices, human resources, child safety, health, or code-of-conduct complaints)?

15. What specific reporting or digital chain-of-custody logging is required from envelope receipt/slitting through scanning, QA, transmission, and physical archiving/destruction?
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your questions, please see 260527-000421 - Addendum # 1 for Councils response.

publicQuestions.question:

3. Inbound volumes: What is the approximate annual volume of inbound mail items and pages, and how many sites or delivery points receive it?

publicQuestions.question:
Hello

I'd like to seek some clarification on this RFQ specifically in relation to the requirement for $10M in Professional Indemnity Insurance cover. This is well above industry standards for a tender of this type.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello,

- will there be an Arts and Culture lead or internal project team who will work with the successful consultant, and with what level of involvement in the design and development of the strategy? - The RFQ refers to strengthening grants, partnerships and investment approaches, as well as identifying resource implications and funding considerations in the implementation framework. Could you please indicate the level of financial analysis expected, from high-level funding estimates and indicative resource requirements, to detailed financial scenario modelling and funding projections?

Many thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
A1. - Please provide your price for the anticipated cost of delivering the services described in the Scope. Pricing should reflect the resources, methodology and effort required to undertake the services and should not be based solely on the available budget. Council's indicative budget for these services is up to $50,000 (excluding GST). The engagement of a Minor Consultancy Contract is not determined solely by the value of the engagement. Rather, it is based on the nature of the services being provided and whether the engagement meets the definition of a consultancy service under Council's procurement framework.

A2. Yes, there is an internal project lead and a direct point of contact to work with the successful consultant that will work closely in the design and development of the strategy. No specific preference in ways of working and the focus is primarily on scope, milestones and effort being delivered.

A3. Council will work with the consultant and provide relevant data based on needs of the project.

A4. Council has not prescribed a specific level of financial analysis. Respondents should use their expertise to determine the appropriate level of analysis required and demonstrate their capability to deliver the services. This may include consideration of funding opportunities, partnerships, resource implications and implementation requirements where relevant to the proposed approach.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.answer:

Respondents should outline their proposed approach to stakeholder and community engagement and demonstrate their capability to facilitate consultation activities, review feedback and incorporate outcomes into the final Strategy should these services be required.

A3. Respondents are expected to hold, or be able to obtain, the insurance coverage specified in the RFQ. Where a Respondent does not currently hold the required insurance, their submission should clearly demonstrate their ability and commitment to obtain the required coverage prior to contract commencement. Evidence may be requested by Council as part of the evaluation and contract award process.

Good Day,

publicQuestions.question:
Hello and greetings!

We would like to reconfirm if the single tender submission max. of 40 pages overall is explicitly required for the tender? Kindly advise further. Thank you!

Warm regards,
publicQuestions.answer: Council is happy to receive the document as a single PDF file.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello and greetings!

Given the need to compile appropriate attachments throughout our responses in the response schedule that may go beyond the maximum 40-page overall requirement of the tender submission, can we alternatively submit the tender with the separated supporting attachments (with appropriate naming convention for reference to the response schedule) compressed altogether as a zip file?

Is also the pricing schedule and program counted on the 40-page requirement of the tender submission, or can it be submitted as a separate document?

Kindly advise. Thank you!

Warm regards,
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

it can be submitted as a separate file.

Good afternoon,

Can you please provide some clarification as soon as possible prior to the tender site visit?

1)	The drawings require installers of post-installed fasteners to be AEFAC accredited. Will equivalent manufacturer training (e.g. Hilti) be accepted, or is AEFAC accreditation mandatory?

2)	Please confirm the required working hours. Volume_2_Project_Brief_Barrier_and_Balustrade.pdf states site access is 7:00am-5:00pm Monday-Friday (Page 5), however night works 9:00pm-4:00am are also specified (Pages 2).

3)	If a tenderer has not not delivered a road barrier project of this type (similar projects completed though), would this experience be considered acceptable for tender evaluation?

4)	If a tenderer does not currently hold formal CC2 certification, can compliance with CC2 requirements, not a formal certification, be accepted for tender submission?

5)	Would the Principal consider an extension of the tender closing date to allow tenderers sufficient time to develop a compliant submission?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Simon,

Answers to your questions below:

Q1) The drawings require installers of post-installed fasteners to be AEFAC accredited. Will equivalent manufacturer training (e.g. Hilti) be accepted, or is AEFAC accreditation mandatory?

A1.	Equivalent training and products are permitted.

2) Please confirm the required working hours. Volume_2_Project_Brief_Barrier_and_Balustrade.pdf states site access is 7:00am-5:00pm Monday-Friday (Page 5), however night works 9:00pm-4:00am are also specified (Pages 2).

A2. Nightworks are the correct working hours: 9pm-4am.

3) If a tenderer has not not delivered a road barrier project of this type (similar projects completed though), would this experience be considered acceptable for tender evaluation?

A3. 3.	Yes, similar experience will still be evaluated.

4) If a tenderer does not currently hold formal CC2 certification, can compliance with CC2 requirements, not a formal certification, be accepted for tender submission?

A4. Recommendation is that either the fabricator holds formal CC2 Certification or they provide a CC2 Compliance Certificate and engage their own third party certifier. For tender submission, proof of CC2 compliance without formal certification would be sufficient, provided there is demonstrated intent to achieve formal certification in the near future prior to tender acceptance.

5) Would the Principal consider an extension of the tender closing date to allow tenderers sufficient time to develop a compliant submission?

A5.	Yes, a 1 week extension has been applied

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Team,

We are currently reviewing the tender documentation for the McKinlay Shire Housing project and would appreciate clarification on the following items.

1. Lot 1 vs Lot 6

Attachment B1’s summary table and pricing workbook place the 3BR house on Lot 1 and the 2 x 2BR units on Lot 6, but the per-site sheets show the reverse. Which is correct, and which lots require Council’s Development Approval?

2. Lot areas and survey

Can Council provide lot areas, dimensions and any existing contour or identification surveys for all four lots?

3. Payment for off-site work

Will Council accept stage-based progress claims (Item 33(b)) aligned to the pricing workbook milestones, AND payment for unfixed plant and materials (Item 34) for modules completed in the factory?

4. DA and infrastructure timing

What timeframe does Council expect for the two Development Approvals, and when will the water and sewer expansion works serving the sites be complete?

5. Furnishings

The pricing workbook includes a ‘Furnishings’ line. Is any furniture or loose equipment in scope?

6. Site office

Can the Superintendent’s site office for 8 people be shared across the four sites (or provided in an existing Council building) given they are all in Julia Creek?

7. Missing documents

Please provide Council’s environmental policy and Code of Conduct referenced in Schedule 10 and Spec cl. 4.4, and confirm working hours referenced in Annexure A Item 26A.

Thanks,
publicQuestions.answer:
1. There is an error in the current Part B Attachment B1 re Lot 1 vs Lot 6. An amended Part B Attachment B1 will be provided via addendum shortly. Site 2 & Site 4 will require Council Planning Approval. This will be undertaken once the approved floor plans, elevations, sections, landscape plans and site plans are provided.

2. Council does not have contour or ident surveys of the lots. Part B Attachment B1 specifies the successful Tenderer is to undertake these.

3. Council's proposed payment arrangements are set out in Annexure Part A of the Conditions of Contract. Item 33(a) provides for monthly progress claims, while Item 34 specifies that no unfixed plant and materials are eligible for payment under Subclause 37.3. Tenderers may propose alternative payment arrangements, including stage-based progress claims aligned with the pricing workbook milestones and payments for completed off-site manufactured modules. Any such proposal must clearly identify the proposed payment milestones, supporting evidence of completed work and appropriate security arrangements. Council will consider any proposed departures as part of the tender evaluation process.

4. DA planning approval is expected to take 4 weeks from provision of all required documents. Council will complete infrastructure upgrades and expansion by 29th February 2027.

5. No loose furniture or equipment is to be supplied. Furnishings relates to blinds, etc

6. A suitable site office can be located on the Eastern end of Site 4.

7. These are public documents and can be found on Councils website at:

Code of Conduct: https://www.mckinlay.qld.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/1/about-council/documents/tenders-and-eois/policies/policies-2025/employee-code-of-conduct-september-2025.pdf

Environmental Policy: https://www.mckinlay.qld.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/2/about-council/documents/tenders-and-eois/policies/environmental-policy-version-50.pdf

Working hours for onsite work are:

6:30am to 5:30pm weekdays

8am to 4pm Saturdays

No work on Sundays or Public Holidays

title: 201253 RFT Prince Edward Park Pedestrian Bridge Design and Construct
description:
Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for the Prince Edward Park Woronora Pedestrian Bridge Renewal Project.

The project involves the demolition of the existing pedestrian bridge and the construction of a new bridge to provide a safe, compliant, and durable pedestrian and cyclist crossing over the Woronora River. The works also include the construction of new shared pedestrian and bicycle path connections associated with the bridge replacement.

The existing bridge, owned by Sutherland Shire Council, provides an important active transport link between Prince Edward Park and Prices Circuit, connecting the northern and southern banks of the Woronora River. Due to the structure's age and condition, the bridge exhibits several defects and no longer meets current design and compliance requirements, affecting its safety, serviceability, and long-term performance.

The Woronora River is an environmentally sensitive area, and the successful Contractor will be required to undertake the works in accordance with all relevant environmental approvals, statutory requirements, and project-specific environmental management measures.

Mandatory site briefing will be required. Meeting location is at Prince Edward Park Carpark off Prince Edward Park Rd Woronora NSW.

publicQuestions.question:
Further to the RFI answered on 21-Oct, we have this follow-up RFI related to a common flood design basis for tender.

SSC has confirmed an updated flood modelling is being prepared but not available to tenderers, and that the contractor is to determine design flow velocity. Flood velocity & flood level directly govern pier and foundation design, bridge soffit level and approach ramp lengths, and therefore the tender price.

Performance Spec. Table 4.1 dictates the soffit level to be the maximum of (a) 400mm above existing soffit level, (b) 300mm freeboard above the 1% AEP design flood level, or (c) minimum vertical clearance required by TfNSW Maritime.

The 1995 Floodplain Management Study indicates a 1% AEP level of RL 3.8 to 3.9m at the site. Section 10.3 requires flood assessment to include climate change which may increase this level by 0.5-1.0m. To comply with Table 4.1 & Section 10.3 (and subject to post-award flood modelling) the proposed bridge deck soffit level could be as high as RL 5.2m (possibly higher). The existing bridge deck soffit level is approx. 3.1m. Therefore, the proposed bridge soffit would be in the order of 2.1m higher than existing soffit leading to significant cost.

Without a common basis, the tender prices will not be comparable, and the risk of post-award changes will be priced differently by each tenderer.

We request that SSC further reviews these flood modelling concerns and provide direction to all tenderers on what to adopt for both (1) flow velocity, & (2) bridge deck soffit level.
publicQuestions.answer:
Following clarification with SSC's Stormwater Asset Team, a new flood study and hydraulic model for the Woronora River is currently being undertaken. However, Council has been advised that the updated flood modelling data will not be available until March 2027, which is beyond the timeframe required to support the current tender process.

Accordingly, tenderers should not rely on the climate change allowance referenced in Section 10.3 of the Flood Assessment, as updated modelling information is not yet available.

For tender purposes, the replacement pedestrian bridge shall be designed with a maximum soffit level increase of 700 mm above the existing bridge soffit level. Any further flood assessment, hydraulic analysis, or design verification required to support the detailed design will be the responsibility of the successful contractor as part of the Design and Construct process.

Could Council please confirm that the intended liability cap is the amount in Schedule 1, Item 13, and whether Council is willing to bring the clause 8.1 indemnities within that cap?

Council cannot legally assume responsibility for liability or indemnity which is the result of actions for which another party should be insured to cover their own acts or omissions.

title: Forward Notification of Upcoming North Coast Line North Culvert Replacement
description:
Forward Notification only - please await tender release on 13th January 2027 before initiating queries about the project.

The North Coast Line Culvert Renewal Project forms part of Queensland Rail's ongoing program to improve the safety, reliability and resilience of the North Coast Line (NCL). Maintaining the condition and performance of drainage infrastructure is essential to protecting the track formation, managing flood risks and ensuring the ongoing reliability of rail operations.

The project involves the replacement of six life-expired corrugated metal pipe (CMP) culverts and grout fill of two CMPs located between 1322.920 km and 1327.880 km on the North Coast Line, within the Nome to Stuart section south of Townsville. The existing culverts have been identified for renewal to address their deteriorating condition and maintain the long-term performance of the corridor's drainage infrastructure.

The proposed works involve the removal of the existing culverts and construction of new reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) culverts in accordance with Queensland Rail’s Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings. The scope includes associated excavation, foundation preparation, culvert installation, headwalls, wingwalls, scour protection, drainage improvements, formation reinstatement, access road reinstatement and protection or relocation of existing services, as required at each location.

title: Expression of Interest: Alternate Transport, NPA to Horn Island Airport
description:
Northern Peninsula Area Regional Council is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from operators to provide alternate transport between the Northern Peninsula Area (NPA) and Horn Island Airport while the NPA Airport (Bamaga) runway is rehabilitated.

Services required:

- A chartered ferry from Seisia wharf direct to Horn Island, based at Seisia for the full period of the airport closure.

- A chartered bus between Horn Island wharf and Horn Island Airport.

- Optional, priced separately: a community bus between a designated stop in each of Injinoo, Umagico, Bamaga, New Mapoon and Seisia and Seisia wharf.

Timing: service starts July 2027, for 4 months, with options to extend to 5 and 6 months. Timetable must allow passengers to check in for Horn Island to Cairns flights.

Location: Seisia (Northern Peninsula Area, Cape York) and Horn Island (Torres Strait). Services cannot be provided remotely.

You can offer all or part of the service, alone or as a consortium. Council is not bound at any stage of this process. The service will go ahead only if funding is secured.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
180 Adidi St
Bamaga, Queensland 4876
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: To be updated
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Wednesday 16 December 2026 10:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Background

The NPA Airport (Bamaga) runway will be rehabilitated from July 2027 and the airport will be closed for the construction period, expected to be about 4 months and possibly up to 6. During the closure, passengers from the five NPA communities (Injinoo, Umagico, Bamaga, New Mapoon and Seisia) will need another way to reach Horn Island Airport and connect to Cairns flights. Council is seeking funding support from the Queensland Government for the service.

This is Stage 1 of a two-stage process. Council will shortlist up to 3 respondents and invite them to tender at Stage 2. Council is not bound at any stage.

Compatibility requirements

- Vessel and crew accreditations and operating approvals that apply to the Seisia to Horn Island route, including those required by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), held or obtainable before July 2027.

- Passenger transport accreditation and driver authorisations for any bus service, held or obtainable before July 2027.

- Appropriate insurance.

- A vessel able to be based at Seisia wharf for the full closure period, and able to berth at Seisia wharf and Horn Island wharf.

- Ferry and bus timetable matched to the scheduled Horn Island to Cairns flights, with enough time for passengers to check in.

- Capacity to extend for a fifth and sixth month.

- Prices must be all-inclusive charter prices, including fuel and maintenance, in Australian dollars excluding GST.

All documents and the response schedules are attached. Lodge your response through this panel by 11:59 pm AEST on Wednesday 16 December 2026.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Desired outcomes and nice to haves

- A reliable service that keeps NPA communities connected to Horn Island Airport and Cairns flights for the full closure period.

- Timetable that gives passengers enough time to check in.

- On-board toilets and seating on the ferry.

- Luggage capacity suitable for air travellers.

- A back-up vessel, driver or vehicle arrangement.

- Clear refuelling and overnight mooring or anchorage arrangements at Seisia.

- Local employment and local subcontractors.

- Willingness to also deliver the optional community bus connection.

Conditions and warranties

- Council is not bound at any stage of this process. The EOI is not an offer, a tender or a contract.

- The service will go ahead only if funding is secured from the Queensland Government.

- Council will not pay for the cost of preparing a response.

- Prices are all-inclusive charter prices in Australian dollars excluding GST, including fuel and maintenance, fixed for the term.

- Respondents must hold, or be able to obtain before July 2027, the accreditations, approvals and insurance that apply.

- Respondents must confirm the information in their response is correct (Schedule A declaration).

Service levels (SLAs)

Service levels, including timetable reliability and passenger communication, will be set out in the tender documents issued to shortlisted respondents at Stage 2. Stage 2 will also address disability access, and security, including the movement of cash and the secure handling of daily mail in and out of the NPA.

Project benefits

- Keeps NPA communities connected to Cairns flights while the runway is rehabilitated.

- Allows the airport runway works to go ahead.

- Local employment and business opportunities for operators and suppliers in the NPA.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could you please clarify whether the following alternatives would be considered:

Granitic sand paths: Can the lawn areas along the sides of the houses be replaced with granitic sand paths? These areas appear to receive limited sunlight, which may affect turf establishment and long-term performance.

Instant turf: Can we price instant turf as an alternative to seeded lawn? With works scheduled for winter, instant turf may provide more reliable coverage and reduce mud during establishment.

Please confirm whether these alternatives can be included in our submission and should be priced separately from the specified works.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thanks for the queries and your interest in the project.

In regard to lawn areas to be replaced by granitic sand paths, council would prefer sticking to what mentioned on the plan for two reasons- 1. this is dictated by Planning Permit requirements and need approval from Planning team to change/amend/alter. 2. other tenderers will be quoting based on what is on the plan. So, the tender evaluation will not be consistent if different tenderers propose different options. During the time of construction, we might change to granitic surface after taking approval from Council's Planning team. For now, please base your quote on the plan provided.

We believe instant turf will be costlier than seeded lawn, but council has no issues with instant turf. We understand the benefits of instant turf over seeded lawn. It will be helpful for the council if the tenderers can mention on their submission which option they are proposing.

title: Learner Logbook Solution
description:
The core objectives of this procurement activity are to select and engage a suitably qualified supplier and offer to deliver a future Learner Logbook (LLB) solution. Delivering the future Learner Logbook solution provides an opportunity to improve the experience of Queensland learner drivers and driver instructors, which forms part of the Queensland Government's commitment to become Australia's most customer-focused government.

The new LLB solution will include a contemporary and accessible user experience on a secure, mobile device application on both Apple IOS and Android operating systems. The Department is seeking a solution that improves on the current in-use application experience for learner driver and supervisor users and department level 1 support admin users. The Department is seeking long-term value for money while delivering a modern, secure, positive and accessible user experience. Further details on what the Department is seeking are in the below in scope, and in the enclosed CDSB1 Requirements.

In Scope

The proposed procurement is intended to secure a modern, supportable, mobile-based digital application for learner drivers and supervisors and supporting admin staff portal for departmental use and reporting, including associated hosting, support, reporting, maintenance, and transition services.

Explicitly Within Scope:

•	Provision of a modern and accessible digital learner logbook application, including native mobile applications for iOS and Android

•	Provision of an Admin Portal used by Department admin users to provide level 1 customer support and perform operational duties.

•	Customisation and configuration to CDSB branding and aligning to Queensland laws, TMR graduated licensing requirements and policies

•	Hosting and operational support arrangements, including Australian-hosted data infrastructure.

•	Reporting and analytics capabilities

•	Transition-In services, including data migration from the legacy platform and comprehensive testing to ensure accurate data transfer.

•	Implementation services, testing, onboarding support and cutover activities

•	Transition-out services for end of contract

•	Maintenance, bug fixes, security maintenance. Ensure uptime and availability to users, including updates, patches and upgrades to operating system versions and Appstore availability

•	Ongoing support as level 2 point of escalation to resolve support queries from the CDSB level 1 team who deal directly with end users

Potential additional items for scope:

•	Integration and enhancement of features, including for example integration with Queensland Government agency systems for data verification and road safety learning methods. Potentially enhancements to be priced into the contract with a price list and initiated by CDSB when decision made to implement additional enhancements. However, this is a nice-to have and would not preclude a successful offer if not offered in initial offering and was offered as a pipeline activity in future years.

The QITC modules for products and services categories likely includes:

•	As a Service, for example Software As A Service (SaaS) or licensed software. Software Maintenance included, including remedial and preventative maintenance, patches, fixes and continual improvement;

•	Software Development Services for the Learner Logbook application which may include bespoke development, customisation or configuration or if additional customisation of an existing application is needed. Potentially there is a suitable learner logbook application in existence with customisation and configuration to meet the Customer’s requirements, or potentially a similar application that can be customised for the purpose of a Learner Logbook application, or a new build.

•	Managed Services (e.g. transition-in services, data migration, hosting, ongoing support with service levels, and transition-out services) system and security testing IE vulnerability testing, Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) testing, Penetration system. Support services at level 2 and above to assist CDSB admin users who are unable to resolve support issues at level 1.

•	ICT Professional Services module to be included but services to be completed under a SOW if /when required by the Customer, which may include enhancements, features, and other services required by the Department.

•	Integration Services for future integrations as required to be performed under a future statement of work (SoW).

Out of scope

•	End user (public consumer) consultation and change management.

•	Level 1 support directly with external users (e.g. learner drivers or supervisors)

•	Integrations with the TMR managed TRAILS.

The Department’s position is the Department will continue providing level 1 support direct to external users. External users contact the Department by calling, emailing, or attending a customer service centre to make support requests, that is, dealing with government staff initially. If CDSB cannot resolve the level 1 query, then the Department will escalate to the supplier, and the supplier will provide level 2 and above support.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
In 2016, the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) launched the Learner Logbook application to support learner drivers in recording the supervised driving hours required to obtain a driver licence. The application and its supporting systems were developed for TMR.

Since its launch, the learner logbook application has received only minor enhancements. The technology is now approximately 10 years old and largely digitises the processes of a paper logbook, limiting its ability to meet contemporary customer and business expectations. App-store feedback also identifies some user issues. There is an opportunity to provide an improved digital experience for learner drivers, supervisors and CDSB administrative users.

Following Machinery of Government changes in mid-2025, responsibility for the Learner Logbook solution transferred to the Department of Customer Services, Open Data and Small and Family Business (CDSB). This includes responsibility for the supporting systems and the ongoing management of the contract and support arrangements.

title: 16818 - Multiple Venues Point of Sale System
description:
Rockhampton Regional Council is seeking the supply, implementation and support of its Point of Sale (POS) solution.

The solution must suitable for venue-based retail, hospitality and event-related transactions. The solution is expected to support common operational requirements across Council venues while allowing for differences in local stock handling, reporting, user access and business processes. The solution must support day-to-day transactions, secure payment handling, stock management, end-of-day reconciliation, reporting, exchanges and administrative oversight.

The Supplier must provide all goods and services required to deliver a complete solution, including software licensing or subscription services, configuration, migration support where applicable, hardware and peripheral advice, integration requirements, testing, training, documentation, go-live support and ongoing helpdesk or support services.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning

Help Enterprises looks forward to the opportunity to tender for this service with QFP.

Our questions are as follows:

1. Can QFD provide historical catering volumes for the past three years, including breakfast, morning tea, lunch, afternoon tea, dinner, retail food sales, and barista coffee sales?

2. What commercial arrangement is QFD considering for the future service, for example a licence agreement, facility management model, commission arrangement, subsidy model, or a traditional catering services contract?

3. Will the future supplier have exclusive rights to provide catering, café, coffee, vending, and food retail services across the Whyte Island site?

4. Can QFD clarify which party will be responsible for utilities, waste disposal, pest control, cleaning, equipment servicing, preventative maintenance, and replacement of kitchen equipment listed in Appendix 1 including equipment responsibility;

 - What motored, portable, hand held and utensil equipment is available, or is Help expected to provide all of these?

 - Is there a list of Crockery and cutlery availability

5. Are there any planned capital upgrades or equipment replacements for the kitchens and dining facilities during the proposed contract period?

6. Can QFD provide indicative frequencies and notice periods for catering events, as referenced within the EOI?

7. What service level expectations apply to after-hours, weekend, public holiday, and emergency response catering requests, including minimum response times? E.g. Re Weekend schedule and requirements - Is there a specific example that can be provided that shows us how much notice is given and the highest demand: As a supported employment agency, we have specific requirements around staffing in weekend work and have to consider shifting to blended/open employment offerings if notice is too short.

8. Can QFD provide any guidance on the anticipated contract term and extension options that may be included in the Invitation to Offer (ITO) stage?

9. Will site inspections be made available to shortlisted suppliers prior to the Invitation to Offer stage to allow detailed assessment of facilities, logistics, and delivery points across the campus?

10. Will suppliers be required to maintain stock for walk-up purchases and retail sales, and can QFD provide historical sales data for sandwiches, wraps, snacks, beverages and coffee?

11. Are there any mandatory sustainability, social procurement, or local content requirements that suppliers should address as part of their submission?

12. If selected as the preferred supplier, would QFD consider allowing the successful contractor to utilise the existing kitchen and catering facilities for external commercial catering activities outside of QFD operations, provided such use does not impact QFD service delivery, security requirements, or site operational needs? If so, what conditions or restrictions would apply?

13. Would QFD support a catering model that incorporates meaningful employment opportunities for people with disability at the Whyte Island facility, and are there any site-specific requirements or considerations regarding accessibility, supervision, training, or workplace modifications that suppliers should be aware of?

14. Is Help expected to provide Consumables: e.g. foil, clingwrap, detergent, dishwasher chemicals.

15. Can you confirm that Help would be responsible for the following or is there a separate contractor;

- Cleaning & maintenance of fixed equipment, repairs/breakdowns.

- Grease trap pumping and hood & canopy service

- Rubbish removal

Thank you very much for your consideration. Helps team looks forward to your reply.

Matthew Berry

Commercial Development Manager
