publicQuestions.question:
Response format

1. Do the page limits in Section 3.0 apply only to the responses to Questions 1 to 5, excluding any cover page and the Section 4.0 respondent forms?

2. Should responses be lodged as one consolidated document or as a separate file for each question, and is a particular file format preferred?

3. May respondents attach supporting material outside the page limits, such as a capability summary or case studies, or will such material be disregarded?

Scope

4. Does the mandated service "production and despatch" refer to the production and delivery of advertising material to media owners, as distinct from creative production under GGS0120-25?

Process

5. Will responding to this RFI be a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent procurement process, and can DPC indicate the expected timing of that process?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1: Do the page limits in Section 3.0 apply only to the responses to Questions 1 to 5, excluding any cover page and the Section 4.0 respondent forms?

A1: The page limits apply to responses to questions 1 to 5 only and do not include the Section 4.0 respondent forms. A cover page is not required.

Q2: Should responses be lodged as one consolidated document or as a separate file for each question, and is a particular file format preferred?

A2: Responses should be submitted as one consolidated document in a format that is readily accessible and printable. Word or PDF format is preferred.

Q3: May respondents attach supporting material outside the page limits, such as a capability summary or case studies, or will such material be disregarded?

A3: Respondents should provide their responses within the page limits specified for each question. Supporting material outside those page limits is not requested.

Q4: Does the mandated service "production and despatch" refer to the production and delivery of advertising material to media owners, as distinct from creative production under GGS0120-25?

A4: For the purposes of this RFI, “production and despatch” refers to the production of non-campaign and recruitment material, as required, and the delivery of advertising material to media owners. It does not refer to creative production under GGS0120-25.

Q5: Will responding to this RFI be a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent procurement process, and can DPC indicate the expected timing of that process?

A5: Interested Respondents are referred to the RFI Terms and Conditions, specifically section 5, for information on how RFI submissions will be reviewed and considered, and on possible future procurement activities, which may involve open or limited processes. It is also possible that no procurement process will result from the RFI. For these reasons, no timeframe can be provided at this stage. DPC strongly encourages any entity interested in a possible future procurement activity to submit a response to the RFI.

publicQuestions.question: Could you please clarify the level of detail expected for Q2 regarding the proposed remuneration model?
publicQuestions.answer: Respondents should provide an appropriate level of detail to clearly explain how their proposed remuneration model would operate and support value for money, within the page limit specified in the RFI. Detailed pricing is not required at this stage.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there,

Do you have a list of all the properties & any figures regarding the amount of jobs etc that have been raised in the past in all areas?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has a vast portfolio of structures and buildings across our large municipality, with over 800 structures which includes up to 400 buildings.

The building portfolio is made up of the following:

•	Council staff occupied properties, such as admin centres, Corporate offices, library’s, Customer Service Centres, major sporting centres.

•	Council managed Commercial leased properties, such as Cafes, Restaurants or Caravan Parks.

•	Council managed Community leased properties, such as sporting buildings / stadiums or small local sporting clubs.

•	Council privately leased properties, such as private parkland or road reserve areas.

Regarding the number of jobs that we typically see at our properties, this is difficult to capture holistically, as this varies depending on age of the condition and age of the asset. External factors such as weather conditions and use also plays an important part in the call our rate of any one particular property.

Using an example from each of the above categories, please see below for insight into this query regarding FY:25/26:

•	Council staff occupied properties,

Bairnsdale library: Call outs: 14, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 4

273 Main St, Bairnsdale (Corporate Centre): Call outs: 9, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 6

BARC Sporting facility: Call outs: 12, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 8

•	Council managed Commercial leased properties;

Omeo Caravan Park; Call outs: 5, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 2

Eagle Point Cafe; Call outs: 4, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 2

•	Council managed Community leased properties;

Lindenow Kindergarten; Call outs: 3, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 1

Paynesville Medical Centre; Call outs: 2, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 1

•	Council privately leased properties;

Bairnsdale Property X: Call outs: 2, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 1

Lakes Entrance Property X: Call outs: 3, Planned routine maintenance tasks: 1

The provision of Plumbing Services to East Gippsland Shire Council will cover all buildings, but also many other assets such as parks and sporting fields which may have toilets and or water connections, but no buildings associated. Such as Bruthen Main St (Village Green), this asset may require attendance for toilet maintenance, tap repairs or vandalism rectifications.

Council will assess each request and reach out to a panel supplier for acceptance based on location, nature of the work and response time. The working relationship the Council has with the contractors is important to communicate and understand workload and capability given the specific circumstances.

title: Long-Term Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country
description:
Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country (Long-Term) - WS5659204351

The Coordinator of Energy has determined, under clause 3.11A.4 of the Electricity System Market (ESM) Rules, to trigger a Non-Co-optimised Essential System Services (NCESS) procurement process by Western Power for Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country.

The proposed services aim to address reliability and system strength concerns during planned or unplanned outage events affecting one or more 132 kV transmission lines supplying the North Country.

Call for NCESS Submissions

Western Power invites NCESS Submissions from prospective NCESS providers to deliver Reliability Services and/or System Strength Services located in the North Country. The North Country is defined as the area supplied by the Rangeway, Geraldton and Chapman substations.

This tender relates to the Long-Term contract term option (10-25 year terms). Proponents may offer a solution that fully or partially meets the requirements for either service (or both).

Activation requirements, performance measures, preferred connection locations and other technical requirements are set out in the Final NCESS Service Specification.

Queries may be submitted by email to emerging.technology.portfolio@westernpower.com.au or via the Q&A function in the VendorPanel portal.

Please submit NCESS Submissions via VendorPanel no later than 5:00pm (AWST) on 1 February 2027.

Interested NCESS providers should register with VendorPanel to be informed of whether any supporting documentation such as clarifications to questions may be published.

publicQuestions.question:
**Clarification request – minimum project experience requirements**

Please clarify the requirement for successful completion, as Principal Contractor, of at least three road pavement rehabilitation or reconstruction projects within the Northern Rivers region in the last five years, with a minimum contract value of $5 million:

1. Is this a mandatory pass/fail criterion, with non-compliance resulting in exclusion from further evaluation?

2. Does the $5 million minimum apply to each of the three projects, or to their combined contract value?

3. Must each reference project include in-situ stabilisation, sprayed sealing and associated drainage works?

4. Would Council accept equivalent experience demonstrated through multiple lower-value contracts of comparable scope and complexity undertaken outside the Northern Rivers region, supported by client references, project performance records, and evidence of resources and financial capacity?

If equivalent experience is not currently permitted, would Council consider amending the criterion through a formal addendum to allow otherwise suitably experienced and capable contractors to participate?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum 3.

publicQuestions.question:
We reference the updated Mandatory Participation Criteria communicated in Addendum 2 being “The Tenderer must demonstrate successful completion, as a Principal Contractor, of at least 3 road pavement rehabilitation or reconstruction projects in the last 5 years, involving in-situ pavement stabilisation, sprayed sealing and associated drainage works within the Northern Rivers region of NSW, with a minimum contract value of $5 million”.

We kindly request whether this is considered a strict mandatory criterion for involvement in the tender. Our organisation has substantial experience in the delivery of stabilisation projects as the Principal Contractor supported by specialist subcontractors throughout QLD. The precise wording for the above mandatory criteria indicates a precise level of expectation which we do not strictly meet. We would appreciate advice from Lismore City Council whether this will preclude our organisation from tendering this package of works if we cannot satisfy each of the key criteria outlined above.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum 3.

publicQuestions.answer: Refer to Addendum 4.

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning

Documents: RCS IFC 24050-1142 Issue 3 (DM01142 & DM01748), Sheet 1 typical section and Sheets 4–5; Scope of Works (Addendum 5) Tables 3, 4 and 6; Pricing Schedule Rev 2 Item 17.U (Additional Scope Item 23).

Issue: Drawing 24050-1142 notes "DM00666 – Ch. 16108.395 to Ch. 17170.420. See GHD DM00666 Cawongla Rd Design Report for retaining wall and road design details". Its retaining wall typical section is marked "Retaining wall design by others". DM00666 therefore overlaps the last 142 m of the tendered works, Ch 16.108–16.250 (Section 23, DM01748). That length is priced in Additional Scope Item 23 as 310 mm lightly bound base with a 14/7 double/double seal. The overlap also contains:

drain excavation at Ch 16.108 (right) and Ch 16.175–16.180 (left);

the signs at Ch 16.110 and Ch 16.140;

Drainage Line 6 (existing 375 mm culvert);

the Martin Road intersection tie-in.

The Scope of Works expressly excludes DM00787 as GHD works by others, but it doesn't mention DM00666. The GHD drawings and design report weren't issued with the tender.

 Questions:

Please confirm that the DM00666 retaining wall and GHD road works (Ch 16.108–17.170) are by others and not part of this Contract.

Between Ch 16.108 and Ch 16.250, should the Contractor:

(a) build the works as shown on 24050-1142 and priced in Additional Scope Item 23; or

(b) stop at Ch 16.108, reducing Item 17.U from 150 m to about 8 m?

If (a), will the DM00666 works be built before, during or after this Contract? Are there constraints near the wall, such as an exclusion zone, vibration or compaction limits, or limits on plant and stockpile loads? Will the GHD design be provided so we can match edges, drainage and levels?

If (b), please confirm the tie-in detail and levels at Ch 16.108, and that Item 17.U quantities will all be remeasure able accordingly.
publicQuestions.answer: Refer Addendum 6.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning, please find below RFI

3.	Scope cl 5.3(b) and Pricing Schedule items 9.4.1, 9.U.1, 15.4.1 and 15.U.1 require edge treatment “as detailed on the drawings… as per the details and tables on the drawings”. The IFC Pavement Transition and Edge Treatment Detail sheets for DM02152 (sheet 24) and DM01143 (sheet 17) show three edge treatment types. However, no tables, chainages or extents are provided to show which type applies where. a.	provide the edge treatment type and extent (chainage and side) for Sections 8 and 16;

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

Please see below RFI.

The Pricing Schedule (05._T26_11_Cawongla_Rock_Valley_Road_Schedule_of_Prices_Lump_Sum_Breakdown) includes Item 1.7 Project Management and Item 1.8 Site Facilities for the Lump Sum works. Additional Scope Items do not have equivalent items to allocate overheads and facilities in the same way as the Lump Sum works. The Tenderer requests confirmation on how overheads are to be managed for the additional scope items.

a)	Spread across direct items.

-	Overheads and facilities for the additional duration of Additional Scope Items are to be included in the Additional Scope Item rates, spread across the direct items in proportion to impact on contract duration.

b)	Priced with an extension of time.

-	Rates are to exclude overheads and facilities.

-	Add 3. Item 1 confirmed that the time for completion excludes Additional Scope. If Additional Scope Items are directed, the Time for Completion will be assessed, and overheads and facilities will valued under the Contract at the time.
publicQuestions.answer: Refer Addendum 6.

publicQuestions.question: Will clearing ang grubbing go ahead on all locations even if the additional scope areas do not proceed? publicQuestions.question:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for the opportunity to tender for this request. Please provide the following noting key interest is category 2.

1. Which roles are in Category 2? Can Council supply a Job Dictionary for one of them?

2. Roughly how many assessments a year?

3. Should our results be recorded on the Suitable Duty Register, or in a separate report that maps to it?

4. Can a psychologist sign the register, given it asks for a "Doctor / Specialist"?

5. Is telehealth acceptable for any or all of the assessment?

6. Is Council looking for reports in prose and are there any pre-determine templates (acknowledging risk ratings matrix)?

Thank you for your consideration

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Respondents,

Please find response belowL

1. Which roles are in Category 2? Can Council supply a Job Dictionary for one of them?

Council is seeking information from the market proposing possible approaches to fitness for work assessments for roles. Vendors are encouraged to provide proposals that detail an approach for how Council could conduct suitable assessments for roles at different levels of the organisation. Council has not yet determined the ongoing requirement for this category, seeking to understand how the market foresees that such an undertaking could occur for a workforce of its diverse nature and varying levels of risk.

2. Roughly how many assessments a year?

Council engaged approximately 600 new starter employees in the past 12 months.

3. Should our results be recorded on the Suitable Duty Register, or in a separate report that maps to it?

The Suitable Duty Register is utilised in our Workers Compensation Return to Work program – it is not relevant to this engagement, albeit that it is included in the Job Dictionary template. The results of your assessments should be provided on your own report template, covering suitability for relevant aspects of the role.

4. Can a psychologist sign the register, given it asks for a "Doctor / Specialist"?

Yes, a suitably qualified psychologist could provide the report on the provider’s template as per the clarification in question 3 above.

5. Is telehealth acceptable for any or all of the assessment?

Providers are encouraged to outline their assessment methodology and suitable methods of interaction with our people based on ensuring that a reliable and replicable methodology can be utilised to ensure consistency in decision making.

6. Is Council looking for reports in prose and are there any pre-determine templates (acknowledging risk ratings matrix)?

Council is seeking a standardised template/s to be provided by the Provider, ensuring that there is a consistent application of Council’s risk matrix and that recommendations are made in light of Council’s terminology to assist review and decision-making. Council reserves the right to seek further clarification or additional information from the provider on individual assessments where required.

Thank you

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon Yanine

Thank you for providing the information regarding the tender.

We are considering submitting a response for Category 1, Pre-employment Medical Assessments. Before progressing, we were hoping to better understand the Council’s requirements around lung function testing/spirometry.

In particular, could you please provide some further context regarding:

the rationale for including lung function testing within the current pre-employment assessment, if it is in fact included;

which roles or worker groups currently require this testing;

any identified workplace exposures that have led to this requirement, for example dusts, silica, fumes, chemicals or other respiratory irritants;

whether the testing is intended to establish a pre-employment baseline, form part of statutory health monitoring, or assess fitness for a specific role; and

what lung function information or reporting the Council currently receives from its provider, including whether there is a particular testing protocol or reporting standard required.

Understanding the underlying occupational risk and the Council’s intended use of the results will help us determine the most appropriate testing methodology and ensure our proposed service is fit for purpose.

Thank you in advance
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Respondents,

Please find responses below:

•	the rationale for including lung function testing within the current pre-employment assessment, if it is in fact included;

Lung function testing is required only for identified roles. The Safety Work NSW Codes of Practice for How to manage and control asbestos in the workplace and Managing the risks of silica from engineered stone in the workplace outline Council’s obligations in providing regular testing to workers who are likely to be exposed to airborne contaminants such as asbestos and crystalline silica. Spirometry (lung function) testing is organised every two years for employees who may be exposed to airborne contaminants.

•	which roles or worker groups currently require this testing;

Roles that have been identified for this program as part of the existing employee establishment include; Art teachers working specifically with ceramics, Qualified Trade staff, Civil Works road crews.

•	any identified workplace exposures that have led to this requirement, for example dusts, silica, fumes, chemicals or other respiratory irritants;

title: Aquatic & Recreation Management System
description:
Bayside Council is seeking submissions from qualified and experienced respondents for the procurement of a cloud-based Aquatic and Recreation Management System, including implementation, configuration, data migration, integration, raining, ongoing support and maintenance services.

The proposed solution must support customer managements, memberships, self-service portal, bookings, programs, point-of-sale transactions, payments, communications, reporting and related aquatic and recreation operations across Council facilities.

The solution will be implemented in phases, initially supporting Council’s existing aquatic and recreation services, followed by the new Botany Aquatic Centre, which is expected to open in November 2027. Further details of the implementation scope and requirements are provided in Volume 3.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Must Have requirements: Where a Must Have requirement will be fully delivered and available before go-live of the relevant phase, but is not in the current production release at the time of tender, should the Tenderer mark it as compliant with a delivery date, or disclose it as a non-compliance under the Mandatory Participation Criteria?

2. Phase 1 timing: Can Council confirm the target go-live date for each Phase 1 site (Angelo Anestis Aquatic Centre, Botany Golf Course and Arncliffe Youth Centre)?

3. Access control hardware: Can Council advise the make and model of the existing turnstiles, gates and card readers at each site, and whether Council intends to reuse them or expects the Tenderer to supply replacement hardware?

4. Point of sale and payments: Can Council advise the number of point-of-sale terminals at each site, the existing card terminals and merchant or payment provider, and whether Council intends to retain them?

5. Direct debit: Which direct debit provider does Council currently use for memberships, and does Council intend to retain it?

6. TechnologyOne integration: Which TechnologyOne product and version does Council use (for example, Ci Anywhere / SaaS), and what is the preferred integration method (API or file-based) for revenue and general ledger postings?

7. Data migration: Can Council advise the current system or systems in use, and approximate record volumes for customers and members, Learn to Swim participants and remaining visit passes?

8. Contract term: What is the intended contract term, including any extension options, for calculating total cost of ownership in Schedule C2?

9. Users: How many staff users (including casual and front-desk staff) and concurrent users are expected across all sites?

10. Hosting: Does Council require all data, including backups, to be hosted in Australia?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions, please note the following responses:

1. Must Have requirements: Where a Must Have requirement will be fully delivered and available before go-live of the relevant phase, but is not in the current production release at the time of tender, should the Tenderer mark it as compliant with a delivery date, or disclose it as a non-compliance under the Mandatory Participation Criteria?

Response:

Tenderer can mark it as compliant but must state when the functionality will be available.

2. Phase 1 timing: Can Council confirm the target go-live date for each Phase 1 site (Angelo Anestis Aquatic Centre, Botany Golf Course and Arncliffe Youth Centre)?

Response:

Target go-live is 31 May 2027

3. Access control hardware: Can Council advise the make and model of the existing turnstiles, gates and card readers at each site, and whether Council intends to reuse them or expects the Tenderer to supply replacement hardware?

Response:

Unknown

4. Point of sale and payments: Can Council advise the number of point-of-sale terminals at each site, the existing card terminals and merchant or payment provider, and whether Council intends to retain them?

Response:

Approximately 10 in total which needs to be retained if possible.

5. Direct debit: Which direct debit provider does Council currently use for memberships, and does Council intend to retain it?

Response:

Debit Success

6. TechnologyOne integration: Which TechnologyOne product and version does Council use (for example, Ci Anywhere / SaaS), and what is the preferred integration method (API or file-based) for revenue and general ledger postings?

Response:

Ci Anywhere 2026B, preferred integration method is API.

7. Data migration: Can Council advise the current system or systems in use, and approximate record volumes for customers and members, Learn to Swim participants and remaining visit passes?

Response:

2000 Learn to Swim participants, 1700 members, remaining visit passes depends by the time we do data migration.

8. Contract term: What is the intended contract term, including any extension options, for calculating total cost of ownership in Schedule C2?

Response:

This is outlined in Volume 2

9. Users: How many staff users (including casual and front-desk staff) and concurrent users are expected across all sites?

Response:

Approximately 50

10. Hosting: Does Council require all data, including backups, to be hosted in Australia?

Response:

No but preferrable

The “Reference” column on the Non Functional Requirements sheet is empty and isn’t explained in the cover sheet. Could Council say what it’s for, and whether tenderers need to fill it in?

Could Council give an overview of the inventory at each site, including the item types, roughly how many products/SKUs, and which items are for hire rather than sale?

How is inventory managed today (Links Modular, TechnologyOne, spreadsheets or another system)? Do existing inventory records need to be migrated to the new system?

We appreciate your time and assistance and look forward to submitting our proposal.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions, please note the following responses:

1. The “Reference” column on the Non Functional Requirements sheet is empty and isn’t explained in the cover sheet. Could Council say what it’s for, and whether tenderers need to fill it in?

Response:

Please ignore this column

2. Could Council give an overview of the inventory at each site, including the item types, roughly how many products/SKUs, and which items are for hire rather than sale?

Response:

Approximately 500 retail SKUs are managed across food, beverages, swimming, golf, gym and sporting equipment, with selected equipment such as golf clubs also available for hire.

3. How is inventory managed today (Links Modular, TechnologyOne, spreadsheets or another system)? Do existing inventory records need to be migrated to the new system?

Response:

Managed in Links Modular and spreadsheets

title: Construction of Croudace Street (West) Kerb and Gutter Upgrade
description:
Walcha Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake road and drainage improvement works along Croudace Street (West), Walcha NSW.

The proposed works involve upgrading and formalising roadside drainage, pavement infrastructure and driveway connections, while minimising disruption to adjoining residents and the surrounding road network.

The successful contractor will be required to complete the works in accordance with the specifications, drawings and requirements detailed in the attached Request for Tender (RFT) documentation.

Further information regarding the scope of works, submission requirements and anticipated timeframes is provided in the attached RFT documentation.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
2w Hamilton St
Walcha, New South Wales 2354
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The natural beauty of the Shire is quite breathtaking. The Shire is home to the magnificent Macleay Gorges and boasts some 205,000 hectares of dedicated national park, wilderness and state forest. Parts of our Werrikimbe National Park are World Heritage listed.

The Shire is also a well known trout fishing mecca, boasting some 1,500 km of trout streams which are a home to Rainbow and Brown trout. The township of Walcha is 1,067 metres above sea level, with one of the highest point in the district being at "The Flags" (42 kilometres south of Walcha) which is 1,400 metres above sea level. The highest point is in the Riamukka area, 38 kilometres south of Walcha, where the Grundy Trig Station and the Grundy Fire Tower are situated which is recorded as 1,463 metres. The Shire covers an area of 640,028 hectares (2,475 square miles/6,400 square kilometres). The population of the Shire is approximately 3,224 (Census 2016) which includes approximately 1,700 in the Town of Walcha.

- Deliver a quality finished product that meets Council's requirements and provides long-term improvements to the road infrastructure.

Contractor performance will be monitored by Council's nominated representative against the agreed scope of works, project milestones, quality requirements and contractual obligations.

title: Remove and Replace Roof Structures, Opal Street WTP Filters
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council operates the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant (WTP) located in Emerald, Queensland. The WTP incorporates four rapid gravity sand filters which form a critical component of the potable water treatment process.

Each filter is currently protected by an individual structural steel roof structure. Over time, these roof structures have deteriorated and are approaching the end of their serviceable life. In addition to their deteriorated condition, the existing roof structures do not adequately facilitate the operational requirements associated with periodic filter media replacement.

During future filter media replacement campaigns, one-tonne bulk sandbags are required to be lowered into the filter compartments via crane. The existing roof structures do not provide suitable openings through which these bags can be safely lowered into the filters. This creates operational difficulties and increases risk during maintenance activities.

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking responses from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures over the four rapid gravity filters.

The replacement roof structures must incorporate suitable access openings that facilitate the future lowering of one-tonne bulk bags of filter media into each filter compartment by others under a separate contract.

The Works are to be delivered under a Design and Construct Contract.

The Contractor must provide all labour, design services, engineering services, supervision, plant, equipment, materials, transport, certifications and incidentals required to complete the Works.

The Works include, but are not limited to:

• Site inspection and verification of existing conditions.

• Detailed design of replacement roof structures for four rapid gravity sand filters.

• Structural design certification by a Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ).

• Preparation and submission of design documentation and drawings.

• Attendance at, facilitation of and incorporation of feedback from an 80% design review workshop with Central Highlands Regional Council Water Utilities personnel. The Contractor must present theproposed design, demonstrate how operational requirements have been addressed, and provide draft design documentation for review prior to finalisation of the design.

• Removal and lawful disposal of existing roof structures. This includes the temporary covering of the sand filter opening to avoid any contaminants entering the filter media.

• Supply and installation of new roof structures.

• Provision of access openings to facilitate future filter media replacement activities.

• Supply and installation of all structural steelwork, roofing, flashings, lighting, stormwater runoff piping to prevent filter contamination, fixings and protective coatings.

• Final inspection and commissioning.

• Provision of as-constructed drawings and documentation.

• Handover of the completed Works.

The Contractor must be responsible for delivering a complete and fit-for-purpose solution.

Prior to commencing work on site, the Contractor must prepare, submit, revise and implement project-specific management plans suitable for the Works, including safety/WHS, environmental, quality, demolition, construction methodology/site management and traffic/pedestrian/access management plans, as applicable.

The replacement of filter media is specifically excluded from this Contract and will be undertaken by others under a separate contract.

Where the Opal St WTP Filter Media Replacement technical specification prepared by AECOM is provided with this RFT, only Sections 3.0 Materials and Construction, 4.0 Design and Documentation and 5.0 Roof Structure Removal and Reinstatement apply to this Contract, and only to the extent relevant to the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures. All other sections of that document are provided for information only unless expressly referenced in this Specification. In the event of inconsistency, this Specification takes precedence.

The Contractor must supply all labour, supervision, engineering services, design services, plant, equipment, materials, transport, temporary works and incidentals necessary to complete the Works.

The Works must be undertaken at the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant, Opal Street, Emerald, Queensland.

The Contract will commence within 7 days after the Award Letter and Contractual Arrangement are provided to and signed by the successful Contractor. Central Highlands Regional Council anticipates the contract end date to be as per the approved contract schedule.

Can you clearly define the Battery limits on the Existing concrete structure.

Further to this The AECOM specification is relevant here because it actually contains a dedicated “Concrete Rehabilitation” section, covering concrete breakout/removal, exposed reinforcement treatment, substrate preparation, repair materials, reinstatement, finishing, curing, inspection and testing. So I need to understand a clear battery limit.

The design requirements also explicitly say the new roof design must “include lighting and rainwater disposal.”

Can you please provide the Design or Design intent for both of these items. Where is the power coming from? Has the engineering been completed? What lights do you require and where? How many of them? Can you confirm the expected shutdown/staging arrangement? Can only one complete filter pair/two cells be taken offline at a time, and must each filter be completely returned to service before the next roof is removed?

What is the maximum allowable outage for each filter? Is there a preferred low-demand period or particular months when Council wants construction undertaken?

Are there existing structural drawings for all four filter concrete structures? We understand the filters were built at different times and may not be identical.

Does Council have a preferred new roof arrangement? Skillion, gable, similar to existing, or is the geometry entirely contractor-designed?

What corrosion protection system does Council expect for the structural steel? Is hot-dip galvanising acceptable/preferred, or is a duplex/coating system required? The new design has a minimum 25-year service-life requirement.

Please clarify exactly how Council expects the two access openings per filter to operate. Must operators be able to physically open them without mechanical lifting equipment, or is crane removal of a roof cassette acceptable?

Is the specified minimum 2 m × 2 m clear opening required for each individual filter cell without exception?

How does Council envisage the one-tonne bulk bags being lowered through the roof? What crane/telehandler will normally be used, and from which side of each filter?

If removable roof sections are acceptable, does Council require permanent certified lifting points and a documented lifting procedure?

What permanent working-at-heights system is expected? Static line, fall-arrest anchors, ladder attachment points, roof access walkway, or simply engineered attachment provisions?

What temporary protection is required over the open filters during demolition and construction? Does Council require a rigid engineered cover, sealed membrane system, or another defined standard?

Can a reusable temporary filter cover be moved progressively from Filter 1 to Filter 4, or does Council require multiple covers to be available simultaneously?

Are there contamination-control requirements beyond physically covering the filter? For example restrictions on grinding, hot work, galvanised material handling, drilling, dust generation or chemicals near an operating filter.

Can we perform hot works above/adjacent to the filters once an approved temporary cover is fitted? Or does Council expect essentially all cutting/welding to be completed off site?

Where can cranes be positioned for each of the four filters? We need to establish available radius and likely crane capacity.

Are there known underground services beneath the proposed crane/outrigger locations? Can Council supply service plans?

Does Council have information on pavement/ground bearing capacity for crane outriggers? If not, what verification will be required?

Who performs plant isolations — Council operators or AMM? What notice period is required?

Is condensation underneath the roof currently an issue? Does Council expect insulation or anti-condensation roof backing?

If the insurer cannot issue the final certificate in time, will Council accept a broker's cover note or binder at lodgement, with the certificate to follow before the first Purchase Order?

2. Joint names wording (Deed Sch 1 Item 9, cl 11.3). Many liability insurers will not add a principal as a joint named insured, but will note the principal's interest and provide a principal's indemnity extension with cross liability and waiver of subrogation. Would Council accept "Kempsey Shire Council noted as an interested party, with principal's indemnity, cross liability and waiver of subrogation" as meeting Item 9?

3. Products liability. For a services-only contract, is a combined public and products liability policy with a $20m limit for each of public liability and products liability acceptable? Is products liability required on an "any one occurrence" basis or an annual aggregate basis?

4. Workers compensation (Deed Sch 1 Item 9). Item 9 says "Workers' Compensation or Personal Accident & Illness". Will Council accept personal accident and illness cover for subcontractors who are sole traders without employees?

5. Motor vehicle and works insurance (RFT 3.3). Please confirm that comprehensive motor vehicle cover is "as applicable" and that works insurance (120% replacement cost) applies only if a specific Purchase Order requires it.

6. Professional indemnity. Deed Sch 1 Item 9 says PI is not required, but the Response section 11 table has a PI row and PO T&C 10.a.iii mentions $1m PI for professional services. Please confirm we can answer "Not required".

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

7. Critical Defect response (Deed cl 14.2(a), definitions in cl 1.1). Clause 14.2(a) requires a Critical Defect to be rectified within 2 hours of notification. For a scheduled footpath cleaning service, could Council please give an example of what it would treat as a Critical Defect? Would Council accept a tenderer based outside the Shire (about 450 km away) proposing either (a) a local subcontract crew, approved under cl 12.2, to attend and make safe within 2 hours, or (b) a different response window for full rectification, for example make-safe or acknowledgement within 2 hours and rectification by the next night? If so, should this be shown as a departure in the Response section 3 table?

8. Subcontractor approval (Deed cl 12.2, 11.1(b); Response 5.1.4). Does naming a subcontractor in Response 5.1.4 count as a request for Council's approval under cl 12.2, with approval given at award? If not, what information does Council need (insurances, SWMS, licences), and how long does approval usually take? Can further subcontractors be approved during the Term?

9. Local subcontractor for routine cleaning (Deed cl 12.2, 12.3). Will Council approve routine cleaning being delivered by a named local (Kempsey/Port Macquarie) subcontractor, with the head contractor managing, supervising and auditing the work and remaining liable for it? What information does Council need to approve a subcontractor?

Pricing basis and documents

10. Contract Sum (Response 9.1; Schedule of Rates). Should the lump sum Contract Sum be the estimated annual price (the total of the breakdown table for one year) or the total for the whole initial 36-month term? Are prices held fixed for the whole term, including option years, or is any annual adjustment available (Deed Sch 1 Item 6)?

11. GST basis (RFT 4.21 vs Response section 9 and Deed cl 19). RFT 4.21 says all prices must include GST, but the Response section 9 pricing tables and Deed cl 19 ask for prices exclusive of GST. Which basis should be used? Should every rate in the pricing schedule be entered GST-inclusive, or exclusive of GST with GST shown separately?

12. Central Kempsey group area (RFT 3.2 Service Schedule; Response section 9 breakdown row 7). The Specification lists "All footpaths & bin enclosures" on Belgrave St (Kempsey Traffic Bridge to Stuart St), John St (Belgrave to Verge), Forth St (Clyde St to York Lane), Smith St (Forth to Stuart) and the Riverside Park footpath (Forth to John) as approximately 8,750 mÂ², cleaned once a year before Christmas. The Response pricing table shows this row's area as "Refer specification". Could Council please confirm that 8,750 mÂ² is the total area to be priced for the whole group, and whether it covers both sides of each street? It is about 19% of the annual area, so it materially affects the price.

13. Missing attachments (Response section 9 and 8.1). Response section 9 asks for the Pricing Schedule "in Microsoft Excel format", and section 8.1 refers to a Modern Slavery Supplier Questionnaire. Neither is among the four documents we have (RFT, Draft Deed of Standing Offer, PO Terms and Conditions, and the Response document). Could Council please publish them, or confirm whether completing the tables in the Response document is enough?

Environment and site

14. Wastewater disposal (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 10.2(b), 7.2). Does Council have a preferred or approved discharge point for recovered wash water, such as a Council sewer access point or treatment plant under a trade waste approval, or must all recovered water go to a licensed liquid-waste facility? In particular, may captured wash water be discharged to Council sewer under a liquid trade waste approval (s68, Local Government Act 1993), or must it all be removed off-site to a licensed facility? If an s68 approval is needed, who issues it in Kempsey Shire, and are there fees?

15. After-hours contact (Deed cl 12.8). Is the after-hours contact only for notifications during and around programmed overnight shifts, or does Council expect an on-call attendance capability outside programmed works?

16. Water supply. May the contractor draw water from Council hydrants or standpipes in Kempsey, South West Rocks and Crescent Head? If so, what permit, metering and charges apply? Is water available at the Horseshoe Bay picnic shelter?

17. Hours and noise (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 10.1(c), 10.3). Are there set start and finish times or noise limits for overnight work near residences in any of the locations? Are there any locations where Council prefers early-morning rather than late-night work?

18. Vehicle parking at night. Can work vehicles and the recovery unit park on the kerb or in loading zones next to the work area overnight? Is a permit required?

19. Surfaces and sealants (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 8.4). Can Council tell us the main surface types at each location (e.g. sealed pavers, exposed aggregate, plain concrete, timber at the picnic shelter) and any sealants under warranty or with manufacturer cleaning limits?

20. Scope inclusions. Does the scope include chewing gum removal and oil or stain treatment, or only general high-pressure cleaning? Does "bin enclosures" include cleaning the bins themselves?

Evaluation, lodgement and administration

21. Evaluation weightings (RFT 2.5). The evaluation table lists (a) Price, (c) Criterion 2 Capability, (e) Criterion 4 Methodology and (f) Criterion 5 WHS, with no weightings. Items (b) and (d) and Criteria 1 and 3 are missing. Could Council please confirm the full list of criteria and their weightings? Are Sustainability (Response section 8) and Financial Viability (section 10) scored?

22. Portal and closing time (RFT cover, 4.3, 4.6; Response cover table). Please confirm that questions should go through the VendorPanel forum (RFT 4.3 refers to the "eProcure portal"). The Response cover states "2:00pm â€“ AEST on 05/11/2026", but NSW is on daylight saving time (AEDT) on that date. Is the deadline 2:00 pm Sydney local time?

23. Partial or unbundled offers (RFT 4.8, 4.23). May a tenderer price only some locations, or must every location in the breakdown table be priced? If Council awards locations separately, will the rates per service stand on their own?

24. First services. With commencement on 1 Dec 2026, does Council expect the annual pre-Christmas services, the first monthly Smith St clean and the December quarterly Horseshoe Bay clean to be completed in December 2026?

25. Payment documents (Deed cl 15.8, Sch 2). Please confirm that a statutory declaration and Subcontractor's Statement are needed with each weekly payment claim, or whether one per Completed Purchase Order is enough.

26. Local preference. Does using a local subcontractor for most of the work count toward any local-preference consideration in the evaluation?

Thank you for your help.

(edited on 20/Nov/2026 09:49 AM)

Hi There,

Please see below answers to your questions. Please note that some Questions are still currently under review and will be responded to once an answer has been decided on.

Insurance (mandatory criterion, RFT 2.4)

1. Timing of evidence (RFT 2.4, 3.3; Response section 11; Deed cl 11.1-11.2). Will Council accept a public and products liability policy that is bound and current before the closing time, evidenced by a certificate of currency dated before closing? If the insurer cannot issue the final certificate in time, will Council accept a broker's cover note or binder at lodgement, with the certificate to follow before the first Purchase Order?

-	Tenderers should provide current evidence of the required insurance cover with their submission. Where a final CoC is not available by the tender closing time, Council may accept appropriate evidence from the insurer or authorised insurance broker confirming that the required cover is current. The successful tenderer will be required to provide satisfactory CoC for all required insurances prior to contract commencement an/or issue of any PO.

2. Joint names wording (Deed Sch 1 Item 9, cl 11.3). Many liability insurers will not add a principal as a joint named insured, but will note the principal's interest and provide a principal's indemnity extension with cross liability and waiver of subrogation. Would Council accept "Kempsey Shire Council noted as an interested party, with principal's indemnity, cross liability and waiver of subrogation" as meeting Item 9?

-	Council acknowledges that insurers may use different policy structures and endorsements. Council will consider equivalent insurance arrangements where the tenderer can demonstrate that the proposed cover provides protection consistent with the requirements of the Deed. Any proposed alternative to the insurance requirements should be clearly identified in the tenderer's submission as a departure, together with supporting details of the proposed cover, for Council's assessment.

3. Products liability. For a services-only contract, is a combined public and products liability policy with a $20m limit for each of public liability and products liability acceptable? Is products liability required on an "any one occurrence" basis or an annual aggregate basis?

-	A combined Public and Products Liability policy may be acceptable provided the policy satisfies the minimum coverage and limit requirements specified in the tender and contract documents.

Tenderers should provide details of the basis and limits of their proposed cover with their submission. Any variation from the stated insurance requirements should be identified as a departure for Council's consideration.

4. Workers compensation (Deed Sch 1 Item 9). Item 9 says "Workers' Compensation or Personal Accident & Illness". Will Council accept personal accident and illness cover for subcontractors who are sole traders without employees?

-	Tenderers and subcontractors are required to maintain the insurances applicable to their business and employment arrangements. Where a subcontractor is a sole trader without employees and Workers' Compensation insurance is not applicable, appropriate Personal Accident and Illness cover may be provided in accordance with the requirements of the Deed.

Evidence of the applicable insurance arrangements may be requested by Council prior to approval of the subcontractor.

5. Motor vehicle and works insurance (RFT 3.3). Please confirm that comprehensive motor vehicle cover is "as applicable" and that works insurance (120% replacement cost) applies only if a specific Purchase Order requires it.

-	Comprehensive Motor Vehicle insurance is required where vehicles are used in connection with the Services.

The requirement for Works Insurance will apply where relevant to the nature of the works being undertaken and in accordance with the requirements of the Deed and applicable Purchase Order. Tenderers should identify any proposed departure from the stated insurance requirements in their submission.

6. Professional indemnity. Deed Sch 1 Item 9 says PI is not required, but the Response section 11 table has a PI row and PO T&C 10.a.iii mentions $1m PI for professional services. Please confirm we can answer "Not required".

-	Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for the Services under this tender. Tenderers may therefore mark Professional Indemnity as “Not Applicable” in the relevant section of the Response document.

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

7. Critical Defect response (Deed cl 14.2(a), definitions in cl 1.1). Clause 14.2(a) requires a Critical Defect to be rectified within 2 hours of notification. For a scheduled footpath cleaning service, could Council please give an example of what it would treat as a Critical Defect? Would Council accept a tenderer based outside the Shire (about 450 km away) proposing either (a) a local subcontract crew, approved under cl 12.2, to attend and make safe within 2 hours, or (b) a different response window for full rectification, for example make-safe or acknowledgement within 2 hours and rectification by the next night? If so, should this be shown as a departure in the Response section 3 table?

- All defects are required to be repaired by the contractor in a timely manner. Please note Clause 14.2 will be amended to: "Without limiting clause 14.1, the Contractor must rectify a Defect within a reasonable timeframe agreed with the Contract Manager, having regard to the nature, severity and urgency of the Defect. Such notification to rectify the relevant Defect shall, where the relevant Defect is an Ordered Services Defect, be deemed to be a Variation directed under clause 13.1 unless the relevant Defect has occurred as a result of a failure to perform or complete any part of the Services in accordance with the Contract, in which case the Contractor will have no Claim arising out of, or in any way in connection with, the Defect."

8. Subcontractor approval (Deed cl 12.2, 11.1(b); Response 5.1.4). Does naming a subcontractor in Response 5.1.4 count as a request for Council's approval under cl 12.2, with approval given at award? If not, what information does Council need (insurances, SWMS, licences), and how long does approval usually take? Can further subcontractors be approved during the Term?

-	Identification of a proposed subcontractor in the tender response does not, of itself, constitute Council approval of that subcontractor. Tenderers should provide the information requested in the Response document for proposed subcontractors. Council may undertake appropriate due diligence prior to approval, including consideration of relevant licences, qualifications, insurances, WHS documentation and capability. Additional subcontractors may be proposed during the contract term, subject to the requirements and approval provisions of the Deed.

9. Local subcontractor for routine cleaning (Deed cl 12.2, 12.3). Will Council approve routine cleaning being delivered by a named local (Kempsey/Port Macquarie) subcontractor, with the head contractor managing, supervising and auditing the work and remaining liable for it? What information does Council need to approve a subcontractor?

-	Council will permit the use of suitably qualified subcontractors for routine clean-ing services, subject to the approval requirements of the Deed. Proposed sub-contractors should be identified in the tender submission, together with relevant details of their capability, insurances and WHS compliance. The head contractor will remain responsible for all Services performed by an approved subcontractor.

Pricing basis and documents

10. Contract Sum (Response 9.1; Schedule of Rates). Should the lump sum Contract Sum be the estimated annual price (the total of the breakdown table for one year) or the total for the whole initial 36-month term? Are prices held fixed for the whole term, including option years, or is any annual adjustment available (Deed Sch 1 Item 6)?

- Thank you for your question.

Contract Sum: Please provide both the annual price (being the total of the breakdown table) and the overall Contract Sum for the full three-year initial term. Both amounts should be clearly stated in your response to section 9.1.

Respondents should base their Contract Sum on the rates submitted at the time of tender. Rates may be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Contract, with any increase capped at CPI.

GST: All prices are to be inclusive of GST, including the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum, in accordance with clause 4.21 of the RFT. Where section 9 refers to rates excluding GST, please disregard this wording and provide GST-inclusive figures.

Pricing basis and documents

11. GST basis (RFT 4.21 vs Response section 9 and Deed cl 19). RFT 4.21 says all prices must include GST, but the Response section 9 pricing tables and Deed cl 19 ask for prices exclusive of GST. Which basis should be used? Should every rate in the pricing schedule be entered GST-inclusive, or exclusive of GST with GST shown separately?

 - All prices must include GST. This covers the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum. Clause 4.21 of the RFT applies. Where section 9 asks for rates excluding GST, disregard that wording and give GST-inclusive figures.

12. Central Kempsey group area (RFT 3.2 Service Schedule; Response section 9 breakdown row 7). The Specification lists "All footpaths & bin enclosures" on Belgrave St (Kempsey Traffic Bridge to Stuart St), John St (Belgrave to Verge), Forth St (Clyde St to York Lane), Smith St (Forth to Stuart) and the Riverside Park footpath (Forth to John) as approximately 8,750 mÂ², cleaned once a year before Christmas. The Response pricing table shows this row's area as "Refer specification". Could Council please confirm that 8,750 mÂ² is the total area to be priced for the whole group, and whether it covers both sides of each street? It is about 19% of the annual area, so it materially affects the price.

- Council confirms that the Central Kempsey group area may be priced as one com-bined area. The approximate area of 8,750 m² applies to the overall group identified in the Specification and includes both sides of the relevant streets.

13. Missing attachments (Response section 9 and 8.1). Response section 9 asks for the Pricing Schedule "in Microsoft Excel format", and section 8.1 refers to a Modern Slavery Supplier Questionnaire. Neither is among the four documents we have (RFT, Draft Deed of Standing Offer, PO Terms and Conditions, and the Response document). Could Council please publish them, or confirm whether completing the tables in the Response document is enough?

- Prices must be broken down by individual site and by year, inclusive of GST. Suppliers may provide this pricing within the Response Document or, alternatively, submit a separate supplier-prepared Excel spreadsheet, provided the required pricing breakdown is clearly identified.

Environment and site

15. After-hours contact (Deed cl 12.8). Is the after-hours contact only for notifications during and around programmed overnight shifts, or does Council expect an on-call attendance capability outside programmed works?

- Council confirms that the Contractor is not required to provide an on-call or after-hours service. Any requirement within the draft Deed for the Contractor to be con-tactable at all times will not apply and will be amended accordingly. The Contractor will, however, be required to nominate a principal contact who is available during normal business hours.

16. Water supply. May the contractor draw water from Council hydrants or standpipes in Kempsey, South West Rocks and Crescent Head? If so, what permit, metering and charges apply? Is water available at the Horseshoe Bay picnic shelter?

- Council confirms that a standard hose connection is available for the Contractor’s use at each location. A standard tap connection is available at the Horseshoe Bay Picnic Shelter. Where a tenderer’s proposed equipment or methodology requires an alternative water supply, such as filling a water tanker, this requirement should be considered and allowed for in their submission. Paid water fill stations are available at Sherwood and Armidale Roads (Kempsey), Belmore Road (Crescent Head), and Gregory Street (South West Rocks).

17. Hours and noise (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 10.1(c), 10.3). Are there set start and finish times or noise limits for overnight work near residences in any of the locations? Are there any locations where Council prefers early-morning rather than late-night work?

- As outlined in the Scope, the services are expected to be undertaken outside normal business hours. Respondents should therefore provide rates that reflect this requirement.

18. Vehicle parking at night. Can work vehicles and the recovery unit park on the kerb or in loading zones next to the work area overnight? Is a permit required?

- Council’s preference is that vehicles and equipment are not positioned on the kerb; however, this may be permitted where no practical alternative is available. Contrac-tors may also occupy multiple parking spaces where required to undertake the works, provided the work area is clearly and safely delineated using appropriate traf-fic cones or other suitable traffic control measures.

19. Surfaces and sealants (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 8.4). Can Council tell us the main surface types at each location (e.g. sealed pavers, exposed aggregate, plain concrete, timber at the picnic shelter) and any sealants under warranty or with manufacturer cleaning limits?

- Council confirms that the majority of surfaces requiring treatment are concrete footpaths. Tenderers should, however, consider the following surface types when determining their proposed methodology and pricing:

•	Clyde Street Mall: brick pavement

•	Crescent Head: combination of concrete footpath, timber and pavers

•	South West Rocks: exposed aggregate

•	West Kempsey CBD: exposed aggregate

Tenderers should ensure their proposed cleaning methodology is suitable for the relevant surface types.

20. Scope inclusions. Does the scope include chewing gum removal and oil or stain treatment, or only general high-pressure cleaning? Does "bin enclosures" include cleaning the bins themselves?

- Council requires stains and chewing gum to be removed from the nominated sur-faces as part of the cleaning works. Where a particularly heavy or difficult stain is identified and its removal may result in damage to the surface or surrounding as-sets, the Contractor must notify Council’s nominated contact prior to proceeding so that an appropriate treatment approach can be agreed.

The bins themselves do not require cleaning or maintenance. For bin enclosures, the successful Contractor will be required to unlock the enclosure using a key provided by Council, temporarily remove the bin, clean the enclosure to remove scum and other build-up, return the bin to the enclosure, and securely lock the enclosure following completion.

Evaluation, lodgement and administration

21. Evaluation weightings (RFT 2.5). The evaluation table lists (a) Price, (c) Criterion 2 Capability, (e) Criterion 4 Methodology and (f) Criterion 5 WHS, with no weightings. Items (b) and (d) and Criteria 1 and 3 are missing. Could Council please confirm the full list of criteria and their weightings? Are Sustainability (Response section 8) and Financial Viability (section 10) scored?

- Council confirms that evaluation weightings are not disclosed within the RFT docu-mentation. The lettering sequence shown against the evaluation criteria is an admin-istrative error only. All evaluation criteria are correctly listed and remain unchanged.

22. Portal and closing time (RFT cover, 4.3, 4.6; Response cover table). Please confirm that questions should go through the VendorPanel forum (RFT 4.3 refers to the "eProcure portal"). The Response cover states "2:00pm â€“ AEST on 05/11/2026", but NSW is on daylight saving time (AEDT) on that date. Is the deadline 2:00 pm Sydney local time?

- Council confirms that all tender enquiries and clarification questions must be submitted through the VendorPanel forum. Any reference to the “eProcure portal” in the RFT is an administrative error and should be read as a reference to Vendor-Panel.

The tender closing time is 2:00 pm Sydney local time on 26 November 2026 (AEDT).

23. Partial or unbundled offers (RFT 4.8, 4.23). May a tenderer price only some locations, or must every location in the breakdown table be priced? If Council awards locations separately, will the rates per service stand on their own?

- Council confirms that tenderers are required to submit a response covering all loca-tions identified in the RFT. Partial submissions for selected locations will not be con-sidered.

24. First services. With commencement on 1 Dec 2026, does Council expect the annual pre-Christmas services, the first monthly Smith St clean and the December quarterly Horseshoe Bay clean to be completed in December 2026?

- Council confirms that the pre-Christmas cleaning works will be arranged separately from this procurement process due to the limited timeframe prior to the Christmas period. Services under the agreement resulting from this RFT will commence from 1 January 2027.

25. Payment documents (Deed cl 15.8, Sch 2). Please confirm that a statutory declaration and Subcontractor's Statement are needed with each weekly payment claim, or whether one per Completed Purchase Order is enough.

-	Council does not anticipate weekly payment claims under this arrangement. Services will generally be ordered and invoiced against individual Purchase Orders as the Services are performed. Required supporting documentation should be provided with the relevant payment claim/Purchase Order in accordance with the contract requirements.

26. Local preference. Does using a local subcontractor for most of the work count toward any local-preference consideration in the evaluation?

-	Local preference will be assessed in accordance with Council's applicable Local Preference Purchasing Procedure and the evaluation methodology stated in the tender documentation. The use of a local subcontractor does not, by itself, mean that the tenderer qualifies as a local supplier for the purposes of Council's local preference provisions.

Hi There,

Please see below answers to your questions. Please note that some Questions are still currently under review and will be responded to once an answer has been decided on.

Insurance (mandatory criterion, RFT 2.4)

1. Timing of evidence (RFT 2.4, 3.3; Response section 11; Deed cl 11.1-11.2). Will Council accept a public and products liability policy that is bound and current before the closing time, evidenced by a certificate of currency dated before closing? If the insurer cannot issue the final certificate in time, will Council accept a broker's cover note or binder at lodgement, with the certificate to follow before the first Purchase Order?

-	Tenderers should provide current evidence of the required insurance cover with their submission. Where a final CoC is not available by the tender closing time, Council may accept appropriate evidence from the insurer or authorised insurance broker confirming that the required cover is current. The successful tenderer will be required to provide satisfactory CoC for all required insurances prior to contract commencement an/or issue of any PO.

2. Joint names wording (Deed Sch 1 Item 9, cl 11.3). Many liability insurers will not add a principal as a joint named insured, but will note the principal's interest and provide a principal's indemnity extension with cross liability and waiver of subrogation. Would Council accept "Kempsey Shire Council noted as an interested party, with principal's indemnity, cross liability and waiver of subrogation" as meeting Item 9?

-	Council acknowledges that insurers may use different policy structures and endorsements. Council will consider equivalent insurance arrangements where the tenderer can demonstrate that the proposed cover provides protection consistent with the requirements of the Deed. Any proposed alternative to the insurance requirements should be clearly identified in the tenderer's submission as a departure, together with supporting details of the proposed cover, for Council's assessment.

3. Products liability. For a services-only contract, is a combined public and products liability policy with a $20m limit for each of public liability and products liability acceptable? Is products liability required on an "any one occurrence" basis or an annual aggregate basis?

-	A combined Public and Products Liability policy may be acceptable provided the policy satisfies the minimum coverage and limit requirements specified in the tender and contract documents.

Tenderers should provide details of the basis and limits of their proposed cover with their submission. Any variation from the stated insurance requirements should be identified as a departure for Council's consideration.

4. Workers compensation (Deed Sch 1 Item 9). Item 9 says "Workers' Compensation or Personal Accident & Illness". Will Council accept personal accident and illness cover for subcontractors who are sole traders without employees?

-	Tenderers and subcontractors are required to maintain the insurances applicable to their business and employment arrangements. Where a subcontractor is a sole trader without employees and Workers' Compensation insurance is not applicable, appropriate Personal Accident and Illness cover may be provided in accordance with the requirements of the Deed.

Evidence of the applicable insurance arrangements may be requested by Council prior to approval of the subcontractor.

5. Motor vehicle and works insurance (RFT 3.3). Please confirm that comprehensive motor vehicle cover is "as applicable" and that works insurance (120% replacement cost) applies only if a specific Purchase Order requires it.

-	Comprehensive Motor Vehicle insurance is required where vehicles are used in connection with the Services.

The requirement for Works Insurance will apply where relevant to the nature of the works being undertaken and in accordance with the requirements of the Deed and applicable Purchase Order. Tenderers should identify any proposed departure from the stated insurance requirements in their submission.

6. Professional indemnity. Deed Sch 1 Item 9 says PI is not required, but the Response section 11 table has a PI row and PO T&C 10.a.iii mentions $1m PI for professional services. Please confirm we can answer "Not required".

-	Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for the Services under this tender. Tenderers may therefore mark Professional Indemnity as “Not Applicable” in the relevant section of the Response document.

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

7. Critical Defect response (Deed cl 14.2(a), definitions in cl 1.1). Clause 14.2(a) requires a Critical Defect to be rectified within 2 hours of notification. For a scheduled footpath cleaning service, could Council please give an example of what it would treat as a Critical Defect? Would Council accept a tenderer based outside the Shire (about 450 km away) proposing either (a) a local subcontract crew, approved under cl 12.2, to attend and make safe within 2 hours, or (b) a different response window for full rectification, for example make-safe or acknowledgement within 2 hours and rectification by the next night? If so, should this be shown as a departure in the Response section 3 table?

- All defects are required to be repaired by the contractor in a timely manner. Please note Clause 14.2 will be amended to: "Without limiting clause 14.1, the Contractor must rectify a Defect within a reasonable timeframe agreed with the Contract Manager, having regard to the nature, severity and urgency of the Defect. Such notification to rectify the relevant Defect shall, where the relevant Defect is an Ordered Services Defect, be deemed to be a Variation directed under clause 13.1 unless the relevant Defect has occurred as a result of a failure to perform or complete any part of the Services in accordance with the Contract, in which case the Contractor will have no Claim arising out of, or in any way in connection with, the Defect."

8. Subcontractor approval (Deed cl 12.2, 11.1(b); Response 5.1.4). Does naming a subcontractor in Response 5.1.4 count as a request for Council's approval under cl 12.2, with approval given at award? If not, what information does Council need (insurances, SWMS, licences), and how long does approval usually take? Can further subcontractors be approved during the Term?

-	Identification of a proposed subcontractor in the tender response does not, of itself, constitute Council approval of that subcontractor. Tenderers should provide the information requested in the Response document for proposed subcontractors. Council may undertake appropriate due diligence prior to approval, including consideration of relevant licences, qualifications, insurances, WHS documentation and capability. Additional subcontractors may be proposed during the contract term, subject to the requirements and approval provisions of the Deed.

9. Local subcontractor for routine cleaning (Deed cl 12.2, 12.3). Will Council approve routine cleaning being delivered by a named local (Kempsey/Port Macquarie) subcontractor, with the head contractor managing, supervising and auditing the work and remaining liable for it? What information does Council need to approve a subcontractor?

-	Council will permit the use of suitably qualified subcontractors for routine clean-ing services, subject to the approval requirements of the Deed. Proposed sub-contractors should be identified in the tender submission, together with relevant details of their capability, insurances and WHS compliance. The head contractor will remain responsible for all Services performed by an approved subcontractor.

Pricing basis and documents

10. Contract Sum (Response 9.1; Schedule of Rates). Should the lump sum Contract Sum be the estimated annual price (the total of the breakdown table for one year) or the total for the whole initial 36-month term? Are prices held fixed for the whole term, including option years, or is any annual adjustment available (Deed Sch 1 Item 6)?

- Thank you for your question.

Contract Sum: Please provide both the annual price (being the total of the breakdown table) and the overall Contract Sum for the full three-year initial term. Both amounts should be clearly stated in your response to section 9.1.

Respondents should base their Contract Sum on the rates submitted at the time of tender. Rates may be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Contract, with any increase capped at CPI.

GST: All prices are to be inclusive of GST, including the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum, in accordance with clause 4.21 of the RFT. Where section 9 refers to rates excluding GST, please disregard this wording and provide GST-inclusive figures.

Pricing basis and documents

11. GST basis (RFT 4.21 vs Response section 9 and Deed cl 19). RFT 4.21 says all prices must include GST, but the Response section 9 pricing tables and Deed cl 19 ask for prices exclusive of GST. Which basis should be used? Should every rate in the pricing schedule be entered GST-inclusive, or exclusive of GST with GST shown separately?

 - All prices must include GST. This covers the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum. Clause 4.21 of the RFT applies. Where section 9 asks for rates excluding GST, disregard that wording and give GST-inclusive figures.

12. Central Kempsey group area (RFT 3.2 Service Schedule; Response section 9 breakdown row 7). The Specification lists "All footpaths & bin enclosures" on Belgrave St (Kempsey Traffic Bridge to Stuart St), John St (Belgrave to Verge), Forth St (Clyde St to York Lane), Smith St (Forth to Stuart) and the Riverside Park footpath (Forth to John) as approximately 8,750 mÂ², cleaned once a year before Christmas. Could Council please confirm that 8,750 mÂ² is the total area to be priced for the whole group, and whether it covers both sides of each street? It is about 19% of the annual area, so it materially affects the price.

- Council confirms that the Central Kempsey group area may be priced as one com-bined area. The approximate area of 8,750 m² applies to the overall group identified in the Specification and includes both sides of the relevant streets.

13. Missing attachments (Response section 9 and 8.1). Response section 9 asks for the Pricing Schedule "in Microsoft Excel format", and section 8.1 refers to a Modern Slavery Supplier Questionnaire. Neither is among the four documents we have (RFT, Draft Deed of Standing Offer, PO Terms and Conditions, and the Response document). - Prices must be broken down by individual site and by year, inclusive of GST. Suppliers may provide this pricing within the Response Document or, alternatively, submit a separate supplier-prepared Excel spreadsheet, provided the required pricing breakdown is clearly identified.

Environment and site

15. After-hours contact (Deed cl 12.8). Is the after-hours contact only for notifications during and around programmed overnight shifts, or does Council expect an on-call attendance capability outside programmed works?

- Council confirms that the Contractor is not required to provide an on-call or after-hours service. Any requirement within the draft Deed for the Contractor to be con-tactable at all times will not apply and will be amended accordingly. The Contractor will, however, be required to nominate a principal contact who is available during normal business hours.

16. Water supply. May the contractor draw water from Council hydrants or standpipes in Kempsey, South West Rocks and Crescent Head? If so, what permit, metering and charges apply? Is water available at the Horseshoe Bay picnic shelter?

- Council confirms that a standard hose connection is available for the Contractor’s use at each location. A standard tap connection is available at the Horseshoe Bay Picnic Shelter. Where a tenderer’s proposed equipment or methodology requires an alternative water supply, such as filling a water tanker, this requirement should be considered and allowed for in their submission. 17. Hours and noise (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 10.1(c), 10.3). Are there set start and finish times or noise limits for overnight work near residences in any of the locations? Are there any locations where Council prefers early-morning rather than late-night work?

- As outlined in the Scope, the services are expected to be undertaken outside normal business hours. Respondents should therefore provide rates that reflect this requirement.

18. Vehicle parking at night. Can work vehicles and the recovery unit park on the kerb or in loading zones next to the work area overnight? Is a permit required?

- Council’s preference is that vehicles and equipment are not positioned on the kerb; however, this may be permitted where no practical alternative is available. Contrac-tors may also occupy multiple parking spaces where required to undertake the works, provided the work area is clearly and safely delineated using appropriate traf-fic cones or other suitable traffic control measures.

19. Surfaces and sealants (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 8.4). Can Council tell us the main surface types at each location (e.g. sealed pavers, exposed aggregate, plain concrete, timber at the picnic shelter) and any sealants under warranty or with manufacturer cleaning limits?

•	Crescent Head: combination of concrete footpath, timber and pavers

•	West Kempsey CBD: exposed aggregate

Tenderers should ensure their proposed cleaning methodology is suitable for the relevant surface types.

20. Scope inclusions. Does the scope include chewing gum removal and oil or stain treatment, or only general high-pressure cleaning? Does "bin enclosures" include cleaning the bins themselves?

- Council requires stains and chewing gum to be removed from the nominated sur-faces as part of the cleaning works. Where a particularly heavy or difficult stain is identified and its removal may result in damage to the surface or surrounding as-sets, the Contractor must notify Council’s nominated contact prior to proceeding so that an appropriate treatment approach can be agreed.

The bins themselves do not require cleaning or maintenance. For bin enclosures, the successful Contractor will be required to unlock the enclosure using a key provided by Council, temporarily remove the bin, clean the enclosure to remove scum and other build-up, return the bin to the enclosure, and securely lock the enclosure following completion.

23. Partial or unbundled offers (RFT 4.8, 4.23). May a tenderer price only some locations, or must every location in the breakdown table be priced? If Council awards locations separately, will the rates per service stand on their own?

25. Payment documents (Deed cl 15.8, Sch 2). Please confirm that a statutory declaration and Subcontractor's Statement are needed with each weekly payment claim, or whether one per Completed Purchase Order is enough.

-	Council does not anticipate weekly payment claims under this arrangement. Services will generally be ordered and invoiced against individual Purchase Orders as the Services are performed. Hi There,
