-	Tenderers should provide current evidence of the required insurance cover with their submission. Where a final CoC is not available by the tender closing time, Council may accept appropriate evidence from the insurer or authorised insurance broker confirming that the required cover is current. The successful tenderer will be required to provide satisfactory CoC for all required insurances prior to contract commencement an/or issue of any PO.

2. Joint names wording (Deed Sch 1 Item 9, cl 11.3). Many liability insurers will not add a principal as a joint named insured, but will note the principal's interest and provide a principal's indemnity extension with cross liability and waiver of subrogation. Would Council accept "Kempsey Shire Council noted as an interested party, with principal's indemnity, cross liability and waiver of subrogation" as meeting Item 9?

-	Council acknowledges that insurers may use different policy structures and endorsements. Council will consider equivalent insurance arrangements where the tenderer can demonstrate that the proposed cover provides protection consistent with the requirements of the Deed. Any proposed alternative to the insurance requirements should be clearly identified in the tenderer's submission as a departure, together with supporting details of the proposed cover, for Council's assessment.

3. Products liability. For a services-only contract, is a combined public and products liability policy with a $20m limit for each of public liability and products liability acceptable? Is products liability required on an "any one occurrence" basis or an annual aggregate basis?

-	A combined Public and Products Liability policy may be acceptable provided the policy satisfies the minimum coverage and limit requirements specified in the tender and contract documents.

Tenderers should provide details of the basis and limits of their proposed cover with their submission. Any variation from the stated insurance requirements should be identified as a departure for Council's consideration.

4. Workers compensation (Deed Sch 1 Item 9). Item 9 says "Workers' Compensation or Personal Accident & Illness". Will Council accept personal accident and illness cover for subcontractors who are sole traders without employees?

-	Tenderers and subcontractors are required to maintain the insurances applicable to their business and employment arrangements. Where a subcontractor is a sole trader without employees and Workers' Compensation insurance is not applicable, appropriate Personal Accident and Illness cover may be provided in accordance with the requirements of the Deed.

Evidence of the applicable insurance arrangements may be requested by Council prior to approval of the subcontractor.

5. Motor vehicle and works insurance (RFT 3.3). Please confirm that comprehensive motor vehicle cover is "as applicable" and that works insurance (120% replacement cost) applies only if a specific Purchase Order requires it.

-	Comprehensive Motor Vehicle insurance is required where vehicles are used in connection with the Services.

The requirement for Works Insurance will apply where relevant to the nature of the works being undertaken and in accordance with the requirements of the Deed and applicable Purchase Order. Tenderers should identify any proposed departure from the stated insurance requirements in their submission.

6. Professional indemnity. Deed Sch 1 Item 9 says PI is not required, but the Response section 11 table has a PI row and PO T&C 10.a.iii mentions $1m PI for professional services. Please confirm we can answer "Not required".

-	Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for the Services under this tender. Tenderers may therefore mark Professional Indemnity as “Not Applicable” in the relevant section of the Response document.

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

7. Critical Defect response (Deed cl 14.2(a), definitions in cl 1.1). Clause 14.2(a) requires a Critical Defect to be rectified within 2 hours of notification. - All defects are required to be repaired by the contractor in a timely manner. Please note Clause 14.2 will be amended to: "Without limiting clause 14.1, the Contractor must rectify a Defect within a reasonable timeframe agreed with the Contract Manager, having regard to the nature, severity and urgency of the Defect. Such notification to rectify the relevant Defect shall, where the relevant Defect is an Ordered Services Defect, be deemed to be a Variation directed under clause 13.1 unless the relevant Defect has occurred as a result of a failure to perform or complete any part of the Services in accordance with the Contract, in which case the Contractor will have no Claim arising out of, or in any way in connection with, the Defect."

Will Council approve routine cleaning being delivered by a named local (Kempsey/Port Macquarie) subcontractor, with the head contractor managing, supervising and auditing the work and remaining liable for it? What information does Council need to approve a subcontractor?

-	Council will permit the use of suitably qualified subcontractors for routine clean-ing services, subject to the approval requirements of the Deed. Proposed sub-contractors should be identified in the tender submission, together with relevant details of their capability, insurances and WHS compliance. The head contractor will remain responsible for all Services performed by an approved subcontractor.

Pricing basis and documents

10. Contract Sum (Response 9.1; Schedule of Rates). Should the lump sum Contract Sum be the estimated annual price (the total of the breakdown table for one year) or the total for the whole initial 36-month term? Are prices held fixed for the whole term, including option years, or is any annual adjustment available (Deed Sch 1 Item 6)?

- Thank you for your question.

Contract Sum: Please provide both the annual price (being the total of the breakdown table) and the overall Contract Sum for the full three-year initial term. Both amounts should be clearly stated in your response to section 9.1.

Respondents should base their Contract Sum on the rates submitted at the time of tender. Rates may be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Contract, with any increase capped at CPI.

GST: All prices are to be inclusive of GST, including the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum, in accordance with clause 4.21 of the RFT. Where section 9 refers to rates excluding GST, please disregard this wording and provide GST-inclusive figures.

Pricing basis and documents

11. GST basis (RFT 4.21 vs Response section 9 and Deed cl 19). RFT 4.21 says all prices must include GST, but the Response section 9 pricing tables and Deed cl 19 ask for prices exclusive of GST. Which basis should be used? Should every rate in the pricing schedule be entered GST-inclusive, or exclusive of GST with GST shown separately?

 - All prices must include GST. This covers the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum. Clause 4.21 of the RFT applies. Where section 9 asks for rates excluding GST, disregard that wording and give GST-inclusive figures.

12. Central Kempsey group area (RFT 3.2 Service Schedule; Response section 9 breakdown row 7). The Specification lists "All footpaths & bin enclosures" on Belgrave St (Kempsey Traffic Bridge to Stuart St), John St (Belgrave to Verge), Forth St (Clyde St to York Lane), Smith St (Forth to Stuart) and the Riverside Park footpath (Forth to John) as approximately 8,750 mÂ², cleaned once a year before Christmas. The Response pricing table shows this row's area as "Refer specification". Could Council please confirm that 8,750 mÂ² is the total area to be priced for the whole group, and whether it covers both sides of each street? It is about 19% of the annual area, so it materially affects the price.

- Council confirms that the Central Kempsey group area may be priced as one com-bined area. The approximate area of 8,750 m² applies to the overall group identified in the Specification and includes both sides of the relevant streets.

13. Missing attachments (Response section 9 and 8.1). Response section 9 asks for the Pricing Schedule "in Microsoft Excel format", and section 8.1 refers to a Modern Slavery Supplier Questionnaire. Neither is among the four documents we have (RFT, Draft Deed of Standing Offer, PO Terms and Conditions, and the Response document). Could Council please publish them, or confirm whether completing the tables in the Response document is enough?

- Prices must be broken down by individual site and by year, inclusive of GST. Suppliers may provide this pricing within the Response Document or, alternatively, submit a separate supplier-prepared Excel spreadsheet, provided the required pricing breakdown is clearly identified.

Environment and site

15. After-hours contact (Deed cl 12.8). Is the after-hours contact only for notifications during and around programmed overnight shifts, or does Council expect an on-call attendance capability outside programmed works?

- Council confirms that the Contractor is not required to provide an on-call or after-hours service. Any requirement within the draft Deed for the Contractor to be con-tactable at all times will not apply and will be amended accordingly. The Contractor will, however, be required to nominate a principal contact who is available during normal business hours.

16. Water supply. May the contractor draw water from Council hydrants or standpipes in Kempsey, South West Rocks and Crescent Head? If so, what permit, metering and charges apply? Is water available at the Horseshoe Bay picnic shelter?

- Council confirms that a standard hose connection is available for the Contractor’s use at each location. A standard tap connection is available at the Horseshoe Bay Picnic Shelter. Where a tenderer’s proposed equipment or methodology requires an alternative water supply, such as filling a water tanker, this requirement should be considered and allowed for in their submission. Paid water fill stations are available at Sherwood and Armidale Roads (Kempsey), Belmore Road (Crescent Head), and Gregory Street (South West Rocks).

17. Hours and noise (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 10.1(c), 10.3). Are there set start and finish times or noise limits for overnight work near residences in any of the locations? Are there any locations where Council prefers early-morning rather than late-night work?

- As outlined in the Scope, the services are expected to be undertaken outside normal business hours. Respondents should therefore provide rates that reflect this requirement.

18. Vehicle parking at night. Can work vehicles and the recovery unit park on the kerb or in loading zones next to the work area overnight? Is a permit required?

- Council’s preference is that vehicles and equipment are not positioned on the kerb; however, this may be permitted where no practical alternative is available. Contrac-tors may also occupy multiple parking spaces where required to undertake the works, provided the work area is clearly and safely delineated using appropriate traf-fic cones or other suitable traffic control measures.

19. Surfaces and sealants (RFT 3.2; Deed cl 8.4). Can Council tell us the main surface types at each location (e.g. sealed pavers, exposed aggregate, plain concrete, timber at the picnic shelter) and any sealants under warranty or with manufacturer cleaning limits?

- Council confirms that the majority of surfaces requiring treatment are concrete footpaths. Tenderers should, however, consider the following surface types when determining their proposed methodology and pricing:

•	Clyde Street Mall: brick pavement

•	Crescent Head: combination of concrete footpath, timber and pavers

•	South West Rocks: exposed aggregate

•	West Kempsey CBD: exposed aggregate

Tenderers should ensure their proposed cleaning methodology is suitable for the relevant surface types.

20. Scope inclusions. Does the scope include chewing gum removal and oil or stain treatment, or only general high-pressure cleaning? Does "bin enclosures" include cleaning the bins themselves?

- Council requires stains and chewing gum to be removed from the nominated sur-faces as part of the cleaning works. Where a particularly heavy or difficult stain is identified and its removal may result in damage to the surface or surrounding as-sets, the Contractor must notify Council’s nominated contact prior to proceeding so that an appropriate treatment approach can be agreed.

The bins themselves do not require cleaning or maintenance. For bin enclosures, the successful Contractor will be required to unlock the enclosure using a key provided by Council, temporarily remove the bin, clean the enclosure to remove scum and other build-up, return the bin to the enclosure, and securely lock the enclosure following completion.

Evaluation, lodgement and administration

21. Evaluation weightings (RFT 2.5). The evaluation table lists (a) Price, (c) Criterion 2 Capability, (e) Criterion 4 Methodology and (f) Criterion 5 WHS, with no weightings. Items (b) and (d) and Criteria 1 and 3 are missing. Could Council please confirm the full list of criteria and their weightings? Are Sustainability (Response section 8) and Financial Viability (section 10) scored?

- Council confirms that evaluation weightings are not disclosed within the RFT docu-mentation. The lettering sequence shown against the evaluation criteria is an admin-istrative error only. All evaluation criteria are correctly listed and remain unchanged.

22. Portal and closing time (RFT cover, 4.3, 4.6; Response cover table). Please confirm that questions should go through the VendorPanel forum (RFT 4.3 refers to the "eProcure portal"). The Response cover states "2:00pm â€“ AEST on 05/11/2026", but NSW is on daylight saving time (AEDT) on that date. Is the deadline 2:00 pm Sydney local time?

- Council confirms that all tender enquiries and clarification questions must be submitted through the VendorPanel forum. Any reference to the “eProcure portal” in the RFT is an administrative error and should be read as a reference to Vendor-Panel.

The tender closing time is 2:00 pm Sydney local time on 26 November 2026 (AEDT).

23. Partial or unbundled offers (RFT 4.8, 4.23). May a tenderer price only some locations, or must every location in the breakdown table be priced? If Council awards locations separately, will the rates per service stand on their own?

- Council confirms that tenderers are required to submit a response covering all loca-tions identified in the RFT. Partial submissions for selected locations will not be con-sidered.

24. First services. With commencement on 1 Dec 2026, does Council expect the annual pre-Christmas services, the first monthly Smith St clean and the December quarterly Horseshoe Bay clean to be completed in December 2026?

- Council confirms that the pre-Christmas cleaning works will be arranged separately from this procurement process due to the limited timeframe prior to the Christmas period. Services under the agreement resulting from this RFT will commence from 1 January 2027.

25. Payment documents (Deed cl 15.8, Sch 2). Please confirm that a statutory declaration and Subcontractor's Statement are needed with each weekly payment claim, or whether one per Completed Purchase Order is enough.

-	Council does not anticipate weekly payment claims under this arrangement. Services will generally be ordered and invoiced against individual Purchase Orders as the Services are performed. publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

I am reviewing the tender documentation for COW000198 — Supply and Delivery of Corporate Uniforms and would appreciate clarification on the following:

Subcontracting: Can the successful tenderer engage third-party clothing manufacturers, embroidery businesses and logistics providers while remaining the principal contractor responsible for fulfilment?

Local fitting facilities: Can the mandatory local fitting service be provided through an established clothing retailer or subcontractor located within the Cassowary Coast region?

Business location: Is a tenderer based outside the Cassowary Coast region eligible, provided all local fitting, delivery and service requirements are met?

Supplier experience: Will council consider the experience, references and manufacturing capabilities of proposed subcontractors when assessing a tenderer's suitability?

Purchase volumes: Can council provide approximate historical annual uniform expenditure, garment quantities and the number of employees eligible to order uniforms?

Insurance: Must the principal contractor personally hold the full $20 million public and product liability cover, or can insurance held by approved subcontractors contribute to satisfying this requirement?

Pricing: Is there any provision for exceptional price adjustments during the initial 36-month term if wholesale garment or freight costs increase substantially?

Samples: Can fabric swatches and garment samples be provided by the proposed manufacturing partner, and are physical samples required before the tender closing date?

Thank you for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Mark Pidgeon

maek.pidgeon@gmail.com
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon,

Thank you for your enquiry. Clarifications are detailed below.

Subcontracting: Council refers to Clause 11 of Part 2. Contract, which outlines the requirements for subcontracting, assignment and novation. Council also highlights the Applicable Policies in Item 10 of the Reference Schedule, particularly the Contractor Code of Conduct.

Local fitting facilities and Business location: Council will evaluate all conforming submissions. Responses are required to demonstrate the supplier’s ability to perform the services in accordance with the requirements set out in Part 3. Scope

Supplier experience: Submissions will be assessed as per the evaluation criteria set out in Part 1. Request for Tender

Purchase Volumes: Council refers to clause 1.8 (Guarantees) which states no guarantee of expenditure, quantities of purchase or frequency of purchases will be provided by the Principal.

Insurance: Council refers to clause 22.1 or Part 2. Contract which states:

“The Supplier must effect the insurances stated in the Reference Schedule and any other insurance which the Supplier considers is necessary to protect its interests or which is required by law.”

Council also refers to clause 22.3, which requires the Supplier to ensure that any subcontractor, supplier or consultant of the Supplier to have equivalent insurances to the extent that they are applicable to the part of the Services to be carried out by the subcontractor, supplier or consultant.

Pricing: Council refer suppliers to clause 3.6 (Fixed-Price Costing) of Part 3. Scope and clause 15 of Part 2. Contract.

Samples: Relevant samples must be provided as per Part 3. Scope clause 2.6 (Fabric Swatch Sample).

title: 2627-24 || Provision of Delivered Meals
description:
Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to prepare, package and deliver nutritious, high-quality meals to eligible older people and younger people with a disability living within the City of Greater Dandenong.

The service includes menu planning, meal preparation, individual order packing and labelling, and delivery to clients’ homes. Tenderers must outline the range of standard, dietary, culturally appropriate and modified meal options they can provide, together with their food-safety, quality-assurance, delivery, reporting and business-continuity arrangements.

The proposed contract will operate on a Schedule of Rates basis from 21 March 2027 to 30 June 2029, with no extension option. The anticipated annual service target is approximately 25,854 meals for around 140 current clients. These figures are indicative only and Council does not guarantee any minimum quantity, expenditure or revenue.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Council delivers the Commonwealth Home Support Programme and the Home and Community Care Program for Younger People. Delivered meals support eligible clients to live independently in their own homes.

Tenderers must demonstrate relevant experience and sufficient personnel, production facilities, food-safety systems, delivery resources and contingency arrangements to provide the service from commencement. Tenderers must also comply with the tender specification, applicable food-safety and aged-care requirements, privacy obligations, worker-screening requirements and Council’s contract conditions.

The Services are supported by Commonwealth and Victorian Government funding. Continuation of the Services during the proposed Contract Term is dependent on Council continuing to receive sufficient funding. If the relevant funding ceases, is reduced or materially changes, Council may reduce, suspend or discontinue all or part of the Services in accordance with the Contract.

The Council is committed to leading our City, protecting our environment, caring for our people, making our City vibrant, liveable, healthy and accessible, and economically and financially sustainable.
The Blue Mountains is one of only two cities in the world surrounded by a World Heritage Area and sits within the Sydney drinking water catchment servicing 1.7 million people.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Blue Mountains City Council delivers an extensive program of bush fire hazard reduction work (also known as fire mitigation), Natural Areas Management, Natural Areas Visitor Facilities and Urban Forestry - Tree Management on Council managed land across the local government area. This includes the creation and maintenance of asset protection zones, vegetation and surface maintenance on fire trails, and preparation work associated with hazard reduction burning. Almost all this work is delivered by external service providers.

Council to assess contractor capability and value for money whilst streamlining the administrative process for commissioning of routine maintenance work. Contractors were then chosen on a best-fit basis for the work required at each site.

publicQuestions.question:
We are an ecological consultancy and do not provide bush regeneration crews or plant. Could Council please confirm:

Whether ecological consultancy services will be considered under Panel B through the “Related additional services” row of the Panel B pricing schedule. Examples include flora and fauna surveys, threatened species and Threatened Ecological Community (TEC) assessments, vegetation, bushland and restoration management plans, monitoring and reporting, and ecological impact assessments (for example Reviews of Environmental Factors (REFs) and Test of Significance assessments) supporting Natural Area Management works.

If so, whether a tenderer may apply for Panel B offering these services only, without pricing the bush regeneration crew and plant items (items 1 to 17)?
publicQuestions.answer: The services outlined in Panel B are primarily related to on ground activities only, rather than specialist assessments and monitoring. Not pricing any of the other services indicated in the request issued, would result in flagging the submission for consideration on an eligibility list only.

publicQuestions.question: For Panel A, can a sole operator with a ride-on mower and standard gardening equipment tender for and undertake only suitable mowing/vegetation maintenance items, excluding tree removal, chipping and fire trail construction? Is a minimum crew required? Please clarify the minimum machinery specifications and whether both ROPS and FOPS are mandatory for a ride-on mower used only for mowing in suitable open areas, and whether all Panel A pricing items must be quoted or only the services offered.
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes, a sole operator with a ride-on can submit a tender but noting that we are looking for people that can address all or most of the panel requirements.

No minimum crew is required nor minimum machinery specs. As ROPS & FOPS are not mandatory for ride-on mowers, we would be looking at your safety documents as to how you would minimise the risks.

Council would be looking for how you and your equipment could undertake the work and what you would be charging for the service.

publicQuestions.question:
Rate review date

The pricing schedules for Panels B and C state that at the conclusion of each financial year, being 30 June, the tenderer may review its schedule of rates for the following financial year.

Clause 4.3(2) of the Panel Services Agreement and clause 4.1 of Annexure 1 instead say rates cannot be varied until 12 months after the contract starts. Which applies?

The 1 July date suits both Council and contractors. Works under each order are to be completed by 30 June (RFT clause 2.6) and Council issues new purchase orders from 1 July, so a rate change on that date never falls part-way through an order or a budget year. 1 July is also when the mandatory annual wage increases take effect, and wages are more than 85% of a contractor's costs for this work. Annual CPI figures line up with the financial year as well so there is clean data.

The other issue with a review tied to the anniversary of execution or commencement is that the RFT gives only an indicative timetable for those dates. In practice the anniversary could fall anywhere between February and July, so tenderers cannot know how long their tendered rates must hold and cannot price with certainty.

Can Council confirm the date of the first rate review?
publicQuestions.answer:
The option to review the schedule of rates will be at the end of the financial year, 30th June, with any changes taking effect from July 1st.

An addendum will be issued to reflect adjustment to the contract terms to align this.

publicQuestions.question:
Hours in a day

The pricing schedules ask for an hourly rate, hours in a day and a daily rate. Can tenderers nominate their own standard day length (for example 7 or 8 hours on site), and will Council compare tenders on the hourly rate or the daily rate?
publicQuestions.answer: Tenderers can set their own standard hours e.g 7 or 8 hours which is to be detailed in the returnable pricing schedule. The tenderers response to all components of the returnable pricing schedule will be reviewed.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Anne,

I’ve been reviewing the Natural Environmental Services panels tender and would appreciate clarification on whether Council would welcome a submission covering specialist environmental mapping and monitoring services.

TALONYX is an environmental intelligence consultancy. We use drones, remote sensing, GIS and spatial analysis to help land managers assess site conditions, plan works and track the results of management decisions.

For this program, our services could include:

Weed, vegetation and habitat mapping to help target and plan works.

Baseline and repeat surveys of bush regeneration, creekline, wetland and post-fire recovery sites.

Mapped records of erosion, access and visible infrastructure condition.

Spatial reporting linking completed works with subsequent observations, supporting program reporting and funding acquittals.

Panel B appears the closest fit, with potential applications under Panels A and C. I note clause 2.5 permits submissions for part of a panel.

Would Council consider these services within scope as a standalone specialist offering, or are they expected to be provided only as part of a contractor’s on-ground works package? If a specialist submission is appropriate, could you please advise which panel and pricing items would be most suitable?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer: The services outlined in Panel B and C are primarily related to on ground activities only rather than specialist environmental mapping and monitoring. Not pricing any of the other services indicated in the request issued, would result in flagging the submission for consideration on an eligibility list only.

publicQuestions.question: For a sole trader with no employees offering only suitable ride-on mowing and manual garden maintenance under Panel A, and no professional advice, tree assessment, chemicals or civil works: please confirm whether the $5 million Professional Indemnity insurance in Schedule 2 Item 16 is required for this limited scope, or whether the "if required" qualification in Item 14 applies. Please also confirm the acceptable evidence for Workers Compensation where the tenderer is a sole trader with no employees. Finally, the mechanical fuel management standard restricts ordinary work to 7am–5pm Monday–Friday: may the returnable daily rate use a 10-hour day with actual hours recorded, subject to breaks and site requirements?
publicQuestions.answer:
If you do not have professional indemnity insurance and do not consider it required for services offered please state this in your response.

A sole trader you would need to provide evidence of what cover would be in place to protect yourself, in the case of a workplace injury. Council is required to ensure any sole traders employed by it can demonstrate as a minimum personal accident insurance would be in place.

The hours proposed relate to the rate set and should be indicated in the pricing schedule, subject to adequate evidence of safe work practices.

publicQuestions.question: For a partial Panel A offer limited to ride-on mowing on open grassed areas by a sole trader with no employees, can a tender be lodged before the required insurance is in place? Please confirm the policy types and minimum cover limits for this scope, and whether certificates of currency are required at lodgement, before panel appointment or before the first work order.
publicQuestions.answer: You would need to provide evidence of what insurance you have in place. If you are already in business as a minimum some level of Public Liability insurance is required to cover you in case of injury or damage to a third party. Motor vehicle registration and insurance. Proof of insurance when submitting a tender is preferred or details for what arrangements would be put in place.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Blue Mountains City Council,

Could you please confirm if heritage advisory is part of the services under this panel?

Many Thanks.
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for the query. The services outlined are primarily related to on-ground environmental activities rather than specialist heritage advisory services. However, Council will retain your details in case we should require these services at a later point.

publicQuestions.question: Can Council confirm if the Urban Forestry component is open to independent arboricultural consultancy, or are you seeking responses from suppliers who can offer BOTH reporting and tree maintenance services?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, Urban Forest is open to independent arboricultural consultancy. Don’t have to provide tree maintenance services.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please confirm whether the hourly and daily rates requested for plant and equipment under the Tree/Shrub Management Services Schedule of Rates (Items 6–26) are intended to be dry-hire rates (equipment only) or wet-hire rates (including an appropriately qualified operator)?

Where equipment is supplied with an operator, could Council also clarify whether operator labour is to be included in the plant rate or charged separately under the applicable labour categories?
publicQuestions.answer:
Rates (Items 6–26) are intended wet-hire rates (including an appropriately qualified operator.

Operator labour is to be included in the plant rate.

publicQuestions.question: Thank you for confirming that rate reviews will take effect from 1 July. With contracts expected to commence in January/February 2027, can Council confirm whether the first adjustment will take effect from 1 July 2027, or whether rates remain fixed until 1 July 2028?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council would consider an application that would allow appointed contractors to increase rates in accordance with Rise and Fall Adjustment Clause 4 Price Adjustment in draft Service Agreement. To apply from 1 July each year using the Rise and Fall Adjustment Formula Clause 4.9 that would be submitted at least two weeks before 1 Jul for approval.

This should be addressed by tenderers in Schedule 10 Contract Departures (see updated Returnable Schedules document provided), as part of your submission as it impacts pricing offer made.

publicQuestions.question: Can Council please confirm whether the plant and equipment rates requested under Panel D are intended to be dry hire (equipment only) or wet hire (inclusive of a suitably qualified operator)?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for the query. Council is predominantly looking for wet-hire rates, ie equipment inclusive of a suitably qualified operator.

Whatever is listed just needs to be clearly specified and understandable in the schedule.

publicQuestions.question:
Can Council confirm if you will consider responses for the Urban Forestry component from a consultancy who ONLY provides;

-Tree diagnostic assessment e.g. Picus tomograph, Resistograph

-Specialist arboriculture services for tree health checks and monitoring, including independent AQF level 5 Arborist assessment

-Specialist pest control assessment

and NOT tree & weed management, maintenance and disposal, stump grinding sawmilling?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that it will accept and consider submissions from specialist arboricultural consultancies that provide only a subset of the services listed under the Urban Forestry component, including:

• Tree diagnostic assessments, including PiCUS tomography and Resistograph testing.

• Specialist arboricultural services, including tree health assessments, ongoing monitoring and independent AQF Level 5 arborist assessments.

• Specialist pest and disease assessments.

Respondents are not required to provide the full range of Urban Forestry services, including tree and weed management, maintenance and disposal, stump grinding or sawmilling.

Respondents should clearly identify the services they are submitting for and demonstrate their relevant qualifications, experience and technical capabilities.

All submissions will be assessed in accordance with Council's nominated evaluation criteria and procurement requirements.

publicQuestions.question: Under the Bush regeneration, revegetation and environmental restoration works, (Bush regeneration, revegetation and environmental restoration works – Rope based climbing hours.) Could you please clarify if it is for a sole climber e.g. Certificate 3 Arborist or if it is for a team (e.g. 1 climber and 1 rescue climber) Where a climber has limited bush regeneration experience, can they work under the guidance of an appropriately experienced and qualified person.
publicQuestions.answer: The hours for rope-based climbing are usually recorded as a team with details of the team’s configuration to be outlined within the returnable pricing schedule. Any information regarding personnel experience and qualifications including trainee staff should be outlined in the appropriate section of the returnable schedules.

The pricing schedules for Panels B and C state that at the conclusion of each financial year, being 30 June, the tenderer may review its schedule of rates for the following financial year.

Clause 4.3(2) of the Panel Services Agreement and clause 4.1 of Annexure 1 instead say rates cannot be varied until 12 months after the contract starts. Which applies?

The 1 July date suits both Council and contractors. Works under each order are to be completed by 30 June (RFT clause 2.6) and Council issues new purchase orders from 1 July, so a rate change on that date never falls part-way through an order or a budget year. 1 July is also when the mandatory annual wage increases take effect, and wages are more than 85% of a contractor's costs for this work. Annual CPI figures line up with the financial year as well so there is clean data.

The other issue with a review tied to the anniversary of execution or commencement is that the RFT gives only an indicative timetable for those dates. For this program, our services could include:

Weed, vegetation and habitat mapping to help target and plan works.

Baseline and repeat surveys of bush regeneration, creekline, wetland and post-fire recovery sites.

Mapped records of erosion, access and visible infrastructure condition.

Spatial reporting linking completed works with subsequent observations, supporting program reporting and funding acquittals.

If you are already in business as a minimum some level of Public Liability insurance is required to cover you in case of injury or damage to a third party. Motor vehicle registration and insurance. Proof of insurance when submitting a tender is preferred or details for what arrangements would be put in place."},{"askedAt":"2026-11-19T02:24:00.000Z","question":"Hi Blue Mountains City Council,

title: 2027-007 Whyanbeel Water Main Replacement
description:
Douglas Shire Council (DSC) invites Tenders from suitably qualified Contractors for the design and construction of the Whyanbeel Water Main Replacement along Karnak Road and Whyanbeel Road, Whyanbeel. The Works include completion, coordination, verification and RPEQ certification of the Principal-supplied tender / Preliminary Design to

Issue for Construction status, together with the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of the new water main and associated fittings, valves, hydrants, scours, air valves, property service connections, trenchless sections, the Lombardi crossing, earthworks, temporary works, service protection and relocation, cut-ins to the existing

network, restoration and as-constructed documentation.

title: WT19-25/26 Construction of reticulation Sewer Gravity Main at Gannan Street, Clifton
description:
Clifton is a rural town in the Toowoomba Region, Queensland, located south of Toowoomba City. The town’s wastewater infrastructure, much of which dates to 1971, is reaching the end of its useful life. A sewer system includes pipelines that convey wastewater and manholes that provide access for inspection and maintenance. As Clifton grows, the existing system is no longer adequate to meet current and future demands.

The existing reticulation sewer main along the northern edge of properties on Gannan Street has deteriorated and experiences frequent failures, leading to high maintenance costs and service disruptions. The Clifton Sewer Gravity Main Inspection confirmed the system is no longer fit for purpose and identified this section for replacement to improve reliability.

The project involves constructing approximately 410 m of new reticulation sewer main in accordance with the approved IFC Design Drawings, replacing the existing main. The new alignment will be located on land north of Gannan Street along Wiedman Road.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Penrith City Council (Council) undertakes a range of Road Transport activities involving heavy vehicles, plant, materials, road construction and maintenance, waste transport and services, material transport, deliveries, loading and unloading activities, and the engagement of external contractors and suppliers.

These activities place Council and its personnel in various roles within the Heavy Vehicle National Law (HVNL) Chain of Responsibility (CoR) framework. Council has recently undertaken an audit which has identified CoR compliance gaps within the organisation that require improvement. These identified gaps being addressed will form a key part to this project but are not to limit the outcomes of the project to only these items.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced consultant to undertake a review of Council’s current Chain of Responsibility arrangements and develop a comprehensive:

•	Chain of Responsibility Policy;

•	Safety Management System;

•	Chain of Responsibility Management Plan;

•	Chain of Responsibility Procedure;

•	Continuous Improvement Strategy; and

•	Training program.

Supporting Documentation

Respondents may provide any supporting documentation where relevant, including:

•	Fee Proposal / Pricing Schedule (mandatory)

•	Project Methodology

•	Resumes of key personnel

•	Relevant project case studies

•	Referee details

•	Example deliverables or templates

Supporting documentation will be considered in conjunction with the respondent's criteria responses.
buyerQuestions: Describe your understanding of Penrith City Council's operating environment, Chain of Responsibility (CoR) obligations, and the key compliance and operational risks associated with Council-owned and contractor-operated heavy vehicle activities. Demonstrate your understanding of Heavy Vehicle National Law (HVNL) requirements, contractor and supply chain responsibilities, Council's identified compliance improvement objectives, and the transition from NHVAS to Heavy Vehicle Accreditation (HVA), including General Safety Accreditation (GSA) and Maintenance Assurance Program (MAP) requirements. Outline the critical success factors required to establish a practical, risk-based and auditable CoR framework across Council.

Describe the methodology you will use to deliver the project from commencement through to final implementation. Include your approach to legislative and regulatory review, current-state assessment, operational review, CoR role mapping, risk assessment, gap analysis, development of the Policy, Safety Management System, Management Plan, Procedure, training framework, supporting documentation, audit framework and implementation roadmap. Explain how your methodology will ensure practical implementation outcomes, stakeholder ownership, compliance assurance and continuous improvement across Council's operations.

Describe how you will engage with Council stakeholders to identify, validate and document CoR obligations, operational risks, accountabilities and existing controls. Include your approach to consultation with Executive Leadership Team members, Directors, Managers, Fleet and Workshop Operations, Construction and Maintenance teams, Waste Operations, Procurement, Contract Management, Risk and Governance, WHS, Human Resources and relevant contractors. Explain how interviews, workshops, site inspections and operational observations will be used to assess both documented processes and actual operational practices.

Provide evidence of your organisation's experience delivering comparable Chain of Responsibility, heavy vehicle compliance, governance, risk management, NHVAS and/or HVA projects. Include examples involving local government, government agencies, heavy vehicle operators, infrastructure or civil construction environments. Outline the qualifications, experience and technical expertise of the personnel proposed for this project and describe tangible outcomes achieved for previous clients, including implementation, compliance improvement, accreditation outcomes or risk reduction measures.

Demonstrate how your proposal represents value for money while ensuring delivery of all project requirements and outcomes. Describe how your proposed methodology, resourcing, project controls, stakeholder engagement approach, implementation support and knowledge transfer activities contribute to achieving successful project outcomes.
Respondents must provide a detailed fee proposal guided by the details in Section 21, of the Consultant Brief CoR Policy Management Plan and Procedure Framework. The fee proposal may be submitted as a separate attachment (spreadsheet format preferred) and must clearly identify all project costs, including project stages, deliverables, resource allocations, assumptions, exclusions, optional services, hourly and daily rates for additional services, and any post-delivery support arrangements.
Council will consider both the proposed price and the overall value offered, including the quality of the proposed service, methodology, experience, resources, risk management approach and anticipated project outcomes.

Provide details of your organisation's physical presence and business operations within the Penrith Local Government Area (LGA), including information requested under Quotation Schedule 1, Section 1.4. State whether your organisation is permanently based within the Penrith LGA, employs permanent staff operating from permanent premises within the Penrith LGA, and the duration of this presence.
If your organisation is not locally based, describe how you will support the local community, ensure accessibility to Council stakeholders, provide timely onsite support and maintain an effective presence throughout delivery of the project. Include any local partnerships, subcontractors or regional resources that will be utilised.

title: PR000138 - Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement
description:
Charters Towers Regional Council invites tenders from suitably qualified respondents to complete the works required for the Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement Project.

This project, Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement, includes the replacement of the existing elevated walkway to access the Weir Tower during flood inundation events. The project will include the removal and demolition of the existing structural steel walkway including the platform and handrails. The existing steel trestles will be maintained and remediated (abrasive blasted and painted).

Further information can be found in the Tender documentation.

Council reserves the right to invite all tenderers to change their tenders to take account of a change in the tender specification.

Council's representative for this tender is Paul Weston, Procurement & Depot Coordinator, who can be contacted on 07 4761 5300.

•	Where butting frame sections. Are specified as 6 CFW to be a part penetration butt weld of equivalent DTT applied or full penetration?

publicQuestions.answer: Please see recently uploaded attachment "Question Responses #1"

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

We currently reviewing the tender documentation for the Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement (PR000138).

We would like to seek clarification on whether Council would consider an alternative design incorporating Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) structural members in selected sections of the proposed walkway, in lieu of the specified steel members.

Under our proposed approach, the new intermediate trestle would remain steel, as specified in the tender documentation, while selected walkway structural components would be replaced with suitable FRP members.

Any proposed alternative would be subject to structural engineering verification and compliance with the relevant Australian Standards, design loads, performance requirements and project specifications.

Could Council please confirm:

1. Whether an alternative design incorporating FRP structural members would be acceptable for consideration.

2. Whether such an alternative could be submitted as part of our tender response, subject to supporting engineering documentation and approval.

We appreciate your clarification and look forward to your response.
publicQuestions.answer:
Respondents may submit an alternate response, however, are encouraged to do so as per clause 5.6 of the Procurement Process Conditions (included with the RFQ package).

Council has no objections to alternative design incorporating FRP structural members. That is on the basis that the Contractor submits, as part of their tender, construction issue drawing signed by an RPEQ which demonstrate compliance with the relevant Australian Standards, design loads, performance requirements, and project specifications.

Please note that all components including the handrails shall be designed and certified to be structurally adequate to both the log impact and debris loads to AS5100:2018 as defined on the Lancini Consulting Engineers drawing T26022-S002 Rev 0.

The Contractor must also demonstrate within the construction programme the impact to timeline for Fabrication drawing development prior to fabrication commences.

Tenders are invited from qualified entities to undertake the replacement of the existing Cuttagee Bridge at Cuttagee Lake with a new two lane structure with a shared path and barriers, and associated roadworks and ancillary work.

The Works include construction of a Temporary Bridge and Track to facilitate public traffic access while the existing bridge is demolished, and the replacement bridge is constructed.

Pre-tender meetings will be held:

•	Online via MS Teams on Thursday, 12 November 2026 at 10:00am AEDT

•	MANDATORY - Onsite at project location (Southern end of existing bridge) on Wednesday, 18 November 2026 at 1:00pm AEDT

Tenderers are to register via VendorPanel confirming attendee names and contact details a minimum of two business days prior to each session.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
** ABOUT THE BEGA VALLEY **

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

** ABOUT COUNCIL **

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

** WHAT COUNCIL DOES **

Provide and maintain community facilities such as:
•	Parks and sportsgrounds
•	Playgrounds and skate parks
•	Sapphire Aquatic centre Pambula and swimming pools throughout the shire
•	Sports and recreation facilities throughout the Shire
•	Local libraries in Bega, Bermagui, Eden and Merimbula
•	Preschools and Childcare centres in Bega and Eden, and our Mobile service for Candelo and Bemboka
•	Merimbula Airport, Bega Saleyards and Cemeteries throughout the Shire

We care for the environment by:
•	Managing and enhancing bushland areas
•	Providing environmental and waste education and recycling services
•	Responding to pollution incidents and prosecuting polluters
•	Monitoring the water quality of the Shire’s estuaries
•	Planting trees and controlling noxious weeds
•	Beneficially recycling and reusing treated effluent

We create a safer place to live by:
•	Maintaining and improving roads, footpaths and stormwater drains
•	Working with emergency organisations such as the Rural Fire Service, State Emergency Service, NSW Police and NSW Surf Life Saving
•	Managing the keeping of companion animals
•	Inspecting food premises
•	Treating and supplying drinking water to our community
•	Treating sewage to a high standard to protect human health

We enhance our community by:
•	Listening to community views
•	Holding citizenship ceremonies, Australia Day Celebrations and the Seniors week luncheon known as the Golden Gig
•	Offering services for seniors, young people, new migrants and people with a disability
•	Providing grants to community organisations
•	Supporting local community groups such as sporting clubs, arts, migrant groups and charities
•	Encouraging and promoting volunteering in our communities

We plan for the future by:
•	Planning and managing the urban environment
•	Preserving heritage sites
•	Consulting with the community about its needs
•	Developing long term strategic plans for Council and the Shire

title: Wilson Plains Road Floodway Construction
description:
Scenic Rim Regional Council situated in South-East Queensland, is recognized for its stunning landscapes and vibrant communities. The Council is dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for residents and visitors through sustainable development and economic growth, partnering with reputable contractors to support ongoing projects.

Scenic Rim Regional Council (“Council” or “Principal”) is seeking tenders in response to this Request for Tender (“RFT”) for the floodway replacement at Wilsons Plains Road.

These works are funded under the Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA) guidelines administered by the Queensland Reconstructions Authority (QRA) with funding from the Queensland and Australian Governments.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Scenic Rim region is a thriving rural paradise set in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range and surrounded by world heritage listed national parks. Home to a population of more than 37,780, the region covers 4248sq km and is located an hour south of Brisbane and an hour inland from the Gold Coast. Known for its breathtaking scenery, it is a popular tourist destination offering visitors plenty to see and do. From its myriad of wineries and art galleries to expansive bushwalking tracks, state of the art equine facilities, growing rural communities and friendly country charm, the Scenic Rim region is a must see destination.

Its main towns are Beaudesert, Boonah, Rathdowney, Kooralbyn, Kalbar, Aratula, Canungra, Tamborine Mountain, Harrisville and Peak Crossing. The region's primary businesses are agricultural/horticultural production, the equine industry and tourism/ecotourism. The Scenic Rim region contains more than 30,000 hectares of parkland, including national parks and council controlled parks. The region also contains three dams: Lake Moogerah, Lake Maroon and Wyaralong Dam. Supported by a thriving economy, a farming industry and a vibrant arts community, the Scenic Rim has a strong community spirit and friendly locals.

title: WT41 – 25/26 Yarraman Landfill Rehabilitation
description:
Spanning a geographical footprint of 12,973 square kilometres, the Toowoomba Regional Council (Council) area is an inclusive and environmentally rich one that embraces the future while respecting the past. As part of Council’s Waste Management Strategy (2021), it has committed to, amongst other things, to implement a Disposal Management Plan, which includes measures to rehabilitate expired landfills and pan for future needs of the region.

The site is located over Lot 366 CSH568 Crown Land Reserves (for Rubbish and Sanitary purposes) and Lot 501 CSH568 Crown Land Reserves (for Forestry Reserve purposes). Council has committed to the capping and rehabilitation of the closed landfill area on D’ Aguilar Highway (A17) as shown in Figure 1 – Locality Plan.

The purpose of this tender is to engage a Contractor to construct a phytocap as part of the rehabilitation and closure plan, that will cap the retired landfill site.

The Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) completed the construction of a new Waste Management Facility adjacent to the old, retired landfill site. As part of the rehabilitation of this site and to formally lodge the Closure Plan with DETSI, the retired site needs to be formally capped to engineer’s design and EA specifications.

The detailed design of a phytocap has been completed by ACT Williams (ATCW) with a full technical specification and Bill of Quantities (BOQ), prepared for pricing.

Offerors can attend a pre-tender site meeting on 7 December 2026 at 10am. Contact Tjaart Grové on tjaart@tituscivil.com.au to confirm attendance.

services, asset information management and associated reporting and contract administration.

publicQuestions.question: Reading the tender documents and on page 9 of the Returnable Schedule - Schedule 7 Lump Sum offer with the breakdown of service categories, are we able to quote for the Annual Essential Safety Measures, Mechanical, Electrical and Fire only?
publicQuestions.answer: Council's preferred contracting model is to appoint a single Head Contractor responsible for the delivery and management of the full scope of Building Maintenance Services, including Fire, Electrical, Hydraulics, HVAC and other associated services. This approach is intended to provide Council with a single point of accountability, consistent service delivery and streamlined contract administration. Accordingly, Council does not intend to consider non-conforming tenders that propose splitting the scope into separate contracts. However, Council recognises the specialist expertise offered by individual service providers and actively encourages specialist contractors to participate in the tender process by partnering with a suitably qualified Head Contractor, either through subcontracting arrangements or as part of a broader service delivery team. Council welcomes such arrangements, provided the Head Contractor retains overall responsibility and accountability for the delivery of the full scope of services in accordance with the tender requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
[Clarification Request – Current Service Delivery & Contract History]

Dear Procurement Team,

To better understand the baseline operational context for this project, could Council please provide clarification on the following:

1. Who currently delivers the building maintenance services across the facilities?

2. Under what contracts or arrangements are the present services currently governed?

Thank you for your assistance!
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Council is not at liberty to divulge any information regarding the incumbent service providers, other than that which is already in the public domain.

Q2. The new Contract will be substantially different from the existing arrangements, which were set up as part of a multi-Council engagement with the market.

publicQuestions.question:
Please confirm whether certification to ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 is mandatory, or whether equivalent in house designed and implemented management systems are acceptable.

Where the initial asset verification identifies additional assets or materially different quantities, will the recurring PPM and ESM lump sum be adjusted to reflect the verified scope?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Please refer to Schedule 6 and Schedule 11 of the Returnable Schedules. Tenderers are requested to provide details of their current systems for work health and safety management, quality management and environmental management, and how they will be applied to this contract. There is no explicit ISO compliance or certification requirement.

Q2. Please refer to the Returnable Schedules - Schedule 7: Lump Sum Offer, and Clause 2.4 of the Technical Specification. The successful Tenderer will be required to breakdown their PPM and ESM pricing on a ‘per building’ basis within the first thirty (30) days of Contract Award. This breakdown will then be used to benchmark and assess additional PPM and ESM tasks which may arise following the asset data verification process. The recurring PPM and ESM lump sum will then be adjusted accordingly.

title: RFQ2627/005 - Forrest Avenue Wisbey Street Roundabout Detailed Design
description:
The City is seeking an experienced design consultant to undertake the detailed design of a new roundabout at the intersection of Forrest Avenue and Wisbey Street.

The upgrade is being driven by the development of the new South West Aboriginal Medical Service (SWAMS) Health Hub at Jaycee Park. The additional traffic and access demands generated by the facility require the existing intersection to be upgraded to a roundabout to maintain safe and efficient operation for all road users.

The City is providing a concept design, which the successful consultant will develop through to a construction-ready detailed design. The design is to address civil works, stormwater drainage, street lighting and service/utility design and coordination, with due consideration given to road safety, construction and whole-of-life cost, and asset lifecycle.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
SWAMS is developing a new Health Hub at Jaycee Park, which is currently under construction and scheduled to open in 2027. As a condition of the Health Hub development approval, SWAMS is required to construct a roundabout at the intersection of Forrest Avenue and Wisbey Street to provide safe access to the facility from Forrest Avenue.

The City is project-managing the design and construction of the roundabout on behalf of SWAMS.

A concept design and a Road Safety Audit have been prepared for the intersection by Shawmac, and are provided with this Request for Quote as the basis for the detailed design (Appendices C and D). The City is also arranging a geotechnical and environmental investigation, which is expected to be available by January 2027 and will be provided to the successful consultant.

A new Transbunbury bus stop to service the new Health Hub is included in the concept plan as a future provision only. The City has been corresponding with the PTA regarding the proposed bus stop / embayment and will supply the correspondence to the successful consultant.

Good morning,

During our review of the tender documentation, we noted that Request-Appendix_C-Forrest_Av_Wisbey_St_Roundabout_Road_Safety_Audit contains a completed Feasibility Design Road Safety Audit prepared by Anthony Anastas and Richard Jois of Shawmac Traffic & Safety. The audit identifies itself as a Feasibility Design Audit undertaken during the concept development phase.

To ensure consistent interpretation of the RFQ requirements, could the City please clarify the following:

Does the Road Safety Audit provided in Appendix C satisfy the road safety audit requirements for the project scope?

Is the successful consultant required to engage an independent Road Safety Auditor to undertake an additional audit during the detailed design phase?

If an additional audit is required, please confirm:

The required audit stage (e.g. Stage 2, Stage 3, or other).

Whether the audit is to be included within the consultant's lump sum fee.

Whether the audit is to be treated as a provisional sum or optional service.

If a further audit is required, are there any requirements for Main Roads WA accreditation or specific auditor qualifications?

This clarification will assist us in preparing a consistent and comparable fee proposal.

Thank you for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Appendix C. No, the Road Safety Audit at Appendix C does not satisfy the road safety audit requirements of this RFQ. As noted in clause 2.2, it was undertaken on the development application plans and pre-dates the concept design at Appendix D. It is provided for information. Under clause 2.3, the Consultant is to review it at Stage 1 and address its findings in the design, including the lighting finding (clause 2.5.4(e)). A separate audit of the concept design is not required.

2.	Additional audit required. Yes. Under clause 2.5.6, the Consultant is to arrange a Stage 3 (Detailed Design) Road Safety Audit in accordance with Austroads Guide to Road Safety Part 6. The Consultant is also to respond to the audit findings in a Road Safety Audit Response Report. This is the only audit required under this contract.

3.	Pricing.

Price the auditor's fee as the provisional sum at Item 6 of the Price Schedule. It is included in the Total Lump Sum Price for comparison purposes and will be adjusted to the actual, substantiated cost. Responding to the audit and amending the design for accepted findings are core design work. Include that effort in the stage prices.

4.	Auditor requirements. As stated in clause 2.5.6, the audit is to be undertaken by a suitably qualified auditor who is accredited by Main Roads WA and independent of the Consultant's design team. Respondents should name the proposed auditor or audit team leader in their submission and give their accreditation details. The successful Consultant must give the City evidence of the auditor's accreditation and independence before engaging them.

Can you provide the evaluation weightings for quality, price, Local Industry, Social Procurement and Environmental criteria?

 Is supplier-hosted eLearning acceptable, and which SCORM/xAPI, WCAG and reporting requirements are mandatory?

Can you confirm pre-existing curriculum, methodology and IP remain supplier property if customised?

Schedule 3 requires four references while Schedule 14 requires three. Can the same referees be used in both?

Which Victorian Child Safe Standards requirements apply if training is delivered only to adult Council employees?
publicQuestions.answer:
Would it be possible to offer some clarification on the following:

What annual volumes, session numbers, workforce groups and delivery-mode split are anticipated for Category 4?

Council is unable to guarantee annual volumes, session numbers or a fixed delivery-mode split for Category 4. Training will be engaged on an as-required basis throughout the contract term, based on identified organisational and workforce needs.

Council currently employs approximately 1,000 staff across a diverse workforce, including corporate/office-based, community-based, operational, field-based and customer-facing employees, as well as people leaders. Delivery requirements may include face-to-face, virtual instructor-led, eLearning and blended learning, depending on the training requirement and target audience.

How many Category 4 suppliers will be appointed and how will call-off work be allocated?

Council has not predetermined a fixed number of suppliers to be appointed to Category 4. Appointments will be determined through the tender evaluation process based on the submissions received and Council’s requirements. Appointment to the panel does not guarantee any minimum volume of work. Services will be engaged on an as-required basis, and Council may engage one or more panel providers for a particular training requirement, having regard to the nature of the requirement, relevant expertise, availability, suitability and value for money.

Can you provide the evaluation weightings for quality, price, Local Industry, Social Procurement and Environmental criteria?

Council is not publishing the valuation weightings for this process.

Is supplier-hosted eLearning acceptable, and which SCORM/xAPI, WCAG and reporting requirements are mandatory?

Council’s preference is we host eLearning on our LMS

Can you confirm pre-existing curriculum, methodology and IP remain supplier property if customised?

Tenderers should refer to the Intellectual Property provisions contained within the tender documentation. Where a tenderer proposes an alternative arrangement in relation to pre-existing intellectual property, curriculum, methodology or customised materials, this should be clearly identified as a departure or proposed alternative in the tender response. Any proposed departures will be considered as part of the tender evaluation process.

Schedule 3 requires four references while Schedule 14 requires three. Can the same referees be used in both?

Yes. The same referees may be used to satisfy the reference requirements in Schedules 3 and 14, provided the information supplied meets the requirements of each Schedule. Tenderers must still provide the minimum number required under each Schedule. Accordingly, at least four references should be provided to satisfy Schedule 3.

Which Victorian Child Safe Standards requirements apply if training is delivered only to adult Council employees?

Council is a child safe organisation. Where training is delivered solely to adult Council employees, child safety requirements will apply as relevant to the services being delivered. Successful tenderers will work with Council’s Child Safety Officer to determine the appropriate child safety requirements and content for the training and intended audience.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Category 4 - Delivery modes

For Category 4 (Discretionary Training), will Council consider providers offering face-to-face and virtual instructor-led training only, or is the capability to provide self-paced eLearning also a mandatory requirement?

2. Category 4 - Scope of services

Can tenderers nominate and respond to selected training topics within Category 4, based on their areas of expertise, or are they required to demonstrate capability across all topics listed in this category?

3. Rapid Global - Registration requirements and fees

The tender documentation requires tenderers to register with Rapid Global at Risk Level 6 and upload relevant documentation before submission, while noting that full compliance is only required for successful tenderers.

Could Council please confirm whether tender-stage registration and questionnaire completion are free of charge, with any applicable annual subscription fee only becoming payable if a tenderer is successfully appointed to the panel?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Category 4 - Delivery modes

For Category 4 (Discretionary Training), will Council consider providers offering face-to-face and virtual instructor-led training only, or is the capability to provide self-paced eLearning also a mandatory requirement?

Yes. Council will consider Category 4 providers offering face-to-face and virtual instructor-led training only. Self-paced eLearning is not a mandatory requirement for Category 4. Council is open to a range of delivery modalities, and tenderers should clearly identify the delivery modes they are able to provide.

2. Category 4 - Scope of services

Can tenderers nominate and respond to selected training topics within Category 4, based on their areas of expertise, or are they required to demonstrate capability across all topics listed in this category?

Tenderers may nominate and respond to selected training topics within Category 4 based on their areas of expertise. Tenderers are not required to demonstrate capability across all topics listed within the category and should clearly identify the topics for which they are tendering.

3. Rapid Global - Registration requirements and fees

The tender documentation requires tenderers to register with Rapid Global at Risk Level 6 and upload relevant documentation before submission, while noting that full compliance is only required for successful tenderers.

Could Council please confirm whether tender-stage registration and questionnaire completion are free of charge, with any applicable annual subscription fee only becoming payable if a tenderer is successfully appointed to the panel?

Tenderers are required to register with Rapid Global at the Risk Level specified in the tender documentation as part of the tender submission requirements. Tenderers are responsible for any costs associated with completing the required Rapid Global registration process, including any applicable registration or subscription fees. At the tender stage, tenderers are required to complete the registration requirements identified in the tender documentation. Full compliance with all applicable Rapid Global requirements is only required for tenderers who are successfully appointed.

publicQuestions.answer:
For a Category 4 offer limited to live, non-accredited workshops on Psychological Safety and Managing Stress and Burnout, does Council require a TAE qualification or RTO involvement, or can the facilitator demonstrate the Section D requirements through relevant postgraduate qualifications, current professional development and adult facilitation experience?

For live, non-accredited Category 4 workshops, including Psychological Safety and Managing Stress and Burnout, Council does not require a TAE qualification or Registered Training Organisation involvement. Facilitators may demonstrate the requirements through relevant qualifications, current professional development, subject matter expertise and demonstrated adult facilitation experience. Where nationally recognised or accredited training is proposed, the relevant qualification and regulatory requirements will apply.

Schedule 3 requests four similar contracts from the past three years, while Schedule 14 requests at least three references. For a sole practitioner, will Council accept a mix of the practice’s contracts and relevant work delivered personally in previous employment, clearly identified as such? If the practitioner cannot disclose a former employer’s contract value, what evidence will Council accept in that field?

Council will accept relevant experience from both the tenderer's current practice and work personally delivered through previous employment, provided this is clearly identified in the submission. References should relate to comparable services and demonstrate the practitioner's relevant experience and capability.

Where a contract value from previous employment is confidential, unavailable or cannot be disclosed, the tenderer may state "Confidential/Unable to disclose" and provide sufficient alternative information to demonstrate the scale and relevance of the engagement, such as the nature and scope of services, client type, duration, participant numbers and the practitioner's role.

For an owner-operated provider delivering to adult staff, which Level 6 documents should be uploaded to the Amalgamated Councils of Victoria workspace for any inapplicable employee or workers compensation items?

Once you have registered and logged in to Rapid Global at the required risk level, the system will prompt you for the required documentation relevant to that risk level.

publicQuestions.question:
Tender 2627-23 – Clarification regarding delivery modes

Section D (Scope of Services – General) states that providers "may offer one or more delivery channels" and "may tender for a single category or multiple categories". However, the Delivery Requirements section states that providers "must demonstrate capability to deliver" face-to-face, virtual instructor-led, self-paced eLearning and blended training.

Category 3 (Mandatory and Compliance Training) requires topics to be available "as self-paced eLearning modules and, where requested, facilitated workshops".

Could Council please confirm:

Whether a tenderer that responds to Category 3 only, and offers self-paced eLearning only (including SCORM/xAPI content compatible with Council's LMS or delivered through a hosted platform), will be considered a conforming tender.

Whether the formats listed under Delivery Requirements are mandatory for every category tendered, or are evaluated as a preference in line with the Scope of Services – General statement.

Whether tenderers that do not offer a delivery mode should enter "N/A" against the corresponding line items in Schedule 2 (Schedule of Rates).
publicQuestions.answer:
Section D (Scope of Services – General) states that providers "may offer one or more delivery channels" and "may tender for a single category or multiple categories". However, the Delivery Requirements section states that providers "must demonstrate capability to deliver" face-to-face, virtual instructor-led, self-paced eLearning and blended training.

The delivery formats listed under Delivery Requirements are intended to describe the range of delivery modes Council is seeking across the panel. Tenderers are not required to provide every delivery mode for every category. Tenderers may offer one or more delivery channels, with preference given to providers that can support multiple delivery methods where relevant to the category and services offered.

Category 3 (Mandatory and Compliance Training) requires topics to be available "as self-paced eLearning modules and, where requested, facilitated workshops".

A tenderer responding to Category 3 only may offer self-paced eLearning without also providing facilitated delivery. Tenderers should clearly identify the delivery modes offered and demonstrate how their proposed solution meets the relevant Category 3 and eLearning requirements.

Could Council please confirm:

Whether a tenderer that responds to Category 3 only, and offers self-paced eLearning only (including SCORM/xAPI content compatible with Council's LMS or delivered through a hosted platform), will be considered a conforming tender.

Yes. A tenderer responding to Category 3 only may offer self-paced eLearning only, including SCORM/xAPI-compatible content integrated with Council’s LMS. The absence of facilitated workshop delivery will not, in itself, make the tender non-conforming. Tenderers must otherwise meet the relevant requirements of the tender documentation.

Whether the formats listed under Delivery Requirements are mandatory for every category tendered, or are evaluated as a preference in line with the Scope of Services – General statement.

The delivery formats listed under Delivery Requirements describe the range of delivery modes Council is seeking across the panel. Tenderers are not required to provide every delivery mode for every category.

Tenderers may offer one or more delivery channels, with preference given to providers that can support multiple delivery methods where relevant to the category and services offered. This is consistent with the general scope, which allows providers to offer one or more delivery channels.

Whether tenderers that do not offer a delivery mode should enter "N/A" against the corresponding line items in Schedule 2 (Schedule of Rates).

Yes. Where a delivery mode or fee does not apply to the tenderer’s proposed services, tenderers should enter “N/A” against the corresponding item in Schedule 2. The Schedule specifically directs tenderers to indicate “N/A” where a fee is not applicable

publicQuestions.answer: Council is a child safe organisation. Where training is delivered solely to adult Council employees, child safety requirements will apply as relevant to the services being delivered. Successful tenderers will work with Council’s Child Safety Officer to determine the appropriate child safety requirements and content for the training and intended audience.
