publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

I have a few questions about the SHS/PTM Wellington Rd tender

1. What are the outputs and associated reporting requirements for SHS?

2.	What is the split of the room types - studio, 2 bedroom, 3 bedroom in the 40 unit complex and the units for the 20 families?

3.	Could you please clarify what the statement (“The provision of 24/7 support/concierge will work alongside PTM services’’) means for the SHS working alongside PTM services in terms of scope and the dept’s expectations

a.	More specifically, is the expectation the CHP PTM will have staff 24/7 as well as the SHS and what provision will be in place to contact the CHP/PTM when an issue arises during and after hours

4.	Could you please define ‘concierge’ services, in terms of scope and the depts expectations for the SHS services

5.	Could you please clarify who will be on the Allocation Panels:

a.	In the Statement of Requirements on p 3 it includes the RCHP and Fortitude Valley Housing Service Centre and on p 6 it states the SHS provider will participate in the Allocation Panel and Governance Group meetings.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum No 2 for responses to the above questions.

publicQuestions.question:
In Attachment 1 - Statement of Requirements, it states that the RCHP is required to use rental income for:

"sourcing and purchasing of communal furniture and unit furniture fit out"

Will the Dept be providing funding to the RCHP for establishment costs including purchase of assets, set up salary costs, furniture and fittings, whitegoods, and equipment?
publicQuestions.answer:
No, the Registered Community Housing Provider will not receive funding for establishment costs, including asset purchases, staffing establishment costs, furniture and fittings, whitegoods, equipment, or other set-up expenses.

Respondents are responsible for demonstrating how these costs will be met within a financially sustainable operating model. The respondent's proposal should clearly outline its financial capacity and the ongoing sustainability of the proposed service model, consistent with the relevant evaluation criteria and information requirements outlined in the procurement documents.

publicQuestions.question: The resolution on the Wellington Road Plans is extremely low and impossible to read. Are you able to provide higher resolution plans please.
publicQuestions.answer:
There is an opportunity for providers to attend a non-mandatory site walkthrough of Wellington Road, East Brisbane on Thursday 19 November 2026.

Providers interested in attending are requested to register their interest by Thursday, 12 November 2026.

Following the close of registrations, further information regarding the confirmed date, time and attendance arrangements will be provided directly to registered providers, noting attendance is limited to one representative per organisation.

Detailed architectural drawings are not available for release through this procurement process. The plans included in the procurement documentation are indicative only and are provided to assist respondents in understanding the location and arrangement of shared common areas, residential spaces, and non-residential spaces. Respondents should base their submissions on the information contained in the procurement documentation and observations made during the site walkthrough.

publicQuestions.question:
Could you please clarify:

Are the concierge hours counted towards the minimum 3,931 case management hours a year in the contract?

And if so, what are the counting rules?
publicQuestions.answer:
No. The minimum annual requirement of 3,931 case management hours relates to the delivery of specialist homelessness support and case management services for families accommodated within the Supportive Housing program.

The 24/7 onsite concierge service is a separate service requirement, and concierge hours are not counted towards the minimum 3,931 case management hours per year.

publicQuestions.question:
Could you please clarify:

The Statement of Requirements says the housing provider “will also manage the office space”, and its mobilisation tasks include “property fit out”. It’s responsible for “communal and unit furniture fit out”, but the documents don’t say who furnishes the support service’s office. Who is responsible for furnishing the office?
publicQuestions.answer:
The procurement documents do not specifically allocate responsibility for furnishing the support service office. The department anticipates that the successful Registered Community Housing Provider and Specialist Homelessness Service provider will work collaboratively during mobilisation to determine office accommodation arrangements and any associated furnishing or fit-out requirements.

Respondents should outline any assumptions underpinning their proposed operating model, including any assumptions regarding office accommodation and associated fit-out requirements.

publicQuestions.question: Could you please clarify if the concierge is expected to manage visitors to the building?
publicQuestions.answer: The department has not prescribed detailed operational responsibilities for the concierge role beyond the requirements outlined in the procurement documentation. The Specialist Homelessness Services provider is required to deliver a 24/7 onsite support/concierge service staffed at a minimum SCHADS Award Level 5. Respondents should describe their proposed service model, including how visitor management, resident engagement and site presence will be delivered, where relevant. Responsibility for security functions, including monitoring access to premises and deterring unauthorised access, sits with the Registered Community Housing Provider through the provision of onsite security services.

publicQuestions.question: When the SCHADS level 5 practitioners respond to a crisis as part of family case plan, can those hours be counted towards the 3931 annual case management hours?
publicQuestions.answer:
No. Where a staff member is rostered to perform the 24/7 support/concierge function, those hours are not counted towards the minimum annual requirement of 3,931 case management hours, regardless of whether the staff member responds to incidents, crises or support needs during that shift. A 24/7 support/concierge position is required to ensure there is always appropriately skilled onsite support available.

The minimum annual requirement of 3,931 case management hours relates to the delivery of specialist homelessness support and case management services and is separate to the requirement to provide a 24/7 onsite support/concierge service. Providers should ensure that case management hours and concierge hours are separately identified and recorded.

publicQuestions.question: Could you please clarify the concierge role: is the concierge expected to be at the desk 24/7 or are they expected to respond to crises, incidents and matters within the building?
publicQuestions.answer: The department has not prescribed a specific operating model for the concierge function, including whether the concierge is required to remain at a reception desk at all times. The requirement is for a 24/7 onsite support/concierge service staffed by appropriately skilled personnel at a minimum SCHADS Award Level 5 to ensure appropriately skilled onsite support is available at all times. Respondents should outline their proposed operating model and demonstrate how it will meet this requirement. The department expects the concierge function to support residents through an onsite presence and provision of support services; however, providers may determine the most appropriate balance between maintaining availability onsite and responding to support needs, crises, incidents and other matters that arise within the building. Security responsibilities remain the responsibility of the Registered Community Housing Provider through the provision of onsite security services.

publicQuestions.question:
Question 1: The successful SHS provider will be responsible for delivering support services to families in only 20 of the 40 dwellings. How does the department propose that the SHS provider manage the families from the other 20 units, who are not the SHS's clients when presenting with support needs or assistance in relation to confidentiality, privacy, safety and offering a duty of care?

Question 2: Can we also please request a copy of the lease?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question 1 Answer: The department expects respondents to outline in their submission how they would manage interactions within the development, including arrangements for responding to support needs, maintaining privacy and confidentiality, managing safety concerns, and meeting relevant duty of care obligations.

While the successful Specialist Homelessness Services provider will be contracted to deliver support services to families residing in the 20 dwellings designated for the Supportive Housing program, respondents should demonstrate how they would work within a shared residential environment and collaborate with other onsite stakeholders, including referral pathways, escalation processes and protocols for responding to issues involving residents who are not their clients.

Respondents should clearly articulate any assumptions, roles, responsibilities and operational arrangements that underpin their proposed service delivery model.

Question 2 Answer: The draft lease is currently undergoing final review. The department acknowledges the importance of this document to respondents and is working to release it as soon as possible. Once finalised, the lease will be issued to all respondents via an addendum on the Vendor Panel website.

publicQuestions.question: Please can you advise if the Specialist Homelessness Services provider is expected to have access to free, onsite office accommodation (managed by the Community Housing Provider), or if there is a cost associated with this or other offsite office accommodation, that should be factored in.
publicQuestions.answer:
As outlined in the Statement of Requirements, the Registered Community Housing Provider will be responsible for managing the office space within the Wellington Road tower.

The Registered Community Housing Provider must grant the successful Specialist Homelessness Services provider access to part of the non-residential space to carry out the support services. This access must not be by way of sub-lease.

The department does not prescribe the detailed operational arrangements between the Registered Community Housing Provider and Specialist Homelessness Services provider. Respondents should outline any assumptions regarding office accommodation and associated operating arrangements within their submission.

publicQuestions.question: Is the Invitation to Offer closing date 10am on Friday 27 November (as stated on the Invitation to Offer documentation) or 11am Tuesday 1 December (as stated on the Vendor Panel website).
publicQuestions.answer:
Please refer to Addendum No 3 that outlines an extension to the closing date/time of 10am AEST on Tuesday 1 December 2026 (and as stated on the Vendor Panel website).

Please also note that the closing date/time for Questions is 10am AEST on Tuesday 24 November 2026.

publicQuestions.question: As onsite support/concierge service staff are to be paid at a minimum SCHADS Level 5, what is the expected pay level for Case Managers?
publicQuestions.answer:
The department has not prescribed a minimum employment classification for Case Managers.

Respondents are expected to propose a service delivery model that aligns with the Statement of Requirements, Supportive Housing Policy and contemporary best practice. As outlined in Criterion 1, respondents must detail their proposed service delivery model, including planned FTE, staffing structure and respective employment levels as reflected in Attachment 2a - Costings Template.

The proposed staffing profile, employment classifications and associated costs will be considered as part of the evaluation of respondents' service delivery model and value for money.

publicQuestions.question: Could the Department please confirm the maximum household composition/number of household members that may be accommodated within each of the 20 Supportive Housing for Families tenancies at Wellington Road, including the maximum household size anticipated for the two-bedroom and three-bedroom properties?
publicQuestions.answer:
Refer to the previous response regarding the dwelling mix and dual-key configuration within the Wellington Road development.

The Wellington Road Building comprises 8 three-bedroom apartments, 24 two-bedroom apartments and 8 studio apartments. The studio apartments are designed to share a common foyer with an adjoining two-bedroom apartment, creating a dual-key arrangement that provides flexibility to accommodate larger family groups while maintaining separate living spaces and privacy.

The Department has not prescribed a maximum household composition or household size for individual tenancies within the development. The successful Registered Community Housing Provider and Specialist Homelessness Service will be responsible for determining appropriate household allocations in accordance with relevant policies, household needs, dwelling size and bedroom configuration.

It is expected that tenancy allocations will be appropriate to the size and configuration of the dwelling, while making effective use of the available housing stock to meet the needs of eligible households.

publicQuestions.question: Can the Department confirm whether the Wellington Road development will be handed over with a fully operational CCTV system, including cameras, recording equipment and monitoring capability? If CCTV installation is not included in the construction scope, is the successful CHP expected to fund and install the system?
publicQuestions.answer:
The Wellington Road development will be handed over with a fully installed and operational CCTV system, including cameras, recording equipment and recording storage capability. Live CCTV viewing will be available from the reception area.

The successful Registered Community Housing Provider will be required to work with the contractor prior to handover to support final system configuration, including preferred camera viewing and monitoring arrangements. Further information regarding the CCTV system and recording storage will be provided to the successful provider following contract award.

The contractor will provide training on the CCTV system, associated equipment and system administration prior to handover.

Any modifications, reconfiguration, upgrades or additions to the CCTV and security system following handover will be the responsibility of, and at the cost of, the successful Registered Community Housing Provider.

publicQuestions.question: Are the CCTV access control system and electronic entry arrangements included in the building works.
publicQuestions.answer: Refer to the response provided regarding CCTV, access control and security systems. These systems are included as part of the building works and will be operational at handover

description:
OVERVIEW

Fraser Coast Regional Council is inviting offers from suitably qualified and experienced Tenderers for CTWW007 - 26/27 - Maryborough Landfill: Cell 9B - Design and Construct.

MANDATORY TENDER BRIEFING

A Tender Briefing is mandatory for this tender. The details are outlined below:

Date: Thursday, 29 October 2026

Time: 10:00am (AEST)

Location: Maryborough Landfill - 269 Ariadne Street, Maryborough QLD 4650 - Main Entrance / Site Office

Booking Required: YES

Point of Contact for Booking: Email - procurement@frasercoast.qld.gov.au

Other Details (incl. Dress Code / PPE): High-visibility shirt or vest; long pants; boots; sunscreen and a wide-brim hat

SUBMISSION OF TENDER DOCUMENTS

Please be advised that tender response forms are to be submitted as three (3) documents only and in the following format:

- Non-Price Response Form: PDF including all supporting documentation as one (1) document. This PDF must not contain any price related criteria.

- Price Response Form: Excel

- Contract Amendments and Particulars: Excel

Failure to comply with this requirement may result in a non-conforming offer.

title: FOGO Marketing, Engagement, Education and Behaviour Change Project
description:
MidCoast Council invites tenders from suitably qualified consultants to design, develop, deliver and evaluate a comprehensive Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) marketing, engagement, education and behaviour change campaign.

The successful Consultant will translate Council’s Education and Behaviour Change Strategy and Plan Framework into a coordinated campaign that helps residents understand the new service, prepare for its introduction and correctly separate food and garden organics.

Services include community research and audience analysis; behaviour change and campaign planning; creative development and message testing; production of accessible content and reusable engagement materials; media planning and buying; community outreach and face-to-face engagement; launch support; ongoing reinforcement; and evaluation and handover.

Tenderers must propose the quantities, formats, frequency, coverage and resources for each deliverable for Council’s assessment, supported by pricing and estimated professional effort in the response schedules.

The proposed consultancy period is contract execution to 30 September 2029, subject to the contract’s milestone and time-adjustment provisions. 1 July 2028 is the planning assumption for facility operations, not a confirmed household FOGO service commencement date. Council will confirm service commencement and authorise date-sensitive activities when facility and collection readiness permit.

Services will support communities across the MidCoast Council local government area, NSW. Research, planning, design and reporting may be undertaken remotely where appropriate. The Consultant must provide on-ground engagement and other attendance required by its accepted delivery proposal.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The consultancy forms part of Council’s integrated FOGO Program, comprising the processing facility, collection service transition, and education and behaviour change projects. The successful Consultant will report to Council’s FOGO Program Manager and coordinate with Waste Services, Communications and Engagement teams, and relevant contractors through Council-approved arrangements.

The MidCoast includes towns, villages and dispersed rural communities with different waste service arrangements. Current arrangements include standard three-bin services, rural two-bin services and properties without a green bin. These arrangements do not, by themselves, establish future FOGO eligibility. Campaign content must use Council-confirmed service information so residents receive instructions applicable to their property and implementation stage.

The campaign must:

- Align with Council’s Education and Behaviour Change Strategy, Plan Framework and branding requirements.

- Address audience needs identified through the supplied evidence and approved research, including accessibility, literacy, digital access and rural communication needs.

- Integrate Council-owned channels with appropriate television, social media, digital, print, newspaper, billboard and other physical media.

- Include reusable materials for community stalls, displays and education activities.

- Provide accessible final outputs and editable source files, templates, records and campaign assets that Council can maintain and adapt.

Facility readiness controls service commencement. Tenderers must demonstrate how they will sequence early research and reusable work, manage approval gates, and reprogram or pause activities while minimising avoidable expenditure. The response schedules include common 3-, 6- and 12-month delay scenarios for evaluation purposes; these are not forecast delays or guaranteed additional work.

Council’s tender documents define the detailed requirements, acceptance criteria, pricing arrangements and conditions of contract.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a practical, evidence-based campaign that builds community understanding and supports correct participation in the FOGO service before, during and after its introduction.

Desired outcomes include:

- Clear, consistent and service-specific information that helps residents understand what changes, when it changes and how to use their service correctly.

- Research-informed messages and activities that address behavioural barriers and motivators.

- Accessible engagement that reaches relevant audiences across the MidCoast.

- Reliable delivery of approved campaign assets, media and community activities.

- Transparent reporting on outputs, reach, engagement and behavioural outcomes, distinguishing the Consultant’s contribution from factors controlled by service design, facility performance or other parties.

- A complete handover that enables Council or another supplier to maintain and adapt the campaign.

Council will assess relevant experience, behaviour change capability, methodology, delivery capacity, program flexibility, demonstrated outcomes and value for money. Tenderers may identify optional enhancements separately, with their benefits and costs clearly stated.

The contract requires defined deliverables, documented approvals, regular program and risk reporting, and written acceptance against agreed criteria. Correction of poor work, errors, omissions or non-compliance is the Consultant’s responsibility and does not consume an included review round.

Publication, launch activities and non-refundable commitments require the applicable written Council approvals. Changes to scope, fees or delivery dates must follow the contract’s authorisation processes. Critical milestones and delay damages apply as specified in Part B.

The Consultant must also meet the contract’s professional standards, insurance, privacy, security, intellectual property, accessibility, records, safety and handover requirements. Council requires transparency about subcontractors, third-party costs, supplier benefits and proposed use of AI.

Subject: RFT VP531174 – FOGO Marketing, Engagement, Education and Behaviour Change – Clarification Questions

Dear David,

Thank you for the opportunity to respond to MidCoast Council's FOGO Marketing, Engagement, Education and Behaviour Change tender.

Having reviewed the documentation, we would appreciate clarification on several matters to ensure our submission is appropriately scoped, accurately costed and aligned with Council's expectations.

1. Indicative budget and available funding (priority)

Could Council please advise whether an indicative budget, approved funding allocation or anticipated contract value has been established for the full program?

Given the breadth of services required across research, strategy, creative development, community engagement, advertising, production, implementation and evaluation, an indicative budget range would assist tenderers in developing proportionate and commercially realistic proposals.

2. Advertising, production and media expenditure

Could Council confirm whether paid media, printing, fabrication, household distribution, research incentives and other third-party production costs are expected to be included within the overall consultancy budget, or whether separate Council-controlled budgets are available for these activities?

If separate budgets exist, could Council provide indicative allocations?

3. Budget allocation across program phases

Has Council established indicative expenditure allocations for the four campaign phases — Have You Heard, Are You Ready, FOGO Is Here and How Is It Going — or is the successful consultant expected to recommend the allocation of resources and expenditure across the entire program?

4. Existing research and campaign assets

Could Council clarify what existing audience research, community consultation findings, behavioural insights, creative assets and communications materials will be available to the successful consultant?

5. Household reach and distribution requirements

Could Council provide an indicative number of households expected to receive the FOGO service and associated education materials, including any known distinctions between urban, regional, rural and multi-unit residential properties?

6. Community engagement delivery

Is Council expecting the consultant to directly resource and deliver all community engagement activities, including staffing, venues, travel and event logistics, or will Council personnel and existing community networks provide delivery support?

7. Council communications resources

Could Council clarify the extent to which its existing communications channels, staff resources, website infrastructure, customer service functions and community engagement networks will be available to support campaign implementation?

8. Campaign performance and evaluation

Does Council have established participation, contamination reduction or behaviour-change targets against which the campaign will be evaluated? Will operational data, including contamination rates and FOGO uptake, be made available to the consultant?

9. Facility readiness and program timing

Given the dependency on the proposed FOGO facility and service commencement, could Council clarify how significant changes to launch timing would affect campaign scheduling, contracted resources and associated costs?

Thank you for your assistance. We look forward to preparing our submission.

Kind regards,

Dr Lisa Portolan

Managing Director

Horizon Communication Group

publicQuestions.question:
Dear David,

Thank you for the opportunity to tender for the FOGO Education and Behaviour Change program. We would be grateful for clarification on the following points.

Contract and program

1. Contract dates: Please confirm the contract execution and commencement dates. Part B (CP03) gives commencement as 1 July 2027, Part A says commencement is to be determined with award in February 2027, and D3.3 refers to execution in January 2027 and to Part B v0.9 (the issued version is v1.1).

2. Timing of service information: When does Council expect to confirm the service details needed for gate G1 (service area and eligible properties, accepted materials, caddy and liner rules, red bin frequency and the collection calendar)?

3. Review process and closures: For the 10-business-day review periods (RV1), will Council provide one consolidated set of comments covering all teams? Will Council be closed over Christmas and New Year, and if so, on which dates?

Households and distribution

4. Household numbers: How many properties currently receive a Council kerbside waste service, and how many will receive the FOGO service? Please break this down by service type (town three-bin, rural two-bin, properties without a green bin) and, if possible, by town or area.

5. Mail-outs and address data: Can Council supply an address list of serviced properties for household distribution, or include FOGO material in an existing Council mailing such as rates notices? If so, at what cost and on what dates?

6. Caddy delivery: We note P2-08 household distribution is to be priced separately. Will Council or its collection contractor supply and deliver kitchen caddies and liners to households, and if so, when is caddy delivery planned, so we can time household materials to arrive close to it?

Outdoor media and events

7. Across-street banners: Does Council have across-street banner tether or anchor points in town main streets? If so, in which towns, how many sites, what banner size do they take, and who installs and removes banners? Are Transport for NSW approvals needed where the main street is a state road?

8. Pole banners: Does Council have pole banner brackets in Taree and other town centres? If so, how many poles are available, what size and fixing do they take, how are sites booked, and who installs the banners?

9. Event stalls: For pop-up stalls at shows, festivals and markets, will Council arrange or pay site fees, or should these be priced in? Does Council have marquees, trailers or other event equipment we can use?

10. Council-owned channels: Which Council channels can carry FOGO content at no cost (website, e-news, social media, on-hold messages, newsletter, noticeboards, libraries and customer service centres), and what are their lead times?

People, engagement and research

11. Staff training: Approximately how many customer service and frontline staff should receive FOGO training, and at which locations? Can Council provide training rooms at no cost?

12. Aboriginal engagement and interpreting: Which Aboriginal organisations and protocols should we work through for Council-facilitated engagement, and are cultural consultation fees expected to be paid by the consultant? Does Council have an existing interpreting arrangement (such as TIS National) we should use?

13. Waste audits: We note audit briefs are developed in the research phase. When does Council plan to carry out the baseline and post-rollout audits, will they be funded by Council outside this contract, and will results be shared with the consultant?

Documents

14. Please provide the documents referenced in Part A section 2 that were not in the tender pack: the Statement of Business Ethics, the WHS Contractor Handbook, and Council's AI and cyber security requirements.

Thank you for your help.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Contract dates

Council anticipates considering the contract award at a Council meeting in February 2027; there is no Council meeting scheduled for January. The contract execution date will depend on the award decision, completion of any necessary negotiations and signing by both parties. The commencement date is 1 July 2027, as stated in Part B (CP03). The reference in D3.3 to Part B v0.9 is an outdated version reference; the issued version is v1.1.

2. Timing of service information

 Council expects to confirm the service details required for gate G1 in January–February 2027.

3. Review process and closures

Council will coordinate its review and provide consolidated comments for each submission within the applicable 10-business-day RV1 review period. Council does not close over Christmas or New Year, except on public holidays.

Households and distribution

4. Household numbers

Council will upload the current household and service-type data separately to the tender.

5. Mail-outs and address data

Council may be able to include FOGO material in a rates notice mail-out; however, this is unlikely to align with the recommended timing for behaviour change and service commencement. Tenderers should therefore price household distribution on the basis that they are responsible for it. Council can provide the successful tenderer with an address list of serviced properties.

6. Caddy delivery

Council’s waste collection contractor will deliver kitchen caddies and liners. Delivery is expected approximately four to six weeks before the FOGO collection service commences. Tenderers should plan household materials to align with that timing.

Outdoor media and events

7. Across-street banners

Council does not have across-street banner sites available for this campaign.

8. Pole banners

Council does not have pole banner sites available for this campaign.

9. Event stalls

Council will pay event site booking fees. Tenderers should include in their pricing a new marquee, banners and interactive stall materials designed specifically for FOGO.

10. Council-owned channels

The successful tenderer may propose content for Council’s external communication channels. The tenderer will prepare the required content including posts, media releases and videos and submit it to Council’s communications officer for review and release through appropriate channels. Channel availability and lead times will be coordinated with Council during delivery.

People, engagement and research

11. Staff training

Approximately 30 customer service staff will require training; numbers may vary with vacancies. Council can provide training rooms at no cost.

12. Aboriginal engagement and interpreting

Council’s Aboriginal Liaison Officer will be the initial contact and will connect the successful tenderer with relevant Aboriginal organisations and advise on appropriate engagement protocols, Council also has an Aboriginal reference group that will also be a channel that the successful tenderer will be connected through. Tenderers should identify any proposed cultural consultation costs in their pricing. Council has not confirmed an interpreting arrangement for this work; any interpreting requirements should be identified in the tender response.

13. Waste audits

Tenderers should provide pricing for the design and delivery of waste audits in the “Options, Alternatives and Departure Prices” section of Schedule D.

Documents

14. Referenced documents

Council uploaded the Statement of Business Ethics, WHS Contractor Handbook and Council AI and cyber security requirements to the tender platform on 27 November 2026.

title: 1583-2026Q RFQ - Dams Condition Audit
description:
The Council seeks to appoint a consultant to undertake condition assessments of six Council-recognised dam assets across the municipality. The audit will establish a consistent baseline of asset condition and information, identify defects and safety-related concerns, and provide practical, asset-specific recommendations for inspection, surveillance, maintenance and ongoing asset management.

The scope of works is generally as depicted in Appendix A, which includes but is not limited to:

•	Review information supplied by Council and prepare an asset-by-asset inspection plan.

•	Inspect the six in-scope dams and assess accessible and observable components, including embankments, spillways, inlet/outlet structures, hydraulic components, downstream areas and public interfaces, as applicable.

•	Assess and grade condition using Council’s five-point condition grading scale at component level, identify and prioritise defects, record photographs and promptly escalate any imminent or potentially serious risks.

•	Recommend asset-specific routine and detailed inspection/surveillance frequencies, event-based triggers, monitoring requirements and maintenance activities. Council has not prescribed frequencies; the consultant must determine and justify them for each asset.

•	Identify component useful life, renewal requirements and estimated costs, and distinguish routine maintenance, repairs, specialist investigations and capital works.

•	Collect and verify asset information and provide editable registers, a consolidated electronic dataset and data dictionary, reports, photographs and annotated plans as required by the specification.

•	Provide an inception submission, six individual dam assessment records/reports, draft and final deliverables, and a close-out briefing.

The six assets included in this commission are:

1. Arthur Streeton Reserve Retarding Basin/Lakes

2. Dalvida Dam

3. Harry Pottage Memorial Reserve Retarding Basin

4. Peck’s Dam

5. Radio Park Retarding Basin

6. Kalparrin Gardens Lake

The consultant must identify any specialist investigations or services considered necessary and clearly distinguish these from the base scope. No intrusive works, operation of asset controls, confined-space entry or disturbance of the dam structure may be undertaken without Council’s prior written approval and appropriate competent personnel and controls. Any proposed additional work must be separately identified and priced and must not proceed without Council’s written approval.

We are reviewing RFT VP532820 for Corpus Christi Primary School and would appreciate clarification on the following:

1. Are there any licence fees, commissions or other charges payable to CSPD or the school? Are any minimum order volumes guaranteed?

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could Council please clarify the extent of the Contractor’s design and certification responsibilities for the Helen Street Footbridge?

In particular, please confirm whether the existing piles/foundations, piers, headstocks, abutments, bearings and primary supporting structure are to remain and are outside the physical replacement/upgrade scope, with the Contractor’s design primarily covering the new FRP deck, railing system, connections/fixings, interfaces and associated temporary works.

Please also confirm:

1. whether the Contractor is required to structurally assess and certify the adequacy of the retained foundations and substructure;

2. whether the nominated 100-year design life applies to the new works only or also to the existing retained structure; and

3. whether Attachment_3-IFC, which appears to comprise the existing 2009 as-built drawings, is provided for reference only, with the Contractor responsible for producing new IFC documentation for the proposed remediation works.

This clarification will assist us in appropriately defining and pricing the required design, investigation and construction scope.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the existing piles/foundations, piers, headstocks, abutments, bearings and primary supporting structure are outside the physical replacement and upgrade scope of works.

The Contractor's design responsibilities are primarily associated with the new FRP deck system, railings, fixings, connections, interfaces with the existing structure, and any associated temporary works required to complete the remediation works. Notwithstanding this, following removal of the existing decking, if any damage to the galvanised protective coating of existing steel girders is identified, the Contractor shall undertake appropriate remedial treatment/touch-up works as required.

In response to the specific queries raised:

1. The Contractor is not required to replace or upgrade the existing foundations or substructure. However, the Contractor is required to assess the proposed new works and verify their loading and structural adequacy on the girders/retained structure. This assessment must demonstrate that the new deck system, railing system, fixings and associated works can be safely supported by the existing structure. Attachment 3 (IFC/As-Built Drawings) includes the original design load considerations and is provided to assist with this assessment.

2. The nominated 100-year design life applies to the new remediation works only.

3. Attachment_3-IFC comprises the existing as-built drawings and is provided for reference purposes only, with the Contractor responsible for producing the design report and new IFC documentation for the proposed remediation works.

publicQuestions.question: The "DESIRED OUTCOME" reference photo in the tender scope specification document shows balustrades with bicycle railings. However, the existing pedestrian bridge's balustrades do not have bicycle railings. Can you please clarify whether bicycle railings are required for the new balustrades?
publicQuestions.answer:
The bridge will be used by both pedestrians and cyclists and therefore the balustrade design shall be suitable for shared-path operation.

The image provided is indicative of the preferred design intent and demonstrates a bicycle-friendly handrail profile integrated with the bridge balustrade. Council's preference is for a balustrade system that accommodates safe use by cyclists while maintaining pedestrian safety, visibility, durability and low maintenance requirements.

title: TRC000544 Supply of High Voltage Asset Maintenance
description: Council is seeking tenders from suitably experienced companies for ongoing implementation of a maintenance program for its High Voltage (HV) Assets listed in the HV Asset List and Schedule of Rates spreadsheet. Council has a requirement to ensure these are adequately maintained in accordance with relevant legislation and industry best practice. Council is committed to providing reliable essential services, and these HV assets are essential to the operation of parts of the water and wastewater networks that Council operates. The primary aim of this contract is to ensure Council has sufficient expertise and capacity to call upon to deliver this service for HV assets.

153 Herries St
Toowoomba City, Queensland 4350
Australia

publicQuestions.question:
The Request for Offer and Specifications (Section 3, Part A and Section 9) states that pricing for the fixed price maintenance program is to be in accordance with WIS-M-006 High Voltage Network Operation and Maintenance Manual (DM#11812931), which details the minimum required maintenance activities. This document does not appear to be included in the tender documents.

Could Council please issue WIS-M-006 to all offerors as an addendum, or advise how it can be obtained?

If Council requires a confidentiality deed before releasing it, please advise the form required.
publicQuestions.answer: This document has now been included in the attachments.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please clarify the following:

1. Weed Hygiene Declaration – The Request for Offer (Plant biosecurity requirements) requires offerors to complete and return a Weed Hygiene Declaration with their offer. This form does not appear to be included in the tender documents. Could Council please provide the form?

2. Site inspection – Will Council offer a site inspection or briefing for the C1, C2, Perseverance, Wetalla and Wivenhoe sites before the closing date? If not, can Council provide photos, single line diagrams and the most recent maintenance reports and protection setting files for the HV assets?

3. Maintenance frequency – In the HV Asset List and Schedule of Rates workbook, some intervals on the “Current Schedule” tab appear to differ from the “Service Frequency” column on the “TO COMPLETE – Schedule of Rates” tab. Please confirm which document should be used for pricing, and confirm the L2 services Council expects to be delivered within the initial 2-year term.

4. Pricing basis – For the Part A items, please confirm whether the rate entered should be the price per single service event per asset, with “Expected Qty” representing the number of assets, or a total price over the contract term.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. This requirement can be ignored and was issued in error.

2. Council will not be offering a site inspection or briefing for the sites. SLDs and high level information are attached. Photos, maintenance reports and protection settings will be provided to the successful offeror only. Council can confirm that all assets are in good condition, protection settings are stored and maintenance reports up to date and to a suitable standard for a competent contractor.

3. The "current schedule" tab has the correct timing for works. Pricing should be completed in the schedule of rates tab. Columns G & H on the schedule of rates tab are indicative only and works will be invoiced on a "per service" basis. For example, if during the course of the contract it is determined that C1 requires a L2 major service on all components every year instead of the frequencies listed, the quoted rate will be used for each attendance to site.

4. As per comment 3, column G & H are indicative representations from Council only to ensure offerors have capacity. Pricing should be per single service event per asset.

publicQuestions.question:
Can Council please confirm whether the high voltage asset maintenance services covered under TRC000544 are currently delivered by an external contractor? If so, could Council identify the incumbent service provider and advise how long they have been delivering these services?

Could Council please provide the previous contract reference number, contract commencement date, contract duration and awarded supplier for the high voltage asset maintenance services covered by this Request?

Are the current high voltage maintenance services delivered by locally based personnel, or does Council currently engage contractors who mobilise personnel from outside the Toowoomba region?
publicQuestions.answer:
HV maintenance services covered under TRC000544 were previously delivered by an external contractor over an approximate period of 2 years. Council will not provide further information on this previous engagement.

Council will not provide this information.

Offerors should detail where their personnel are based to provide an indication of capacity. Council works with both local contractors and organisations from outside the region.

publicQuestions.question:
Section 4 mandatory requirement: electrical contractor licence, minimum 5 years' experience.

Please confirm how Council will assess the Part A requirement that the "company hold electrical contractors' licence with minimum five (5) years' experience":

1. Is the five years assessed against the date the offeror's licence was issued, or can it be satisfied by the experience of the offeror's nominated Qualified Technical Person and key personnel? - experience of the offeror's nominated Qualified Technical Person and key personnel

2. Where the offeror's licence has been held for less than five years, will Council accept an offer in which a licensed subcontractor or joint venture partner with more than five years' licence history performs part of the works? - Yes, I have already reached out and have backing by a national company, and also have support from multiple small - medium business owners in this sector.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Offerors should provide evidence which demonstrates a high likelihood of success. Council's position is that an organisation which has held an electrical contractor's licence for 5 years meets that criteria. Council will consider alternative evidence which demonstrates equivalent experience and likelihood of success however, Council reserves the right to determine whether an organisation meets that threshold at its sole discretion.

2. Council's RFO document states that subcontractors may be considered for the engagement. Council will assess the skills and experience of the offered solution holistically and as per the response to question 1.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

We would appreciate clarification on the following items:

1. Geotechnical Report

As Council previously approved the seawall works on the opposite side of the canal, we understand that a geotechnical investigation may have been undertaken as part of those works. Could Council please provide a copy of this report, if available, to assist with our assessment of the ground conditions?

2. Connection to Bridge Abutment

Does Council require the proposed new seawall to be structurally connected to the existing bridge abutment, or is the new seawall to be designed as a freestanding structure?

3. Bridge Load Restrictions

Can Council please confirm whether there are any load restrictions on the existing bridge, particularly regarding the movement of heavy plant, machinery and construction materials?

4. Construction Staging Area

Would Council be able to assist in obtaining permission to use part of the nearby shopping centre car park as a temporary staging area for plant, equipment and materials during construction?

5. Construction Timeframe and Ground Conditions

Can Council please confirm the required timeframe for completion of the works?

6. Acid Sulphate Soil Management

Would Council be able to provide a suitable area for the temporary storage and treatment of acid sulphate soil material, should this be encountered during construction?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Answers below and attachment will also be posted, with pictures.

1. Geotechnical Report

As Council previously approved the seawall works on the opposite side of the canal, we understand that a geotechnical investigation may have been undertaken as part of those works. Could Council please provide a copy of this report, if available, to assist with our assessment of the ground conditions

Council have reviewed reports within proximity to the proposed seawall works and note there are no significant variations in ground conditions and soil profile when compared with Appendix 4 – Borehole Logs provided in Tender documentation.

2. Connection to Bridge Abutment

Does Council require the proposed new seawall to be structurally connected to the existing bridge abutment, or is the new seawall to be designed as a freestanding structure?

The bridge abutment shall not be integrated into the new design in a capacity greater than the existing seawall to abutment interface connection.

Depending on contractor proposed methodology, the bridge abutment may require temporary support considerations, such as lateral support due to the demolition of deteriorated wall.

3. Bridge Load Restrictions

Can Council please confirm whether there are any load restrictions on the existing bridge, particularly regarding the movement of heavy plant, machinery and construction materials?

Tenderers shall allow for the delivery and construction methodology to be undertaken primarily via marine access.

Due to bridge loading limitations and the requirement to maintain public access along Belgrave Esplanade at all times, access to the seawall works area is expected to be predominantly by barge and associated marine plant.

Bridge loading restrictions are to be nominated by a qualified structural engineer at the cost of the contractor to verify load capacity. This assessment is to be verified by Council prior to commencement of works.

4. Construction Staging Area

Would Council be able to assist in obtaining permission to use part of the nearby shopping centre car park as a temporary staging area for plant, equipment and materials during construction

It is not Council's preference for the adjacent shopping centre car park to be used as a temporary staging area for plant, equipment, and materials. While Council may assist in facilitating discussions with relevant stakeholders, no guarantee can be provided regarding the availability or suitability of the site for this purpose.

Refer to annotated aerial image identifying areas that may be suitable for temporary staging. The locations shown are indicative only. The successful Contractor shall assess and confirm the suitability of any proposed staging, stockpiling, or temporary work areas. The Contractor shall ensure that storage of materials, stockpiles, plant, equipment, and temporary works does not impose excessive surcharges on existing seawall structures, and all such surcharges shall be minimised wherever practicable.

5. Construction Timeframe and Ground Conditions

Can Council please confirm the required timeframe for completion of the works?

Due to the urgency of the works, Council intends to award the contract in December. The works are required to be completed as soon as practicable following contract award. To assist in expediting project delivery, Council has provided supporting documentation, including a Preliminary Planning Approval Pathway Report, to facilitate timely approvals and commencement of the works.

6. Acid Sulphate Soil Management

Would Council be able to provide a suitable area for the temporary storage and treatment of acid sulphate soil material, should this be encountered during construction?

Refer to annotated aerial image identifying areas that may be suitable for the temporary stockpiling of acid sulfate soil material. The locations shown are indicative only. The successful Contractor shall assess and confirm the suitability of any proposed stockpiling and treatment areas and ensure that all acid sulfate soil treatment activities are undertaken in a location approved/verified by an environmental consultant and Council. The selected location shall minimise the risk of environmental harm, including the potential for sediment, contaminants, or treatment by-products to enter adjacent waterways.

publicQuestions.question:
Retention of temporary shoring and permitted wall alignment

May shoring installed to protect the adjoining properties during construction remain permanently behind the finished seawall? Please confirm the reference line and allowable tolerance for the finished waterway face, what survey or hydraulic evidence Council would require to approve any offset, and whether the base tender price must allow for removal of all temporary shoring.
publicQuestions.answer:
A solution incorporating a retained shoring wall behind the existing seawall may be considered. The Contractor shall ensure that the proposed permanent seawall is designed as a standalone structure and does not rely on the retained shoring wall for load-bearing capacity, stability or any other structural support. Once the permanent works are completed, the retained shoring wall shall be assigned zero structural capacity in the design.

It is the Contractor's responsibility to assess whether retention of the shoring wall would adversely affect the functionality or maintainability of the seawall, or impact adjoining properties, services or utilities. Accordingly, the Contractor shall determine whether removal of the temporary shoring is required and allow for this in its tendered price.

The Contractor shall minimise encroachment into the waterway wherever practicable. Any proposed offset from the existing seawall alignment shall be supported by appropriate engineering justification and any supporting assessments which may include approval pathways, hydraulic studies, flood impact assessments and survey information. Council's acceptance of any offset will be subject to review of the supporting documentation.

publicQuestions.question:
Permanent anchorage beneath adjoining properties

Will Council consider a seawall design that requires permanent ground anchors beneath Nos 1, 3 and 5 Shoalhaven Road, subject to engineering acceptance and landowner consent? Please identify any existing easements or agreements that permit installation, inspection or replacement of anchors. Where new permanent rights are required, will Council be a party to the agreement, and how should tenderers allow for an owner delaying or declining consent?
publicQuestions.answer:
The Contractor is responsible for determining the suitability and approval requirements of any proposed permanent ground anchor solution, including any landowner consents, easements, licences or other property rights that may be required. Applicable planning requirements are to be established by a suitably qualified environmental planning consultant from the planning panel nominated in the RFT. Refer to Appendix 3 for existing seawall survey and adjacent property boundaries.

Council may assist in facilitating discussions with affected landowners following contract award; however, this will not be available during the tender period.

publicQuestions.question:
Use of the reserve at 128R Belgrave Esplanade

Does one of the indicative staging areas on Council’s annotated aerial include the reserve beside the bridge at 128R Belgrave Esplanade? If so, may tenderers assume it will be available for temporary storage of materials and equipment, subject to verifying its suitability and maintaining public access? Please identify the usable area, approval process, available dates, fees and reinstatement requirements.
publicQuestions.answer:
The annotated aerial image identifying zones that may be suitable staging areas are shown indicative only.

Council does not guarantee the availability, timing, usable area, or conditions of use for any proposed staging area.

All planning approvals, site access requirements and permitted land use arrangements are to be confirmed by the Contractor through the Planning Pathway Consultant engaged from Council’s nominated planning panel, as identified in the RFT.

publicQuestions.question:
Existing foundations, anchors and monitoring records

Can Council provide any available as-built plans or installation records showing the locations and depths of existing foundations at No. 1 Shoalhaven Road and existing seawall anchors along the three affected properties? Please also identify any existing movement-monitoring records and any restrictions on disturbing or removing the existing supports.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has provided available as-built drawings in Appendix 2 for information only. The awarded Contractor is responsible for verifying the location and depth of all existing foundations, anchors and other assets on site.

An additional as-built drawing, Appendix 2 - As-Buit Drawings Original 5, has been located and incorporated into Appendix 2. While it relates to a general previous seawall restoration works, it may assist in understanding the typical existing structure. Archived information is limited, and all details must be verified by the Contractor.

No additional movement-monitoring records are included in the information provided at this time. The Contractor is responsible for identifying and managing any constraints associated with the disturbance or removal of existing supports.

publicQuestions.question:

Council has advised that nearby investigations show no significant variation from the Appendix 4 borehole logs. For Deliverable 2, may tenderers base their price on a site-specific geotechnical assessment using the available records, with further investigation if the geotechnical engineer identifies a need? Alternatively, does Council require a minimum field investigation at the failed wall to be included in every base tender?
publicQuestions.answer:
The information provided in Appendix 4 is supplied for reference and tender pricing purposes only.

In accordance with the Deliverable 2 requirements, the awarded Contractor shall engage a suitably qualified geotechnical engineer to undertake the required geotechnical investigations and assessments as per RFT.

publicQuestions.question:
Pricing of excavation and acid sulfate soil

Please identify which Appendix 1 items are paid on actual measured quantities and which rates apply only to approved variations. For rock excavation and acid sulfate soil treatment and disposal, what quantities and units should tenderers use in the base price where the extent of the work is unknown?
publicQuestions.answer:
All quantities are to be included within the Tenderer's lump sum price based on the information made available in the tender documentation. The Schedule of Rates is to be completed to establish agreed rates for potential variations and additional works.

Please modify Lump Sum Breakdown line items 5.7, 5.8 as follows:

5.7 | Acid Sulfate Soils (ASS) Management [Provisional Quantity 550 tonnes]

5.8 | Rock Excavation [Provisional Quantity 300 tonnes]

Once provisional sum allocation consumed further quantities will be assessed as per Schedule of Rates.

Please modify Schedule of Rates to include additional items below:

30 | Excavation and Treatment of Acid Sulfate Soils

31 | Excavation and Disposal of Acid Sulfate (if not treated on site)

32 | Excavation and Disposal of Rock

Note:

Tenderers are to allow for disposal of General Solid Waste (GSW) within their Lump Sum Price, excluding the provisional quantity items identified above.

Refer to SOR for other soil classifications such as RSW, Hazardous Waste, Contaminated Soil etc.

The Lump Sum Breakdown of Appendix 1 shall not be modified aside from above instructions.

The SoR of Appendix 1 may only have line items added in addition to instructions above.

publicQuestions.question:
Site possession and commencement of the construction period

Council has advised that it intends to award the contract in December and requires completion as soon as practicable. For tender programming, what event starts the contractual construction period, and when should tenderers assume access to the work areas will be available? Please clarify whether design and approvals are expected to proceed before possession of the site is granted.
publicQuestions.answer:
t is the Contractor's responsibility to determine the program and sequencing of the works. The Contractor is to establish the applicable planning approval pathway, noting that Council has provided a preliminary planning pathway in Appendix 7.

Following contract award, access to the site will be available for activities such as geotechnical investigations, survey and set-out, confirmation of the wall extent, and other preliminary investigations. Refer to key deliverables in RFT.

Temporary stabilisation works, including but not limited to additional rock bag support, may be undertaken following contract award where necessary.

Construction works are not to commence until the design documentation, methodology, and planning approval pathway have been reviewed and accepted by Council in accordance with the RFT requirements.

For tender programming purposes, the Contractor should allow for construction to commence following Council's review and acceptance of the planning and design key deliverables in RFT such as detailed design package, durability reports, methodology, planning approval pathway, etc.

publicQuestions.question:
Workers compensation evidence

Part B lists a $5 million minimum against “Works Compensation”. Will Council accept a current statutory workers compensation Certificate of Currency that does not state a dollar limit? If further evidence is required, please specify what must be provided at tender and what may be provided before mobilisation.
publicQuestions.answer: A current statutory works compensation Certificate of Currency as required by law will be accepted.

publicQuestions.question:
Alternative designs and tender departures

Where a tenderer proposes an alternative design or seeks approval for a departure from a stated requirement, must it also submit a separately priced conforming base offer? Please confirm where the alternative, its price and any associated departures should be recorded in the tender response.
publicQuestions.answer:
Tenderers must submit a conforming tender that complies with the requirements of the Request for Tender. Where a tenderer wishes to propose an alternative design solution that departs from the specified requirements, the alternative proposal must be submitted and priced separately as a lump sum in addition to the conforming tender submission (Example: Conforming Option A and Non-conforming Option B).

For any alternative proposal, the tenderer shall provide sufficient supporting information from the RFT, including but not limited to:

Completed Pricing Schedule Returnable for the alternative proposal.

A document outlining the alternative solution, including the proposed program (Section 6) and responses to all relevant tender questions and requirements (Sections 12 to 14).

The Council reserves the right to assess the conforming tender and any alternative proposal independently. Submission of an alternative proposal without a conforming tender may result in the alternative proposal not being considered.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 01 – Extent of Seawall Replacement

References: RFT Part A – Scope of Works; Appendix 3 – Existing Seawall Survey; Appendix 8 – Public Works Site Inspection Report; Appendix 9 – Client Brief, Section 1.1.

a. Can Council provide a marked-up survey identifying and/or exact extent and total length of seawall replacement and all interfaces with adjoining structures?

c. Are adjoining wall sections, return walls, anchor systems and transitional works outside the nominated replacement limits included in the lump sum?

d. Will additional replacement works identified during detailed design or subsequent investigations be treated as a variation?

RFI 02 – Existing Seawall Components and Demolition

References: RFT Part A – Deliverable No. 7, Demolition and Removal of Existing Seawall; Appendix 2 – As-Built Drawings; Appendix 8 – Public Works Site Inspection Report.

a. Are all existing tie rods, anchor blocks, buried foundations and ancillary structural components required to be completely removed, or may redundant elements remain in situ where they do not interfere with the new works?

b. Does the demolition scope include existing structural elements extending into adjoining private properties?

c. Can the existing temporary rock bags be reused or incorporated into approved temporary or permanent works, or is complete removal and disposal required?

RFI 03 – Existing Seawall Stability and Temporary Protection

References: RFT Part A – Demolition and Temporary Works; Appendix 8 – Public Works Site Inspection Report.

a. Has the existing temporary rock bag stabilisation system been assessed as adequate for the anticipated period before permanent construction?

b. Who is responsible for monitoring and maintaining the existing seawall and temporary stabilisation measures during the design and approvals period?

c. Who bears the cost and responsibility for additional stabilisation should the existing structure deteriorate or collapse before site possession?

d. Will Council consider a separately authorised early works package if additional emergency stabilisation becomes necessary?

RFI 04 – Existing Bridge Abutment

References: Appendix 8 – Public Works Site Inspection Report; Council's Previously Issued Tender Q&A, Question 2 – Connection to Bridge Abutment.

a. Has Council assessed whether the existing seawall provides lateral support or restraint to the bridge abutment?

b. Are any permanent bridge abutment repairs, strengthening or modifications included in the scope?

c. Has Council established acceptable movement limits, monitoring requirements or other structural protection criteria for the bridge during demolition and reconstruction works?

RFI 05 – Bridge Load Restrictions and Access

References: Council's Previously Issued Tender Q&A, Question 3 – Bridge Load Restrictions; RFT Part A – Site Access and Construction Methodology.

a. Can temporary controlled pedestrian or traffic restrictions be implemented for lifting operations or critical construction activities while maintaining alternative public access? Namely, is council's requirement for maintaining public access along Belgrave Esplanade at all times relevant to only pedestrians or vehicles, or both?

b. What is Council's anticipated review period for the contractor's bridge load assessment?

RFI 06 – Geotechnical Information and Latent Conditions

References: Appendix 4 – Borehole Logs; Council's Previously Issued Tender Q&A, Question 1; Proposed Contract clauses 8.2A and 25.1A.

a. How will materially different ground conditions, unexpected rock levels, buried obstructions, unsuitable founding material or unforeseen groundwater conditions be treated under the Contract?

b. Will Council amend clause 25.1A to provide an entitlement to a variation and/or EOT for latent conditions that could not reasonably have been identified from the tender documentation?

RFI 07 – Private Property, Permanent Anchors and Landowner Consent

References: RFT Part A – Site Ownership and Statutory Approvals, clauses 1.4–1.9; Appendix 2 – As-Built Drawings; Appendix 9 – Client Brief.

a. Does Council hold existing easements, licences or other property rights permitting permanent structural anchors beneath adjoining privately owned land?

b. Where permanent anchors extend beneath private property, is Council or the contractor responsible for obtaining landowner consent, easements and associated legal agreements?

c. Will additional costs or delays associated with obtaining landowner consent be treated as variations and/or grounds for EOT?

d. Does Council prefer a structural design that avoids permanent encroachment beneath private property?

e. Will Council facilitate access to private properties for geotechnical investigations, temporary works, structural monitoring and dilapidation surveys?

RFI 08 – Adjacent Properties and Structural Monitoring

References: Appendix 8 – Public Works Site Inspection Report; Appendix 9 – Client Brief, Section 2.6 – Dilapidation Survey.

a. Can Council provide any existing dilapidation reports, movement monitoring records or documented damage relating to adjoining properties?

b. Has Council identified any pre-existing settlement, cracking or structural damage attributable to the existing seawall failure?

c. Are structural movement limits, vibration criteria, monitoring frequency and trigger levels to be nominated by Council or established by the contractor's engineer?

d. Will the contractor be responsible for documented pre-existing damage or deterioration unrelated to its construction activities?

e. What procedure will apply to third-party damage claims where pre-existing wall movement or settlement may have contributed to the damage?

RFI 09 – Acid Sulfate Soils and Contaminated Material

References: RFT Part A – Earthworks clauses 5.11–5.13; Appendix 11 – SSC Earthworks Specification; Council's Previously Issued Tender Q&A, Question 6.

a. Can Council provide any existing acid sulfate soil investigations, contamination assessments or waste classification reports?

b. Will acid sulfate soil excavation, treatment, transport and disposal be measured and paid under the Schedule of Rates or included in the lump sum?

c. How will unforeseen contaminated or hazardous material be valued where the waste classification differs from tender assumptions?

d. Will Council allow provisional quantities or additional schedule rates for acid sulfate soils and contaminated material pending further investigations?

RFI 10 – Existing Services and Stormwater Infrastructure

References: RFT Part A – Design Scope, clauses 2.9–2.11; Appendix 9 – Client Brief, Section 2.5; Appendix 13 – SSC Stormwater Drainage Specification.

a. Can Council provide all available existing council services and stormwater drainage drawings for the affected area?

b. Must all existing stormwater connections passing through the seawall be replaced, or may suitable existing infrastructure be retained?

c. Are upgrades to stormwater infrastructure beyond the immediate seawall reconstruction limits included in the scope?

d. Has Council identified any private drainage connections or unrecorded services within the works area?

e. How will unidentified or incorrectly recorded underground services affecting the works be treated under the Contract?

RFI 11 – Flooding, Hydraulic Performance and Design Levels

References: RFT Part A – Objectives and Outcomes; Appendix 5 – Gwawley Bay Catchment Flood Study (2012); Appendix 6 – Gwawley Bay Catchment Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan (2015).

a. What flood event, design water level, sea level rise allowance and hydraulic design criteria must be adopted for the replacement seawall?

b. Is a site-specific flood impact or hydraulic assessment mandatory for all proposed structural solutions?

c. Will minor adjustments to the existing seawall alignment be permitted where hydraulic assessment confirms no adverse flood impacts?

d. Must the new seawall capping beam match the existing RL, or should allowance be made for future sea level rise?

e. Can Council provide available flood model files and hydraulic data for the contractor's assessment?

RFI 12 – Planning and Environmental Assessments

References: RFT Part A – Statutory Approvals, clauses 1.0–1.9; Appendix 7 – Preliminary Planning Pathway Advice, Sections 6 and 7.

a. Does Council anticipate the works proceeding as development without consent under Part 5 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, subject to completion of a REF?

b. Which specialist assessments are mandatory for the REF, including coastal engineering, flooding, ecology, fisheries, heritage, arboriculture, noise and contamination?

c. Has Council undertaken preliminary consultation with relevant approval authorities, and can any correspondence be provided?

d. Will additional statutory approval requirements arising from the selected structural solution remain at the contractor's cost and program risk?

f. What is Council's anticipated timeframe for review and determination of the REF and associated approvals?

RFI 13 – Planning Approval and Contract Condition Precedent

References: Proposed Contract – Formal Instrument of Agreement, clause 5, Condition Precedent; RFT Part A, clauses 1.0–1.9; Appendix 7 – Preliminary Planning Pathway Advice.

a. Clause 5 states that the Contract does not come into effect until Development Consent has been obtained by the Principal. How does this requirement apply if the project proceeds under Part 5 without Development Consent?

b. Will clause 5 be amended to reflect the applicable statutory approval pathway?

c. Is Council or the contractor responsible for formally determining the REF and obtaining any additional statutory approvals?

d. Will the contractor be formally engaged and entitled to payment for design, investigations and planning documentation before construction approvals are obtained?

e. How will delays or additional costs arising from Council or third-party approval processes outside the contractor's control be treated?

RFI 14 – Design Review Periods and Hold Points

References: RFT Part A – Project Milestones and Deliverables; Proposed Contract Annexure Part A, Item 18; AS 4902 clause 8.3.

a. Does the 21-day Superintendent review period apply separately to the 30% concept, 90% detailed and 100% IFC design submissions?

b. Does the same review period apply to revised submissions following Council comments?

c. Must the contractor include the full 21-day period for each submission and resubmission in its construction program?

d. Will Council review delays exceeding the contractual review periods constitute grounds for EOT and/or additional costs?

e. Is independent structural design verification or peer review required beyond certification by the contractor's nominated engineers?

RFI 15 – Construction Duration, Extension of Time and Liquidated Damages

References: Proposed Contract Annexure Part A, Items 7, 26, 28 and 29; AS 4902 clauses 34.3 and 34.7; Council's Previously Issued Tender Q&A, Question 5.

a. Does Council have a required completion date or maximum allowable design and construction duration?

b. Will the contractor's tendered program and nominated practical completion date form the contractual completion period following acceptance?

c. What date will be used to establish commencement of the contractual completion period: contract award, site possession, approval completion or another milestone?

d. Will Council permit EOT claims for delays in obtaining statutory approvals, landowner consents or Council design approvals outside the contractor's reasonable control, notwithstanding Annexure Part A, Item 28?

e. Will delays attributable to Council's design review, determination or approval processes be considered qualifying causes of delay?

RFI 16 – Pricing Schedule and Commercial Conditions

References: Appendix 1 – Pricing Schedule Returnable; RFT Part A, clauses 5.11 and 5.13; Proposed Contract clauses 8.2A, 25.1A and 36.2A; Annexure Part A, Items 12–14, 24 and 33; Appendix 9 – Client Brief, Section 2.3.

a. Clauses 5.11 and 5.13 refer to Schedule of Rates payment for acid sulfate soil treatment/disposal and rock excavation. Which specific Schedule of Rates items apply to these works?

b. Will Council issue additional Schedule of Rates items for acid sulfate soils, rock excavation and associated treatment/disposal activities where corresponding items are not provided?

c. Are these works intended to be included in the lump sum or measured and paid based on actual quantities?

d. Given the prohibition on amending Appendix 1, how should tenderers include additional rates?

e. Will Council accept provisional quantities or rates for unforeseen rock excavation, contaminated material, unsuitable ground and additional foundation works?

f. Will Council amend clause 25.1A to provide entitlement to additional costs and/or EOT for unforeseen site conditions that could not reasonably have been identified during tendering?

g. Can Council confirm if cash retention in lieu of bank guarantees will be an acceptable form of security?

h. Will Council consider contract departures expressly identified in the tender returnable schedules?

j. Will council accept Professional Indemnity insurance for the Contractor being procured after tender award or is a current Certificate of Currency required to be included to submit a confirming tender and meet the mandatory requirement?

RFI 17 – Request for Extension of Tender Closing Date

References: RFT Lodgement Details – Closing Date 30 November 2026 at 2:00 pm; RFT Part H – Conditions of Tendering, Extend or Shorten Tender Period; RFT Part A – Design and Construct Scope; Appendices 1–15.

Given the requirement for contractors to develop a D&C solution, undertake preliminary engineering assessments, establish marine construction methodologies, obtain specialist subcontractor quotations and assess the contractual risks identified above:

a. Will Council extend the tender closing date by 14 calendar days, from Monday 30 November 2026 to Monday 14 December 2026 at 2:00 pm, to allow adequate consideration of the technical and commercial clarifications and preparation of competitive, appropriately priced submissions?

b. Will Council extend the tender enquiry cut-off date accordingly and issue consolidated responses at least five business days before the revised tender closing date?

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Scope of Services

Landfill Gates Electrical Control and Automation Upgrade Scope of Works.

Leeton Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced electrical and automation contractors to submit tender proposals for the upgrade of the Leeton Landfill Boom gates' electrical control and automation systems.
