publicQuestions.question: Mandalay scope. Could Council confirm the division of responsibility for the Mandalay integration: which configuration work is carried out by Council or by Mandalay's support, and which is expected from the contractor? Is the Mandalay Moxa relay existing and remaining, and can Council provide the interface details or point list for the gate signals?
publicQuestions.answer: The Moxa relay controller is existing and will be retained. The contractor is to replace the existing interface cabling between the existing switchboard and the Moxa relay controller. Once installed, Mandalay support will test the interface to confirm that outputs from the Moxa controller are received at the switchboard and correctly open the gates. The contractor should allow to attend and assist during this testing.

publicQuestions.question: Control panel equipment. The specification nominates a 10" Beijer HMI. Will Council accept an equivalent operator terminal from another manufacturer, provided it meets the functional requirements? Also, is the "10 inch operator display panel mounted on the enclosure" the same device as the 10" HMI, or a second display?
publicQuestions.answer: Council will accept an equivalent operator terminal from another manufacturer, provided it meets all functional requirements of the specification. The 10 inch operator display panel mounted on the enclosure is the same device as the 10" HMI; a second display is not required.

publicQuestions.question: Gates and existing equipment. How many boom gates are in scope, and are the existing gate drives, loop detectors, photocells and safety devices to be retained and reused, or replaced as part of this work?
publicQuestions.answer:
Five gates are in scope:

•	Entry gate

•	Gate to landfill

•	Contractor entry

•	Contractor exit

•	Public exit

publicQuestions.question: Site services information. Does Council hold as-built or site drawings showing the existing conduit and cable routes, and the supply point for the new panel? If so, can they be issued by addendum?
publicQuestions.answer: Council does not hold drawings of the existing conduit and cable routes or the supply point for the new panel. Tenderers are encouraged to inspect the site to inform their pricing.

publicQuestions.question: Programme. Does Council have a required or preferred completion date, and are there periods when the landfill cannot be disrupted?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council’s preferred completion date is the end of the financial year, however, we would like the project completed as efficiently as possible with minimal disruption to landfill operations.

The landfill is quieter on alternate weeks, so any required shutdowns would preferably occur during these periods. A full-day shutdown can be arranged with sufficient notice, but the landfill must remain operational for most of the project.

Weekend works could also be considered to minimise disruption and help shorten the project timeframe.

With a population of around 110,000 as at June 2008 and a projected annual growth rate of 2.1 per cent, the region’s estimated population in 2031 is about 173,000 people.

Its coastal location is complemented by its spectacular natural environment. This includes 31 beautiful beaches, a picturesque blue river and a pristine rainforest hinterland.

Only an hour’s flight from Brisbane, the Mackay region boasts an enviable lifestyle and a buoyant economy with the benefits of a fastgrowing coastal city. It is the gateway to the rich coal deposits in the Bowen basin.

It is the largest sugar-producing region in Australia and nearly a third of Queensland’s export goods originate from the Mackay region.

There are about 25 different nationalities represented in the region, including people from Malta, South Africa, the Netherlands and Germany. The region also boasts the largest Australian South Sea Islander population.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The consultancy will require demonstrated experience in strategic planning, cemetery planning, demographic and demand forecasting, stakeholder engagement, public infrastructure planning, and the preparation of strategic policy documents for local government or similar organisations.

Tenderers should have the capability to undertake site inspections, analyse existing cemetery assets and operations, engage with key stakeholders, and provide practical recommendations to support long-term cemetery planning and service delivery. The consultancy will be undertaken in accordance with the requirements outlined in the Request for Tender documentation, including the Scope and Consultancy Agreement.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The desired outcome is the delivery of a comprehensive Cemetery Strategy and prioritised Action Plan that provides a clear strategic framework for the provision and management of Cemetery Land and cemetery services across the Mackay Region over the next ten years.

Deliverables include the completion of project working papers, assessment of current cemetery provision, future demand forecasting, stakeholder engagement activities, and final strategy documentation as specified in the tender documents.

The successful consultant will be required to demonstrate sound project management, deliver agreed milestones within the project timeframe, and provide recommendations that support equitable, affordable and sustainable interment options while informing future land and service planning decisions. All services are to be provided in accordance with the tender conditions, contract requirements and agreed project program.

title: 201270 Reactive Sand Dune and Beach Track Maintenance Works
description:
Council invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced civil, coastal and earthworks contractors to provide reactive sand dune, beach access track and related coastal maintenance works across Council-managed coastal land and assets.

The Services are required to respond to unpredictable sand movement, storm impacts, erosion, windblown sand, constrained beach access, damage to restoration areas, public safety risks and associated minor civil maintenance needs.

(b) coir and jute mesh grade

(c) dune fencing type

13.	Part A 4.4: Can plant be stored overnight at beach car parks or reserves? What are the permitted working hours (weekdays, weekends, public holidays)?

15.	Site briefing: Will the 11 November briefing minutes and Q&A be issued as an addendum?
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Respondents,

Please find responses below:

1. Attachment 1 – Materials: Section D starts at item 3. Were items 1 and 2 left out intentionally (e.g. imported sand)?

Numbering was accidentally missed being corrected during formatting. Which has been amended in the REVISED A1 Pricing Schedule.

2. Attachment 1 – Plant item 10: Can water for the water cart be charged separately per kL? If it must be included, what usage should we assume?

Water Cart is to be priced as a wet-hire hourly rate, inclusive of the water cart, suitably qualified operator, and fuel.

Water supply can be charged separately on a $/kL basis where a cost is incurred by the Contractor. Tenderers must state the proposed $/kL rate and any assumptions regarding water source or access charges. Mobilisation/demobilisation is to be priced separately under the applicable revised Schedule of Rates item.

3. Attachment 1 – Work Activities: Please define the units:

(a) Item 11: per labourer-hour or per crew-hour?

The unit “hour” means per labourer hour, not per crew hour. Where multiple labourers are required, each labourer's hours will be charged individually. Plant, cartage and disposal are to be charged separately where applicable.

(b) Items 9 and 13: what quantity is one “item”?

Items 9 and 13: Council will amend the unit from “item” to “linear metre” to provide a consistent pricing basis. Rates are to include supply, installation, maintenance during the associated works and removal of the temporary controls, including all labour, posts/stakes, fixings, and associated materials. Specialist or substantially different site-specific controls may be subject to a separate quotation.

(c) Item 4: what typical track width and sand depth?

Tracks are generally approximately 3.2 m wide, although this varies by location. Sand accumulation depth is variable and cannot be standardised. The required clearance extent will be identified in each Work Request.

4. Part A – Evaluation Criteria: What are the criteria weightings, including price, and how will prices be compared (scenario basket, hourly rates or unit rates)?

Evaluation weightings are not disclosed. Pricing will be assessed using a representative scenario basket to provide a consistent like for like comparison of tendered rates.

5. Part A – Deliverables/KPIs: What response times apply to emergency and to planned Work Requests? Is 24/7 availability required?

24/7 availability is not required for routine or planned works. Contractors are expected to provide an afterhours contact for emergency notifications where required.

As a general guide, emergency Work Requests should be acknowledged within 1 hour with mobilisation targeted within 4 hours where reasonably practicable; urgent works should generally be attended within 24 hours; and routine/planned works will be undertaken within the timeframe nominated or agreed in the relevant Work Request.

Actual response requirements may vary depending on the nature of the incident, public safety risk, weather, tides, site access, environmental constraints and plant availability.

6. Part A – 4.1: Will Council provide profiles, set-out and before/after surveys? How will m³ quantities be measured for payment?

Council does not generally provide profiles, set out or before/after surveys for routine reactive works. Works are typically undertaken and paid based on authorised labour and plant hours at the accepted Schedule of Rates, rather than measured m³ of sand moved. Where survey, profile control or volumetric measurement is required for a specific project, this will be identified in the Work Request.

7. Part G – PSA / Attachment 1, Call-outs item 6: If works are stopped by weather, tides, shorebirds or events after mobilisation, will Council pay standby at schedule rates?

Standby may be payable at the accepted Schedule of Rates only where the Contractor has mobilised to site and Council directs the Contractor to remain on standby due to weather, tides, shorebird management requirements, events, or other site conditions outside the Contractor's reasonable control.

Standby charges are not automatically payable where works cannot proceed. The Contractor must notify Council as soon as practicable and obtain approval from Council's authorised representative before standby charges are incurred.

Where Council determines that works should cease and the Contractor should demobilise rather than remain on standby, standby will cease to be payable. Standby will not be payable for delays attributable to the Contractor, including plant breakdown, insufficient resources, failure to appropriately plan the works or failure to meet Contract requirements.

Any approved standby will be paid at the applicable accepted Schedule of Rates and supported by relevant daily records.

8. Attachment 1 – Section E: Please describe one or two typical work scenarios, including sand volume and the time normally allowed to complete.

Works are reactive and can vary considerably by location. Typical works include clearing accumulated sand from beach access tracks or relocating sand to reinstate eroded tracks. Volumes vary significantly, with locations such as Wanda Beach potentially involving hundreds of tonnes of sand. Completion timeframes cannot be standardised and will be nominated or agreed for each Work Request based on the scope, volume, access, tides, weather, and environmental constraints.

9. Part A 6.1 / Proposed Term: Please confirm the term and extension options (4 + 1 + 1 years?).

Contract term is 4 years with possibility of extensions of 2x 1year extensions at Council discretion

10. Part A 6.2/6.3: Please indicate annual spend or number of Work Requests, typical job size, the beaches most affected, and the number of panel contractors.

Due to the reactive nature of the Contract, Council is unable to provide a reliable annual expenditure or number of Work Requests. The frequency, timing and value of works will vary depending on weather events, storm impacts, coastal processes, sand movement, and operational requirements. No minimum value, quantity or volume of work is guaranteed under the Contract.

Individual Work Requests may range from relatively minor works involving the clearance or maintenance of a single beach access track through to larger works involving multiple tracks, significant sand movement, dune restoration, or storm remediation. Previous reactive works have generally ranged from approximately $5,000 to $50,000 per individual engagement; however, this is provided as an indication only and does not represent a minimum, maximum, or guaranteed value of future Work Requests.

Works may occur across Council managed coastal areas, with likely locations including Greenhills Beach, Wanda Beach, Elouera Beach, and North Cronulla Beach, as well as other coastal locations within the Contract scope as required.

Council intends to appoint multiple contractors to the panel. The final number of contractors will be determined following evaluation of the tenders received and Council does not guarantee any particular distribution or allocation of work between appointed contractors. RFT 201270 Reactive Sand Dune and Beach Track Maintenance Works provides that work may be allocated having regard to availability, response capability, site requirements, specialist plant, performance, price, workload, value for money and operational risk

11. Part A – Objectives: Will Council provide ecologists or environmental officers for shorebird, vegetation, and heritage matters? Are there seasonal restrictions in the Bate Bay CMP area?

Routine beach track maintenance and most reactive works are not expected to require dedicated ecological or environmental supervision. Where works involve dune restoration or identified environmental, shorebird, vegetation or heritage constraints, Council will identify the applicable requirements in the Work Request and provide relevant assessments, approvals and completion of Review Environmental Factors (REF) documentation where required. Specialist environmental input will be arranged where identified as necessary for the works.

There are no blanket seasonal restrictions nominated under this Contract. However, site specific or seasonal restrictions may apply where sensitive fauna, vegetation or other environmental constraints are identified, and these will be communicated through the relevant Work Request. Contractors must comply with these requirements and immediately notify Council if unexpected environmental or heritage issues are encountered.

12. Part A 4.2/4.3: Please confirm the approved specifications for:

(a) Track material - Council confirms that the track material referred to in the Pricing Schedule relates to chain and slat beach access track systems. These may comprise either timber slats or an approved recycled-material equivalent.

The revised Pricing Schedule will separately identify timber chain and slat track and approved recycled material chain and slat track to provide a consistent basis for tender pricing. The required product and material will be specified by Council in the relevant Work Request. Alternative products must not be used without prior Council approval. The Revised Schedule of Rates will be amended to reflect this specification

(b) coir and jute mesh grade –

Coir Mesh: 100% natural biodegradable coir erosion-control mesh, minimum 400 gsm, open weave and suitable for coastal dune stabilisation and revegetation, including appropriate biodegradable/natural-fibre fixings.

Coir Logs: 100% natural biodegradable coir erosion logs 200mm x 3m logs

Jute Mesh: 100% natural biodegradable jute erosion-control mesh, minimum 500 gsm, open weave and suitable for coastal dune stabilisation and revegetation, including appropriate biodegradable/natural-fibre fixings.

(c) dune fencing type –

For tender pricing purposes, Council confirms that the reference dune fencing specification is single strand plain wire fencing using treated pine or durable hardwood posts, including strainers, galvanised plain wire, fixings and all labour required for complete installation.

The Revised Schedule of Rates will be amended to reflect this specification on a $/linear metre basis. Where a different fencing system is required for a site-specific Work Request, Council will identify that requirement and any adjustment to the tendered rate will be agreed prior to commencement.

Pricing assumption: Tenderers should clearly identify the material/product assumed in their submitted rate. Site-specific requirements that materially differ from the nominated pricing basis will be identified in the relevant Work Request and priced in accordance with the Contract.

13. Part A 4.4: Can plant be stored overnight at beach car parks or reserves? What are the permitted working hours (weekdays, weekends, public holidays)?

Plant Storage - Plant may remain on site overnight were approved by Council for the relevant Work Request and where it can be safely located without obstructing public, vehicle, pedestrian, emergency, or Council access. All plant left on site remains entirely at the Contractor's risk, including responsibility for security, insurance, theft, vandalism, and damage. Council accepts no responsibility for unattended plant or equipment.

Working Hours –

Unless otherwise specified or approved by Council, works are generally to be undertaken during the following standard hours:

-	Monday to Friday: 7:00 am to 6:00 pm

Weekend, public holiday and after-hours work must be authorised by Council and will be charged in accordance with the accepted Schedule of Rates.

-	Saturday: 8:00 am to 1:00 pm

-	Sundays and public holidays: No works, unless specifically authorised by Council.

Council may approve work outside these hours where required due to emergency response, storm events, tides, public safety, operational requirements, or other site-specific circumstances. Any after hours, weekend or public holiday work must be authorised by Council and undertaken in accordance with applicable approvals and the accepted Schedule of Rates.

14. Part A 7.1: No performance penalties or incentives appear in the PSA. Please confirm whether any apply.

Council confirms that no specific financial performance penalties or performance incentives apply under this Contract.

Contractor performance will be monitored against the nominated KPIs and through Council's performance appraisal process. Unsatisfactory performance or non-compliance may result in corrective action and may be considered in the allocation of future work, contract continuation, or extension options, subject to the terms of the Contract.

15. Site briefing: Will the 11 November briefing minutes and Q&A be issued as an addendum?

Briefing has had to be rescheduled to Tuesday 17th November 1pm to 2pm, and all Q& As will be posted on Vendor Panel.

Please refer to Addendum No1 and respective attachment titled REVISED A1 - Pricing Schedule - Reactives and Dune Beach Track for updates.

Note to attach signed Addendum No1 with the submission.

Thank you

title: Surplus Vacant Land Strategy 2.0 Consultancy Services
description:
*Please also download the 3 attachments relating to this request.

SERVICES REQUIRED

Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced consultant to provide multidisciplinary advisory services and independent advice to support the development of Council’s Surplus Vacant Land Strategy 2.0.

The consultancy will support Council at key stages of the project, including review and validation of the assessment methodology, portfolio assessment and options analysis, prioritisation, targeted assessment of complex or priority landholdings, and development of the final Strategy and implementation roadmap.

The engagement is intended to supplement Council’s internal capability with specialist expertise where required, while supporting a consistent, evidence-based and defensible approach to the assessment of Council’s land portfolio and development of strategic recommendations.

Council will retain responsibility for project management, development and maintenance of the Master Land Register, coordination of internal stakeholders and all governance and decision-making processes.

The consultant will work collaboratively with Council officers and provide clear, practical, integrated and evidence-based advice to inform Council’s assessment, prioritisation and strategic decision-making.

EXPECTED TIMING

The project commenced in September 2026 and has a target completion date of 30 June 2027.

LOCATION OF DELIVERY

The Services will be delivered primarily remotely. Should in-person meetings, site inspections, workshops or stakeholder engagement activities be required, then these will be undertaken within the Central Highlands Regional Council local government area. Council's principal office location is at Emerald, Central Queensland.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Council is undertaking Surplus Vacant Land Strategy 2.0 to establish a comprehensive and evidence-based understanding of its land portfolio and provide a strategic framework for the future management and utilisation of Council land across the region.

The project will establish a verified, region-wide register of relevant Council freehold land, Council-controlled trust land, underutilised sites and other land requiring strategic consideration. Building on this foundation, Council will assess the current and potential strategic role of individual land parcels, including opportunities for retention, protection, activation, development, tenure arrangements, partnerships, disposal or acquisition.

The Strategy will consider how Council's land portfolio may contribute to broader community and organisational priorities, including housing outcomes; commercial investment and economic development; industry activation; strategic projects; Council operations and infrastructure; civic and community facilities; recreation, sport and youth activities; open space; and broader liveability outcomes. Opportunities will be considered having regard to available evidence, land capability, constraints, demand, partnerships and Council's strategic priorities.

A consistent and defensible assessment and prioritisation approach will be developed to evaluate the benefits, constraints, readiness, risk, cost, market demand and strategic alignment of individual landholdings. This will support clear parcel-level recommendations and staged implementation pathways for future formal consideration by Council.

publicQuestions.answer:
Response to Q1 (re: Pricing Methodology)

Council acknowledges that the number of properties requiring detailed assessment and the level of consultancy input cannot be precisely defined at this stage of the project.

In accordance with Evaluation Criteria 5 - Cost and Value for Money, respondents are requested to provide:

•	any fixed-cost services and associated deliverables;

•	consultancy hourly and/or daily rates and estimated effort for the requested services;

•	any project management costs;

•	any travel rates/costs; and

•	any additional costs, assumptions or exclusions.

Respondents may propose a pricing structure that includes both fixed-fee components and schedule-of-rate components where appropriate. Council will assess submissions based on the transparency, reasonableness and overall value for money of the proposed pricing approach.

Respondents should clearly identify all assumptions underpinning their pricing, particularly where costs are influenced by the number of properties ultimately requiring detailed investigation or specialist assessment.

This approach provides flexibility for both Council and respondents while ensuring pricing can be compared fairly during evaluation.

_________

Response to Q2 (re: Availability of Surplus Vacant Land Strategy 1.0)

Council advises that previous work undertaken for the Surplus Vacant Land project primarily comprised an assessment report rather than a formal strategy document.

Respondents should otherwise base their submissions on the scope and requirements outlined in the RFQ documentation.

_________

Response to Q3 (re: Number and Types of Properties)

The project is currently in the landholding reconciliation and investigation phase. As such, the final number, nature and suitability of properties to be considered under the Strategy has not yet been determined.

The consultancy is intended to provide a strategic framework and methodology that can be applied across Council's vacant land portfolio as potential surplus land opportunities are identified. Respondents should therefore base their submissions on delivering the services outlined in the RFQ rather than a prescribed number of properties.

For context, the portfolio may include a range of vacant land types across the Central Highlands Region, however Council cannot guarantee the number of properties that may ultimately progress through detailed assessment as part of this project.

publicQuestions.question: Could Council please clarify whether it intends to lead the development of the Strategy, with the consultant primarily providing specialist advice, guidance and capability uplift to Council’s internal team?
publicQuestions.answer:
Confirming the Strategy is Council-led.

The consultancy will support Council at key stages of the project, including review and validation of the assessment methodology, portfolio assessment and options analysis, prioritisation, targeted assessment of complex or priority landholdings, and development of the final Strategy and implementation roadmap.

The engagement is intended to supplement Council’s internal capability with specialist expertise where required, while supporting a consistent, evidence-based and defensible approach to the assessment of Council’s land portfolio and development of strategic recommendations.

Council will retain responsibility for project management, development and maintenance of the Master Land Register, coordination of internal stakeholders and all governance and decision-making processes.

The consultant will work collaboratively with Council officers and provide clear, practical, integrated and evidence-based advice to inform Council’s assessment, prioritisation and strategic decision-making.

publicQuestions.question:
Page 4 of the Supplier response form identifies

Evaluation Criteria 1: Conformance to Requirements Detail how you will meet the requirements identified in both Section 1 and Attachment A – Specification.

I am trying to understand specifically what document this criteria refers to. Does this mean Section 1 and Appendix A of the RFQ document?
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes, Evaluation Criteria 1 refers to the document ‘1. RFQ260278 - Request for Quotation (Section 1 and Attachment A)’ specifically:

• Section 1 – Request for Quotation, Part 2. Requirements (commencing on Page 3), which outlines the required consultancy services, scope, support services and deliverables; and

• Attachment A – Specification, Part 2. Technical/Functional Requirements (commencing on Page 6), which outlines the mandatory requirements and detailed scope of work.

Suppliers should demonstrate how their proposed services, experience, resources and approach will meet these requirements within their response to Evaluation Criteria 1.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Would you be able to provide an approximate number of properties that need to be considered?

Is there a preference for certain properties to be considered more than others?

Regards,
publicQuestions.answer:
The number of parcels to be considered through this project has not yet been finalised. Council has obtained landholding records from Titles Queensland which indicate ownership or trusteeship of approximately 300 freehold lots and 300 trustee/reserve lots.

As part of Phase 2, Council is currently compiling, reconciling and validating these records to establish a definitive land portfolio dataset. It is anticipated that a significant proportion of these parcels will be excluded from detailed assessment and validation in Phase 3. This may include, for example, properties that support critical infrastructure or operational assets, are required for the ongoing delivery of Council services or are otherwise identified through preliminary screening as unsuitable for surplus land consideration.

At this stage, Council has not identified specific properties to be prioritised over others. One of the objectives of the project is to establish a robust and evidence-based framework for identifying and assessing potentially surplus land across the portfolio.

Suppliers are requested to submit their responses by the advertised closing date and time.

publicQuestions.question: Can Council please confirm whether the successful Contractor is required to hold a current Builder's Licence to undertake the works under this tender, particularly in relation to the construction of the Amenities Building? Please let us know.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the Amenities Building is a non-residential public facility within a park. The works are being undertaken under Part 5 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, pursuant to the development-without-consent provisions of Chapter 2, Part 2.3, Division 12 of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021.

A current NSW general builder’s licence is not required solely by reason of constructing this non-residential building. However, the successful Contractor must satisfy the tender requirements for relevant construction experience, technical capability, competent supervision and appropriately qualified personnel.

The Contractor’s obligations extend to delivering compliant completed works and providing the supporting inspection, testing and certification documentation.

In particular:

1.	Licensed trades and competent supervision

All work requiring a statutory licence, registration or accreditation must be undertaken by appropriately authorised contractors and personnel. This includes electrical, plumbing, drainage, gasfitting and other regulated specialist work, where applicable. The Contractor must verify the relevant credentials, maintain appropriate supervision and provide evidence of current licences and qualifications when requested by Council.

2.	Compliance with project requirements

The Contractor must carry out the works in accordance with the contract drawings and specifications, Council’s Part 5 determination and applicable REF mitigation measures, relevant statutory and authority requirements, applicable National Construction Code provisions, relevant Australian Standards and manufacturers’ installation requirements. Any discrepancies or proposed departures must be referred to Council’s nominated representative for resolution before the affected works proceed.

3.	Inspections and testing during construction

The Contractor must coordinate and allow for the inspections, hold points and testing required under the contract, including inspections by Council’s nominated consultants and relevant service authorities. This includes providing adequate notice before work is concealed, covered or otherwise made inaccessible. Inspection and test records must be maintained and submitted as required.

4.	Construction compliance documentation

The Contractor must obtain and provide certificates and supporting records relevant to the works undertaken. These include, as applicable:

•	Structural engineer’s inspection reports and construction compliance certification for structural elements.

•	Concrete, compaction and other specified material or installation test results.

•	Waterproofing installation certification and specified testing records.

•	Electrical compliance certificates and electrical testing records.

•	Plumbing and drainage compliance certificates, inspection records and relevant authority acceptance.

•	Services commissioning records and certification for installed systems.

•	Product conformity and installation documentation demonstrating compliance with specified requirements, including accessibility and slip resistance where relevant.

 Certificates must clearly identify the work covered, the relevant drawings, specifications or standards, and the credentials of the person issuing them. A general statement from the head contractor will not replace specialist certification where such certification is required.

5.	Completion and handover

The Contractor must provide all completion documentation required under the contract, including work-as-executed drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, warranties, asset information, commissioning results and the complete construction compliance records. Required documentation must be submitted within the contractual timeframes to enable Council and its nominated consultants to verify compliance and accept the completed works.

The original "04_RFT_10_Mort_Bay_Park_Upgrade_BOQ_" spreadsheet file has the similar content as the received "VP532668_04 RFT 54 Mort Bay Park Upgrade BOQ_" spreadsheet except that there are now Timber Options and 5.0 Shelter items. Is there an updated RFT_10 BOQ showing Safety Fencing quantity is to be 450lm, or existing pathway milling has nominated a quantity of 2402m2, etc?

In the document Part 3.4 Pathway Upgrades, Sheet X02 as shown in drawing L001 revB is different from the finishes plans on drawing L302 rev B (Asphalt area differs). Could the Council confirm the area of "P1 - Asphalt with Build Up" will remain at 1,780m2 as nominated in the BoQ?
publicQuestions.answer:
The original "04_RFT_10_Mort_Bay_Park_Upgrade_BOQ_" spreadsheet file has the similar content as the received "VP532668_04 RFT 54 Mort Bay Park Upgrade BOQ_" spreadsheet except that there are now Timber Options and 5.0 Shelter items. Is there an updated RFT_10 BOQ showing Safety Fencing quantity is to be 450lm, or existing pathway milling has nominated a quantity of 2402m2, etc?

Response: For site safety measures, refer to Addendum 03 for Council's response.

In the document Part 3.4 Pathway Upgrades, Sheet X02 as shown in drawing L001 revB is different from the finishes plans on drawing L302 rev B (Asphalt area differs). Could the Council confirm the area of "P1 - Asphalt with Build Up" will remain at 1,780m2 as nominated in the BoQ?

Response: The BoQ quantity is correct.

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning Inner West

If heritage approval for Separable Portion B is delayed beyond February 2027, will associated remobilisation, extended preliminaries and program impacts be treated as a contract variation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council anticipates receiving the Heritage S60 approval by the end of February 2027.

The Contractor shall make allowance for a potential delay of 4 to 8 weeks.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Can you please confirm the Asphalt works for the area between the new Amenities Building and the existing jetty. In the site briefing it was discussed we would carry out asphalt works for the pathway from the new amenities building and towards the existing jetty. This area is not marked up on the Pathway Upgrade Drawings and has this area been included in the BOQ.
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes, there is a connecting path between the amenities block and and the existing playground path.

Please refer to Part 3.1A Mort Bay Park Amenities Landscape and Civil Works documentation.

The works involve the refurbishment and reconfiguration of existing departmental spaces, including the conversion of the current Dirty Utility, Staff Toilet, and adjacent shell office area into a dedicated endoscopy procedure room and associated supporting functions.

The scope includes completion of any remaining design development, construction, coordination and management of subcontractors, commissioning, defects management and handover within a live operational hospital environment. The project will deliver a contemporary procedure room designed to support complex endoscopy procedures and will include associated building and engineering services modifications such as:

•	Medical gases

•	ICT and communication infrastructure

•	Hydraulic services

•	Mechanical services and HVAC modifications

•	Nurse call and clinical systems

•	Radiation shielding requirements

•	Fire services modifications and compliance upgrades

The successful Contactor will be responsible for coordinating all aspects of project delivery, including stakeholder management, construction staging, commissioning activities, certification requirements, operational readiness and final handover.

publicQuestions.question:
PDG-46769-1 / VP534040 – Tender clarification questions

To assist us in preparing a conforming tender and pricing the required services on a consistent basis, please provide written clarification of the following matters.

1.	Tender closing date and clarification deadline

Please confirm the operative closing date and time. The ITT cover and VendorPanel Request Summary state 2.00 pm AEST on 10 December 2026, whereas ITT clause 2.8.1 states 3 December 2026 and clause 2.9.4 lists 10 December 2027. Please also confirm the supplier query deadline, as clause 2.2.1 requires queries at least two business days before closing, while the Request Summary permits queries until tender close.

2.	Award, commencement and completion dates

Please confirm the award and commencement dates to be adopted in the tender programme and the required contractual completion date. The documents refer to December 2026 commencement, early to mid-January 2027 commencement, an allowance of four weeks from tender close, and a VendorPanel decision date of 21 January 2027. The Project Brief also specifies completion by 30 April 2027 but schedules design development and final reporting through May 2027. Please identify the required draft and final report dates and the Council review and approval periods tenderers should allow.

3.	Shore Street West FWD quantity and lane coverage

Site 4 BOQ item 1.1 records a quantity of 1963 with the unit “Lane km”. Please issue the corrected quantity and confirm the carriageways, through lanes, turning lanes and other areas to be tested within the stated 1,113 m road section. A marked-up coverage plan would assist tenderers in pricing FWD testing and traffic management consistently.

4.	FWD spacing and investigation limits

Please confirm the FWD spacing applicable to each road, including whether the 30 m interval stated for Double Jump Road is intended, while several other mainland BOQ items specify 20 m. Please also confirm the testing and design limits at intersections and the included Bunker Road roundabout, including whether connecting approaches are included. For Giles Road Section 1, please reconcile the endpoint stated as No. 42–46 in Table 1 with the No. 42–26 reference on the location-plan caption.

5.	Measurement, payment and changes to quantities

The Project Brief states that borehole and laboratory quantities are for costing and payment will be based on quantities ordered and agreed by Council. Please confirm which BOQ items are remeasurable at tendered rates and which remain lump sum. Where Council changes quantities, adds road sections or requires further visits, please confirm how associated traffic management, mobilisation, island freight and engineering costs are to be assessed, particularly where those costs sit within lump sum items.

6.	Council-supplied traffic, survey and pavement information

Please identify the information Council will provide for each road and when it will be available, including classified traffic counts, heavy vehicle or axle-loading information, adopted growth rates, survey, pavement construction and maintenance records, previous investigations and known drainage or groundwater issues. Please confirm whether new traffic counts, topographical survey or other data collection must be included in the base tender, or will be separately instructed if the supplied information is insufficient.

7.	Design deliverables, estimates and review allowance

Please confirm whether the base scope is limited to investigation, analysis and pavement design reports, or also includes detailed construction drawings, treatment and tie-in plans, cross-sections, widening or drainage design, specifications, quantities and construction cost estimates. For option comparison, please confirm the required level of cost-estimate detail, any Council rates and MCA criteria or weightings to be used, and whether a whole-of-life cost assessment is required. Please also confirm the expected number of meetings and consolidated report review rounds to be included.

8.	Four design alternatives and provisional stabilisation testing

Please confirm the required approach where investigation results demonstrate that fewer than four technically suitable treatment alternatives exist for a road, including whether an assessed and rejected alternative may be documented with reasons. Please also confirm that P1–P5 are rate-only items, excluded from the base tender total and undertaken only following written Council approval. For pricing each provisional item, please clarify the number of binder types, dosages and trial mixes required within each “test pit” rate, beyond the expressly listed tests.

9.	Service clearance and supplementary intrusive investigations

Please identify any available service-location information and known access or subsurface constraints. Please confirm where tenderers should price physical service-clearance work, including vacuum excavation or potholing where required. If auger refusal, bound pavement layers or insufficient sample recovery requires coring, a test pit, relocation or a return visit beyond the stated borehole method, please confirm the approval and payment arrangements for that supplementary work.

10.	Pavement reinstatement

Please confirm the required borehole reinstatement detail, including backfill, compaction, asphalt thickness, type and the surface treatment needed to match the existing roads. Given the small asphalt quantities and various constraints, would Council accept a nominated alternative permanent reinstatement system where the specified method is impracticable or contradictory, subject to approval?

11.	Working hours, access restrictions and additional investigations

Please advise the permitted working hours, any mandatory night work, restricted lane-closure periods, school or bus-route constraints, stakeholder notification requirements and traffic permit lead times along with council review times for various activities that require council approval. Please also identify known safety, environmental, cultural heritage or contamination constraints affecting the investigation sites, and confirm whether any specialist assessment, sampling or approval beyond the stated pavement investigation scope is required in the base tender.

12.	Section B returnable requirements

Please confirm that the applicable returnable schedules are A–K and whether the X7 “Site Specific Demolition Management Plan” heading at the end of Section B is an unused template entry that does not apply to this pavement investigation and design commission.

13.	Project chainages, agreed datum and establishment costs

Please provide Council’s adopted chainage references for each of the 12 projects, including road/asset identifiers, the reference alignment, chainage origin and increasing direction, project start and end chainages, and coordinates or identifiable control points linking those references to Council’s GIS, asset management systems and historical records.

Please confirm that an agreed chainage datum, together with any applicable survey coordinate and level datum, will be established with Council before fieldwork and used consistently for FWD testing, boreholes, defect mapping, design and reporting, including separate carriageways and disconnected road sections.

Where adequate references or control cannot be provided, please confirm who is responsible for establishing, surveying, verifying and obtaining approval of them. Please identify whether this work must be included in the base tender and under which BOQ item, or, if separately instructed, how the associated surveying, mobilisation, traffic management and engineering costs will be authorised and recovered.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could you please clarify the required testing quantities under Section 3 – Material Laboratory Testing in relation to the 4 boreholes specified in Item 2.1:

Item 3.4 (4-day Soaked CBR – 4 point): The description refers to "base and subbase material retrieved from each borehole", which implies 2 tests per borehole (1 base + 1 subbase, or 8 No. total). However, the scheduled quantity is (1 test per borehole).

Items 3.1, 3.2 & 3.3 (Moisture Content/OMC-MDD, Grading, and Atterberg Limits): The descriptions refer to "base, subbase and subgrade material retrieved from each borehole", which implies 3 tests per borehole (1 base + 1 subbase + 1 subgrade). However, the scheduled quantity is (2 tests per borehole). Could you please confirm the quantities.

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your query. Please see below response

Item 3.4 – 4-Day Soaked CBR (4 Point)

Historically, most roads investigated by Council comprise a base layer over subgrade, with no distinct subbase layer present. Accordingly, tenderers shall allow for the number of tests specified in the BOQ.

Should a subbase layer be encountered in any borehole, the subbase material shall be sampled and stored separately from the base material and clearly identified in the borehole logs. Any additional testing required on subbase material will be discussed and agreed with Council, and shall be reimbursed based on the applicable tendered rates provided for base material.

Items 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 – Moisture Content/OMC-MDD, Grading and Atterberg Limits

Tenderers shall allow for the number of tests as specified in the BOQ.

Should a subbase layer be encountered in any borehole, any additional testing requirements will be discussed and agreed with Council, and shall be reimbursed based on the applicable tendered rates provided for base material.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi, Could you please give clarification for below questions with regards to existing electrical line and new BBQ.

1. What does the existing line currently supply (the existing BBQ only, or other items such as lights)? What is its cable size and type, and is it single-phase or three-phase?

2. Where is the point of supply (switchboard / meter / pillar location), and who owns the line?

3. Who arranges isolation, and will the contractor have access to the switchboard for isolation and reconnection?

4. For the relocation, does Council want a new continuous cable run from the point of supply, or is jointing to the existing cable (underground joint or pit) acceptable?

5. Is the existing supply adequate for this load? If an upgrade of the circuit, switchboard or supply is needed, is it part of the contract or a Council cost?

6. Does Council require Christie's optional time clock to limit after-hours operation?

7. Supply of the BBQ: SOR item 10e says "Install new BBQ". Is the BBQ supplied by Council (and if so, will it include the cooktops and grease trap/waste kits), or is the contractor to supply and install?

8. Does the "electrical cabinet" in spec 8.1 mean the GPOs and isolation within the BBQ cabinet, or a separate pedestal/switch cabinet? If separate, is there a Council standard type and location?

9. Preliminaries 2.47 says Council pays for alterations to mains or services required as a result of the Works. Does this cover relocating this line, or should tenderers include it in their price?

If the details in 1–3 are not known, please confirm whether tenderers should include a provisional sum for locating and tracing the existing circuit, and say how much.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer

Kindly see responses to your questions as follows:

1. What does the existing line currently supply (the existing BBQ only, or other items such as lights)? What is its cable size and type, and is it single-phase or three-phase? Council records and site investigations indicate an existing metered electrical supply associated with the BBQ precinct. Available records indicate the supply is three-phase. However, the cable size, cable type, connected loads and available spare capacity have not been independently verified by Council. Tenderers shall make their own assessment of the existing installation and allow for any investigations necessary to complete the Works, refer to the drawings package.

2. Where is the point of supply (switchboard / meter / pillar location), and who owns the line? Council owns the line, and as it has been indicated on drawings, an existing electrical meter is located adjacent to the existing Carpark(refer to the drawings package).

3. Who arranges isolation, and will the contractor have access to the switchboard for isolation and reconnection? The Contractor shall arrange all required isolations and reconnections and will be provided access to the point of supply as required to complete the Works.

4.For the relocation, does Council want a new continuous cable run from the point of supply, or is jointing to the existing cable (underground joint or pit) acceptable? The Contractor shall provide a new cable run from the point of supply to the relocated BBQ location.

5. Is the existing supply adequate for this load? If an upgrade of the circuit, switchboard or supply is needed, is it part of the contract or a Council cost? Based on the available information, Council expects the existing electrical supply to be suitable for servicing the proposed BBQ installation. However, Council has not independently verified the capacity, condition, or suitability of the existing electrical infrastructure. Tenderers shall satisfy themselves as to the adequacy of the existing supply and include for all works reasonably required to provide a complete and operational installation.

6. Does Council require Christie's optional time clock to limit after-hours operation? No. A time clock is not required.

7. Supply of the BBQ: SOR item 10e says "Install new BBQ". Is the BBQ supplied by Council (and if so, will it include the cooktops and grease trap/waste kits), or is the contractor to supply and install? Council will supply the new BBQ. The BBQ will be supplied as a complete kit, including all components required by the manufacturer for a functional installation. The Contractor shall allow for installation, commissioning and all associated works required to provide a complete and operational installation.

8. Does the "electrical cabinet" in spec 8.1 mean the GPOs and isolation within the BBQ cabinet, or a separate pedestal/switch cabinet? If separate, is there a Council standard type and location? No separate electrical pedestal or switch cabinet is required.

9. Preliminaries 2.47 says Council pays for alterations to mains or services required as a result of the Works. Does this cover relocating this line, or should tenderers include it in their price? No. Tenderers shall include for relocation, modification and reconnection of the existing electrical service required to complete the BBQ installation as indicated in the contract documentation. Clause 2.47 does not remove the Contractor's obligation to include for works clearly identified within the tender documentation.

If the details in 1–3 are not known, please confirm whether tenderers should include a provisional sum for locating and tracing the existing circuit, and say how much. No provisional sum is required. Council has provided the available information regarding the existing electrical supply, including surveyed underground service information and meter location details. Tenderers are responsible for satisfying themselves as to existing site conditions and shall include for any investigations, service proving, locating, tracing and verification works reasonably required to complete the Works.

title: Construction - Bight Bridge Replacement
description:
In May 2025 MidCoast Council (MCC) encountered a record-breaking flood event severely impacting critical infrastructure which is now eligible for replacement under the NSW Reconstruction Authority (NSW RA) guidelines. MCC has completed detailed investigations, designs, TfNSW specifications, and now seeks tender from suitably qualified and experienced civil contractors to replace Bight Bridge Wingham NSW 2429.

Bight bridge is located approx. 15min drive west of Taree spanning the Manning River and is accessed via Tinonee Rd and Lobban Rd. The bridge is currently closed with access limited to either side.

Construction commencement is subject to receipt of suitable tender and NSW RA construction funding approvals.

title: Standing Offer Arrangement (SOA) - Wound Care, Bandages & Dressings
description:
Queensland Health, is undertaking an open-market Invitation to Offer (ITO) to establish a new statewide Standing Offer Arrangement (SOA) for the supply of wound care consumables across Queensland Health's 16 Hospital and Health Services (HHSs), including metropolitan, regional, rural and remote healthcare facilities.

The scope of this procurement includes wound care dressings, bandages, compression products and associated consumables, organised into four major product categories:

- Bandages

- Primary Contact and Barriers

- Alginate and Gelling Fibres

- Foams, Hydrocolloids and Hydrogels

The objective of this procurement is to establish a statewide arrangement that provides access to clinically suitable, fit-for-purpose wound care products, achieves value for money and supports continuity of supply across Queensland Health.

Suppliers are invited to submit offers in accordance with the requirements outlined in the ITO documentation.

SOA274 - Wound Care Products

SOA286 - Bandages, Surgical Sponges, Tapes, Surgical Pens, Scalpel Blades and Stitch Cutters

Not all products covered by the existing arrangements are included in this procurement. The specific product inclusions, exclusions and applicable technical requirements are detailed in Part B - Specification of the ITO documentation.

- Supporting effective distribution through Queensland Health Distribution Centres and direct-to-facility delivery arrangements.

publicQuestions.question:
VP532672 / CSD127811 Wound Care, Bandages & Dressings

1. Attachment 2, Indicative usage tab (FY25 usage by category). Can the Principal provide FY25 indicative usage by sub-category and by Hospital and Health Service? Category totals do not show where demand sits across the 16 HHSs, which affects how suppliers plan stockholding and delivery to each region under Part B Schedule 1, clause 7.1 (inventory levels).

2. Part A 1.7.2, Stage 2 (clinical and technical suitability) and Part C 5.5 (clinical suitability evidence). Health services generally will not purchase a product until it is on contract and for the past several years since entering the market have been told explicitly to wait for this revised SOA. A product range that is newly included on the ARTG, or new to the Australian market, therefore has no Queensland Health or other Australian usage and is unlikely to be on a formulary. Please confirm:

(a) whether independent clinical references (evidence type 1) and published clinical evidence (evidence type 3) together satisfy the requirement for such a range;

(b) whether the Principal will consider a conditional or Secondary award for a range that meets the mandatory requirements but has limited usage history, subject to clinical evaluation after award; and

(c) whether ranges registered after this ITO closes can be added later through the Product Additions, Substitutions, Improvements and Innovation special condition in Part B, Item 27 (special conditions, SOA conditions).

3. Specification, General Product Requirements (Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods requirements) and Part A 1.11 (requirements to be a conforming offer). Where an ARTG application for a product range has been lodged with the TGA before the closing date and inclusion is granted after it, will the Principal accept the ARTG certificate through clarification before the Stage 2 desktop assessment? publicQuestions.answer:

2. A product range does not need existing Queensland Health or Australian usage, or formulary inclusion, to be offered.

publicQuestions.question:
Sub-category 3.4.11 (Antimicrobial Solution/Gel, sterile, single use): request to reconsider the sterility requirement

The clarification of 13 November confirmed that a solution must be supplied sterile to be nominated to sub-category 3.4.11, and that non-sterile solutions do not qualify. Sub-category 3.4.11 is the only sub-category in the arrangement for wound cleansing and irrigation solutions. We ask the Principal to reconsider, for these reasons.

Hypochlorous acid wound irrigation solutions, and some polyhexanide solutions, are included on the ARTG under the GMDN term for a non-sterile antimicrobial wound irrigation solution. The TGA has accepted them for cleansing and irrigating acute and chronic wounds, including cavities. They are preserved, multi-dose products and are in routine use in Australian hospitals, including in Queensland.

There is no practical difference in use between the sterile-labelled and non-sterile-labelled products in this class. Both are formulated with an antimicrobial or preservative ingredient whose purpose is to keep the solution free of microbial growth after the bottle is opened, and both are used from the same opened bottle for weeks. The 13 November clarification accepts that sterility is not required to be maintained after opening. For a 350 mL or 500 mL multi-use bottle, that means every application after the first comes from a bottle whose seal has been broken, whichever label it carries. From first opening, both products rely on the same thing: the preservative system and the in-use period validated by the manufacturer and stated in the instructions for use. The non-sterile-labelled products are included on the ARTG for use on open wounds in that form. We are not aware of evidence that a sterile label at supply improves clinical outcomes for a preserved, multi-dose wound irrigation solution.

HealthShare Victoria is tendering the same product group now (Skin Integrity, HPVITS2026-200, category 12.01 Antimicrobial Wound Cleansing and Irrigation Solutions). Its Statement of Requirements has one mandatory criterion for the category: the product must be safe for use on acute and chronic wounds as stated in its instructions for use. Sterility is not a requirement. Suppliers simply declare whether each product is sterile or non-sterile, alongside format and pH, and it carries no weighting. Sterile and non-sterile products compete in the one category.

The effect on competition is large. Under the current wording only the sterile-labelled products can be offered, so the sub-category is in practice limited to one or two incumbent products, and equivalent ARTG-included products cannot be compared with them on clinical performance or price.

In short, requiring sterility at supply secures at most one sterile application from a bottle that is then used for weeks. That offers limited clinical benefit, if any, and it comes at the cost of excluding a whole class of TGA-accepted products.

Questions:

a) Will the Principal accept in sub-category 3.4.11 an antimicrobial wound irrigation solution that is included on the ARTG for use on open wounds, is preserved, and is supplied non-sterile, where the manufacturer’s validated in-use period after opening is stated?

b) If not, will the Principal add a sub-category for preserved, multi-dose antimicrobial wound cleansing and irrigation solutions, so that these products can be offered and clinically evaluated?

c) If neither, please confirm that these products are intentionally outside the scope of the arrangement, so that Hospital and Health Services know they will continue to be bought outside it.
publicQuestions.answer: Following a review with clinical advisors, Queensland Health will amend sub-category 3.4.11 to include both sterile and non-sterile antimicrobial wound cleansing and irrigation solutions and gels. An addendum setting out the amended requirements will be issued shortly, and will replace the response of 13 November on sub-category 3.4.11.

publicQuestions.question: Are compression wraps, used as an alternative to bandaging, within the scope of this ITO?
publicQuestions.answer: No. Compression wraps and garments are not within the scope of this ITO.

publicQuestions.question:
Evidence type 5 (other Australian health service usage): non-hospital providers

Addendum 1, item 13 (references from community clinicians) confirms that independent clinical references must come from clinicians practising within an Australian hospital setting.

Can Queensland Health please confirm whether that hospital-only restriction also applies to evidence type 5 (other Australian health service usage)?

Specifically, does documented supply to the following count as other Australian health service usage:

a) community nursing and district nursing organisations

b) specialist wound care services and clinics operating outside a hospital

c) private hospitals

If only some of these count, please state which.
publicQuestions.answer:
The requirement for clinicians to practise within an Australian hospital setting applies only to independent clinical references. It does not apply to other Australian health service usage.

Documented usage by any of the services listed at (a), (b) and (c) may be provided as other Australian health service usage, where the evidence meets the requirements of Part C, item 5.5.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Independent Clinical References (Section 5.5)

a. Remuneration of Clinicians

Section 5.5 states that clinicians must not be "remunerated" by the supplier or manufacturer. Does this exclude clinicians who have previously received payment for non-product-specific educational activities?

b. Reference Requirements

Could Queensland Health clarify the difference between a written reference and a clinician endorsement under Section 5.5, including the requirements for each? Is there a preferred template or format, or will any document containing the required information be accepted?

2. Sample Evaluation Requirements

Following the tender briefing, and given the short timeframe between sample request and delivery, could Queensland Health provide further clarification on the sample evaluation process, including anticipated sample quantities, whether requirements will vary by category, whether samples are required for all SKUs or representative products only, and any supporting documentation that should accompany samples (e.g. IFUs, product literature or specification sheets)?
publicQuestions.answer:
1a. Remuneration of clinicians

No. Previous payment for non-product-specific educational activities does not, of itself, exclude a clinician. The clinician must not be employed by or contracted to the Supplier or manufacturer, and must not be remunerated for providing the reference.

1b. Reference requirements

There is no difference in requirements between a written reference and a clinician endorsement. Either is acceptable, provided it includes the information set out in Part C, item 5.5. No template is provided, and any document containing the required information will be accepted.

2. Sample evaluation

Sample requirements, including quantities and delivery instructions, will be issued to Suppliers whose product ranges satisfy Stage 2. Sample quantities will vary by sub-category. Samples will generally be requested for representative products within each product range, rather than every SKU.

Queensland Health notes the time between sample requirements being issued and the delivery window. To assist Suppliers with planning, it may provide indicative information, such as the number of evaluation sites for each sub-category, before sample information/locations are issued.

IFUs, product literature and specification sheets should be submitted electronically with the offer and will be made available to the Clinical Evaluation Panel in that format. Printed copies are not required with samples.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:
Tender Clarification Question – Clinical Suitability Evidence (Generic Products)

We seek clarification regarding the application of clinical suitability evidence to generic medical products.

For product ranges that are widely recognised as generic products with an established standard of care and intended use (for example, crepe bandages, conforming bandages, tubular bandages and similar commodity products), can clinical suitability evidence relating to the generic product type be accepted where the offered product is functionally equivalent and intended for the same clinical purpose?

Specifically, where published clinical evidence, clinician endorsements, formulary inclusion, or Australian health service usage records relate to the generic product category rather than the supplier's specific brand, will this evidence satisfy the requirements of Part C Section 5.5, provided the offered product has equivalent intended use, design characteristics and performance?

Or is Queensland Health requiring that all clinical suitability evidence and usage documentation be specific to the exact brand and product range being offered?
publicQuestions.answer:
Published clinical evidence may relate to the product type, technology or mechanism, where it is relevant to the offered product range and the nominated indication.

The other evidence types (independent clinical references, formulary, standing offer or contract inclusion, and usage) must relate to the offered product range, as each is required to identify the product (Part C, item 5.5).

publicQuestions.question: In accordance with the principles of non-discriminatory treatment under the Australia and New Zealand Government Procurement Agreement (ANZGPA), and recognizing the close alignment of clinical practice standards across both jurisdictions, could Queensland Health please confirm whether documented clinical usage, trial data, and practitioner references from New Zealand health professionals will be accepted as equivalent to Australian clinical evidence for the purposes of this evaluation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Queensland Health has reviewed the clinical suitability evidence requirements in relation to the Australia and New Zealand Government Procurement Agreement (ANZGPA). Please refer to Addendum 2, which extends two clinical suitability evidence types to include New Zealand health services:

- formulary, standing offer or contract inclusion; and

- other health service usage.

No additional evidence type has been created. Australian and New Zealand evidence of the same type count as one evidence type; for example, usage within both an Australian and a New Zealand health service counts as one type. Each product range must still demonstrate at least two different evidence types.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Sean,

Thank you for your previous clarifications regarding the ISO certification requirements.

Could you kindly refer this matter to the relevant Queensland Health team for further review? We are concerned that the requirement for non-manufacturing Australian ARTG Sponsors to hold their own ISO 9001 or ISO 13485 certification may have resulted from a misunderstanding when the tender requirements were drafted.

Our concerns are:

1. **ISO 13485 and ISO 9001:** While these standards can apply to different organisations, manufacturing quality control is the responsibility of the legal manufacturer, not a non-manufacturing Australian Sponsor.

2. **Other state tenders:** Other Australian state government medical consumables tenders have never required non-manufacturing Sponsors or distributors to hold their own ISO certification. The requirement has consistently applied to manufacturers.

3. **TGA requirements:** The TGA does not generally require non-manufacturing ARTG Sponsors to hold their own ISO 9001 or ISO 13485 certification solely because they act as Sponsors.

**We believe that most non-manufacturing Australian Sponsors and distributors are unlikely to hold such certification, making this a very unusual requirement that could potentially exclude a significant number of otherwise qualified suppliers.**

Could Queensland Health please reconsider whether this additional mandatory requirement is necessary and appropriate, particularly where the legal manufacturer already holds valid ISO 13485 certification?

We would sincerely appreciate a further review and clarification before the tender closes.

Thank you very much for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Queensland Health has reviewed the requirement and it will remain unchanged.

For a Supplier that is not the legal manufacturer, the certification requirement relates to the Supplier's own role in the supply chain, including storage, distribution, traceability, complaints handling and recall management. Manufacturing quality is addressed separately through the legal manufacturer's ISO 13485 certification. The requirement is a condition of this SOA, not a TGA regulatory requirement, and is consistent with Queensland Health's previous arrangements for these goods.

publicQuestions.question:
Subject: Request for a sub-category for non-sterile, preserved topical wound creams and gels (Specification Revision 1, category 4.3; Part A 1.7.2)

We supply a topical wound cream included on the ARTG as a non-antimicrobial wound dressing (GMDN 58133). Its intended purpose is to maintain a moist wound environment. It is indicated for acute wounds and, under the direction of a healthcare professional, chronic dermal lesions including pressure, diabetic and venous ulcers, burns and post-surgical wounds. It is applied to the wound surface under a secondary dressing.

It is a water-based, preserved, multiple-use formulation supplied non-sterile in 3 g and 15 g tubes. The IFU states a 60-day in-use period after opening, supported by preservative effectiveness testing.

The Specification has no sub-category in which this product type can be offered. Sub-categories 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 (amorphous hydrogel) match its function, its tube format and the 15 g reference size, and 4.3.1 already provides for preserved products. However, both are limited to sterile products.

In its response of 13 November on 3.4.11, the Principal noted that sterility is not required to be maintained after a multiple-use pack is opened. For a multiple-use tube, a sterile label on supply covers only the first application. Every later application relies on the preservative system and the in-use period validated by the manufacturer and stated in the IFU, whichever label the product carries. Limiting category 4.3 to sterile products excludes a class of ARTG-included topical wound products from comparison on clinical performance and price.

We ask the Principal to consider the same approach it took for 3.4.11:

a) add a sub-category within category 4.3 for non-sterile, preserved topical wound creams and gels in multiple-use presentations with a validated in-use period; or

b) amend 4.3.1 to include non-sterile preserved products.

Thank you for your consideration.
publicQuestions.answer:
Queensland Health acknowledges that amorphous hydrogels may be supplied non-sterile, for use in accordance with the conditions stated in the IFU, including any validated in-use period after opening.

An addendum will be released amending sub-categories 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 to include sterile and non-sterile products.

In addition, as Secondary product ranges are only purchased following a written request from the Principal, routine purchasing under the SOA is made from Preferred product ranges. Where more than one Preferred product range is awarded within a sub-category, Hospital and Health Services select between them having regard to their clinical needs. publicQuestions.question:
We have a new-to-market product that we would like to submit. The product has been sourced following requests from several senior Neonatologists and is TGA registered. However, we are not expecting to receive stock until early 2027, when we intend to commence clinical trials.

As the product is new to market and has not yet been introduced into clinical practice, we currently do not have clinical usage data, references or published literature to support its submission.

Could you please clarify the following:

1. Would we still be eligible to submit the product for consideration, with the possibility of being conditionally awarded, given that the product is TGA registered but does not yet have clinical usage data or published supporting evidence?

2. If this is not possible, would there be an opportunity to have the product added to the contract at a later stage, once stock is available and clinical trials have commenced?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. No. Each product range must demonstrate at least two clinical suitability evidence types at the closing date and provide samples when requested. Conditional awards are not available.

2. Any addition of new products during the SOA term will be at the discretion of Queensland Health, in accordance with the provisions of the SOA (Part B, Item 19), and having regard to statewide clinical need. Product additions are not guaranteed.

The clarification of 13 November confirmed that a solution must be supplied sterile to be nominated to sub-category 3.4.11, and that non-sterile solutions do not qualify. Sub-category 3.4.11 is the only sub-category in the arrangement for wound cleansing and irrigation solutions. We ask the Principal to reconsider, for these reasons.

Hypochlorous acid wound irrigation solutions, and some polyhexanide solutions, are included on the ARTG under the GMDN term for a non-sterile antimicrobial wound irrigation solution. The TGA has accepted them for cleansing and irrigating acute and chronic wounds, including cavities. They are preserved, multi-dose products and are in routine use in Australian hospitals, including in Queensland.

There is no practical difference in use between the sterile-labelled and non-sterile-labelled products in this class. Both are formulated with an antimicrobial or preservative ingredient whose purpose is to keep the solution free of microbial growth after the bottle is opened, and both are used from the same opened bottle for weeks. The 13 November clarification accepts that sterility is not required to be maintained after opening. For a 350 mL or 500 mL multi-use bottle, that means every application after the first comes from a bottle whose seal has been broken, whichever label it carries. From first opening, both products rely on the same thing: the preservative system and the in-use period validated by the manufacturer and stated in the instructions for use. The non-sterile-labelled products are included on the ARTG for use on open wounds in that form. We are not aware of evidence that a sterile label at supply improves clinical outcomes for a preserved, multi-dose wound irrigation solution.

HealthShare Victoria is tendering the same product group now (Skin Integrity, HPVITS2026-200, category 12.01 Antimicrobial Wound Cleansing and Irrigation Solutions). Its Statement of Requirements has one mandatory criterion for the category: the product must be safe for use on acute and chronic wounds as stated in its instructions for use. Sterility is not a requirement. Suppliers simply declare whether each product is sterile or non-sterile, alongside format and pH, and it carries no weighting. Sterile and non-sterile products compete in the one category.

The effect on competition is large. Under the current wording only the sterile-labelled products can be offered, so the sub-category is in practice limited to one or two incumbent products, and equivalent ARTG-included products cannot be compared with them on clinical performance or price.

In short, requiring sterility at supply secures at most one sterile application from a bottle that is then used for weeks. That offers limited clinical benefit, if any, and it comes at the cost of excluding a whole class of TGA-accepted products.

Questions:

a) Will the Principal accept in sub-category 3.4.11 an antimicrobial wound irrigation solution that is included on the ARTG for use on open wounds, is preserved, and is supplied non-sterile, where the manufacturer’s validated in-use period after opening is stated?

b) If not, will the Principal add a sub-category for preserved, multi-dose antimicrobial wound cleansing and irrigation solutions, so that these products can be offered and clinically evaluated?
