The clarification of 13 November confirmed that a solution must be supplied sterile to be nominated to sub-category 3.4.11, and that non-sterile solutions do not qualify. Sub-category 3.4.11 is the only sub-category in the arrangement for wound cleansing and irrigation solutions. We ask the Principal to reconsider, for these reasons.

Hypochlorous acid wound irrigation solutions, and some polyhexanide solutions, are included on the ARTG under the GMDN term for a non-sterile antimicrobial wound irrigation solution. The TGA has accepted them for cleansing and irrigating acute and chronic wounds, including cavities. They are preserved, multi-dose products and are in routine use in Australian hospitals, including in Queensland.

There is no practical difference in use between the sterile-labelled and non-sterile-labelled products in this class. Both are formulated with an antimicrobial or preservative ingredient whose purpose is to keep the solution free of microbial growth after the bottle is opened, and both are used from the same opened bottle for weeks. The 13 November clarification accepts that sterility is not required to be maintained after opening. For a 350 mL or 500 mL multi-use bottle, that means every application after the first comes from a bottle whose seal has been broken, whichever label it carries. From first opening, both products rely on the same thing: the preservative system and the in-use period validated by the manufacturer and stated in the instructions for use. The non-sterile-labelled products are included on the ARTG for use on open wounds in that form. We are not aware of evidence that a sterile label at supply improves clinical outcomes for a preserved, multi-dose wound irrigation solution.

HealthShare Victoria is tendering the same product group now (Skin Integrity, HPVITS2026-200, category 12.01 Antimicrobial Wound Cleansing and Irrigation Solutions). Its Statement of Requirements has one mandatory criterion for the category: the product must be safe for use on acute and chronic wounds as stated in its instructions for use. Sterility is not a requirement. Suppliers simply declare whether each product is sterile or non-sterile, alongside format and pH, and it carries no weighting. Sterile and non-sterile products compete in the one category.

The effect on competition is large. Under the current wording only the sterile-labelled products can be offered, so the sub-category is in practice limited to one or two incumbent products, and equivalent ARTG-included products cannot be compared with them on clinical performance or price.

In short, requiring sterility at supply secures at most one sterile application from a bottle that is then used for weeks. That offers limited clinical benefit, if any, and it comes at the cost of excluding a whole class of TGA-accepted products.

Questions:

a) Will the Principal accept in sub-category 3.4.11 an antimicrobial wound irrigation solution that is included on the ARTG for use on open wounds, is preserved, and is supplied non-sterile, where the manufacturer’s validated in-use period after opening is stated?

b) If not, will the Principal add a sub-category for preserved, multi-dose antimicrobial wound cleansing and irrigation solutions, so that these products can be offered and clinically evaluated?

c) If neither, please confirm that these products are intentionally outside the scope of the arrangement, so that Hospital and Health Services know they will continue to be bought outside it.","answeredAt":"2026-11-18T00:16:00.000Z","answer":"Following a review with clinical advisors, Queensland Health will amend sub-category 3.4.11 to include both sterile and non-sterile antimicrobial wound cleansing and irrigation solutions and gels. title: Construction, Refurbishment, Demolition and Mechanical & Electrical Capital Works
description:
Logan City Council (Council) invites Tenders from suitably qualified and experienced organisations for inclusion on a ‘Pre-Qualified Supplier Arrangement’ for the provision of construction, refurbishment, demolition and associated infrastructure works across Council’s facilities, buildings and broader asset portfolio.

The arrangement is intended to provide Council with access to a panel of capable contractors to support the delivery of a diverse range of capital works and infrastructure projects. Works may include the design, construction, refurbishment, expansion, renewal, upgrade, demolition and commissioning of new and existing assets, together with associated building, mechanical, electrical and related infrastructure works.

The proposed arrangement comprises the following panel categories:

Panel 1	Tier 1 Major Projects and High Risk

Panel 2	Tier 2 Medium Projects

Panel 3	Tier 3 Small to Medium Projects

Panel 4	Mechanical and Electrical Capital Works

Panel 5	Modular Buildings

Council intends to appoint multiple Contractors to each panel to ensure sufficient market coverage, capacity and flexibility to meet current and future project requirements.

ENQUIRIES:

Any questions and responses shall be collated, documented and distributed to all tenderers to ensure equity and fairness to all respondents.

All enquiries in relation to this tender must be submitted via the VendorPanel Online Forum.

LODGEMENT OF SUBMISSIONS:

Completed responses must be submitted using the tender response spreadsheet via the VendorPanel Portal. You are able to reference and attach relevant separate documentation as part of your response to questions to support your submission.

Any difficulty completing or uploading your submission should be urgently reported to the VendorPanel Help Desk on (03) 9095 6181 or support@vendorpanel.com.au.

CLOSING DATE AND TIME:

The Tender can only be submitted electronically through VendorPanel and prior to the Closing Date. At any time prior to the Closing Date, Council may issue additional or different information to tenderers, which shall be taken into account in preparation of the Tender.

publicQuestions.question:
VP531468

Sections 2a, 2b, 2c

All referencing “Demolition and/or site remediation”

Demolition contractors are licensed by Worksafe Qld. We are not licensed by QBCC.

You have noted mandatory requirement for QBCC Builder – open licensed

Therefore, is this tender for BUILDERS ONLY – who will then tender documents to subcontractors including demolition contractors?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that a QBCC Builder licence, in accordance with the requirements for each Panel, is a mandatory requirement for appointment to panels 1, 2, 3 and 5.

The references to demolition and/or site remediation in Specifications 2a, 2b and 2c describe works that may form part of projects undertaken through the panel.

publicQuestions.question: In the response for for Tier 1 and Tier 2, it staes for Open Class licences only. Could this also inclue Medium Rise licences? for example if you were to carry out a major refurbishment at one of your assets that would be between $1M - $7M you would only require a Medium Rise Licence.
publicQuestions.answer: Council would like contractors appointed to Tiers 1 and 2 to hold an Open Class licence so they have the capability to undertake the full range of works that may come through those panels. While some projects, such as a major refurbishment, may only require a Medium Rise licence, we would still engage an Open Class licensed contractor to manage those works. Limiting Tiers 1 and 2 to Open Class licence holders therefore gives Council greater flexibility across the range of projects that may arise.

publicQuestions.question: Regarding panel 3 - Tier 3, are you accepting QBCC licence Builder Restricted to Shopfitting?
publicQuestions.answer:
QBCC Builder – Low Rise licence is the minimum requirement for appointment to Panel 3. A Builder Restricted to Shopfitting licence does not meet this mandatory minimum requirement and limits the capability.

While some projects undertaken through Panel 3 may include fit-out or similar works, Council requires contractors appointed to the Panel to have the flexibility to undertake the broader range of works that may arise under the arrangement.

publicQuestions.question:

1. Question: Could Council kindly indicate the likely range of liquidated damages rates for Panel 4 Work Orders, and whether a cap may be applied, noting Annexure item 36 currently shows “No Limit”? (S03 items 35–36) – helps tenderers price delay risk appropriately

Answer: Council advises that the applicable contract conditions, including whether liquidated damages apply, will be determined on a project-by-project basis. S03 – Annexure has been provided as a sample and will be completed with the relevant project-specific details at the time of RFQ.

Each RFQ will identify the form of contract under which the project will be delivered, which may be AS2124, AS4300 or Council’s Minor Works Contract, having regard to the size, scale and nature of the works.

The RFQ will include the relevant draft Work Order, Annexure or Contract Information Sheet setting out the project-specific terms of engagement. Where liquidated damages apply, the applicable rate and any limit or cap will be specified, enabling invited respondents to take these requirements into account when preparing their quotation.

2. Question: Would Council be open to considering an overall limitation of liability and a mutual exclusion of consequential loss, either in the Deed or through Work Order special conditions? (Deed; S07 cl 37.2) – aligns with common industry risk allocation and insurability

Answer: Any proposed departures from, qualifications to, or amendments to the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed, including in relation to limitation of liability or consequential loss, are to be clearly identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance as part of the Tender submission.

Tenderers should identify the relevant clause, the proposed departure or qualification, and provide sufficient supporting information for Council’s consideration.

Any proposed departures will be considered by Council as part of the tender evaluation process. Council does not propose to amend the Tender Documents in response to this query.

3. Question: Would Council consider releasing 50% of security at Practical Completion rather than at Administrative Completion? (S05 cl 5.7; S03 item 13) – supports contractor cash flow, particularly on smaller works

Answer: Council advises that security requirements will be determined on a project-by-project basis and specified in the relevant RFQ documentation.

For projects delivered under Council’s Minor Works Contract, Council may provide for 50% of the security to be released at Practical Completion.

For projects delivered under AS2124 or AS4300, security will be reduced and released in accordance with the applicable contract conditions. Any proposed departure in relation to the timing of the reduction or release of security should be identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance for Council’s consideration.

4. Question: Could Council please confirm our understanding that total security is 5% of the Estimated Contract Sum, provided as two bank guarantees of 2.5% each? (S05 cl 5.3(b)(i); S03 item 12) – the clause wording could be read either way

Answer: Yes. Where the Annexure of Amended AS2124 or AS4300 nominates bank guarantees as the required form of security, the security will be provided as two equal bank guarantees of 2.5% of the Contract Sum each, totalling 5%.

As previously advised, security requirements will be determined on a project-by-project basis having regard to the requirements of the particular project. The applicable form and amount of security will be specified in the relevant RFQ documentation.

5. Question: Would Council consider including latent conditions relief, similar to S05 cl 12, in the Minor Works Contract for unforeseen existing services? (S07 cl 10.1) – gives a consistent approach across contract forms

Answer: Council does not propose to amend the Minor Works Contract as part of this Tender process.

At the time of RFQ, Council may consider project-specific amendments to the allocation of latent conditions risk, having regard to the nature and risk profile of the project and where an alternative risk allocation may provide a better commercial outcome for Council.

Any proposed project-specific qualifications or conditions should be clearly identified in the Contractor’s RFQ response for Council’s consideration.

6. Question: Would Council consider allowing delay costs for Council-caused delays, and extensions of time for authority delays and force majeure events, under the Minor Works Contract? (S07 cl 1.1, 27.5) – brings it in line with S05

Answer: Council does not propose to amend the Minor Works Contract as part of this Tender process.

At the time of RFQ, Council may consider project-specific amendments in relation to delay costs and extensions of time, having regard to the nature and risk profile of the project and where an alternative risk allocation may provide a better commercial outcome for Council.

Any proposed project-specific qualifications or conditions should be clearly identified in the Contractor’s RFQ response for Council’s consideration.

7. Question: Could Council please confirm whether set-off across Contracts is intended to apply to amounts due and payable, rather than amounts claimed or estimated? (Deed cl 4(j); S05 cl 14C.3(b), 42.11) – assists cash flow planning across concurrent projects

Answer: Council notes the request for clarification. Where a Tenderer seeks clarification of or proposes a qualification or amendment to the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed this should be clearly identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance, including the Tenderer’s proposed wording, for Council’s consideration as part of the tender evaluation process.

8. Question: Could Council please confirm the minimum professional indemnity cover required for Panel 4 tenderers undertaking construct-only works? (Form 5 note; S03 item 23A) – so we can confirm our cover meets the requirement

The level of coverage held must be disclosed in the Tender Response Forms and identified as a non-compliance in Form 6 – Contract Compliance for Council’s consideration as part of the tender evaluation process.

Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for projects that are strictly construct-only. However, projects delivered under the Panels may include design, engineering, certification or professional advice.

Where Professional Indemnity insurance is required for a particular project, the applicable insurance requirements will be determined having regard to the nature and scope of the services and specified in the relevant RFQ and associated Work Order documentation.

SCI/72/2027 – Panel 4 clarification questions

1. Form 5 – Workers compensation

Where a tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold a WorkCover Queensland policy (work is done by the principal and by subcontractors who hold their own cover), please confirm that answering the workers compensation section "N/A – as required by law" meets Mandatory Requirement 3.

For a tenderer that is an individual trading under a registered business name, please confirm that (a) an ABN Lookup extract and the ASIC business name registration are acceptable instead of an ASIC company extract, and (b) the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed can be executed by the individual (Execution Type 4).

3. Mandatory Requirement 4 – Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan

Please confirm that a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan (to be made project-specific for each Work Order), together with example SWMS, satisfies Mandatory Requirement 4 for Panel 4.

4. Specification 12 – KPI 2 (RFQ participation at least 75%)

Will Panel 4 RFQs be issued by sub-category (e.g. Electrical only)? Will an RFQ outside a contractor's nominated sub-categories, or one that the contractor formally declines for capacity reasons, count towards the 75% participation KPI?

5. Deed clause 6.4 – Monthly meetings

Please confirm that the monthly meeting under clause 6.4 applies only while a contractor has active Projects, and whether it can be attended online.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Form 5 – Workers compensation

Where a tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold a WorkCover Queensland policy (work is done by the principal and by subcontractors who hold their own cover), please confirm that answering the workers compensation section "N/A – as required by law" meets Mandatory Requirement 3.

Answer: Yes. Where a Tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold workers compensation insurance, responding “N/A – as required by law” is acceptable for the purposes of Mandatory Requirement 3.

2.	Form 2 – Individual (sole trader) tenderers

For a tenderer that is an individual trading under a registered business name, please confirm that (a) an ABN Lookup extract and the ASIC business name registration are acceptable instead of an ASIC company extract, and (b) the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed can be executed by the individual (Execution Type 4).

Answer: Yes. Where the Tenderer is an individual operating as a sole trader under a registered business name, an ABN Lookup extract and evidence of the registered business name are acceptable in place of an ASIC company extract.

The Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed may be executed by the individual using the applicable execution provisions for an individual.

3.	Mandatory Requirement 4 – Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan

Please confirm that a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan (to be made project-specific for each Work Order), together with example SWMS, satisfies Mandatory Requirement 4 for Panel 4.

Answer: Yes. For the purposes of Mandatory Requirement 4, Tenderers are to complete Response Form 3b. At Tender stage, a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan, together with example SWMS relevant to the types of works being tendered, is acceptable.

Project-specific WHS documentation will be required to be developed and implemented for the relevant works, as applicable, prior to commencement.

4.	Specification 12 – KPI 2 (RFQ participation at least 75%)

Will Panel 4 RFQs be issued by sub-category (e.g. Electrical only)? Will an RFQ outside a contractor's nominated sub-categories, or one that the contractor formally declines for capacity reasons, count towards the 75% participation KPI?

Answer: RFQs will be issued to Panel Contractors considered applicable to the scope of the particular project.

Where an RFQ is not issued to a Contractor because the works fall outside its applicable scope or capability, this will not count against the Contractor’s RFQ participation KPI.

Where a Contractor is invited to participate because the works fall within its applicable scope and capability, but declines to respond due to availability or capacity constraints, this will count towards the 75% RFQ participation KPI.

5.	Deed clause 6.4 – Monthly meetings

Please confirm that the monthly meeting under clause 6.4 applies only while a contractor has active Projects, and whether it can be attended online.

Answer: Yes. The monthly meetings contemplated under clause 6.4 are intended to apply while the Contractor has active Projects. Meetings may be conducted online where appropriate.

title: Design and Construction (D&C) of New Social Housing – Palm Island
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking to engage one or more suitably qualified and experienced Contractors to undertake the Design and Construction (D&C) of 22 new social housing dwellings across multiple sites on Palm Island, Queensland, together with an optional additional Package comprising two (2) dwellings.

The core Works are divided into five (5) Packages, comprising 22 dwellings and 86 bedrooms. An additional Optional Package 6 comprises two (2) dwellings and eight (8) bedrooms. Tenderers may submit a Tender Response for one, several or all Packages, subject to their demonstrated capacity to deliver the Packages tendered.

The Contract is intended to provide Council with a turnkey delivery solution, under which the Contractor is responsible for all investigations, design development, engineering, certification, building approvals, procurement, manufacture where applicable, transportation, mobilisation, construction, site and infrastructure works, utility connections, testing, commissioning, statutory certification, documentation and handover necessary to provide completed, compliant and fully operational dwellings ready for occupation and handover to the Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW), except for matters expressly identified as Council responsibilities.

Council's objective is for all dwellings to achieve Practical Completion and be ready for handover to DHPW by 31 December 2027.

Council will provide Reference Designs establishing the design intent and minimum functional and performance requirements. The Contractor will be responsible for developing and completing the design and may propose design optimisation, including prefabricated, modular, panelised or other off-site construction methodologies, subject to satisfying the requirements of this Specification, the Principal's Requirements and DHPW requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council is delivering a program of new social housing on Palm Island in collaboration with the Queensland Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW).

This procurement comprises the design and construction of 22 new social housing dwellings, providing a total of 86 bedrooms across five (5) Packages and multiple sites on Palm Island.

Package 6 (2 new social housing) is optional. Council may, in its absolute discretion, elect whether or not to proceed with and award Package 6.

Palm Island, also known as Great Palm Island, or by the Aboriginal name Bwgcolman, is the largest of twelve tropical Islands in the Palm Island Group. The settlement is named variously Palm Island, the Mission, Palm Island Settlement or Palm Community.

The group of Islands is less than 20 kilometres from the nearest point on the mainland (Lucinda) and is 65 kilometres north of Townsville over sea. The Islands are serviced by a 20 minute plane ride or one and a half hour ferry ride from Townsville and a one hour barge trip from Lucinda.

Palm Island consists of small bays, sandy beaches, fringing reefs, beautiful freshwater streams and steep forested mountains rising to the highest peak of 548 metres at Bentley Ridge. Other islands in the chain, such as Orpheus and North Palm have globally renowned resorts and marine research stations. Situated in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, the surrounding reefs are as good as any on the outer reef, presenting wonderful fishing and diving opportunities and are used extensively by locals for hunting and gathering and other cultural purposes.

Palm Island is the largest discreet Indigenous community in Australia with approximately 4,000 people residing on Palm Island. There is high mobility between Palm Island and the mainland, and the population can increase to over 5,000 people during festivals and events. There are seven suburbs on the Island, running from Butler Bay in the south to Wallaby Point in the north, with the main, central settlement area, The Mission having the mall, shops, service centres, police station, motel, hospital and health service and Council chambers. Critical services infrastructure, including the Council’s works depots, waste and recycling facility, (Ergon) power station, water and sewer treatment plants, and two water supply reservoirs are at The Farm area, Solomon and Wallaby Point.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Marcio,

I’m Kieran Shirey, founder of LOGiT Australia, an Aboriginal-owned business developing Kin-Neon (kinneon.au), a housing production approach intended to build local manufacturing, assembly and maintenance capability.

Our development work includes mobile production of interlocking stabilised earth blocks, with any use of local materials subject to suitability testing, engineering and the required approvals. We are investigating ways to reduce transport, labour and external contractor dependency while building lasting community capability.

Having reviewed the tender’s provisions for alternative materials and construction systems, we would appreciate clarification on a potential specialist role alongside an appropriately qualified D&C contractor:

1. What technical evidence and approvals must be available at tender submission for an alternative wall or material system, and what may be completed during the subsequent design and approval stages?

2. Would Council and DHPW consider a limited, engineer-reviewed component within a conforming delivery proposal, supported by a fully compliant fallback so that housing delivery does not depend on unresolved R&D? We understand that a non-conforming alternative must accompany a conforming tender.

3. For a specialist participating through a lead D&C contractor, must the specialist also attend the mandatory site visit, or can the lead contractor’s attendance satisfy that requirement?

4. If the development stage makes participation in this tender premature, is there an appropriate separate pathway for discussing a future demonstration or training project? We would follow Council’s nominated process for any such discussion.

5. Please confirm the supplier-question deadline. The Request Summary states 6 November 2026 at 2 pm AEST, while Part A clause 5.10(c) contains different wording and a reference to 6 October.

We are seeking clarification of the appropriate participation and evidence requirements at this stage. We are not representing Kin-Neon as a certified system or offering to undertake the turnkey D&C scope independently.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Technical evidence and approvals

At tender submission, proponents should provide sufficient technical information to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system and its ability to meet the Principal's Requirements, including structural performance, cyclone resistance, durability, thermal performance, maintainability and applicable DHPW standards.

Detailed engineering, testing and statutory certification may be completed during the subsequent design development and approval stages, where appropriate. However, any proposed system must have a credible pathway to compliance, and the successful D&C contractor remains responsible for obtaining all necessary approvals and certifications before construction.

2. Limited application and compliant fallback

Council is open to considering innovative materials or construction systems as part of a conforming D&C proposal, including their limited application to suitable building components.

A fully compliant fallback solution may assist in managing delivery risk. However, any proposed alternative must be clearly identified and supported by sufficient technical evidence to enable its assessment. Council cannot provide advance acceptance of an untested or uncertified system, and any proposed solution would remain subject to the applicable design review, engineering and statutory approval requirements.

3. Mandatory site visit

The mandatory site visit requirement applies to the Tenderer submitting the D&C proposal. Where a specialist participates as a subcontractor or consultant to a Principal Contractor, the Principal Contractor's attendance will satisfy this requirement. Specialist participation in the site visit is encouraged where it would assist with understanding site conditions and delivery requirements.

4. Future demonstration or training opportunities

Council recognises the potential value of initiatives that develop local manufacturing, construction and maintenance capabilities.

Should participation in the current procurement be premature, you are welcome to submit a separate proposal for Council's consideration outside the current tender process. Any future demonstration or training initiative would be subject to Council's priorities, available funding, applicable approvals and procurement requirements.

5. Clarification deadline

I confirm that the deadline for tender enquiries is 2:00 pm (AEST) on 6 November 2026, as stated in the VendorPanel Request Summary. The reference to 6 October in Part A is an administrative error, which Council will clarify through VendorPanel.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Marcio,

Thank you for suggesting I introduce my proposal to the D&C contractors tendering for Palm Island via Vendor Panel. I am an Australian architect with work spanning tropical Queensland to the Tasmanian highlands, and a particular interest in creating pragmatic, economical yet traditionally beautiful buildings and places. As an example, my open-source Tasmanian House model shows how distinctive, characterful homes can be delivered at exceptionally low cost, as documented by ABC News and other publications. During my postgraduate studies I also worked in the Aboriginal town camps of Alice Springs, gaining firsthand experience of the challenges of remote-community housing. Further examples of my work, including alternative masterplans advocating locally characteristic, picturesque and human-scaled settlements, can be found at www.lev.au and www.jirilev.au.

I believe Palm Island presents a wonderful opportunity to establish a new model for social housing, demonstrating that homes can satisfy every technical requirement, including Gold Level accessibility, durability, climatic comfort and affordability, while also contributing to beautiful streetscapes and a genuinely loved township. Some of the island's older high-set houses, generous verandahs and lattice screens already offer lovely precedents.

I would be interested in working with a Principal Contractor to study and evolve this local architectural tradition, creating varied but harmonious houses, gardens and public spaces that contribute to residents' happiness, satisfaction and pride in their community. I believe much could be achieved through thoughtful design without necessarily increasing construction costs. Palm Island could become a nationally significant example of social housing that people are proud to call home and that visitors find attractive and memorable.

Could Council please confirm:

1. May Principal Contractors engage an independent architect to further develop and improve the architectural character, appearance, site layouts and streetscapes of the reference designs, provided all budgetary, functional, accessibility and technical requirements are maintained?

2. May these architectural improvements be included in a contractor's tender proposal and developed further in consultation with Council and the community following appointment?

I would welcome enquiries from interested contractors, whether for an individual package or the wider programme. My involvement could be tailored to their existing teams, programmes and budgets.

Kind regards,

Jiri Lev, architect - jiri@lev.au
publicQuestions.answer:
Council welcomes design enhancements proposed by tenderers, including through the engagement of independent architects, provided all functional, technical, accessibility, budgetary and other tender requirements are met.

Proposed enhancements may be included in tender submissions and will be considered as part of the evaluation process. Any further design development following contract award will be subject to Council approval and the contract requirements.

publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.question:
Regarding vegetation clearing for Package 5, Lots 60A–60D, please provide any available clearing and tree-retention plans, vegetation assessments and applicable approval conditions.

Please also confirm:

- The required clearing extent, including building footprints, access, services and construction working areas.

- Requirements for stump removal, grubbing, backfilling and retained-tree protection.

- Whether on-site chipping or retention of mulch is permitted, and the approved disposal options for vegetation and stumps.

- Whether a separately identified provisional sum for clearing would be accepted where the extent or approval requirements remain unresolved at tender close. If not, please nominate the pricing basis tenderers should adopt.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

1. Vegetation clearing plans and assessments

Council has not provided a separate vegetation clearing or tree-retention plan for Package 5. Tenderers are required to assess existing site conditions during the mandatory site inspection and make appropriate allowances in their submissions.

2. Extent of clearing

The Principal Contractor is responsible for determining the vegetation clearing required to deliver the proposed dwellings, including building footprints, access, services and construction working areas. Clearing should be limited to what is reasonably necessary for the development, subject to applicable approvals and environmental requirements.

3. Stump removal and tree protection

The D&C scope includes all necessary stump removal, grubbing, backfilling, ground preparation and protection of retained vegetation. These works must be undertaken in accordance with applicable standards and approval conditions.

4. Vegetation disposal

On-site chipping and reuse of mulch may be proposed, subject to Council acceptance and applicable environmental requirements. Tenderers are responsible for identifying suitable and lawful disposal arrangements for vegetation and stumps and including the associated costs in their submissions.

5. Pricing basis

Tenderers are required to include vegetation clearing and associated site preparation costs within their lump-sum tender price. A separately identified provisional sum is not proposed for these works.

Tenderers should base their pricing on the reference designs, available site information and their own site investigations, clearly identifying any assumptions made.

Marcio,

We enjoyed the visit and confirm we will be suibmitting a full tender with the PixelBuild product.

•	Access in coordination for port offloading at the pier and ramp with advice on the size of vessel or draft clearance- who do we liaise with.

•	What allocation M2 would be given to laydown area storage of materials and or setting up site sheds

•	Will Council be clearing the lots of abandoned cars and any other miscellaneous items

•	Contacts or guidance on certifiers that have experience working with Palm Island aboriginal Council

•	Is the Council interested in inspecting the product prior to tender submission?

•	Is there an area that we can leave excavated spoil until removed from the island?

•	Can we have any additional work such as retaining walls or road remediation scoped or guidance.

•	Any addendums or updates since.

Regards,

Craig Millar

Director

Level 1, 283 Normanby Rd

Port Melbourne, Vic, 3207

Australia

1300 977 598

cmillar@zancottknight.com | D +61 403 427 395
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in submitting a tender.

1. Port Access and Offloading

Tenderers are responsible for assessing the existing port infrastructure, including pier and ramp access, vessel size and draft restrictions, unloading capabilities and associated logistical constraints.

Tenderers must determine suitable transport and offloading arrangements and include all associated requirements and costs within their tender submissions. Any assumptions regarding port access or infrastructure availability must be clearly identified.

2. Laydown Area and Site Facilities

Tenderers should identify their proposed laydown and storage area requirements (m²), including space required for site sheds and temporary facilities, within their tender submissions.

Council will facilitate access to a suitable area, subject to availability and operational requirements. The provision and installation of site sheds, temporary facilities and associated infrastructure remain the Principal Contractor's responsibility.

3. Site Clearance, Removal and Disposal

The D&C scope includes all necessary site clearance works, including removal and lawful disposal of abandoned vehicles, miscellaneous materials, debris and other obstructions within the housing sites.

For Package 4 – Butler Bay Lot 62, this specifically includes the demolition, removal and lawful disposal of the existing 10-person accommodation camp located on Lot 62D, including associated structures, foundations and redundant services.

Tenderers must assess existing site conditions and include all associated clearance, demolition, transport and disposal costs within their lump-sum tender prices.

4. Building Certifiers

Tenderers are responsible for engaging appropriately qualified building certifiers and obtaining all required certifications and approvals. Council does not nominate or endorse a particular certifier.

5. Product Inspection

Where a prefabricated or modular construction solution is proposed, Council is interested in inspecting the product off-site, prior to its implementation on Palm Island.

Tenderers are encouraged to identify suitable opportunities for inspection, including the proposed location and witness points, as part of their tender methodology.

6. Excavated Spoil Storage

Council will facilitate access to a suitable area for temporary storage of excavated spoil pending its removal or lawful disposal.

Tenderers should identify their anticipated storage requirements, quantities and proposed management arrangements within their submissions.

7. Additional Infrastructure Works

As this is a Design and Construct (D&C) procurement, tenderers are responsible for identifying, designing and constructing all works necessary to deliver safe, compliant and fully functional dwellings ready for occupation, including associated infrastructure.

Tenderers must refer to the Reference Designs, findings from the mandatory site inspections, any further investigations considered necessary, and additional technical information and scope clarifications provided by Council through addenda.

This includes, where required, retaining walls, earthworks, stormwater drainage, road and access improvements, utility connections and associated infrastructure within and surrounding the housing lots.

All necessary investigations, engineering, construction, testing and certification must be included within the proposed scope and lump-sum tender price, in accordance with the allocation of approval responsibilities established in the tender documentation.

8. Addenda and Tender Updates

Council is issuing a further addendum providing additional technical documentation, development approval information and site-specific scope clarifications across the housing packages.

Tenderers should monitor VendorPanel for this and any subsequent addenda, which will form part of the tender documentation.

The tender closing date remains Friday, 27 November 2026 at 2:00 pm AEST.

publicQuestions.answer:
Package 4 – Butler Bay Lot 62D: Existing Accommodation Camp Demolition

Council provides the following clarifications regarding the demolition and removal of the existing 10-person accommodation camp under Addendum 1, Section 6.1, Item 2.

1. Extent of Demolition

No detailed drawings or as-built documentation of the existing accommodation camp are available.

The D&C scope includes the complete demolition, removal and lawful disposal of the existing accommodation camp and associated infrastructure, including buildings, foundations, redundant services and other associated structures.

Tenderers are responsible for assessing existing site conditions, identifying the extent and construction characteristics of the infrastructure and allowing for all necessary works within their submissions.

2. Ownership, Access and Availability

Council will coordinate the vacation of the accommodation camp and provide the Principal Contractor with access to the site in accordance with the agreed construction program.

Council will arrange for the removal of occupants and personal belongings before the site is handed over for demolition.

The precise date of availability will be confirmed during contract finalisation and programming.

3. Hazardous Materials

Tenderers must allow for appropriate pre-demolition investigations, including hazardous materials assessments where required, and ensure that demolition activities comply with applicable legislation and WHS requirements.

Any identified hazardous materials must be managed and disposed of in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The treatment of unforeseen hazardous materials will be governed by the relevant contract provisions concerning latent conditions and variations. No separate provisional sum is established by this clarification.

4. Salvage and Relocation

For tender pricing purposes, tenderers should allow for the complete demolition, removal and lawful disposal of the existing accommodation camp.

As an alternative to disposal, Council may direct the Principal Contractor to relocate certain buildings, structures or components to another location on Palm Island.

Any such relocation requirements, including the scope, destination, methodology and associated costs, would be discussed and agreed with the successful contractor following engagement, if required, and managed in accordance with the contract's variation provisions.

5. Services Disconnection

The Principal Contractor is responsible for coordinating and undertaking all necessary service isolations, disconnections, capping and removal of redundant services associated with the demolition works, including engagement with relevant service providers where required.

Redundant infrastructure must be removed or appropriately terminated to ensure the site is safe and suitable for the proposed subdivision and subsequent residential development.

6. Foundations and Fill

The D&C scope includes removal of existing foundations, slabs, footings and other subsurface infrastructure to the extent necessary to accommodate the proposed subdivision infrastructure, earthworks and residential development.

Tenderers must also allow for the assessment and appropriate management of unsuitable material encountered during the works.

7. Demolition Waste Disposal

Palm Island does not have a landfill facility, only a Waste Transfer Facility.

The Principal Contractor is responsible for the removal and lawful disposal of all demolition waste on the mainland, including any hazardous materials, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

All associated waste handling, loading, transport, barge freight and mainland disposal costs must be included in the lump-sum tender price.

8. Site Reinstatement

Council confirms that site reinstatement means removal of the existing camp infrastructure and preparation of the cleared site to accommodate the proposed subdivision earthworks and associated residential development.

The final site levels, grading, compaction and associated works must be coordinated with the subdivision civil design and applicable engineering requirements.

General

Tenderers must review the Reference Designs, supporting documentation, mandatory site inspection findings and relevant addenda, undertake any additional investigations considered necessary and include the required demolition and site preparation works within their Package 4 lump-sum tender price.

Any material assumptions, exclusions or proposed departures must be clearly identified in the tender submission.

publicQuestions.answer:
Council provides the following clarifications:

1. Package Evaluation and Award

As outlined in the tender documentation, each package will be evaluated independently. Council reserves the right to award individual packages to different tenderers, and there is no guarantee that all packages will be awarded to a single contractor.

Package 6 – Gribble Street remains optional, and Council reserves the right to award or not award this package at its discretion. The decision will be made as part of the tender evaluation and award process.

2. Modular Construction and Alternative Foundations

Tenderers have flexibility to propose alternative design and construction solutions, including prefabricated modular construction and above-ground stump foundations, provided they comply with all applicable statutory requirements, the Principal's Requirements and relevant housing standards.

Tenderers are responsible for demonstrating that their proposed solutions are compliant, technically suitable and appropriate for the site conditions, including providing supporting engineering and technical evidence.

3. Accommodation and Meals

Existing accommodation options on Palm Island include the Palm Island Motel and Klub Kuda, subject to availability.

The Principal Contractor is responsible for arranging its own workforce accommodation, meals and associated logistics.

Council is currently undertaking a separate procurement process aimed at expanding accommodation capacity on Palm Island.

4. Availability of Suitable Fill Material

Suitable compactable fill material may be available on Palm Island, subject to availability and the applicable charges under Council's Fees and Charges Schedule.

However, Council cannot guarantee the availability, quantity or suitability of locally sourced material.

Tenderers should therefore allow for the supply and transportation of suitable compactable fill from the mainland when preparing their tender prices, to avoid reliance on unconfirmed local supply.

5. Limitation of Liability

Any proposed limitation of liability, including a cap of 10% of the contract sum, must be clearly identified as a contractual departure in the relevant Tender Return Schedule.

Council will consider proposed departures during the tender evaluation process. Acceptance of any departure is not guaranteed.

6. Liquidated Damages

Any proposed amendment to the liquidated damages provisions, including a pro-rata reduction based on completed or handed-over dwellings, must be clearly identified as a contractual departure in the relevant Tender Return Schedule.

Council will consider proposed departures during the tender evaluation process. Acceptance of any departure is not guaranteed.

Gregadoo Waste Management Centre Extraction Pumps Renewal & Maintenance

Project Location

Description

The project involves the design, supply, installation, commissioning, maintenance and servicing of nine replacement leachate and groundwater extraction pumps at the Gregadoo Waste Management Centre (GWMC). The works include removal of existing pumps and associated equipment, installation of new pumps with electrical, communications, solar and battery systems, integration with Council’s SCADA network, testing and commissioning, provision of operations and maintenance documentation, and ongoing maintenance for an initial two-year period with options for extension. The Contract comprises the design, supply, installation and commissioning works together with an initial maintenance and servicing period of twenty-four (24) months, with four (4) optional extension periods of twelve (12) months each at Council's sole discretion.

title: Commercial Development and Operation of Workers Accommodation Precinct – Palm Island
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council invites proposals from suitably qualified and financially capable organisations for the commercial development, establishment and operation of a Workers Accommodation Precinct on Palm Island, Queensland.

The precinct is intended to support Council's extensive capital works program and other construction, infrastructure and commercial activities anticipated on the island over the coming years.

Council seeks flexible, commercially sustainable proposals for accommodation facilities and associated infrastructure, potentially including furnished and air-conditioned accommodation, catering and dining facilities, recreational amenities, laundry, carparking, contractor laydown areas and essential services.

Proponents are encouraged to undertake their own market demand assessments and propose suitable accommodation capacity, development staging, investment arrangements and operating models.

Council's preferred arrangement involves a privately financed and operated facility, with the operator contracting directly with accommodation customers and paying Council rent for the use of the land. Proposals involving Council contributions towards enabling infrastructure may also be considered.

Initial accommodation operations are targeted to commence from April 2027. Council is progressing the Development Application separately, and the successful proponent will be required to coordinate with Council's planning consultants and undertake mobilisation activities concurrently with the approvals process.

Proponents are invited to propose commercially appropriate lease durations, renewal arrangements and rental structures. Consideration will also be given to the potential adaptability of the precinct for future hospitality and tourism accommodation purposes.

The proposed development site is located on Great Palm Island, Queensland, within an area endorsed by Council for this purpose.

Further project details, requirements and submission conditions are provided in the Invitation to Tender documents.

Tender closing date: Monday, 23 November 2026 at 2:00 pm AEST.

All formal tender enquiries and submissions must be made through VendorPanel.

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Monday 30 November 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is progressing a substantial capital works program involving housing, roads, utilities, community infrastructure, tourism facilities and other developments. These projects, together with additional investments by government agencies and private developers, are expected to generate significant demand for temporary workforce accommodation on Palm Island.

Existing accommodation facilities have limited capacity to support the anticipated construction activity. Council therefore intends to facilitate the establishment of a commercially operated Workers Accommodation Precinct.

Site and land arrangements

The proposed precinct is located within the Town Area defined under the Palm Island Improved Future Land Practices Indigenous Land Use Agreement (2010). The site has been endorsed by the elected Council, which has confirmed its authority to grant the relevant land interest.

The successful proponent will be expected to enter into an appropriate commercial land tenure arrangement with Council, with the lease duration, renewal arrangements and rental structure to be determined through the procurement and negotiation process.

Planning and development coordination

Council is independently progressing the Development Application through Milford Planning and Langtree Consulting Engineers.

Proponents must ensure their proposed accommodation concepts, layouts, infrastructure requirements and staging arrangements are compatible with the overarching planning and development approval process.

The successful proponent will be required to liaise with Council's appointed consultants and progress mobilisation activities concurrently with the Development Application, targeting initial accommodation operations from April 2027, subject to statutory approvals.

Accommodation and infrastructure requirements

The precinct should provide safe, comfortable, appropriately serviced accommodation suited to Palm Island's remote location and tropical climate.

Proponents should consider accommodation configurations, catering and dining facilities, recreational amenities, laundry, parking, contractor laydown areas, utilities, wastewater management, cyclone resilience, accessibility and other operational requirements.

Accommodation capacity, development staging and infrastructure solutions are intentionally not prescribed. Proponents are expected to assess the market independently and propose commercially viable solutions capable of responding to demand over time.

Commercial considerations

Council prefers privately financed development and operations, with accommodation customers contracting directly with the operator and the operator assuming commercial occupancy risk.

Council contributions towards enabling infrastructure may be proposed where justified. All proposals must include land rental consideration payable to Council.

The potential for future conversion to hospitality and tourism accommodation is desirable but is not a mandatory requirement.

Proponents should refer to the Invitation to Tender documentation, indicative site plan and capital works information for further details.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a commercially sustainable, professionally managed Workers Accommodation Precinct that supports the delivery of Palm Island's substantial capital works program while generating long-term economic and community benefits.

Desired Outcomes

Establish operational workforce accommodation from April 2027, with capacity and subsequent expansion determined by demonstrated market demand.

Deliver safe, comfortable, cyclone-resilient and appropriately serviced accommodation suited to Palm Island's remote tropical environment.

Provide suitable supporting facilities, including full catering and dining services, recreational amenities, laundry, parking, contractor laydown areas and essential infrastructure.

Encourage private sector investment, with proponents independently assessing demand, securing customers and managing commercial occupancy risk.

Establish a financially sustainable arrangement that generates ongoing land rental income for Council.

Enable progressive infrastructure development and expansion in response to construction activity and other accommodation opportunities on the island.

Support local employment, training, Indigenous business participation and economic development.

Desirable Features (Non-Mandatory)

Private ensuite rooms or self-contained accommodation units.

Flexible modular infrastructure that can be relocated, expanded or reconfigured.

High-quality recreational facilities, including a gym and communal spaces.

Energy-efficient design, renewable energy solutions and sustainable water and wastewater management.

Accommodation and facilities adaptable for future hospitality and tourism operations.

Commercial proposals that minimise Council's financial contribution while providing attractive long-term lease returns.

Conditions and Performance Expectations

The successful proponent will be expected to:

Coordinate closely with Council, Milford Planning and Langtree Consulting Engineers throughout planning, design and mobilisation.

Maintain a realistic implementation programme targeting operational readiness from April 2027.

Comply with applicable planning, building, work health and safety, environmental, cultural heritage and operational requirements.

Maintain appropriate insurances, licences, certifications and documented management systems.

Provide effective facilities management, maintenance, housekeeping, catering, security and emergency response arrangements.

Maintain transparent accommodation tariffs, booking arrangements and agreed mechanisms for future price adjustments.

Meet agreed standards for accommodation availability, cleanliness, maintenance, catering quality, customer service and incident response.

Provide regular performance reporting covering occupancy, accommodation capacity, operational performance, maintenance, safety and agreed community benefits.

Maintain the leased land and facilities in good condition and comply with agreed end-of-lease and site handback obligations.

Key Project Benefits

The project is expected to strengthen Palm Island's capacity to deliver major infrastructure and housing investments, reduce accommodation constraints affecting construction contractors, attract private investment, generate rental revenue for Council and create local employment and business opportunities.

Council also recognises the potential longer-term value of infrastructure that could support hospitality and tourism activities following the peak construction period.

Council welcomes innovative proposals and alternative commercial arrangements, provided they demonstrate financial viability, credible delivery capability, appropriate risk allocation and measurable benefits to Palm Island and its community.

Proponents should refer to Parts A, B, C and D of the Invitation to Tender for the detailed requirements, proposed commercial framework and return schedules.

2.2 Replace external wall cladding

Inspect existing external wall cladding and underlying substrate. Remove and dispose of nominated deteriorated cladding; supply and install suitable replacement external cladding, flashings, trims, fixings and weatherproofing. Match existing appearance where practical, subject to Shire approval. Confirm extent, material and finish in quotation. Where required, supply and install new Ametilin reflective insulation prior to cladding being installed.

2.3 Reline internal walls

Remove damaged or unsuitable internal wall finishes in nominated areas and prepare framing/substrate. Supply and install plasterboard (Gyprock or equivalent), moisture-resistant linings in wet areas where required, and ceramic tiles or other Shire-approved finishes as appropriate to each location. Include jointing, waterproofing where required, trims and a paint-ready/finished surface as specified in quotation. Identify rooms and measured areas at site inspection.

2.4 Repair eaves and assess termite damage

Inspect eaves, soffits, fascia edges and accessible supporting timber for evidence of termite (white ant) activity or deterioration. Remove and replace damaged materials and repair affected structural elements only after assessment and Shire approval. Arrange a licensed/appropriately qualified pest management inspection and treatment if active termites or treatment needs are identified; provide findings and treatment records. Quote any concealed structural repairs separately as provisional work.

2.5 Air-conditioning unit

Inspect the existing unit and installation to determine whether repair or replacement is appropriate. Provide a separate price for supply, removal and installation of a suitably sized air-conditioning unit, including commissioning and compliant condensate drainage. Clearly identify electrical/refrigeration work and whether it is included; the Shire may arrange its own electrician or licensed specialist. Confirm capacity, model and location before ordering. title: Complex Utilities Network Assets - Upgrade and Renewal program - MARKET SOUNDING
description:
The City operates a network of water and wastewater assets. Aspects of this infrastructure are ageing, resulting in increasing maintenance, renewal and operational costs, and increasing the risk of asset failure. To maintain reliable services for the community and support future growth, the City is considering a long-term program of upgrade works for complex water and wastewater infrastructure. The program is expected to comprise the replacement and renewal of large-diameter wastewater, water and stormwater pipelines as well as pump station upgrades.

The City has:

•	378 km of sewer rising mains and 3110 km of sewage gravity mains.

•	545 sewage pump stations

•	4 sewage treatment plants

•	488 km of trunk water mains and 2911 km of water reticulation pipelines

•	2,700 km of stormwater drainage pipes.

A significant portion of the contract scope of works will be the renewal and upgrade of large sewer rising mains, including larger diameter pipelines, and upgrading sewage pump stations. This infrastructure is located in an urban environment and may be located in major roads, under bridges or crossing waterways. The program may also contain upgrade of large capacity or complex gravity sewer, water and stormwater assets.

Program delivery is planned to occur over 10 years. While the program is not yet fully defined and is expected to mature with market input, it is expected to include:

•	substantial upgrades to the EWFM system, including installation of sewer rising main pipelines greater than 1m in diameter and upgrades to 19+ pump stations

•	major sewer upgrades in Southport

•	projects to support growth in the City

•	emergent water, wastewater and stormwater projects (note most likely to be wastewater).

•	identify key risks and constraints that may impact upon successful program delivery.

•	explore how the program can sustain competitive tension and deliver value for money over its life.

•	meet the City’s delivery expectations while maintaining a construction packaging strategy that minimises community impacts and meets all of government interfacing projects (such as Gold Coast light rail and Brisbane 2032 Olympics needs).

title: Cyber Security Operations Centre CSOC
description:
SR91442681, Request for information, managed Cyber Security Operations Centre

Energy Queensland is seeking information from established suppliers for a managed Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) service across its corporate IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments.

The indicative scope includes 24x7 security monitoring, alert triage and investigation, incident notification and escalation, threat hunting, threat intelligence, detection and security platform engineering, OT security monitoring, and on-demand incident response and digital forensics. It also includes service management, incident exercises, knowledge transfer, transition and exit support.

Suppliers must support Microsoft Sentinel as EQL’s target security information and event management platform and integrate with EQL’s security platforms and ServiceNow. The service will operate alongside EQL’s internal teams, with EQL retaining incident command, risk acceptance and operational decisions.

This request is intended for suppliers with - An operational Australian-based 24x7 CSOC, Brisbane-based engagement and access to incident response, forensic and OT specialists.

Proven managed monitoring capability across both IT and OT environments.

Relevant electricity-sector or Australian critical infrastructure experience, supported by two comparable customer references.

Capacity to keep all EQL data handling within Australia, with no offshore access.

Willingness to use the Queensland Information Technology Contracting (QITC) framework for a future engagement.

This is an information-gathering and capability-screening activity, not a request for tender or a commitment to procure. It is not intended for software-only, advisory-only, penetration testing or staff augmentation offerings. Responses will inform EQL’s future service requirements and sourcing approach.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Energy Queensland (EQL) currently uses a hybrid managed Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) service across its corporate IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments. EQL retains responsibility for cyber security strategy, governance, risk acceptance, incident command and operational decisions. The managed service provides specialist capability and continuous operational coverage.

The current arrangement is approaching the end of its contracted term. This RFI seeks market information on available capabilities, service models, technologies, commercial approaches and transition practices to inform EQL’s future sourcing strategy. It is not a request for tender or a commitment to procure.

The proposed service must support Microsoft Sentinel as EQL’s target security information and event management (SIEM) platform. Suppliers should describe integration with Microsoft Defender, ServiceNow and other EQL-owned security platforms. Security incident records must be maintained in EQL’s ServiceNow environment or supported through bidirectional integration with supplier tooling.

The current environment includes Palo Alto XSOAR for enrichment, workflows, threat intelligence integration and approved response playbooks. EQL is considering future platform changes. Other than Microsoft Sentinel, the listed platforms provide context and do not commit EQL to retaining every component.

The service must support enterprise IT and passive OT monitoring, work with EQL teams and other service providers, and preserve EQL’s operational control. All EQL data handling must remain within Australia, with no offshore access. Suppliers must support monitoring and response continuity during transition and exit, and explain how service records, detection content, playbooks and documentation remain portable.

title: Cleaning and Waste Management Services at SSCT for 3 Years (Package A, B and C)
description:
Cleaning and waste management services across its venue portfolios for 3 years:

1. Melbourne Sports and Aquatic Centre (MSAC), including Sports House

2. Lakeside Stadium

3. State Netball and Hockey Centre (SNHC)

4. State Basketball Centre (SBC)

5. Albert Park Pit Building

The Invitation is issued as three concurrent packages, endorsed by SSCT's core-and-flex service delivery model:

Package A – Integrated Cleaning and Waste: Routine, periodic, and reactive cleaning; washroom, sanitary and hygiene services; accessible glazing; consumables custodianship; waste collection and resource recovery across all four venues; Tier 1 and Tier 2 event cleaning under the SSCT Event Scale Matrix (Contract Form: Services agreement, single provider)

Package B – Event Cleaning Services Panel (Tiers 3 to 5): Event cleaning for Tier 3 to Tier 5 events under the SSCT Event Scale Matrix (event waste only where directed by SSCT), with committed surge capacity (Contract Form: Panel agreements - standing offer)

Package C – Pre-qualified Specialist Services Panel: Specialist, periodic and ad hoc services by category (Contract Form: Panel agreements - standing offer)

Invitees may offer any one or more of Packages A, B and C. Package B and Package C are panel arrangements

publicQuestions.question:
Please clarify a couple items from the technical specification, regarding the following:

1. Unexpected finds (TS 2.2.4) – The specification only covers asbestos for unexpected finds. Could you please advise how other unexpected finds, such as drums, liquids, clinical or hazardous waste, are to be managed and paid for?

2. Diversion bund base (BOQ 5.01, TS 2.5.1) – BOQ 5.01 describes the diversion bunds as including a clayey fill base, but the specification forms the bunds from phytocap only. Could you please confirm whether a clayey fill base is required under the diversion bunds and is this clay captured in the BOQ?

Thanks,

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

2. BOQ item 2.05, 300m3 of asbestos. Can you clarify if our price is to include loading, carting and disposal off site, OR is to include moving and burying this internally within site?

3. Is heat bonding of joins in Geotextile required at all locations for the gravel toe, batter chutes, causeways, scour protection, etc. or is lapping as per the manufacturer's requirements suitable?
publicQuestions.answer:

2.	The price must allow to move and bury it internally on site by an accredited asbestos handler. Refer page 20 of the Technical Specification.

3.	The requirement for heat bonding of all geotextile joints is to remain as per the Technical Specification.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

Please see below 2 RFI's from our estimating team:

1)	For drain type 1, 2 and 3 the tender drawings show rock scour protection along sections of these drains, please confirm which BOQ item we include pricing to complete the scour protection work.

2)	The tender drawings show construction of a table drain, please confirm if turf is to be placed within this drain, also which BOQ item we include the pricing to complete the excavation and filling to form the drain and turfing if required.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Please include the BOQ item 5.08.

2. The earthworks associated with construction of the Table Drain are covered under the existing Work Item 2.07. However, it's been identified that the specific Work Item for the Table Drain was inadvertently omitted from the For Tender Specification and BOQ. A separate Work Item for the Table Drain should be included, consistent with the approach adopted for Roadside Drains Types 1, 2 and 3.

o	The Table Drain is approximately 54 m in length. For tender purposes, the Contractor is to allow for construction of the Table Drain shown on the Project Drawings (including turf), and the following requirements shall apply:

Works Requirement

•	Contractor shall be deemed to have allowed for all costs in relation to the construction (including site-specific works associated with excavation and filling) and installation of the Table Drain, including turf along the full length of the swale with a native non-invasive species.

•	The supply and installation of topsoil is included in Work Item 2.6.1.

Payment and Measurement

•	Measurement and payment for this item is based on the linear metres of Table Drain installed in accordance with Project Drawings, as measured by survey and agreed by the Superintendent.

title: IRC-IS-0526-T476 Regional LED Lighting Renewal and Upgrade Program 2026-27 v2
description:
Isaac Regional Council (Council) is seeking to engage suitably qualified contractors to undertake investigation, assessment, design, and/or upgrade works across multiple lighting infrastructure projects within the Isaac Regional Council area.

The projects aim to improve public safety, usability, energy efficiency, asset reliability, and compliance with relevant Australian Standards through renewal and upgrade of existing lighting infrastructure at sporting facilities, aquatic centres, and public open spaces.

Each project is a separable portion which may be awarded in part or whole to one or multiple Contractors.

The projects are:

Project 1 - Moranbah Park Lighting Upgrade – Federation Walk

Non-compliance and Rectification Report review, investigation and rectification works, and the upgrade and replacement of public park lighting infrastructure.

Project 2 - Floodlight LED Upgrades at Clermont Swimming Centre and Middlemount Community Swimming Pool

Design and Installation of LED floodlight upgrades at:

a. Clermont Swimming Centre

b. Middlemount Community Swimming Pool

Project 3 - Clermont Sporting Oval Lighting Upgrade

Condition assessment review, investigation, and staged upgrade planning for sporting oval lighting infrastructure including lights, switchgear, underground power, and poles.

Project 4 - Dysart Rugby League Lighting Renewal Design

Design for renewal and upgrade of sporting field lighting infrastructure Dysart Rugby League facility.

Tenderers

An optional site meeting will be held via Teams - see Request for Tender v2 for further details

Tender closes 2pm 8 December 2026

Kind regards Isaac Regional Council

publicQuestions.question:
Council has listed RRJ PVC pipe from 80 to 200mm. Can we use 80 & 100mm SWJ pipe downstram of the control valve ?

Can we install a flow meter downstram of the filter for flow monitoring ? There is not on the pump shed drawings / If so would council prefer magflow or a mechanical flow meter ?

Is the filter backflush mechanism hyddraulically driven or electrically driven ?

Council specifies that services need to me manually potholes. Can they be HydroVaced ?

Do sprinkler laterals need to be sand bedded ?

Do the all pipe collars need to be raised off the trech floor as specified ?? Even 25, 40 & 50mm pipes ?? This is an overkill

Council specifes in the 90day warranty period that material that are damaged throgh vandelism and theft are to be replaced at the contrcors expensive !! Are you for real ??

Council specifies 2.5mm cable in the tender. You can acheive valve closure up to 3km's with 2.1mm. Can we use 2.1mm ??

Can we specify another Control System other than Galcon GSI. MRCC uses Hunter. Can I quote Hunter ??
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer

Please find the below replies.

1. Council has listed RRJ PVC pipe from 80 to 200mm. Can we use 80 & 100mm SWJ pipe downstream of the control valve ?

No. Council requires Rubber Ring Joint (RRJ) PVC pipe to be maintained as specified for all lines from 80mm to 200mm, including downstream of the control valves. Swan Hill soils are prone to seasonal movement, shifting, and thermal expansion/contraction. RRJ provides the necessary joint flexibility to prevent catastrophic cracking under sports ovals, whereas SWJ creates a rigid line vulnerable to ground shear.

2. Can we install a flow meter downstream of the filter for flow monitoring ? There is not on the pump shed drawings / If so would council prefer magflow or a mechanical flow meter ?

Yes, a flow meter is highly desirable. Please install it downstream of the filter in the pump shed. Council prefers an electromagnetic flow meter (magflow) rather than a mechanical meter. Magflow meters have no moving parts, meaning lower long-term maintenance, zero pressure drop across the device, and superior accuracy when handling raw or slightly turbid water typical of irrigation reserves.

3. Is the filter backflush mechanism hydraulically driven or electrically driven?

The backflush mechanism itself is hydraulically driven (using the system's internal water pressure via hydraulic valves to reverse the flow), but it is initiated by an electrical signal/controller (usually a 24V AC or DC pulse trigger via a differential pressure switch or timer). Tenderers must ensure the design accommodates electrical control wiring back to the main cabinet.

4. Council specifies that services need to me manually potholes. Can they be HydroVaced ?

We prefer manual potholing, however, using Hydrovac may be considered as long as due care is taken not to disturb the existing assets. Requested to mention both the options in your quote, if possible.

5. Do sprinkler laterals need to be sand bedded ?

Yes, all sprinkler laterals must be sand bedded. To protect the PVC lines from localized damage and friction leaks caused by sharp clay clods or stones during trench backfilling and future soil compaction, a minimum 75mm to 100mm sand envelope (bedding and overlay) is required. Relying on native site backfill for lateral lines is not approved.

6. Do the all pipe collars need to be raised off the trench floor as specified ?? Even 25, 40 & 50mm pipes ?

Yes, this rule applies across all specified sizes. Raising the collars/sockets off the trench floor ensures that the pipe barrel rests evenly on a continuous underlay of compacted bedding sand rather than bridging across high spots. This avoids localized point-loading stress on the joints once the trench is backfilled and heavy turf-maintenance machinery runs over the ovals.

7. Council specifies in the 90 day warranty period that material that are damaged through vandalism and theft are to be replaced at the contractors' expense.

Please ignore the vandalism and theft part.

8. Council specifies 2.5mm cable in the tender. You can achieve valve closure up to 3km's with 2.1mm. Can we use 2.1mm??

No. Please adhere strictly to the 2.5mm² cable specification. While 2.1mm² cable may achieve valve closure mathematically up to 3km under perfect conditions, Council specifies 2.5mm² to account for standard electrical degradation, voltage drop under heavy simultaneous multi-valve operations, and future network expansions. Sticking to 2.5mm² ensures system reliability and fits Council's regional maintenance compatibility requirements.

9. Can we specify another Control System other than Galcon GSI. MRCC uses Hunter. Can I quote Hunter??

Council prefers sticking to the specifications. However, please feel free to quote for alternatives as well.

Clarification – PVC trench widths and depths

Could Council please confirm the trench width and minimum pipe cover requirements for all PVC pipework, including the DN200 mainline from the pump station to the irrigation valves and all smaller pipes down to DN25, including sprinkler submains and laterals?

The PVC detail on Sheet 3 specifies a minimum trench width of the pipe outside diameter plus 200 mm, allowing 100 mm clearance each side. Does this apply to every pipe size, or would narrower trenches be accepted for smaller pipes where the required bedding, support and compaction can be achieved? If permitted, please specify the minimum widths.

The 600 mm minimum cover is shown on the HDPE/RCP details, while the PVC detail only dimensions 50 mm minimum bedding below the pipe and 150 mm protective embedment above it. Please confirm whether 600 mm cover also applies to all PVC pipe sizes, or specify the minimum cover permitted for mainlines, submains and laterals, including any increased requirements at road, driveway or access-track crossings.

For clarity, please state cover as the distance from finished ground level to the top of the pipe, rather than total trench excavation depth.
publicQuestions.answer:
•	Mainlines (DN80 to DN200): The strict rule of pipe outside diameter (OD) plus 200mm minimum trench width must be maintained for all primary lines. This provides a mandatory 100mm of side-support clearance on each side of the pipe to allow proper compaction of the sand envelope and to visually inspect the Rubber Ring Joints (RRJ).

•	Smaller Lines (DN25 to DN50): For the smaller sub-mains and sprinkler laterals (DN25, DN40, DN50), a narrower trench width is acceptable down to a minimum of the pipe OD plus 100mm (50mm clearance on each side). This variance is strictly conditional on the contractor demonstrating void-free side-support tamping and a complete sand embedment zone around the pipe barrel.

Minimum pipe cover is defined as the distance from the finished ground surface level to the top crown of the pipe barrel. To protect the lines from Swan Hill's highly seasonal clay shifting and aggressive turf care machinery (such as deep spiking and coring), the following cover schedule applies:

•	Mainlines (DN80 to DN200): 600mm minimum cover across all zones.

•	Submains & Laterals (DN25 to DN50): 450mm minimum cover within sports fields and established garden boundaries.

•	Roads, Driveways, and Vehicle Access Tracks: 750mm minimum cover is required across all pipe sizes. If existing underground utilities prevent achieving a 750mm depth at a crossing, the pipeline must be retrofitted through a heavy-duty protective conduit sleeve with a minimum of 450mm cover.
