publicQuestions.question:
1 We note that no geotechnical investigations have been undertaken for the project and that the Contractor is required to accept full responsibility for subsurface and groundwater conditions. Could the Principal please confirm whether any historical geotechnical reports or relevant ground condition information are available for the site? Additionally, given the lack of geotechnical information, could the Principal confirm whether unforeseen ground conditions, including rock excavation, unstable ground and groundwater ingress, would be treated as latent conditions and subject to a variation under the Contract?

2. Section 2 – Introduction of Part B Specification_V2.0 refers to “Decommissioning of the old pump shed and existing pump pit (no work on the shed for the Tennis Club).” Could the Principal please clarify the extent of the decommissioning works, including the dimensions and construction materials of the existing shed and pump pit, the number of pumps and extent of pipework and associated equipment to be removed, and whether complete demolition, removal or backfilling is required? Photos of the existing facilities would also be appreciated to assist with accurate tender pricing.

3. Could the Principal please confirm the location of the existing three-phase power supply connection point and the approximate cable run length required to supply the proposed pump station?

4. Can you please confirm if the pumps are operating under flooded suction or suction lift conditions? The current drawings show check valves on the suction side. If this is a suction-lift application, we understand the need for check valves on the suction side. If it is flooded suction, we recommend relocating the check valves to the discharge side as per standard practice.

5. Could the Principal please provide any available water quality analysis for the source water, particularly typical and peak levels of Total Suspended Solids (TSS), turbidity, pH, and any known algae or organic loading? Information on particle size distribution and seasonal variations in water quality would also be appreciated to assist with the selection and sizing of the filtration system.

6. Could the Principal please confirm the available supply pressure and flow rate for the automatic filter backwash cycle, including during periods of low irrigation demand? The proposed filter requires a minimum operating pressure of 2 bar and a backwash flow rate of approximately 5.6 L/s. Please confirm whether these requirements can be met under all operating conditions, taking into account the backwash discharge line backpressure. If the available pressure and flow rate are insufficient, please confirm whether a dedicated backwash pump and supply pipeline should be included in the Contractor's scope. If required, please identify the available water source and proposed connection point.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. There is an existing geotechnical investigation report that was used to design the irrigation system. It will be added as addendum. Please note unforeseen ground conditions, including rock excavation, unstable ground and groundwater ingress would be treated as latent conditions and subject to a variation under the Contract. The variation needs to be approved by the principal prior to any works commencement in the affected area/location. For more information related to variations, please refer to the tender documents.

2. The existing pump shed is not to be demolished. The tender specification or BOQ does not ask for the shed to be demolished.

3. There is an existing power to the shed. However, running cables for additional power to the shed (only if required) is on the principal. Tenderer doesn't have to consider this. But it is requested to propose the pumps as per the existing power, refer section 4.3.3. of the specifications for Electrical Power Requirement.

4. Operating Condition (Suction Lift): The pumps operate under suction lift conditions, not flooded suction.

 o	Pit Installation - Section View (refer tender drawings) shows the pump shed positioned on top of the dam embankment (minimum bank elevation 68.80 m), drawing water via a DN250 stainless steel suction pipe equipped with a DN250 S/S foot valve from the storage dam (maximum storage elevation 68.50 m, drawing down to 65.80 m).

 o	Provision to be made on the pump manifold for vacuum priming of the pump set.

 o	Additionally, the Grundfos NBG 100-65-200/217 pumps are noted as non-self-priming.

Valve Configuration: Because the system relies on suction lift and vacuum priming, check valves are required to maintain prime. Note that Drawing Sheet 2 of tender drawings (Typical Pump Station Details) currently illustrates check valves on the suction manifold side of each pump, while Sheet 7 also specifies a foot valve at the bottom of the suction line.

5. There is no water quality analysis report. The source water is non-potable raw water from the storage dam. Water to storage dam is supplied from GMW Channel. 400-micron automatic screen filter is recommended to be installed as the baseline requirement.

6. System Operating Pressure & Flow:

 o	The pump station is designed to maintain a constant operating pressure setpoint of 60 m head (approx. 5.88 to 6.0 bar) across all demand conditions—from near-zero flow (managed by the 7.5 kW VSD jockey pump, duty 7.2 L/s @ 60 mH) up to peak irrigation demand (56 L/s @ 60 mH).

 o	Because the automatic filter is installed on the pump station discharge manifold, the available supply pressure upstream of the filter will consistently be ~6 bar during normal system operation, exceeding your required 2 bar minimum.

 o	During low-demand periods, the jockey pump alone supplies 7.2 L/s at 60 m head, which exceeds the 5.6 L/s backwash flow rate requirement. However, if the system is in a "Low Flow Stop" standby state with zero irrigation demand, the filter controller will need to trigger a pump start (or run a backwash cycle immediately prior to system shut-down) to ensure the 60 m head is active.

Backwash Discharge Line & Backpressure:

 o	The backflush line must be sized according to the filter manufacturer's specifications and discharged back into the water storage.

 o	Because the discharge point is at atmospheric pressure at the top of the storage dam bank (~68.80 m EL, roughly 0–1 m above the pump shed floor), static backpressure is negligible, leaving ample differential pressure (~5.8+ bar) across the filter for backwashing.

•	Dedicated Backwash Pump: A dedicated backwash pump is not included in the design or scope, as the main/jockey pump manifold provides sufficient pressure and flow directly at the filter inlet.

publicQuestions.answer:
Irrigation Control System – Multi-Core vs. Wireless Radio Architecture & Cable Sizing

• Control Architecture Clarification (No Multi-Core Field Trenching Required): Following technical review with HR Products (the national distributor for Galcon), the irrigation control system is not reverting to a long-distance multi-core field wiring network. Instead, the Galcon 24-Station GSI Cellular Controller (GSI24AC) at the pump shed will be paired with an Irri-Gator 915MHz Wireless Radio System (comprising a 64-station input board G8R64AC, external transmitter G8RTX, and omni-directional aerial G8ROMNI).

• Field Valve & Receiver Arrangement: Communication to all Stage 1 and future Stage 2 field valves will occur wirelessly via 915MHz radio to local potted field receivers (G8RRX1SP / G8RRX2SP) mounted inside the valve boxes, connected to 12VDC latching solenoid coils.

• Wire Sizing & Spare Cores: Because long-distance multi-core control cables are eliminated from the trenches, Council will not be issuing active/common wire sizing tables or spare core schedules for Stage 2. Tenderers are only required to allow for short, local 12VDC control wiring tails (with a 1 m service coil as per Sheet 3) between the valve box radio receivers and the adjacent DC latching solenoids, plus the GPO and interface cabling inside the pump shed.

(Note: Council already utilizes this exact Galcon GSI + Irri-Gator wireless architecture across other parks and reserves to avoid long copper runs).

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Maddison Blockley-Ireland,

Greetings

Thank you for providing us with the opportunity to participate in Tender 2026-30 – Design, Supply, Construction, Testing and Commissioning of Solar PV System at Forbes Sewage Treatment Plant.

Following our detailed review of the tender documentation, we would appreciate Council's written clarification on the following matters in accordance with Clause 12 of Part 1 – Conditions of Tendering.

We have identified a number of technical, commercial and contractual matters that require clarification to ensure our tender submission is fully aligned with Council's requirements and that the proposed pricing adequately covers the project scope and associated responsibilities.

1. Flood Design Requirements

a) Section 2(c) of Part 2 specifies a flood depth of 1.4 m and a velocity of 0.2 m/s, whereas Section 2.3 refers to a flood depth of 1.2 m and a velocity of 0.4 m/s. Could Council please confirm the applicable design parameters? Pending clarification, we propose to adopt the more conservative combination of 1.4 m flood depth and 0.4 m/s flood velocity for our preliminary design.

b) Section 2.3 refers to an Appendix containing additional flood information. However, this Appendix does not appear to be included in the supplied tender documentation. Could Council please provide the referenced Appendix, including any relevant flood modelling information or supporting reports?

2. Project Commencement and Completion Dates

Part 2, Section 1 indicates that the system is to be installed, commissioned and fully operational by August 2027, whereas Schedule 2 of the Draft Contract specifies a completion date of 30 May 2027.

Additionally, Section 5 of Part 2 specifies a contract commencement date of 25 February 2027 with a duration of six months.

Could Council please confirm the applicable commencement date, contract duration and final project completion date to ensure our proposed project programme is aligned with Council's expectations?

3. Development Approvals and Extension of Time

a) Could Council advise the anticipated timeframes for obtaining the Development Application (DA) and Construction Certificate (CC), including the expected duration of the respective approval processes?

b) As Council is responsible for managing the DA and CC processes, could Council confirm how delays arising from statutory approval processing, Council reviews or other approval-related matters will be managed under the contract?

c) Will the Contractor be entitled to an Extension of Time (EOT) where project delays arise from circumstances beyond the Contractor's reasonable control, including delays attributable to Council or relevant authorities?

4. Pricing and Commercial Requirements

a) Part 1, Clause 15.1 requires tenderers to submit a Schedule of Rates, whereas Appendix 1 provides a fixed lump-sum pricing schedule. Could Council clarify the required pricing format and confirm whether tenderers are expected to submit a fixed lump-sum price, a detailed Schedule of Rates or both?

b) Part 4, Section 4.2 indicates that rates are to be GST-inclusive, whereas Appendix 1 is marked as excluding GST. Could Council confirm the correct GST treatment and the expected format for submitting the tender price?

C) Section 4.1 of Part 2 provides for annual CPI-based price adjustments, with the first adjustment to apply annually after the commencement of the contract. As the contract duration is specified as six months, could Council please confirm whether the CPI adjustment would only apply if the contract extends beyond the initial 12-month period, and whether any price adjustment would be available during the initial six-month project period?

d) Could Council clarify how the following specified project requirements should be allocated within Appendix 1, particularly where separate pricing items are not clearly identified: security fencing and gate, elevated inverter platform and staircase, monitoring system and SIM data, geotechnical investigations, and technical documentation and support associated with the DA process?

e) Could Council confirm whether any provisional sums or contingency allowances are required for unforeseen site conditions, additional civil works or other requirements identified during detailed design and site investigations?

5. Technical Information and Existing Electrical Infrastructure

a) Section 2.6 refers to Council providing an I/O port and PLC relay adjacent to the SCA No. 2 switchboard to facilitate solar system disconnection during generator operation. Could Council provide the generator-start signal details, PLC relay specifications, contact configuration, voltage and interface requirements to enable us to design the appropriate control arrangement?

b) Could Council provide the latest available electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, condition assessment reports and relevant technical documentation for the existing Main Switchboard (MSB), SCA No. 2 distribution board and associated submains, approximately 150 m in length?

c) Are there any existing geotechnical investigation reports or soil condition assessments available for the proposed solar PV installation area? If available, could these please be shared with tenderers to assist with preliminary structural and foundation design?

d) Could Council confirm the applicable network connection requirements, including the relevant Essential Energy connection standards, grid connection approval requirements, export limitations and any specific protection or metering requirements applicable to the proposed solar PV system?

6. Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs)

Section 2.1 of the Specification requires the Contractor to manage the creation and assignment of STCs on behalf of Council.

Could Council please clarify the applicable STC eligibility requirements and the expected arrangements for certificate creation and assignment?

Additionally, could Council confirm whether the STCs and their associated financial benefits are to be assigned entirely to Council, and whether the anticipated STC value should be considered as a deduction from the Contractor's tender price or treated separately?

7. Contractual and Payment Conditions

a) Could Council confirm whether any performance security requirements, including performance bonds, bank guarantees, retention amounts or liquidated damages, will apply to this contract? If applicable, please provide the relevant percentages, amounts, applicable timeframes and release conditions.

b) Could Council confirm whether a progress payment schedule or milestone-based payment arrangement will apply? If so, we would appreciate details of the proposed payment terms, payment milestones and claim submission process.

c) Could Council confirm whether the Draft Contract provided is the final proposed contract form? We note that certain provisions refer to goods, quotations and orders, and the term "Principal" appears to be used without a corresponding definition. We would appreciate clarification on these references and confirmation of whether any amendments are anticipated.

8. Local Preference

The tender evaluation criteria allocate 2.5% to Local Preference. Could Council clarify how local preference will be assessed, including the applicable eligibility criteria and whether consideration will be given to Australian businesses operating outside the Forbes region but within NSW?

We would appreciate receiving Council's written responses as soon as possible to allow us sufficient time to incorporate the clarifications into our technical, commercial and project delivery submissions ahead of the tender closing date.

Thank you for your time and assistance. We appreciate Council's support in clarifying these matters and look forward to your response.
publicQuestions.answer:

Therefore, the project will not be completed under a DA and will not require a CC but will be approved through a Review of Environmental Factors (REF). For this process the contractor is to allow 20 working days following submission of design and engineering certification for the racking (incorporating flood parameters) and electrical components above flood height or resistance. This will form a hold point.

(b) Delays in approvals outside of this timeframe (or other), the contractor will be eligible for Extension of Time (EOT) for Time Only through application of the contract.

(4)(a) Contractor is to provide the price breakdown as per the Schedule of Rates that includes both Exclusive and Inclusive Price.

(d) Please use line items as per below of the Appendix 1 fixed lump-sum pricing schedule:

Item 9 - Monitoring and Communications System - monitoring system and SIM data,

(5)(a)

The existing SCADA system monitors generator start.

The existing SCADA can be configured to open/close a contactor in a PLC cabinet immediately adjacent to SCA #2, but this is not presently set up.

The contacts in the PLC cabinet are rated to 230VAC or 24VDC, so tenderers may provide any solution with a source voltage compatible to the nominated grid protection isolating contactor. ??

(b) Only physical print outs exist, as photographed in the specification. The MSB supplies a distribution board “Inlet Works SCA No2” via a 350/400A circuit breaker. The submains are 2 x 300mm2 1C PVC per phase and run approximately 150m. Council does not have any other documentation or condition assessment reports

(d) Tenderer is to:

- Assume that interface protection is required.?

- Emergency backstop requirements shall be met by pausing generation.

- Assume that export limitation is not required.

- Gross generation monitoring shall be provided.

- The application process for permission to connect is as per Essential Energy requirements.

title: 201274 Cronulla Sports Complex Building Renewal
description:
Sutherland Shire Council is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the Cronulla Sports Complex Pavilion Renewal – Construction Works in accordance with the approved design documentation, technical specifications, relevant Australian Standards, statutory requirements and Council requirements. Tender response MUST provide evidence of successfully completed concrete cancer repair and roof replacement projects, including details of the works undertaken and client referee contact details. The response must also demonstrate relevant experience in construction, refurbishment or remedial works on heritage-listed or heritage-significant buildings, supported by evidence of completed projects. Submission must also demonstrate experience in proactive stakeholder engagement and coordination with local businesses, surf club and the general public. Provide examples of similar projects demonstrating effective stakeholder communication, construction coordination and management of subcontractors.

The Contractor shall provide all labour, supervision, plant, equipment, materials, temporary works, access equipment, testing, certification and other resources necessary to complete the works in accordance with the Contract Documents, approved drawings, specifications, relevant Australian Standards, National Construction Code (NCC), authority requirements and Council requirements.

title: Design and Construction of Dog and Duck Bridge
description:
Forbes Shire Council (Council) invites tenders to appoint one suitably experienced and qualified party capable of delivering the design and construction of a bridge over the existing Dog and Duck Floodway located on Wirrinya Road approximately 9km south of Forbes at Bundaburrah Creek. The project is funded through the NSW Government Regional Transport Resilience Fund and seeks to improve the resilience, safety and serviceability of the existing crossing. The project has completed environmental assessment and hydraulic investigations and is considered ready to proceed to detailed design and construction.

The Contractor shall be responsible for the detailed design, certification and construction of the bridge structure in accordance with the Specification.

There is a non-mandatory pre-lodgment site meeting at 10:30 AM on Thursday, 26 November 2026 at Wirrinya Road, 6.1 km’s south of the Newell Hwy

(33°27'5.52"S, 147°57'57.58"E). Please contact Council's Nominated Contact Person to RSVP. Attendance is not mandatory.

publicQuestions.question: Is the new bridge on the same alignment? Who is responsible for demolition of the existing structure?
publicQuestions.answer: The bridge will be constructed on the existing crossing alignment. Council will construct a temporary sidetrack to maintain access during the works and, as part of those works, will remove the existing concrete causeway and the existing road pavement to the extent of the bridge width. The sidetrack will be removed following completion of the bridge project. Construction of the bridge structure itself, including any clearing of the waterway required for the bridge and abutment works, will be undertaken by the Contractor.
